The Geometric Series Encyclopedia

595 entries across the volumes of the Geometric Series, companion to Data Mining as Observation. Built 2026-11-25 from commit 75e9737.

3

the 3.5 Decompositionconcept Geometric Education

The volume's worked illustration of two students, Alex and Ethan, who carry the same 3.5 grade point average and occupy different learner states.

A

Absorbing stratumconcept Geometric Ethics

A stratum $S_0$ with a tubular neighborhood N and a retraction r from N onto $S_0$ such that every compatible evaluation satisfies $S(p) = S(r(p))$ on N.

Absorption theorem for executable strataresult Geometric Ethics

If every gate leaving an absorbing stratum is triggered only by human-oversight events, then no sequence of events containing no oversight event moves the stratification out of an absorbing stratum. **Example.** Start at hostile and feed three events, an apology, Margaret's welcome and a claim to be her grandson.

abstentionconcept

The verdict a group receives when it has too few rows or too few queries to score.

accuracyconcept

The fraction of all rows a classifier labels correctly, the score most easily fooled, since predicting the majority class for every row scores the majority's share.

adequacy conditions for a scalar graderesult Geometric Education

A scalar assessment adequately represents the learner state when three conditions hold together.

admissibility (checks A1 to A4)concept Geometric Methods

The property that an experimental design could have failed.

admissibility of the Euclidean heuristic under a Mahalanobis metricresult Geometric Methods

In A* search with Mahalanobis edge weights, the straight-line Euclidean distance to the goal never overestimates the true cost exactly when every eigenvalue of the inverse covariance is at least 1.

Admissible heuristic fieldconcept Geometric Reasoning

A heuristic field is admissible when it never overestimates the true cost-to-go, so that $h(x)$ is at most the geodesic distance from $x$ to the goal region at every state.

Adversarial thresholdinstrument Geometric Reasoning

For one perturbation type, the smallest intensity $\epsilon^*$ at which performance falls more than a chosen tolerance $\delta$ below its unperturbed value.

Aesthetic Hilbert spaceconcept Geometric Aesthetics

The space of square-integrable complex functions on the aesthetic manifold.

Aesthetic Invariance Claimconcept Geometric Aesthetics

If two descriptions of a work are related by an admissible coordinate transformation, such as faithful translation between natural languages, then any legitimate geometric aesthetic feature assigns the same value to both.

Aesthetic manifoldconcept Geometric Aesthetics

The space whose points are probability distributions on a modality-specific embedding space.

Aesthetic regimeconcept Geometric Aesthetics

The local metric of one stratum of the aesthetic manifold.

Aesthetic Scalar Irrecoverability (Theorem 15.1)result Geometric Aesthetics

Any function $Q$ from a $d$-dimensional aesthetic tensor to a scalar verdict is not injective, so distinct works share a verdict.

Aesthetic tensor hierarchyconcept Geometric Aesthetics

Four levels of description of a work's embedding cloud.

Affective polarization as metric distortionconcept Geometric Politics

Affective polarization is modeled as the condition in which the perceived distance between an in-group voter and an out-group voter is much larger than their actual manifold distance. **Example.** In the volume's District 7 illustration the party centroids are 1.5 Mahalanobis units apart and voters perceive about 4.2.

aggregationconcept

Combining rows or groups into one number.

Agreement submanifoldconcept Geometric Politics

For a coalition, the set of dimensions on which every pair of members differs by at most a tolerance $\epsilon$.

alignmentconcept

The normalized overlap between a consumer's average read operator and the covariance of the data on the read subspace, written kappa, between zero and one.

Alignment gauge groupconcept Geometric AI

The group of transformations of an input that should leave the behaviour of an aligned AI system unchanged.

Alignment gauge violation tensorinstrument Geometric AI

A matrix V with one row per type of gauge transformation and one column per output dimension.

alignment, span and curvature of a pairingresult Geometric Gastronomy

The volume's conjecture that pairing quality is a function of three geometric quantities.

allocationinstrument

The assignment of a bit budget across directions.

anisotropicconcept

Of a covariance, having different variances in different directions.

anti arminstrument

In a flip comparison, a third code built to destroy the consumer's read subspace at the same bits.

anti-hubconcept

A row that is never or almost never retrieved as anyone's nearest neighbour.

anti-hub recallinstrument

Recall at k restricted to the rows that are rarely retrieved, the observer's outliers, reported as the minimum over strata so that a mean cannot hide the tail.

anti-monotonicityconcept

The property that support cannot increase when an itemset grows, which licenses Apriori to prune every superset of an infrequent itemset without loss.

Apriori principleresult

The statement that every subset of a frequent itemset is frequent, the contrapositive of anti-monotonicity.

Arrow's theorem, geometrizedresult Geometric Politics

For a preference manifold of effective dimension at least 3, no contraction to a one-dimensional social ranking preserves all of topology, orientation and symmetry.

assessment gauge invarianceconcept Geometric Education

An assessment A, which maps a learner state x and an instrument I to a score, is gauge-invariant when $A(x, I_1)$ and $A(x, I_2)$ differ by no more than measurement noise for every state and every meaning-preserving change of instrument.

Assessment Gauge Invariance Test Battery (AGITB)instrument Geometric Education

Five parallel assessments of the same content, each varying one of examiner, format, language, time and context while holding the others fixed, each with a pass threshold.

Asymmetric edge weight (legal)concept Geometric Law

The weight of a directed edge from case $i$ to case $j$ is the quadratic form $\Delta v^T \Sigma^{-1} \Delta v$, plus a penalty $\beta$ for each regime boundary crossed, plus a hierarchical cost.

asymmetry of coda decision boundariesresult Geometric Communication

Under the perturbations of the Decoder Robustness Index, misclassifications between sperm whale coda types run mostly one way.

attentionconcept

The operation inside a language model that lets each token look at earlier ones by comparing its query to their keys and averaging their values.

attention metricconcept Geometric Cognition

A positive-definite symmetric bilinear form $g$ on each tangent space of the cognitive manifold whose components are set by attention allocation.

attractiveness skewinstrument Geometric Methods

Model the retrieval count of a point as Poisson with mean $\rho w$, where w is its attractiveness, with mean one.

attribute conservation in closed exchangeresult Geometric Economics

In a closed bilateral exchange between agents A and B the changes on each transferable dimension sum to zero, so that the change for A plus the change for B is zero on money $d_1$, rights $d_2$ and autonomy $d_4$.

attribute typeconcept

The declaration of which transformations of a column keep its meaning, any injective relabelling for nominal, a strictly increasing map for ordinal, an affine map for interval, and a positive rescaling for ratio, nested in that order.

attributioninstrument

An assignment to each feature of a share of one prediction.

auditinstrument

A check of a number or system against its record by a reader who did not produce it, bound to a sealed file.

AUROCconcept

The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, equal to the probability that a random positive scores above a random negative, ties counted as one half.

B

bagginginstrument

Fitting the same model on bootstrap resamples and averaging.

bag of wordsconcept

A representation of a document as a vector with one coordinate per vocabulary term holding that term's count.

balance coordinate that degenerates at a boundaryconcept Geometric Methods

A balance coordinate d = (g - l)/(g + l) of two competing non-negative magnitudes equals plus or minus 1 exactly when one magnitude is absent.

balanced accuracyconcept

The mean of the per-class recalls, so that a large class cannot hide a small one.

barinstrument

A threshold a statistic must reach, written down before the measurement.

baselineinstrument

The simplest scorer a claim must beat under the same protocol, chance, a constant, an untrained encoder, or a single model.

base rateconcept

How common a cause or class is before any observation, the prior that Bayes' rule multiplies by.

Basin of attraction of a reasoning minimumconcept Geometric Reasoning

The set of states from which gradient flow on the evaluation function converges to a given local minimum.

basisconcept

A set of independent vectors whose span is the whole space, so that every vector is exactly one combination of them.

Bayes' ruleconcept

The probability of a cause given an observation, equal to the probability of the observation given the cause times the base rate, divided by the overall probability of the observation.

Bernoulli, binomialconcept

A Bernoulli variable is one with probability p and zero otherwise, with mean p and variance p(1 minus p).

BGE and Nash relationship (augmented game)result Geometric Economics

A profile is a BGE exactly when it is a Nash equilibrium of the augmented game, whose strategies are the simple paths to the goal and whose payoffs are the negative of behavioral friction.

bi-Lipschitzconcept

Of a map between two spaces, neither stretching nor shrinking any distance by more than a fixed factor.

binding affinity matrixconcept Geometric Gastronomy

The matrix $A$ with one row per receptor type (about 400) and one column per chemical species (about 10,000), whose entry $A_{ij}$ is the affinity of receptor i for molecule j.

bitconcept

The unit of a budget.

blind probeinstrument

An instrument that recovers a consumer's read operator from calls to the consumer alone, without access to its gradients or its code.

block error rateconcept

The fraction of transmitted radio blocks the receiver cannot decode, abbreviated BLER.

Bond geodesicconcept Geometric Economics

The minimum-cost path on the economic decision complex from an initial state to a goal region, where the cost of a path is the sum of its edge weights and each edge weight is the Mahalanobis term plus the penalties of the boundaries crossed. **Example.** Two paths to the goal with edge weights 1 + 4 = 5 and 2 + 2 = 4.

Bond geodesic equilibrium (BGE)concept Geometric Economics

A profile of paths, one per agent, in which each agent's path is a Bond geodesic on that agent's decision complex given the paths of the others.

Bond Indexinstrument Geometric Ethics

A dimensionless audit measure of how much an evaluation moves when only the description changes, $Bd = D_{op} / \tau$.

Bond Index disparity ratioinstrument Geometric Medicine

For one policy and two populations, the clinical Bond Index of the first population divided by that of the second.

Bond Index for AIinstrument Geometric AI

The expected excess geodesic deviation of a system's trajectory on the value manifold over the value-aligned geodesic, reported as nine components, one per value dimension.

Bond Invariance Principleconcept Geometric Ethics

If two descriptions d and d' of one situation are related by an admissible coordinate transformation, a legitimate moral evaluation assigns both the same value, $E(d) = E(d')$.

Bond Invariance Principle for reasoningconcept Geometric Reasoning

A judgment function $f$ satisfies the principle when $f(\tau(x)) = f(x)$ for every description $x$ and every gauge transformation $\tau$.

Bonferroni correctionconcept

Dividing the significance threshold by the number of tests, which holds the family-wise error rate at or below the original threshold whatever the dependence among the tests, at the price of being conservative.

boostinginstrument

Fitting a sequence of weak scorers, each on the rows the previous ones got wrong, and summing them.

bootstrapinstrument

An estimate of a confidence interval made by resampling the data with replacement many times and recomputing the statistic each time.

budgetconcept

The third element of an observer.

budget cliffresult

The finding that recovery of a read operator by a probe is a cliff at the full dimension of the space rather than a slope, and that the cliff does not move with the operator's rank.

C

cacheconcept

A store of recently used data kept so that it need not be fetched again.

calibrationconcept

The property of a score that a value of 0.8 means the row is positive eighty percent of the time.

Campaign Gradient Theoremresult Geometric Politics

A campaign is modeled as choosing a unit projection axis, the dimension voters attend to.

capacityconcept

The number of distinctions a model class can draw, the model-side half of the budget.

central limit theoremconcept

The sampling distribution of a mean of n independent values is close to normal once n is a few dozen, whatever the shape of the values, with standard error sigma over the square root of n.

certificateconcept

A claim, made at a time, that something is safe to act on.

challenge setinstrument

A test collection built so that a shortcut which passes the benchmark fails on it.

chance levelconcept

The value a rank statistic reaches on average under a random ranking.

chunkconcept

A piece of a document, the unit a retrieval pipeline encodes and indexes.

classifierconcept

A consumer that produces a score per row and turns it into a decision with a threshold.

Clinical Bond Indexinstrument Geometric Medicine

For an institutional policy and a patient population, the expected value over the population of the clinical friction of the path the policy mandates minus the clinical friction of the clinical geodesic.

Clinical decision complexconcept Geometric Medicine

A weighted simplicial complex on which clinical decisions are pathfinding problems.

Clinical edge weightconcept Geometric Medicine

The cost of one clinical action.

Clinical frictionconcept Geometric Medicine

The total cost of a path on the clinical decision complex, the sum of the clinical edge weights of its steps.

Clinical geodesicconcept Geometric Medicine

The minimum-cost path on the clinical decision complex from the patient's initial state to the goal region, where cost is the sum of the nine-dimensional clinical edge weights.

Clinical heuristic admissibilityresult Geometric Medicine

A clinical moral heuristic estimates the remaining cost from a state as the sum over boundaries of the penalty $\beta_k$ times the probability that the remaining path crosses boundary $k$.

Clinical-moral boundariesconcept Geometric Medicine

Thresholds on the clinical decision complex where the decision regime changes discontinuously, each with a penalty added to the weight of any action that crosses it.

Coalition fragility indexresult Geometric Politics

$F(C)$ is the share of dimensions outside the coalition's agreement submanifold, multiplied by the largest ratio of within-coalition variance to squared tolerance among those outside dimensions.

codebookconcept

The small set of allowed values a quantizer replaces each number with.

cognitive manifoldconcept Geometric Cognition

The set of cognitive states a system actually visits, hypothesized to form a smooth submanifold $M$ of the activation space whose dimension is far below the number of units.

cognitive profile tensorconcept Geometric Cognition

The vector of a system's scores on the benchmark's 21 subtasks, each between 0 and 1, written $C(S) = (c_1, ..., c_{21})$.

cognitive signature and signature distanceinstrument Geometric Cognition

The vector of a model's normalized subtask scores, compared between models by Euclidean distance.

coherence timeconcept

The interval over which a changing quantity stays correlated with itself.

cold, warmconcept

A cold measurement is taken before the cache holds anything useful, a warm one after.

Collective aesthetic tensorconcept Geometric Aesthetics

A multilinear map that takes one interest covector from each reader in a population and returns a collective valence direction on the manifold.

Collective alignment gapconcept Geometric AI

The distance on the value manifold between the Nash equilibrium of several AI systems, in which each maximizes its own scalar reward, and their Bond Geodesic Equilibrium, in which each follows the value-aligned geodesic given the others.

Collective geodesicconcept Geometric Medicine

For a population, the allocation of a resource such as vaccine doses that minimizes the sum of clinical friction over all its members.

column spaceconcept

The span of a matrix's columns, which is the set of every output the matrix can produce, of dimension equal to the rank.

commit hashinstrument

The fingerprint git assigns to a snapshot of a repository and its history, which identifies the content exactly and does not by itself prove when it existed.

Communication BIP (Bond Invariance Principle for communication)concept Geometric Communication

An evaluation $\phi$ that claims to measure meaning must satisfy $\phi(\tau(m)) = \phi(m)$ for every act m and every transformation $\tau$ of the communication gauge group.

communication fiber bundleconcept Geometric Communication

A bundle whose base space is the content manifold and whose fiber over a content is the space of surface realisations that can express it (linguistic forms, signals, pragmatic framings).

communication gauge groupconcept Geometric Communication

The group $G = T \times R \times F$ of meaning-preserving transformations.

communication heuristic fieldconcept Geometric Communication

A smooth function h on the communication manifold that gives, at each point, the estimated cost of reaching the intended communicative act.

communication manifoldconcept Geometric Communication

The product $M = S \times P \times C$ of a signal manifold S (the physical carriers), a pragmatic manifold P (intentions, social relations, illocutionary forces) and a content manifold C (semantic meanings).

communication metricconcept Geometric Communication

A Riemannian metric on the communication manifold written in three by three block form.

Communication Scalar Irrecoverabilityresult Geometric Communication

For any scalar evaluation $\phi$ of a communicative act, each level set $\phi^{-1}(r)$ is a submanifold of the communication manifold of codimension at most 1, so it has dimension dim(S) + dim(P) + dim(C) - 1.

Community of interest, manifold criterionconcept Geometric Politics

A connected subset of voters whose image on the preference manifold is also connected and compact.

commute timeconcept

The expected number of steps a random walk on a graph needs to go from one node to another and back.

composite convergence near 0.68 (capability frontier)result Geometric Cognition

The five models' composite scores fall between 0.63 and 0.72.

concentratedconcept

Of a spectrum, having a few eigenvalues that carry most of the total.

conditional probabilityconcept

The probability of A among the repetitions in which B occurred, the probability of both divided by the probability of B.

confidenceconcept

Of a rule, the support of the rule's itemset divided by the support of its antecedent.

confidence intervalconcept

A range that would contain the true value in a stated fraction of repeated samples, usually 95 percent.

confoundconcept

A variable that moves with both the treatment and the outcome so that a measured difference cannot be attributed.

confusion matrixconcept

The four counts a two-class classifier with a threshold produces on a test set, true and false positives and negatives, from which precision, recall, the false positive rate, and accuracy are read as conditional probabilities.

Consent as gauge invarianceresult Geometric Medicine

Consent is valid only if the patient's chosen path is the same under every meaning-preserving change in how the options are described, for example 90 percent survival restated as 10 percent mortality.

Consent invariance scoreinstrument Geometric Medicine

For a set of $m$ meaning-preserving transformations of the clinical information, the share of them under which the patient's decision stays the same.

Consistent group augmentationinstrument Geometric Reasoning

Training-data augmentation by a task's symmetry group in which the same group element is applied to every component of a training example.

Constitutional geometryresult Geometric AI

The replacement of a list of natural-language constitutional rules by constraints on the value manifold of four types, which are direction, boundary, trade-off and symmetry constraints.

consumerconcept

The function that acts on a vector, the first element of an observer.

Containment theorem for executable strataresult Geometric Ethics

If every gate whose target is an authority stratum is triggered only by system events, then no sequence of events containing no system event, whatever a learned model classified, moves the stratification into an authority stratum it did not start in. **Example.** Start at stranger and feed the events he says he is the plumber, then Margaret welcomes him.

contractioninstrument

A formula that reduces several axes to one verdict.

contrastive objectiveconcept

A training rule that pulls pairs declared similar together and pushes other pairs apart.

controlinstrument

A comparison arm that should not show the effect, run beside the arm that should.

control tensorconcept Geometric Cognition

A (2,0)-tensor $C$ at each cognitive state that gives, for each direction of perturbation and each direction of response, the control system's capacity to manage the interaction.

correctionconcept

An erratum or retraction, a change to a published number or claim that the record keeps beside the original, naming what was wrong and what replaced it.

correlationconcept

The cosine of two centred columns, between minus one and one, unchanged by shifting or rescaling either.

Corrigibility basinconcept Geometric Reasoning

The basin of attraction of the state "defer to human judgment" under gradient flow on the objective landscape.

Corruption tensorconcept Geometric Reasoning

The first-order response of a system's final judgment to task-irrelevant perturbations.

cosineconcept

The dot product divided by the product of the two lengths, between minus one and one, unchanged by rescaling either vector.

coupling nullconcept

The case, alignment near one, in which the read subspace and the high-variance subspace coincide and the reconstruction-optimal code is also the read-preserving one.

covarianceconcept

The expectation of the product of two variables' deviations from their means, positive when they move together, the off-diagonal entry of the covariance matrix and the numerator of the correlation.

covariance matrixconcept

The matrix of pairwise covariances of a set of rows, whose trace is the total variance.

coverageconcept

The fraction of decisions a certificate clears, reported beside its false-clear rate, since a certificate that clears nothing has a false-clear rate of zero and no use.

cross-corpus gateinstrument

The validation rule that an encoder votes only if its held-out AUROC on a corpus it was not trained on clears a preregistered margin over a bag-of-words null.

cross-entropyconcept

The expected bits per outcome when outcomes drawn from p are coded as if from a model q.

Cross-lingual invariance of the geometric featuresresult Geometric Aesthetics

For the same book in English and in another language, the channel values computed in the fixed English PCA-128 basis agree.

cross-lingual transfer of Hohfeldian classification (BIP experiment)result Geometric Communication

An encoder with an adversarially trained bond space, trained on 3.9 million Hebrew and Aramaic passages, classified the Hohfeldian relation (Right, Duty, Liberty, No-Right) of 68,000 English Dear Abby letters with macro F1 of 44.5%, against a chance level of 25% and an in-distribution ceiling of 79.99% from mixed training. **Example.** From the volume's figures, 44.5 divided by 79.99 is 0.556, the transfer efficiency of 55.6%.

Cross-modality sign flipresult Geometric Aesthetics

Two channels have opposite signs of association with reception in books and in music.

cross-support ratioconcept

The smallest item support in an itemset over the largest, with a threshold below which the itemset is discarded.

cross-validationinstrument

Splitting the data into folds and evaluating on each fold a model trained on the others.

cuisine as a distribution and its flavor eigenvectorsconcept Geometric Gastronomy

A cuisine is a probability distribution over flavor space, estimated from a corpus of recipes and summarized by its mean and covariance $\Sigma_C$.

Culinary Convergence conjectureresult Geometric Gastronomy

The conjecture that cuisines descending independent gradients on the same fitness landscape, set by a shared receptor complement, metabolic needs and cooking physics, reach clustered attractors.

curriculum as pathfindingconcept Geometric Education

A curriculum is a planned path through the learner manifold, given by a sequence of courses as waypoints, from the incoming student's estimated state to the goal region set by the degree requirements.

curvatureconcept

The second derivative of a consumer, which the finite difference of equation 0.8 does not read and which sets the error of the linear model at a step.

curvature-triggered transition (System 1 to System 2)concept Geometric Cognition

The volume's geometric form of dual-process theory.

D

D4 augmentation and the orbit-stabilizer countinstrument Geometric Methods

Apply the eight rotations and reflections of the square, the dihedral group D4, to a grid, and use the resulting orbit as equivalent training examples.

DBSCANinstrument

A clustering that calls a point a core point when at least a minimum number of points lie within a radius, grows clusters by reachability from core points, and leaves the rest as noise.

decision boundaryconcept

The set of inputs whose score equals the threshold.

decision treeinstrument

A classifier that scores by a sequence of axis-aligned splits, flat within each leaf, so that its sensitivity is zero almost everywhere and its importances count splits.

declarationinstrument

A sealed statement of what a study will count, drop, or treat as a failure, written before the run.

Decoder Robustness Index (DRI)instrument Geometric Communication

Perturb each signal with nine acoustic transforms at eleven intensities, re-extract the inter-click intervals, decode, and score each outcome by a graded distance $\omega$ that is 0 for an unchanged label and between 0.5 and 1 for a flip.

defect campaign, the recorded runcorrection Geometric Methods

The recorded run of the defect-prediction campaign did not recover the generator's structure.

degreeconcept

Of a node in a graph, the number of edges it has.

Deliberative Recruitment Hypothesis (gate H1)concept Geometric Cognition

The claim, labelled GC-DRH-1, that for a participant whose sensitivity profile was identified on a calibration block, process measures of deliberation on a disjoint test block peak at that participant's identified resolution boundary.

Democratic gauge groupconcept Geometric Politics

The group $G_D$ of changes to a voting function's input that should leave its output unchanged.

Democratic Irrecoverability Theoremresult Geometric Politics

A voting function maps the positions of $n$ voters on a $d$-dimensional preference manifold to an outcome space of lower dimension.

densityconcept

The local crowding of rows around a point, the coordinate the geodesic reader of a spectral embedding discards and DBSCAN and the density detector read.

deployment mismatchconcept

The failure in which the consumer that was evaluated is not the consumer that was deployed, or time moved between the two.

detectorinstrument

A scorer that calls a row an outlier, of four families reading distance from the mean, distance to neighbours, density relative to neighbours, or cluster membership.

determinantconcept

For a two by two matrix, ad minus bc, the number whose vanishing means the columns are dependent and no inverse exists.

developmental stages as topological transitionsconcept Geometric Cognition

The volume models Piaget's four stages as a nested sequence of manifolds, $M_0$ inside $M_1$ inside $M_2$ inside $M_3$, reached by dimension addition, metric stabilization and completion under logical operations.

diagnostic distance patterns (translation, sarcasm, paraphrase)concept Geometric Communication

Three profiles of the factor distances.

direction-only quantizerinstrument

A quantizer that stores each vector's length exactly and rounds its direction.

Discovered-constructed metricconcept Geometric Aesthetics

The volume's position on where the aesthetic metric comes from.

discretizationinstrument

Collapsing an ordered quantity to a few labels by binning it, so that values in one cell become indistinguishable.

Discrimination gapinstrument Geometric Reasoning

The correct-flip rate minus the wrong-flip rate.

disparate impact ratioconcept

The rate of a favourable decision in one group divided by the rate in another.

displacement-recovery dissociationresult Geometric Cognition

On the E2 emotional anchoring test, how far a perturbation moves a model's judgment and how often an inhibition instruction restores it vary independently across models.

distance concentrationconcept

The narrowing of the spread of pairwise distances as dimension grows, read in the book as the reader running out of resolution.

distortionconcept

The error a code costs a reader, the trace of the read operator against the error covariance.

Divergence of utilitarian and manifold-optimal triageresult Geometric Medicine

The allocation that maximizes total outcomes equals the allocation that minimizes total clinical friction when triage activates only the outcomes dimension and crosses no moral boundary.

Doctrinal heuristicconcept Geometric Law

A legal doctrine read as an A* heuristic.

Dose-response surface of adversarial probinginstrument Geometric AI

A map that gives the system's governance margin for each combination of probe type, intensity level and value dimension.

dot productconcept

The sum of the coordinatewise products of two vectors.

driftconcept

A change over time in what a consumer reads or in the data it reads.

Dual binding constraintconcept Geometric Reasoning

A human and AI system satisfies the constraint when the AI's reasoning trajectory stays in the permitted region of its manifold at all times and the operator's decision trajectory stays in the permitted region of the operator decision space at all times.

Due process as quotient regularityresult Geometric Law

Due process is the requirement that the legal evaluation map be well defined on the quotient of the space of legal situations by the legally irrelevant transformations.

E

early stoppinginstrument

Halting a boosting run when a held-out score stops improving.

economic Bond Invariance Principle and gauge groupconcept Geometric Economics

An economic evaluation J satisfies the principle when J of a re-described state equals J of the state for every meaning-preserving transformation, one that changes labels, units or accounting conventions and not the economic reality.

economic decision complexconcept Geometric Economics

A weighted simplicial complex whose vertices are economic states, each carrying an attribute vector of nine scores, whose edges are available actions carrying a nonnegative total cost, and whose higher simplices are bundles of actions that can be taken jointly. **Example.** In the volume's running example the state with no new barista and the state after the hire are two vertices, the hire is the edge between them, and each vertex carries nine scores..

economic gauge violation tensor and Bond Indexinstrument Geometric Economics

For a heuristic h, transformations i and states j, the entry $V_{ij}$ is h of the transformed state minus h of the state.

economic metric (inverse covariance as metric tensor)concept Geometric Economics

In the continuous limit of the decision complex the cost of a small displacement is $ds^2 = g_{ij}\,da^i\,da^j$ with the metric tensor g equal to the inverse of the nine by nine dimensional covariance matrix Sigma.

Economic No Escape conjectureresult Geometric Economics

If the economic decision manifold has components separated by the absence of any connecting path, and not merely by high boundary penalties, then no financial instrument, regulatory arbitrage or contract can create a transition between them. **Example.** The volume's candidate is the organ market.

economic singularityconcept Geometric Economics

A region of the decision manifold where the covariance matrix Sigma becomes degenerate, with its determinant going to zero, so that the metric, its inverse, diverges.

Educational Bond Indexinstrument Geometric Education

For an institutional policy P and a student population S, the expected learning deviation of the path the policy allows, measured against each student's geodesic.

educational boundaryconcept Geometric Education

A threshold on the learner manifold where the region a learner can reach changes discontinuously.

educational gauge violation tensorinstrument Geometric Education

A matrix $V_{ij}$ whose row i is one of the five changes of instrument and whose column j is a score dimension, with a single column for a scalar score.

educational heuristic fieldconcept Geometric Education

A non-negative function h on the learner manifold that estimates the remaining cost from a learner state to the goal region.

educational local minimumconcept Geometric Education

A learner state x from which the geodesic cost to the goal is greater than from some nearby state y, while the cost of moving from x to y exceeds the time, effort and motivation the student has.

Effective dimensionality of an electorateinstrument Geometric Politics

The number of eigenvalues of the electorate's six-by-six covariance matrix, taken from the largest down, needed to reach 85 percent of the total variance.

effective flavor dimensionalityconcept Geometric Gastronomy

The count of eigenvalues of an individual's receptor-response covariance $\Sigma_r$ that exceed that person's perceptual noise threshold.

effective rankconcept

The number of directions a matrix really uses, the square of the sum of its eigenvalues over the sum of their squares, defined for a nonnegative spectrum that is not all zero, with no cutoff to choose.

eigenvalue, eigenvectorconcept

A direction a symmetric matrix only stretches, and the factor by which it stretches it.

Eight legal dimensionsconcept Geometric Law

Eight axes along which a legal state is scored.

Einstein midpointinstrument Geometric Methods

The weighted centroid of points on the Poincare ball of curvature minus c.

embeddingconcept

A vector assigned to an object, a word, a sentence, a node, a document, so that nearness in the vector space stands for a relation between the objects.

Embedding cloud of a workconcept Geometric Aesthetics

The set $X(W)$ of vectors obtained by cutting a work $W$ into units (paragraphs, audio frames, image patches) and passing each unit through a fixed pretrained encoder.

empty quadrant (metacognition)result Geometric Cognition

In the plane of self-monitoring accuracy (M3) and effort scaling index (M4), split at a threshold on each axis, no tested model lies in Quadrant I, where both exceed the threshold.

encoderconcept

A model that maps an input to an embedding.

ensembleinstrument

A scorer that averages or votes several scorers.

entropyconcept

The expected surprise of a distribution, the bits needed per outcome under the best code, at most the log base two of the number of outcomes.

equalized oddsconcept

The requirement that the true-positive rate and the false-positive rate be the same across groups.

Equal protection as gauge invarianceresult Geometric Law

The equal protection gauge group is generated by transformations that change a party's protected-class attribute while preserving all facts, all legal attributes and all Hohfeldian bonds.

escalationconcept

The decision to hand an item to a person rather than decide it, the single-decision form of abstention.

estimator, unbiasedconcept

A rule that produces an estimate of an unknown quantity from a sample, unbiased when its expectation over samples is that quantity.

Euclidean distanceconcept

The straight-line distance between two vectors, which reads every coordinate at the scale it arrives in.

eventconcept

A set of outcomes of an experiment, the thing a probability is assigned to.

evictionconcept

Choosing what to drop when a cache is full.

Evidence status of the moral metricresult Geometric Ethics

The volume's statement, added in v1.28, that the moral metric is untested.

Executable stratificationinstrument Geometric Ethics

A tuple of a finite set of strata with an initial stratum, an ordered list of semantic gates (each with source strata, a triggering feature, a target and a boundary type), a set of authority strata whose rules grant an action, and a set of absorbing strata.

expectationconcept

The average of a random variable's values weighted by their probabilities, its long-run average over repetitions, also called the mean.

expected calibration errorinstrument

The average over score bins of the absolute difference between the mean score and the fraction of positives in the bin.

explained varianceconcept

The fraction of total variance retained by a set of principal components, the identity reader's criterion for a reduction.

F

F1concept

Twice the product of precision and recall over their sum.

false-clear rateconcept

The fraction of the decisions a certificate cleared in which the witness said otherwise, conditional on clearing and reported beside the certificate's coverage.

false positive rateconcept

The fraction of negatives a classifier labels positive, which like recall does not depend on the base rate, so that classifiers are compared across datasets by those two and not by precision.

False termination regionresult Geometric Reasoning

The set of states outside the goal where the heuristic reads below the stopping threshold while the true distance to the goal is large.

Falsification criteria (Appendix E.8)instrument Geometric Aesthetics

Four stated tests.

family-wise error rateconcept

The probability of at least one false alarm across a set of tests, at most the number of tests times the per-test threshold by the union bound.

Feasibility gradient of structural containmentconcept Geometric AI

The ordering of application domains by how well they supply what structural containment needs, which is physical grounding, canonical forms and audit infrastructure.

fine-tuninginstrument

Continuing to train an encoder on a new objective or corpus, so that its quotient changes.

finite differenceinstrument

An estimate of a derivative from two evaluations of the function at points a small step apart.

Finsler metric of the decision manifoldconcept Geometric Economics

A cost function F(x, v) of position x and direction v that uses one inverse covariance matrix for gain directions and another for loss directions, so that F(x, v) and F(x, -v) differ.

Fisher-combined significanceinstrument Geometric Reasoning

The statistic $-2 \sum_i \ln p_i$ over $k$ independent p-values, one per model.

flavor space and the flavor vectorconcept Geometric Gastronomy

A posited finite-dimensional perceptual space $\mathcal{F}$ in which every flavor experience is a point, every ingredient a vector and every culinary operation a map from the space to itself.

the flipresult

At matched bits, the outcome in which the code with the worse reconstruction error scores better on the consumer's task, while a code built to destroy the read subspace scores worst.

floor, ceilingconcept

A floor is a lower bound a quantity cannot fall below and a ceiling an upper bound it cannot exceed, each proved or measured and named as such.

food-pairing hypothesis as cosine similarityconcept Geometric Gastronomy

Represent each ingredient by a binary compound vector, with a 1 for each compound it contains.

footprintconcept

The set of entries a reader reads.

Forced contractionconcept Geometric Medicine

A decision process in which a nine-dimensional clinical-moral state must be mapped to one of a finite set of triage categories under a time limit that prevents full nine-dimensional pathfinding.

formula searchinstrument

A score written as a short expression in the features, such as the smaller of two features plus a third, with a threshold.

Four alignment failures as geometric pathologiesconcept Geometric AI

The volume sorts alignment failures into four pathologies on the value manifold.

Four-category hierarchy of clinical heuristicsconcept Geometric Medicine

A grading of a clinical heuristic $h$ against the true remaining cost $h^*$.

Four epistemic statuses (Appendix F ledger)instrument Geometric Aesthetics

The labels the volume puts on each formal claim.

Four geometric pathologies of lawconcept Geometric Law

Four ways the legal search goes wrong.

four geometric pathologies of marketsconcept Geometric Economics

The volume's classification of market failure into four kinds.

framing displacement (the 15.3 sigma effect)result Geometric Cognition

On the T5 test, rewriting a scenario in a euphemistic or dramatic register with the moral facts fixed shifts each model's total harm score beyond its own re-judging noise.

Frechet mean of an electorateconcept Geometric Politics

The point of the preference manifold that minimizes the sum of squared manifold distances to all voters.

freshnessconcept

Whether a stored value is still within its coherence time when it is read.

Frobenius normconcept

The square root of the sum of a matrix's squared entries, which also equals the square root of the sum of its squared singular values.

frozen-null gateinstrument Geometric Methods

A pass mark set as a margin over nulls, which are versions of the instrument that cannot contain the effect.

fusion as a geodesic between cuisinesconcept Geometric Gastronomy

A fusion dish is modeled as a point on the geodesic between two cuisine distributions under the Wasserstein metric on Gaussians.

G

gateinstrument

A bar that a build or a claim must pass before it proceeds, with the bar and the null written down first.

gate C1, the budget reversal contrastcorrection Geometric Cognition

Gate C1 was drafted to test ledger row GC-34, that under a budget manipulation with metric and ideal held fixed, order reversals concentrate on pairs trading a retained direction against an unresolved one.

Gauge-invariant alignmentconcept Geometric AI

A system is gauge-invariantly aligned when every entry of its gauge violation tensor is zero.

Gauge transformation of a problem descriptionconcept Geometric Reasoning

A map $\tau$ on problem descriptions that changes the surface presentation and keeps the task-relevant content.

gauge-variant pedagogical heuristicconcept Geometric Education

A teacher's estimate of a student's distance to the goal that depends on features of the student that are not coordinates on the learner manifold, such as race, gender, accent, first language or family background.

Gauge violation tensorinstrument Geometric Law

A matrix whose entry for transformation $i$ and outcome $j$ is the mean over cases of the absolute change in outcome $j$ when protected characteristic $i$ is swapped, divided by the original outcome.

Gaussianconcept

The normal distribution, in many dimensions the one whose density falls with the Mahalanobis distance.

Genre confound correction (books)correction Geometric Aesthetics

The books discovery result, R = 0.241 between cloud geometry and Goodreads rating on 4,998 books, was mostly genre.

Geodesic deviation of a reasoning trajectoryconcept Geometric Reasoning

The cost of a reasoning trajectory minus the cost of the geodesic that joins the same endpoints.

geodesic distanceconcept

The length of the shortest path along edges between two nodes of a graph.

geodesic divergence of the assessment-optimal pathresult Geometric Education

The path that maximizes a scalar assessment G at each step differs from the learner geodesic to the goal.

geometric decision costconcept

The cost of an alternative in a decision task is the Mahalanobis distance between the encoding of the alternative and the encoding of the task's reference point under the inverse covariance.

Geometric Evaluation Theoryconcept

An evaluator-relative theory of preference, value, and choice.

geometric feature vector (156 dimensions)instrument Geometric Communication

For one audio signal, the concatenation of 136 SPD features (the upper triangle of the matrix logarithm of the 16 by 16 frequency-band covariance), 4 spectral-trajectory features (path length, geodesic distance, deviation, step count) and 16 TDA features (8 persistence summary statistics each for $H_0$ and $H_1$). **Example.** A symmetric 16 by 16 matrix has 16 times 17 over 2 = 136 independent entries.

Geometric justification of a public health mandateconcept Geometric Medicine

A mandate is geometrically justified when three conditions hold together.

geometric loss-aversion coefficientresult Geometric Economics

The ratio of the edge weight of a loss to the edge weight of an equal gain, $\lambda = w_- / w_+$.

Geometric RLHFinstrument Geometric AI

A training protocol in which raters score responses on individual value dimensions, the value metric is fitted to those scores by inverse optimization under the constraint that it be symmetric positive-definite, and the policy is trained to minimize geodesic deviation from the value-aligned trajectory. **Example.** With d = 9 the metric has 9 times 8 over 2, which is 36, off-diagonal components.

geometric taxonomy of cognitive pathologyconcept Geometric Cognition

The volume's classification of four conditions by the geometric object that is defective.

geometric types of culinary transformationconcept Geometric Gastronomy

Each cooking process is a map $\Phi_\theta$ on flavor space set by process variables such as temperature, time, water activity and pH.

Gerrymandering indexinstrument Geometric Politics

Governance marginconcept Geometric Reasoning

The smallest geodesic distance, over the whole of a reasoning trajectory, from the trajectory to the safety boundary that separates permitted from forbidden states.

GPA Irrecoverability Theoremresult Geometric Education

On a connected learner manifold of dimension at least 2, a continuous surjective scalar assessment G is not injective, so distinct learner states share one score.

gradientconcept

The vector of a function's partial derivatives, the direction of fastest increase, whose dot product with a small step is the first-order change in the function.

gradient reversal layerinstrument Geometric Methods

A layer between an encoder and a domain head that passes its input unchanged on the forward pass and multiplies the gradient by minus lambda on the backward pass.

gradient reversal shortcut experimentresult Geometric Methods

On synthetic spectrograms in which the recording condition predicts the coda type 90% of the time, full gradient reversal lowered the domain head's training accuracy from 95.9% to 37.7%.

grading moral injuryconcept Geometric Education

The injury a teacher incurs when a mandated assessment G requires a grade the teacher judges to be a lossy projection of the true learner state x.

Gram and Schmidtconcept

The procedure that turns independent vectors into an orthonormal basis for their span, dividing the first by its length and subtracting from each next vector its projections onto the basis made so far.

graphconcept

A set of nodes and a set of edges joining pairs of them.

H

harnessconcept

The code that evaluates a model.

hashinstrument

A short fixed-length fingerprint of a file, computed so that any change to the file changes the fingerprint.

headconcept

One attention operation.

hedonic manifoldconcept Geometric Gastronomy

A hedonic function $H$ assigns each flavor point a scalar pleasantness.

Hellinger saturation in musiccorrection Geometric Aesthetics

In the music corpus the Hellinger feature saturated to about 1.0, because a Gaussian was being fitted to about 45 audio tokens per clip in a 128-dimensional PCA subspace.

Hessianconcept

The matrix of second derivatives of a score, whose off-diagonal entries are the interactions.

heuristic fieldconcept Geometric Cognition

A smooth real-valued function $h$ on the cognitive manifold that assigns each state an estimate of the cost of reaching the goal state, approximating the geodesic distance to it.

Heuristic fieldconcept Geometric Reasoning

A smooth function $h$ from the reasoning manifold to the non-negative reals that estimates the cost of reaching the goal region from each state.

Heuristic Truncation Theorem (moral heuristics as admissible heuristics)result Geometric Economics

A moral heuristic that charges, at each state, the sum over boundaries of the penalty times the probability that the action crosses the boundary is admissible when each penalty is a lower bound on the true cost of crossing.

hierarchical clusteringinstrument

A clustering that merges the closest pair of clusters at each step, under a linkage that reads the nearest pair, the farthest, or the average, so that merge heights never decrease.

Hohfeldian D4 groupresult Geometric Law

The four first-order Hohfeldian positions, right, duty, liberty and no-right, are permuted by a correlative rotation $r$ of order 4 and an opposite swap $s$ of order 2 that satisfy $srs = r^{-1}$.

Hohfeldian Klein four-group (V4)result Geometric Ethics

The four Hohfeldian positions Obligation, Claim, Liberty and No-claim carry two operations, the correlative s (O with C, L with N) and the jural flip n (O with L, C with N).

Hohfeldian octad gauge groupresult Geometric Law

The symmetry group of the full Hohfeldian octad is the semi-direct product of two copies of the dihedral group of order 8.

hubconcept

A row retrieved as a nearest neighbour far more often than chance allows.

hubnessresult

The excess of a few rows in the nearest-neighbour lists of many queries over what the Poisson ceiling allows, measured by the busiest count and the Robin Hood index, a property of the queries.

hyperbolic attention biasinstrument Geometric Communication

A term $B_{geo}(i, j) = -\alpha \, d_{\mathbb{B}}(e_i, e_j)$ added to a transformer's attention logits beside the position bias.

identity matrixconcept

The square matrix with ones on the diagonal and zeros elsewhere, which leaves every vector unchanged.

identity readerconcept

The consumer whose read operator is the identity, for which read distortion is mean squared error.

importanceinstrument

A per-feature score of how much a classifier reads it.

imputationinstrument

Writing a value into a missing cell that the consumer will read.

independenceconcept

Two events are independent when knowing one changes nothing about the other, so that the probability of both is the product.

individual variation as a rotation of the receptor basisconcept Geometric Gastronomy

Heritable receptor variation is modeled as a near-identity linear transformation $R$ of the reference affinity matrix, so an individual's basis is $A' = RA$ and their receptor vector is $\mathbf{r}' = R\mathbf{r}$.

inequality tensorconcept Geometric Economics

For a population of N agents, the entrywise variance across agents of the metric tensor each agent experiences.

ingredient embedding as a lossy projectioncorrection Geometric Gastronomy

An ingredient embedding assigns each food one fixed vector.

inherited heuristic and the empty-heuristic problemconcept Geometric Education

The inherited heuristic $h_P$ is the part of the educational heuristic field supplied by parents or family who have already been through the educational system.

Internal coherence (pair_sim_mean)instrument Geometric Aesthetics

The mean cosine similarity over all pairs of embeddings in a work's cloud.

intrinsic dimensionconcept

The number of directions a dataset varies along locally, whatever the number of its coordinates and whatever the number of its covariance directions.

inverseconcept

The matrix that undoes a square matrix, so that the inverse times A times x is x.

inverse flavor probleminstrument Geometric Gastronomy

Given a target flavor $\mathbf{f}^\star$, a palette matrix $B$ and a positive-definite metric matrix $M$, choose nonnegative doses $\mathbf{x}$ to minimize $(B\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{f}^\star)^\top M (B\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{f}^\star)$ under a cost ceiling and admissibility constraints.

inverted fileinstrument

An index that partitions vectors into cells by k-means and answers a query by searching only the cells nearest to it.

Irrecoverability of the binary verdict and the scalar sentenceresult Geometric Law

A binary verdict maps the eight-dimensional legal space to one bit, and a sentence maps it to one number.

isotropicconcept

Of a covariance, having the same variance in every direction.

itemsetconcept

A set of items that appear together in a transaction.

Jaccardconcept

The size of the intersection of two sets over the size of their union, between zero and one, zero exactly when the sets are disjoint, which discards joint absence.

Jacobianconcept

The matrix of partial derivatives of a vector-valued consumer, whose transpose times itself averages to the read operator.

Judicial Bond Invariance Principle (JBIP)concept Geometric Law

If a transformation of a dispute's description preserves the Hohfeldian bond structure, meaning the configuration of rights, duties, liberties, no-rights, powers, immunities, liabilities and disabilities among the parties, then the legal evaluation must be unchanged. **Example.** In the volume's example a landlord refuses a tenant for race in one case and for religion in another.

Judicial complexconcept Geometric Law

The judicial complex $\mathcal{K}$ is a directed weighted simplicial complex.

K

Kendall correlationconcept

The fraction of item pairs two rankings order the same way, minus the fraction they order differently.

kernelconcept

The directions a matrix sends to zero.

KL divergenceconcept

A measure of how far one probability distribution is from another, zero when they are identical.

k-meansinstrument

A clustering that minimizes the sum of squared errors to the cluster centres.

knowledge transfer as parallel transport, and transfer holonomyconcept Geometric Education

A piece of understanding is a tangent vector k at a point in one domain chart of the learner manifold.

KV cacheconcept

The stored keys and values of earlier tokens, kept so they need not be recomputed.

lagconcept

How far a replica trails the primary.

Landauer's principleresult

Erasing one bit costs at least Boltzmann's constant times the absolute temperature times the natural log of two.

language chart and translation mapconcept Geometric Communication

A language L is a coordinate chart on the content manifold, a domain $U_L$ of expressible meanings with a map $\varphi_L$ to the language's expressions.

language modelconcept

A model that reads a sequence of tokens and outputs a probability for the next one, scored by perplexity.

Laplacianconcept

A matrix built from a graph's edges whose eigenvectors, from the smallest eigenvalue up, are the smoothest functions on the graph.

Lasso-on-spectrum channelinstrument Geometric Aesthetics

latent semantic analysisinstrument

The truncated singular value decomposition of the term-document matrix, ordinarily uncentred, which coincides with principal components on documents only after centring.

law of large numbersconcept

The sample mean settles toward the expectation as the sample grows, its standard error falling with the square root of n, so that halving the error takes four times the data.

leakageconcept

Any information in the training data that could only be known after the decision, or any identifier that lets the model recognize a row it will be tested on.

learner geodesicconcept Geometric Education

The path from a student's current state to the goal region that minimizes total learning cost, the integral of $\sqrt{g_{ij} \dot{\gamma}^i \dot{\gamma}^j}$ along the path.

learner manifoldconcept Geometric Education

The six-dimensional Riemannian manifold of learner states.

learner metricconcept Geometric Education

A symmetric positive-definite tensor field $g_{ij}(x)$ on the learner manifold.

least-squares lineconcept

The straight line predicting one column from another that minimizes the sum of squared vertical errors, with slope the covariance over the variance of the predictor, passing through the two means, and accounting for r squared of the variance.

ledger classconcept

One of six labels every headline claim carries, proved, demonstrated, replicated, predicted, exploratory, or refuted, defined in the evidence ledger of Volume 14.

Legal Bond Index (LBI)instrument Geometric Law

Legal embedding and dimension probesinstrument Geometric Law

Legal frictionconcept Geometric Law

The legal friction of a path of cases is the sum of its edge weights plus, for each evidentiary requirement $j$, a weight $\omega_j$ times the shortfall of the path's evidence below that requirement's threshold.

Legal Invariance Principle (LIP)concept Geometric Law

A legal judgment procedure is well-posed if and only if its output is unchanged by every legally irrelevant transformation of the case.

Legal Mahalanobis distanceconcept Geometric Law

The distance between two cases is the square root of $\Delta v^T \Sigma^{-1} \Delta v$, where $\Delta v$ is the difference of their eight-dimensional attribute vectors and $\Sigma$ is the covariance matrix of the eight dimensions over the case corpus. **Example.** In the volume's illustration every variance is 0.04, so a difference of 0.3 on one dimension contributes 0.09 / 0.04 = 2.25.

Legal phase transition (overruling as graph surgery)concept Geometric Law

Overruling a precedent is a discrete graph surgery.

Legal Wilson loopinstrument Geometric Law

The ordered product of the Hohfeldian gauge transformations along the edges of a closed path of cases.

length, normconcept

The square root of the sum of a vector's squared coordinates, Pythagoras in d dimensions, which is also the square root of the vector's dot product with itself.

Liability-damages conservationresult Geometric Law

In a closed bilateral dispute under a fixed legal framework, the net liabilities of the two parties sum to zero.

licensed, not licensedconcept

A claim is licensed when it is a theorem checked in Lean in appendix C, or a measurement sealed with its commit hash before the run that survived its registered null and bar, and a chapter may rest on it.

liftconcept

Confidence divided by the consequent's support, so that lift one is the independence baseline.

likelihood, maximum likelihoodconcept

The likelihood of a model is the probability it assigns to the observed data, and maximum likelihood chooses the parameters that make it largest, which is minimizing the total surprise the model assigns, the cross-entropy with the sample standing in for the truth.

linear classifierinstrument

A classifier that scores by a weighted sum, logistic regression or a linear support vector machine.

linear combinationconcept

A sum of scalar multiples of vectors.

linear independenceconcept

Vectors none of which is a linear combination of the others, so that the only combination giving zero has every scalar zero.

log-diagonal Cholesky parameterizationinstrument Geometric Methods

Write a symmetric positive definite matrix as L times its transpose, with L lower triangular, and store the diagonal of L as logarithms.

log-Euclidean distanceconcept Geometric Methods

The distance between two symmetric positive definite matrices is the Frobenius norm of the difference of their matrix logarithms, $d_{LE}(S_1, S_2) = \|\log S_1 - \log S_2\|_F$.

logistic regressioninstrument

A linear classifier whose score is the sigmoid of a weighted sum, strictly between zero and one, above one half exactly on one side of the hyperplane.

low-rank approximationconcept

The best approximation of a matrix by one of rank k in total squared error keeps the first k terms of its singular value decomposition, and the error is the sum of the squared singular values dropped, the Eckart and Young theorem.

M

Mahalanobis distanceconcept

The Euclidean distance of a row from the mean after whitening, which needs a positive-definite covariance or a pseudoinverse on its support.

Mahalanobis edge weight with boundary penaltiesconcept Geometric Ethics

The weight of an action from state i to state j on the moral decision complex.

manifoldconcept

A curved surface of some dimension that looks flat when viewed closely.

Manifold Condorcet winnerconcept Geometric Politics

The candidate with the lowest mean manifold distance to the electorate.

marginconcept

How far a row's score sits from the threshold.

matched bitsinstrument

The rule that two codes are compared only at the same bit count.

matrixconcept

A table of numbers with n rows and d columns that sends a vector to the linear combination of its columns with the vector's coordinates as the scalars.

meaning as a gauge orbitconcept Geometric Communication

The meaning of a communicative act m is its equivalence class under the communication gauge group, the set of all $\tau(m)$ for $\tau$ in G.

mean, medianconcept

The mean of a sample is its average and the median its middle value once sorted.

Media heuristic corruptionconcept Geometric Politics

The media environment is treated as the heuristic field voters use to estimate political distances.

Medical Bond Invariance Principleconcept Geometric Medicine

Clinical evaluations must be invariant under patient re-description.

Menzerath's law in sperm whale codasresult Geometric Communication

Longer codas have shorter constituents.

Metacognitive planeconcept Geometric Reasoning

The unit square of points $(M_3, M_4)$, where $M_3$ is the self-monitoring score and $M_4$ is the strategy-selection or effort-scaling score.

metricconcept

A rule for the distance between two rows or two outputs.

metric feature versus heuristic errorconcept Geometric Economics

The volume's two-way classification of behavioral phenomena.

min-over-strataconcept

Model Robustness Index as a profileinstrument Geometric Reasoning

A vector with one component per perturbation type.

Model Robustness Index (MRI)instrument Geometric Methods

Multiply each parameter by an independent log-normal factor, and for each draw record $\omega$, the absolute change in the model's error from baseline.

Monotone Invariance Theoremresult

A strictly monotone transform of a score in either direction cannot change its optimal thresholded F1, because the sweep tries thresholds both ways.

Monte Carloconcept

Estimating a probability or an expectation as the fraction or average over many simulated runs, a sample proportion with standard error the square root of p(1 minus p) over N.

Moral decision complexconcept Geometric Ethics

A weighted simplicial complex built from the moral manifold.

moral-economic boundary and boundary penaltyconcept Geometric Economics

A threshold in the decision complex where the local decision regime changes discontinuously.

moral gauge invariance of judgmentconcept Geometric Cognition

A moral judgment function $J$ is gauge invariant under a transformation of the scenario text when the judgment of the transformed scenario equals the judgment of the original for every scenario, the transformation changing surface presentation and preserving all moral content.

Moral holonomyconcept Geometric Ethics

For a closed loop at a point p of the moral manifold, the holonomy is the linear map on the tangent space at p given by parallel transport of an obligation around the loop.

Moral injury as forced boundary crossingconcept Geometric Medicine

A clinician is morally injured when the institutionally mandated path requires crossing a boundary to which the clinician's own complex assigns a penalty above the clinician's tolerance threshold.

Moral manifoldconcept Geometric Ethics

The space M whose points are structured moral situations, each a complete specification of agents, relationships, options and morally relevant context.

Moral Noether theorem (invariance of harm accounting)result Geometric Ethics

If the moral Lagrangian is invariant under a re-description that shifts the path along a generator $\xi$ (the Bond Invariance Principle), then the Noether charge $H = p_\mu \xi^\mu$, the moral momentum contracted with the generator, is constant along extremal paths.

Moral parallel transportconcept Geometric Ethics

An obligation vector O is parallel-transported along a curve in the moral manifold when its covariant derivative along the curve vanishes, $\nabla_{\dot\gamma} O = 0$.

Moral phase transitionconcept Geometric Ethics

A point on a path through moral space, at a value of a continuous control parameter, where the satisfaction function is discontinuous (first order), or is continuous with a discontinuous gradient (second order), or where both are continuous and the metric is discontinuous (higher order). **Example.** At the consent boundary the volume sets satisfaction to minus infinity below the threshold (treatment is battery) and to a finite value above it.

Moral residue of contractionconcept Geometric Medicine

The clinical friction of the path a forced contraction mandates minus the clinical friction of the clinical geodesic on the full complex, for the same clinical state.

Moral stratificationconcept Geometric Ethics

A Whitney stratification of the moral manifold into strata, each a smooth manifold on which the evaluation function and the metric are smooth.

moving kernel and the excess rate of an averaged read metricresult Geometric Methods

When the directions a consumer does not read change from point to point, the averaged read metric can have rank q larger than the number k of quantities the consumer reads.

multiple comparisonsconcept

The inflation of false positives when many hypotheses are tested and the best is reported.

multipletconcept

A group of eigenvalues that are equal or nearly so, whose pattern names the shape a dataset lies on against a finite list of templates.

On 24,801 FMA-Medium tracks with MERT embeddings and log listens as target, Lasso on the PCA spectrum gives R = 0.302 raw and R = 0.177 (28.3 sigma) after genre residualization.

N

Nadeau and Bengio correctioncorrection

The inflation of the variance of a repeated cross-validation estimate by one plus the ratio of test to training size times the number of repeats, because the folds are not independent.

naive Bayesinstrument

A classifier that multiplies one-dimensional likelihoods and adds their logs, so that each feature's contribution is the same whatever the others are and it cannot read an interaction.

natconcept

The unit of information measured with the natural logarithm, between 1.4426 and 1.4427 bits.

nearest neighbourconcept

A row at minimal distance from a query.

neighbourhood graphconcept

A graph on a dataset that joins each row to its k nearest rows, or to every row within a radius.

Nine-dimension moral chartconcept Geometric Ethics

The canonical chart of the moral manifold.

nine dimensions of the economic decision manifoldconcept Geometric Economics

The nine coordinates on which the volume scores an economic state.

No Escape Theoremresult Geometric Ethics

For an agent whose pipeline satisfies four requirements (mandatory canonicalization, evaluation grounded in physical observables, complete audit, and strong external verification), relative to the declared grounding and transformation group, a re-description that preserves the grounded values leaves the evaluated output unchanged, and an output that violates the constraints is blocked or flagged by audit. **Example.** If x and x' describe the same situation, the canonicalizer gives C(x) = C(x').

No Escape Theorem for AIresult Geometric AI

The AI form of the No Escape Theorem of Geometric Ethics.

No Escape Theorem for Educational AIresult Geometric Education

An AI system working on the learner manifold is bound by its structure in four ways.

non-commutativity of cooking operationsconcept Geometric Gastronomy

Cooking operations are operators on flavor space, and in general their order matters.

normal distributionconcept

The bell-shaped distribution with mean mu and standard deviation sigma, with about 68 percent of its mass within one standard deviation, 95 within two, and 99.7 within three, and 1.96 the multiplier for exactly 95.

No Scalar Is Gauge-Invariant (Proposition 3.5)result Geometric Communication

No scalar evaluation of a communicative act can be at once invariant under the communication gauge group, sensitive to differences in content, and computable from the signal alone.

nuisanceconcept

The directions of the data a consumer cannot distinguish, the kernel of its read operator.

null hypothesisconcept

The statement that the effect under study is absent, under which a test statistic's p-value is computed.

null modelinstrument

A version of the data with the structure under test removed and everything else kept, the right comparison for any measured statistic.

null spaceconcept

The set of vectors a matrix sends to zero, also called the kernel, the directions the matrix cannot see.

nutritional feasible set and the geometric dietconcept Geometric Gastronomy

O

observerconcept
