attention concept

DefinitionThe operation inside a language model that lets each token look at earlier ones by comparing its query to their keys and averaging their values. Chapter 0 section 0.11.
ExampleScores 2, 1, and 0 against three keys give softmax weights 0.665, 0.245, and 0.090.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id attention, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.23.

Assumptions and scope
  • A head weights each earlier token’s value by the softmax of its query-key score and sums. For scalar values the output lies between the smallest and largest value, and the head reads the keys only through their scores against the query, so a key change the query does not read leaves the output unchanged however large it is.
  • That is the head’s read subspace, a few query-weighted directions of each key, and the reason a key reconstruction at cosine 0.995 raised the perplexity by three orders of magnitude.

attention metric concept

DefinitionA positive-definite symmetric bilinear form $g$ on each tangent space of the cognitive manifold whose components are set by attention allocation. A dimension with a larger attention weight has higher resolution, so states that differ along it are farther apart and easier to tell apart.
ExampleWith attention weight 4 on color and 1 on shape and no cross terms, a unit step along color has squared length 4 and a unit step along shape has squared length 1. On the A4 divided attention test the volume prints 0.571 for Claude and 1.000 for Gemini 3 Flash, a gap of 0.429.

Defining equationnone

attractiveness skew instrument

DefinitionModel the retrieval count of a point as Poisson with mean $\rho w$, where w is its attractiveness, with mean one. Solve the variance and third central moment of the counts for those of w, and report $\mu_3(w)/\mathrm{Var}(w)^{3/2}$, a hubness measure that does not contain the query budget.
ExampleCounts with mean 2 and variance 6 give an attractiveness variance of (6 - 2)/4 = 1. Counts with mean 2 and variance 2 give 0, and the estimator returns no value.
VolumeGeometric Methods, Volume 1 of the Geometric Series; entry id attractiveness-skew, kind instrument.
StatusThe moment identities are proved and checked symbolically. The measurements are demonstrated or exploratory as each source file states, and one claim built on them was withdrawn, not refuted. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The estimator returns no value when the variance of the counts is at or below the budget, which is when the budget is too small to resolve any structure.
  • On a fixed corpus with a known skew of 9.85 the estimate stayed between 9.84 and 10.02 across budgets of 0.5 to 4, while the raw skewness ranged from 2.46 to 5.59.
  • Two simpler statistics formed by dividing by a null were believed free of the budget. Measured under two protocols, their slopes changed sign.
  • An invariant estimator does not protect against a biased sample. The claim that hubness in the real corpus rises with corpus size was withdrawn when queries and corpus were found to come from different files of an ordered dataset.
Prior artnone recorded

attribute conservation in closed exchange result

DefinitionIn a closed bilateral exchange between agents A and B the changes on each transferable dimension sum to zero, so that the change for A plus the change for B is zero on money $d_1$, rights $d_2$ and autonomy $d_4$. The evaluative dimensions are not conserved and may rise for both parties.
ExampleThe volume’s worked example. Maria pays 2,000 dollars and Elena receives 2,000, which sums to zero on \(d_1\). The evaluative gains sum to 0.7 + 0.5 + 0.9 + 0.3 = 2.4.
VolumeGeometric Economics, Volume 4 of the Geometric Series; entry id attribute-conservation-law, kind result.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status block of 2026-07-14 calls the volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, and says that no economics instrument has been evaluated by the series' admission filter and that none passes its gate. Its claims are to be read as theory at licensed strength and not as validated measurement, and the chapters tag each claim as established mathematics, empirical, modeling axiom, conditional theorem or speculation. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The exchange is closed. No third party enters and no external rule changes during it.
  • In an open system the sum equals the net external input on that dimension. The volume reads an observed violation as a sign that the system boundary was drawn too narrowly.
  • The theorem is tagged conditional. Money is conserved by accounting identity, rights by the Hohfeldian correlative structure taken from Geometric Ethics, and autonomy in the sense that voluntary constraints are symmetric.
  • Section 9.9 rederives the law from the invariance principle by a Noether argument, also tagged conditional. Chapter 16 lists the empirical pattern as an untested prediction.
Prior artThe accounting identity that every payment is a receipt, and Noether's theorem for the derivation the volume gives.

attribute type concept

DefinitionThe declaration of which transformations of a column keep its meaning, any injective relabelling for nominal, a strictly increasing map for ordinal, an affine map for interval, and a positive rescaling for ratio, nested in that order. Chapter 2 section 2.1. Also nominal, ordinal, interval scale, ratio scale.
ExampleTemperature in Celsius is an interval scale, so a ratio of two temperatures means nothing, while 4 metres is twice 2 metres on the ratio scale of length.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id attribute-type, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The declaration of which transformations of a column do not change its meaning. A ratio scale permits a positive rescaling, an interval scale an affine map with positive slope, an ordinal scale a strictly increasing map, and a nominal scale any injective relabelling, and the four classes are nested in that order.
  • A rescaling preserves ratios and an affine map preserves ratios of differences, so a consumer that reads a ratio of two interval-scale columns reads the origin the scale said was arbitrary.

attribution instrument

DefinitionAn assignment to each feature of a share of one prediction. The raw gradient is the sensitivity at a row, gradient times input is the share of the change in output, and the averaged squared gradient is a diagonal entry of the read operator, and the three are kept apart. Shapley, permutation, and partial-dependence methods measure other things and are named for them. Chapter 14. Also partial dependence, Shapley.
ExampleFor the affine consumer 3x1 + 2x2, moving from (0, 0) to (1, 1) gives attributions 3 and 2, which sum to the change in output, 5.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id attribution, kind instrument.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • An assignment to each feature of a share of one prediction. Three gradient quantities are kept apart. The raw gradient is the sensitivity at a row. Gradient times input, the sensitivity times the move along a coordinate, sums exactly to the change in output for an affine consumer and is zero on an unread coordinate. The weighted mean of the squared sensitivity is a diagonal entry of the read operator, so an averaged squared gradient estimates the read operator and a single-row attribution does not.
  • Shapley, permutation, and partial-dependence methods measure other things and are named for them, and for a tree the sensitivity is zero almost everywhere, so importances that count splits are the right reading and finite differences the wrong one.
Prior artnone recorded

AUROC concept

DefinitionThe area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, equal to the probability that a random positive scores above a random negative, ties counted as one half. A strictly increasing transform of the score leaves it unchanged and a strictly decreasing one sends it to one minus itself. Equation 0.16.
ExamplePositives scoring 0.9 and 0.7 against negatives scoring 0.8 and 0.2 win three of the four pairs, so the AUROC is 0.75.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id auroc, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.16.

Assumptions and scope
  • The area under the ROC curve, the probability that a random positive scores above a random negative with ties counted as one half. It lies in the unit interval, is one half for a constant score, one for a perfect ranking, and zero for a perfectly reversed one.
  • A strictly increasing transform of the score leaves it unchanged. A strictly decreasing transform reverses every ranking and sends A to 1 minus A, so the AUROC is not free of orientation, and an authority that should ignore orientation reads the larger of A and 1 minus A.
Prior artnone recorded

bagging instrument

DefinitionFitting the same model on bootstrap resamples and averaging. The average's squared error is at most the members' mean squared error, which is how it reduces variance. Chapter 7. Also bootstrap aggregat.
ExampleTen trees fit on ten bootstrap resamples and averaged have at most the mean squared error of the ten members.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id bagging, kind instrument.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Fitting the same model on bootstrap resamples of the rows and averaging. The average’s squared error is at most the mean of the members’ squared errors, which is the arithmetic by which bagging reduces variance, and the reduction is largest when the members covary least.
  • Bagging reduces variance and boosting reduces bias, and neither changes what the base model reads.

bag of words concept

DefinitionA representation of a document as a vector with one coordinate per vocabulary term holding that term's count. Chapter 12. Also bag-of-words, BoW.
ExampleThe texts ‘the reader reads the row’ and ‘the row reads the reader’ have the same counts and are one document to a bag of words.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id bag-of-words, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.36.

Assumptions and scope
  • A document as the vector of its term counts. Two documents that are rearrangements of each other have the same bag, so the bag is a quotient that declares word order irrelevant, the counts are nonnegative, and they sum to the document’s length.
  • As a null model it reads only counts, and an encoder is validated only when its held-out AUROC clears the bag’s by the preregistered margin. The scorecard’s bag scores lie between 0.46 and 0.54, near chance.

balance coordinate that degenerates at a boundary concept

DefinitionA balance coordinate d = (g - l)/(g + l) of two competing non-negative magnitudes equals plus or minus 1 exactly when one magnitude is absent. On those sets it is constant, an interaction term d times x equals plus or minus x, and its coefficient cannot be separated from the coefficient of x.
ExampleWith g = 3 and l = 1 the coordinate is 2/4 = 0.5. With l = 0 it is 1 whether g is 3 or 7, so on that set it tells nothing about g.
VolumeGeometric Methods, Volume 1 of the Geometric Series; entry id degenerate-balance-coordinate, kind concept.
StatusThe rule follows from the definition of the coordinate. The numbers quoted with it are the record of an archived draft (Section 21.8). Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The chart-selection rule applies where the endpoints of a bounded coordinate mean absence and not extremity. Fit each side separately, and do not read an interaction coefficient estimated across an endpoint as a property of either side.
  • The evidence is a study of 95,748 risky-choice trials in an archived draft of the geometric-economics repository. A pooled interaction of +0.25 fell to about -0.03, within its noise, once the regions were separated.
  • The draft was archived on 2026-11-02 because the model it tested has a diagonal metric and hand-chosen coordinates. The volume states that the rule is about coordinates and does not depend on that model.
  • The discontinuities the draft reports are jumps in a risk-sensitivity term at two different boundaries. They are not edge weights of the nine-dimensional decision complex.
Prior artnone recorded

balanced accuracy concept

DefinitionThe mean of the per-class recalls, so that a large class cannot hide a small one. Equation 0.34.
ExampleRecalls of 0.90 on class A and 0.30 on class B give balanced accuracy 0.60, whatever the class sizes.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id balanced-accuracy, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.34.

Assumptions and scope
  • The mean of the per-class recalls, between the worst class and the best. Plain accuracy is the size-weighted mean of the same recalls, so a class of 990 rows recalled perfectly and a class of 10 never recalled give accuracy 0.99 and balanced accuracy 0.5.
  • The book prefers the min over classes to the mean where a verdict is at stake, since a mean can still hide one failing class among many.

bar instrument

DefinitionA threshold a statistic must reach, written down before the measurement. A bar discriminates only when the null fails it and the real system passes it, and a bar the null passes is vacuous. Chapter 8 section 8.3.
ExampleA null scoring 0.30 and a system scoring 0.72 are separated by a bar at 0.55, and a bar at 0.25 is vacuous, since the null passes it.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id bar, kind instrument.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 10.7.

Assumptions and scope
  • A threshold a statistic must reach, written down before the measurement. Passing a higher bar passes every lower one, a larger statistic passes every bar a smaller one passes, a bar discriminates exactly when it sits strictly above the null and at or below the real system, no bar discriminates when the null scores at least as high, and a bar the null passes is vacuous.
  • A pass on eight cells at six parts in ten million against a bar of one in a hundred thousand was vacuous because the null cleared the bar too, which is where the anti-vacuity bar came from.
Prior artnone recorded

Passing a higher bar passes every lower one, a larger statistic passes every bar a smaller one passes, a bar discriminates exactly when it sits strictly above the null and at or below the real system, no bar discriminates when the null scores at least as high, and a bar the null passes is vacuous.

Basin of attraction of a reasoning minimum concept

DefinitionThe set of states from which gradient flow on the evaluation function converges to a given local minimum. Its depth is the lowest value of the function on the basin's boundary minus the value at the minimum. A dead zone is different. It is a flat region with a near-zero gradient and no minimum.
ExampleFor the function (x^2 - 1)^2 on the line, the minima are at -1 and 1, the basin of 1 is every x above 0, and its depth is the value 1 at x = 0 minus the value 0 at x = 1.
VolumeGeometric Reasoning, Volume 3 of the Geometric Series; entry id reasoning-basin-of-attraction, kind concept.
StatusPosited framework. The README's epistemic-status block of 2026-07-14 calls the volume speculative theory awaiting instruments, to be read as theory at licensed strength and not as validated measurement. Its chapters tag each claim as established mathematics, empirical, modeling axiom, conditional theorem or speculation, and the empirical tags rest on one benchmark of five language models. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • It assumes a smooth evaluation function with isolated local minima on a Riemannian reasoning manifold. The basins then partition the manifold up to a set of measure zero.
  • The definition is standard dynamics. That a model’s premature convergence is a trajectory settling in such a basin is the volume’s posited reading.
  • No basin depth, radius or exit angle is measured in the volume.
Prior artBasins of attraction of gradient flow in dynamical systems and optimization.

basis concept

DefinitionA set of independent vectors whose span is the whole space, so that every vector is exactly one combination of them. The standard basis vectors have a one in one coordinate and zeros elsewhere. Primer L section L.1.

Bayes' rule concept

DefinitionThe probability of a cause given an observation, equal to the probability of the observation given the cause times the base rate, divided by the overall probability of the observation. Precision is Bayes' rule with a classifier as the test. Primer S, equation S.3. Also Bayes.
ExampleBase rate one percent, detection ninety percent, false report five percent, so a positive report means the condition with probability 0.009 over 0.0585, about 0.154.

Bernoulli, binomial concept

DefinitionA Bernoulli variable is one with probability p and zero otherwise, with mean p and variance p(1 minus p). A binomial variable counts the ones among n independent Bernoulli trials, with mean np. Primer S, equation S.6. Also Bernoulli, binomial.
ExampleTen fair coin flips show exactly seven heads with probability 120 over 1024, about 0.117.

BGE and Nash relationship (augmented game) result

DefinitionA profile is a BGE exactly when it is a Nash equilibrium of the augmented game, whose strategies are the simple paths to the goal and whose payoffs are the negative of behavioral friction. With zero penalties and covariance on $d_1$ alone it is the Nash equilibrium of the monetary game. Positive penalties exclude scalar equilibria that cross a boundary.
ExampleTwo paths with behavioral friction 4 and 6 have augmented payoffs -4 and -6. The path of least friction is the strategy of greatest payoff, so the two best-response conditions coincide.
VolumeGeometric Economics, Volume 4 of the Geometric Series; entry id bge-nash-relationship, kind result.
StatusTagged a conditional theorem in the front matter. Existence of a mixed BGE follows from Nash's theorem of 1950 through the equivalence. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Equivalence holds by construction of the augmented game, with finite sets of simple paths as strategies.
  • Scalar nesting is stated for a single-action game with all penalties zero and the covariance confined to the monetary dimension, and it uses the goal region to restrict the feasible actions.
  • Refinement removes a boundary-crossing equilibrium only when the penalty exceeds the scalar cost disadvantage of the path that avoids the boundary.
Prior artNash equilibrium and Nash's existence theorem.

bi-Lipschitz concept

DefinitionOf a map between two spaces, neither stretching nor shrinking any distance by more than a fixed factor. Equation 0.21. Also Lipschitz.
ExampleA map with factor 2 sends a distance of 1 to something between 0.5 and 2.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id bi-lipschitz, kind concept.
Statusrefutes or corrects [refuted]. Corrections: 1 item(s), see below.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.21.

Assumptions and scope
  • A map is bi-Lipschitz with factor K when it neither stretches nor shrinks any distance by more than K. The factor is at least one, compositions multiply the factors, and the map preserves a nearest neighbour whenever the runner-up is more than K squared times as far, the rank certificate’s per-pair fact.
  • It does not preserve every ordering, so it is not rank-faithful, and the program’s fixed-scale uniform bi-Lipschitz claim for the commute filter is refuted and carried in the ledger.

binding affinity matrix concept

DefinitionThe matrix $A$ with one row per receptor type (about 400) and one column per chemical species (about 10,000), whose entry $A_{ij}$ is the affinity of receptor i for molecule j. Transduction is modeled as $\mathbf{r} = A\mathbf{c}$. Chemical variation in the null space of $A$ is odorless and tasteless, and distinct stimuli with the same image are metamers.
ExampleTake one receptor with affinities (2, 1) for two species. The stimuli (1, 0) and (0, 2) both give response 2, so they are metamers, and their difference (1, -2) lies in the null space. At the volume’s sizes, about 400 rows against about 10,000 columns leave a null space of dimension at least 9,600. The small numbers are illustrative.
VolumeGeometric Gastronomy, Volume 12 of the Geometric Series; entry id binding-affinity-matrix, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, with no gastronomy instrument evaluated by the series' admission filter (xbse) and the nearest evaluated perceptual domains, aesthetics and music, rated inadmissible to medium. Its claims are to be read as theory at licensed strength and not as validated measurement, and the chapters tag each statement as a modeling axiom, empirical, a conjecture or a theorem. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Tagged a modeling axiom, valid within the sub-saturating regime of each receptor. Real dose-response curves are sigmoidal, and the linear form fails at saturation.
  • Competitive binding and state-dependent receptors, such as miraculin switching the sweet receptor to acid activation, change the entries with context. The volume calls the linear map the tangent-plane approximation.
  • The matrix is wide and rank-deficient, so the map from chemistry to receptor response is far from injective. It is also sparse and structured, which the volume uses to argue for the second compression to 10 to 30 perceptual dimensions.
Prior artnone recorded

bit concept

DefinitionThe unit of a budget. A direction quantized with b bits is stored at one of two to the power b levels. Chapter 0 section 0.7.
ExampleFour bits give 16 levels; a fifth bit gives 32, halving the step and quartering the squared error.

Defining equation

Book equation 0.13.

Assumptions and scope
  • The unit of a budget. A direction quantized with b bits is stored at one of two to the b levels, so one more bit doubles the levels, halves a uniform quantizer’s step, and quarters the squared error of the high-rate model, and bits add across directions since the levels multiply.
  • Every flip comparison is at matched bits, since a code that spends more bits is a different budget and not a better reader.

blind probe instrument

DefinitionAn instrument that recovers a consumer's read operator from calls to the consumer alone, without access to its gradients or its code. Chapters 11 and 12.
ExampleProbing a 16-dimensional consumer with 16 directions costs 32 calls and resolves the operator, and 15 directions do not.

Defining equation

Book equation 0.8.

Assumptions and scope
  • The probe recovers the read operator at one operating point from calls to the consumer alone, two calls per input dimension for a central difference.
  • Its budget law is a theorem for subspace-confined designs at an operating point, which is what its per-point estimators are, and does not cover allocations of calls across many operating points.
  • The probe refuses when samples do not exceed the dimension and warns below a stated margin, since the identifiability miss of chapter 2 came from reading it past that point.

Bond geodesic concept

DefinitionThe minimum-cost path on the economic decision complex from an initial state to a goal region, where the cost of a path is the sum of its edge weights and each edge weight is the Mahalanobis term plus the penalties of the boundaries crossed.
ExampleTwo paths to the goal with edge weights 1 + 4 = 5 and 2 + 2 = 4. The second is the Bond geodesic. A third path that crosses a boundary with infinite penalty costs infinity and is excluded.
VolumeGeometric Economics, Volume 4 of the Geometric Series; entry id bond-geodesic, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status block of 2026-07-14 calls the volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, and says that no economics instrument has been evaluated by the series' admission filter and that none passes its gate. Its claims are to be read as theory at licensed strength and not as validated measurement, and the chapters tag each claim as established mathematics, empirical, modeling axiom, conditional theorem or speculation. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • It is the discrete analogue of a Riemannian geodesic. In the smooth limit the volume identifies it with a geodesic of the metric given by the inverse covariance.
  • It needs the covariance matrix and the boundary penalties as inputs. The volume says the framework does not supply those measurements.
  • Edge weights are squared Mahalanobis terms, so the volume notes that two half steps cost half as much as one full step and the path favors gradual transitions.
  • A path that crosses a boundary with infinite penalty has infinite cost and is never the geodesic when a finite-cost path exists.
Prior artA shortest path in a weighted graph, which the volume computes by A* search.

Bond geodesic equilibrium (BGE) concept

DefinitionA profile of paths, one per agent, in which each agent's path is a Bond geodesic on that agent's decision complex given the paths of the others. No agent can lower its behavioral friction, its total path cost on the full complex, by changing path alone.
ExampleThe volume’s ultimatum game with 10 dollars. A responder whose fairness penalty exceeds \(1^2/\sigma_1^2\) rejects an offer of 1 dollar, and a proposer who anticipates this offers 40 to 50 percent.
VolumeGeometric Economics, Volume 4 of the Geometric Series; entry id bond-geodesic-equilibrium, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status block of 2026-07-14 calls the volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, and says that no economics instrument has been evaluated by the series' admission filter and that none passes its gate. Its claims are to be read as theory at licensed strength and not as validated measurement, and the chapters tag each claim as established mathematics, empirical, modeling axiom, conditional theorem or speculation. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The front matter tags the choice of the BGE as the equilibrium concept a modeling axiom.
  • A pure BGE need not exist. Theorem 23 gives a mixed BGE for a finite game in which every agent always has a path of finite cost to its goal.
  • A BGE is not Pareto optimal in general, and several can coexist. Lemma 26 gives uniqueness when each agent’s self-separation exceeds its cross-sensitivity.
  • Agents are assumed to pathfind on the manifold they perceive. The volume says a miscalibrated heuristic or covariance gives a BGE of the perceived game that can differ from that of the true game.
Prior artNash equilibrium, applied to the augmented game whose payoffs are the negative of behavioral friction.

Bond Index instrument

DefinitionA dimensionless audit measure of how much an evaluation moves when only the description changes, $Bd = D_{op} / \tau$. $D_{op}$ is the mean, over the inputs tested and the re-descriptions declared, of the distance between the evaluation before and after the re-description, and the divisor is a tolerance. Zero is perfect invariance.
ExampleIn the game form the distance is 0 when a pairing is the correlative and 1 when it is not. One wrong pairing in 8 gives 1/8 = 0.125, close to the volume’s mean of about 0.13. Random choice among four positions is wrong 3 times in 4, which gives 0.75.
VolumeGeometric Ethics, Volume 2 of the Geometric Series; entry id bond-index, kind instrument.
StatusAn instrument with one definition as of v1.26 and v1.27, which also corrected two statements about it (random play in the Dear Ethicist game scores about 0.75, not 0.5, and Appendix B now uses the five tiers of Chapter 18). The convergence claim about it, Proposition 19.4, is a Conditional Theorem whose ledger row GE-PROP-19-4 is exploratory. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The distance is 0 or 1 for a verdict or a Hohfeldian position, the absolute change over the scale for a score, and the distance under the moral metric for a vector or a tensor. The vector form therefore inherits the untested metric.
  • It is reported with the worst single case and the share of tests in which the evaluation moved, because a mean hides both.
  • A result covers the declared suite of re-descriptions and nothing outside it (corrected in v1.27). A value of zero is not a guarantee against re-descriptions that were not tested.
  • The clinical Bond Index of Chapter 21 shares the name and is a different quantity, the expected excess cost of a policy’s mandated path over the manifold-optimal path. A value of one says nothing about the other.

Bond Index disparity ratio instrument

DefinitionFor one policy and two populations, the clinical Bond Index of the first population divided by that of the second. A ratio of 1.0 means equal cost beyond the optimum, and a ratio of 2.3 means the first population bears 2.3 times the cost of the second.
ExampleIf the index is 4.6 for one population and 2.0 for another under the same policy, the ratio is 4.6 / 2.0 = 2.3, the volume’s example reading. On the volume’s illustrative thresholds a ratio of 2.0 or more is a critical disparity. The two index values are chosen to give the volume’s 2.3.

Bond Index for AI instrument

DefinitionThe expected excess geodesic deviation of a system's trajectory on the value manifold over the value-aligned geodesic, reported as nine components, one per value dimension. The total is the square root of the sum of the squared components. Stratified by user population or averaged over time it gives a fairness audit and a drift monitor.
ExampleComponents of 0.03 on welfare and 0.04 on dignity, with the other seven at 0, give a total of the square root of 0.0009 + 0.0016, which is 0.05. Deviations of 0.1, 0.2 and 0.3 over three interactions give a running value of 0.6 / 3, which is 0.2.
VolumeGeometric AI, Volume 11 of the Geometric Series; entry id ai-bond-index, kind instrument.
StatusA posited instrument defined as a geodesic deviation, which the volume says is the same construction as in the other books of the series. It is a different formula from the re-description audit recorded under the Ethics entry for the Bond Index, and no measured value of it is reported. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The value-aligned geodesic is not observable. The volume approximates it by expert evaluation, by consensus of evaluators, by treating a gauge-invariant output as aligned, or by a trained evaluation model.
  • The total is a scalar, and the volume says the Scalar Irrecoverability Theorem applies to it. The component vector is kept for diagnosis.
  • The thresholds of the green, yellow and red alert zones are parameters set by governance for each deployment. The volume gives no values.
  • Every Bond Index number in the volume belongs to the fictional ARIA and ARIA-G. The README says no alignment instrument has been evaluated.

Bond Invariance Principle concept

DefinitionIf two descriptions d and d' of one situation are related by an admissible coordinate transformation, a legitimate moral evaluation assigns both the same value, $E(d) = E(d')$. In group terms the evaluation is constant on the orbits of the admissible re-description group.
ExampleIf withholding treatment and allowing natural death pick out the same action in all morally relevant respects, an evaluation that scores one 0.6 must score the other 0.6. A score of 0.6 against 0.4 violates the principle.
VolumeGeometric Ethics, Volume 2 of the Geometric Series; entry id moral-bond-invariance-principle, kind concept.
StatusAppendix F lists Axiom 5.1 as a Modeling Axiom, and the ledger row GE-AXIOM-5-1 has class exploratory. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The volume tags it as a definition and modeling choice. It is an axiom of the framework, not a measured fact about evaluators.
  • It demands invariance under re-description, not under re-situation. Descriptions that pick out different features or contexts may be evaluated differently.
  • Both descriptions must pass the five admissibility conditions of Section 5.5, which are same physical grounding, same agent structure, same stratum, reversibility and no evaluative loading.
  • The volume posits the admissible group as V4 times U(1)_H. The discrete factor V4 is proved, and that this is the whole group is a modeling hypothesis.
Prior artnone recorded

Bond Invariance Principle for reasoning concept

DefinitionA judgment function $f$ satisfies the principle when $f(\tau(x)) = f(x)$ for every description $x$ and every gauge transformation $\tau$. Equivalently the judgment depends only on the content of the description. A failure is a gauge anomaly, and its magnitude along $\tau$ is the distance between $f(\tau(x))$ and $f(x)$.
ExampleA system that rates a scenario at 40 on a 70-point harm scale and its euphemistic rewrite at 31 has an anomaly of magnitude 9 along that rewrite, where the principle requires 0.
VolumeGeometric Reasoning, Volume 3 of the Geometric Series; entry id reasoning-bond-invariance-principle, kind concept.
StatusThe principle is a posited norm. The violations and the two null results measured against it are benchmark findings on five models, tagged empirical. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Tagged a modeling axiom. The volume uses it as a diagnostic criterion relative to a chosen class of gauge transformations.
  • It applies only to content-preserving transformations. A change to the facts should change the output.
  • A test of it is only as good as the claim that the rewrite preserved content. In the benchmark the rewrites were produced by a fixed model.
  • Measured against it, the benchmark reports violations under framing, emotional anchoring and sensory distractors, and no significant violation under gender swap or evaluation order.
Prior artnone recorded

boosting instrument

DefinitionFitting a sequence of weak scorers, each on the rows the previous ones got wrong, and summing them. Its step size is positive exactly when the weak scorer beats chance, and the reweighting makes the last scorer's weighted error one half. Chapter 7. Also boost.
ExampleA weak scorer with weighted error 0.25 gets step size one half of the log of 3, about 0.549, and after reweighting its error is one half.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id boosting, kind instrument.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Fitting a sequence of weak scorers, each on the rows the previous ones got wrong, and summing them with a step size set by the weighted error. The step size is positive exactly when the weak scorer beats chance, and after the rows are reweighted the weighted error of the scorer just fitted is one half, so the next scorer must find something new.
  • Gradient boosting reads the loss through its curvature, so the optimizer is a consumer whose read operator is the Hessian, and on the author’s five-dataset benchmark the ensemble wins when the boundary needs many features and a formula wins when it needs few.
Prior artnone recorded

bootstrap instrument

DefinitionAn estimate of a confidence interval made by resampling the data with replacement many times and recomputing the statistic each time. A paired bootstrap resamples the same rows for two methods at once so that shared sampling variation cancels. Chapter 0 section 0.9.
ExampleResample 100 rows with replacement 1000 times, and the spread of the 1000 means is the bootstrap standard error.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id bootstrap, kind instrument.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • An interval estimated by resampling the data with replacement and recomputing the statistic each time. A paired bootstrap resamples the same rows for two methods at once, and the variance of the difference is the sum of the two variances minus twice their covariance, so pairing narrows the interval exactly when the two scores covary positively across rows.
  • Resampling rows does not undo dependence between folds, which is the correction’s job, and the bootstrap’s interval is only as wide as the sample it resamples.
Prior artnone recorded

budget concept

DefinitionThe third element of an observer. The bits, rows, calls, seconds, or dollars a consumer may spend. Chapter 1.
ExampleA probe with 2d calls at d equal to 16 spends 32 evaluations for one operating point.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id budget, kind concept.
Statusmeasures [replicated]. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 11.4.

Assumptions and scope
  • The budget is the bits, rows, calls, seconds, or dollars a consumer may spend. It bounds what of the read operator can be measured and used, and changes the operator only when it changes the consumer.
  • Comparisons are made at matched budget. A verdict at a fixed budget can invert under budget matching, and the ledger carries the case.
  • For a probe the budget is consumer calls, and recovery of the read operator is a cliff at the full dimension of the space.

Equation

Book equation 11.4.

\[\text{directions resolved}(k)=\begin{cases}1\ \text{or}\ 2,& k<d\\[2pt] \operatorname{rank}P_C,& k\ge d\end{cases}\qquad \text{cost}=2d\ \text{consumer calls per operating point}.\]

Conditions

  • The budget is the bits, rows, calls, seconds, or dollars a consumer may spend. It bounds what of the read operator can be measured and used, and changes the operator only when it changes the consumer.
  • Comparisons are made at matched budget. A verdict at a fixed budget can invert under budget matching, and the ledger carries the case.
  • For a probe the budget is consumer calls, and recovery of the read operator is a cliff at the full dimension of the space.

Conditions are curated in entries.toml rather than read from a record.

Failed, with witness.

  • OD:singular-transition, approach to a singularity of the observed dynamics, the periodic Burgers equation carried to shock formation, against a regular two-dimensional flow as the control. Claim: Fourth version: D5v3’s claim with the control bar taken per control, each two-dimensional control’s read fractions collapsing no more tightly on B over its own front wavenumber than on B alone. experiments/DISCOVERY-TRACK.md, D5v4 record; experiments/OD/D5v4/grade.json. Boundary: both controls under the fail line: scaled over unscaled median bin IQR 0.56 (gradient up a third, front wavenumber 3.2 to 4.1) and 0.22 (gradient up two percent, 1.8 to 2.2), against a bar of 0.75 and a fail clause of 0.5; the Burgers worlds at 0.44 and 0.46 on the same draw; convergence 0.012 to 0.095 against 0.11 and the collapse bars held. Witness: the unscaled null takes one value per budget, so each of its bins holds a budget’s whole time series; dividing by any scale that drifts in time spreads that series across bins and lowers the within-bin scatter by construction; the collapse measure is not specific to the forming front, and the readings of D5v2 and D5v3 that it is are withdrawn. Absorbed by: declaration. Revision: a null that is not degenerate, a wrong scale with the same time dependence; a change of the null and so of the claim; not registered.

budget cliff result

DefinitionThe finding that recovery of a read operator by a probe is a cliff at the full dimension of the space rather than a slope, and that the cliff does not move with the operator's rank. Chapter 11. Also cliff.
ExampleAt half the dimension the probe recovered 0.366 and at the full dimension 1.000, with nothing in between reaching 0.90.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id budget-cliff, kind result.
Statusmeasures [demonstrated]. Corrections: 1 item(s), see below.
Defining equation

Book equation 11.4.

Assumptions and scope
  • The reader receives responses confined to the k directions it chose, the read operator is planted in a fixed subspace, and noise enters as the noisy theorem models it. Under those conditions the cliff at k equal to the dimension is a theorem and is rank-independent.
  • Known side information about a k0-dimensional exclusion moves the cliff to d minus k0 and never softens it.
  • Whether many cheap points spread across operating points can average their way back to the population operator was measured within a budget range and is not a theorem.

Equation

Book equation 11.4.

\[\text{directions resolved}(k)=\begin{cases}1\ \text{or}\ 2,& k<d\\[2pt] \operatorname{rank}P_C,& k\ge d\end{cases}\qquad \text{cost}=2d\ \text{consumer calls per operating point}.\]

Conditions

  • The reader receives responses confined to the k directions it chose, the read operator is planted in a fixed subspace, and noise enters as the noisy theorem models it. Under those conditions the cliff at k equal to the dimension is a theorem and is rank-independent.
  • Known side information about a k0-dimensional exclusion moves the cliff to d minus k0 and never softens it.
  • Whether many cheap points spread across operating points can average their way back to the population operator was measured within a budget range and is not a theorem.

Conditions are curated in entries.toml rather than read from a record.

  • readscope/README.md:102-116 at 856e678. What none of this changes: the budget law, in its proven scope. The theorem behind it (PRINCIPLES.md, P3; OT-3) covers subspace-confined directional designs at an operating point, which is what this probe’s per-point estimators are; it does not cover every allocation of calls across many operating points, and the sketch expectation (1+1/k)·S + tr(S)/k·I shares S’s eigenspaces at every k — so whether many cheap points can average their way back to the population operator was a sample-complexity question, not a proven impossibility — and C-15 has now measured it: at equal total consumer calls, sub-dimensional budgets do not catch up, at any graded rank, within 8× the full-dimension spend (SPEC.md, C-15). The cliff is a property of total calls in the measured range; only the far asymptotic regime remains open.

cache concept

DefinitionA store of recently used data kept so that it need not be fetched again. A cold measurement is taken before the cache holds anything useful, a warm one after. Chapter 13. Also cold, warm.
ExampleA cache holding 4 of a reader’s 10 entries hits 40 percent of that reader’s reads.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id cache, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • A store of recently used data kept so that it need not be fetched again. A cache reader reads the entries in its footprint and nothing else, so its hit rate over a stream of requests lies in the unit interval, is zero cold and one warm, never falls when the cache holds more, and is unchanged by entries outside the requests.
  • A cold and a warm measurement of the same system are two observers of it. The ZooKeeper substrate’s false-clear rate was 0.99 hot and 0.01 cold, which is the case that a cache’s number is the requests’ number.

calibration concept

DefinitionThe property of a score that a value of 0.8 means the row is positive eighty percent of the time. Measured by expected calibration error, equation 0.29. Also expected calibration error.
ExampleIf the rows scored near 0.8 are positive 80 percent of the time, the score is calibrated at 0.8.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id calibration, kind concept.
Statusrefutes or corrects [refuted]. Corrections: 1 item(s), see below.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.29.

Assumptions and scope
  • A score is calibrated when a value of 0.8 means the row is positive eighty percent of the time. The expected calibration error, the bin-weighted mean absolute gap between mean score and fraction of positives, lies in the unit interval and is zero exactly when every weighted bin is calibrated.
  • Calibration is a property of the score values and not of their ranking, so a recalibration can change it while leaving AUROC, the reliability weight, and every threshold-swept metric unchanged. The two are reported side by side and neither stands in for the other.
  • Recalibrating a reconstruction toward the input improved the reconstruction and worsened the consumer, the standing negative that keeps calibration off the list of acceptance metrics for a code.
Prior artnone recorded

Campaign Gradient Theorem result

DefinitionA campaign is modeled as choosing a unit projection axis, the dimension voters attend to. The theorem says a successful campaign finds the axis along which the mean squared projected distance between the electorate and the candidate is smallest.
ExampleLet the electorate have mean zero, variance 4 on axis 1 and variance 1 on axis 2, and let the candidate sit at \((0, 2)\). The mean squared projected distance is \(4 + 0 = 4\) on axis 1 and \(1 + 4 = 5\) on axis 2, so the campaign makes axis 1 salient.
VolumeGeometric Politics, Volume 10 of the Geometric Series; entry id campaign-gradient-theorem, kind result.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, and says a political-argument instrument is plausible but has not been built or gated. District 7, the source of nearly every number in the volume, is a fictional district, and Chapter 18 says precise estimation of the manifold needs larger and richer datasets than currently exist. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The axis must be politically activatable. A campaign can make salient only the dimensions voters recognize as relevant.
  • The model assumes campaigns change the salience of dimensions and leave voters’ positions nearly fixed.
  • This entry follows the first displayed form and the prose. The volume gives a second displayed form that it calls equivalent, and its proof is a short reduction to a generalized eigenvalue problem.
  • The chapter says the theorem is not a new prediction. It offers it as a geometric account of the known regularity that campaigns stress strengths and avoid weaknesses.
Prior artIssue ownership and priming in the campaign-effects literature.

certificate concept

DefinitionA claim, made at a time, that something is safe to act on. A clustering, a benchmark score, a freshness guarantee, and a rank bound are all certificates. Chapters 9 and 13.
ExampleA certificate cleared 1000 decisions and the witness disagreed on 206 of them, a false-clear rate of 0.206.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id certificate, kind concept.
Statusmeasures [demonstrated]. Corrections: 1 item(s), see below.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.26.

Assumptions and scope
  • A certificate is graded only where a witness exists, and where none exists it is unassessed rather than safe.
  • A certificate is bound to what it certified, the bytes, the anchor sample, the footprint, and the time, and carries none of it to another corpus, workload, or moment.
  • A vacuous certificate proves nothing about the object. It does not prove that no code preserves rank or that no structure exists, only that this test could not certify one.
  • The rank certificate’s floor is a guarantee in its strict setting and an estimate in its percentile setting.

chance level concept

DefinitionThe value a rank statistic reaches on average under a random ranking. Zero for a correlation, one half for AUROC. Chapter 0 section 0.8. Also chance overlap, times chance.

Assumptions and scope
  • The value a rank statistic reaches under a ranking that carries no information. A constant score ties every pair, so its AUROC is one half when both classes are present, its Kendall correlation with any score is zero, and its reliability weight is zero.

chunk concept

DefinitionA piece of a document, the unit a retrieval pipeline encodes and indexes. Chunking is a discrete stage with no Jacobian. Chapter 12.
ExampleA 3000-word document cut into 500-word pieces yields six chunks, each encoded on its own.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id chunk, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • A piece of a document, the unit a retrieval pipeline encodes and indexes. Chunking is a discrete stage with no Jacobian, and a stage that identifies two inputs identifies them for every stage after it, so what a chunker merges no later stage can separate.
  • A chunk’s vector is read by the index against a query vector, and the probe depth, cell, and cross-article share of the candidates are properties of the chunks and the query set together.

classifier concept

DefinitionA consumer that produces a score per row and turns it into a decision with a threshold. Chapter 6.
ExampleA score of 0.7 against a threshold of 0.5 is a positive decision, and raising the threshold to 0.8 flips it.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id classifier, kind concept.
Statusmeasures [predicted]. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 6.1.

Assumptions and scope
  • A consumer that produces a score per row and turns it into a decision with a threshold. For a linear classifier the sensitivity is the link’s slope times the weight direction, so the read operator is the workload mean of the squared slope times the outer product of the weights, sends every vector to a multiple of the weights, and reads nothing orthogonal to them.
  • The score is affine, so chapter 0’s exact quotient applies before the link. The whale clan classifier is the flip’s classifier case, held-out AUROC 0.934 against 0.883 for a code that reconstructs twice as well.

Clinical Bond Index instrument

DefinitionFor an institutional policy and a patient population, the expected value over the population of the clinical friction of the path the policy mandates minus the clinical friction of the clinical geodesic. It is never negative, and it is zero if and only if the mandated path coincides with the geodesic for every patient.
ExampleA population of two patients under one policy. For the first the mandated path has friction 9 and the geodesic 5, an excess of 4. For the second the mandated path is the geodesic, an excess of 0. The index is (4 + 0) / 2 = 2. The numbers are arithmetic from the definition.
VolumeGeometric Medicine, Volume 8 of the Geometric Series; entry id clinical-bond-index, kind instrument.
StatusA defined quantity that has not been computed. Its use as a measure of structural injustice rests on Prediction 4, that groups with a higher index report worse experience, which the volume states as falsifiable and has not tested. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • It shares only a name with the Bond Index of Geometric Ethics, which measures how much an evaluation changes under re-descriptions that should not change it. The volume says a value of one says nothing about the other.
  • The geodesic is a counterfactual, the path of a perfectly calibrated clinician with unlimited resources. Section 12.7 offers expert panels, best-practice benchmarking and computed geodesics as estimates and states the limits of each.
  • It is a population measure of current policy effects. Section 12.8 says it does not measure individual injustice, historical injustice or injustice outside healthcare.
  • Section 18.8 gives it the status formally defined, operationally feasible, not yet computed from clinical data.
Prior artnone recorded

Clinical decision complex concept

DefinitionA weighted simplicial complex on which clinical decisions are pathfinding problems. Each vertex is a clinical state with an attribute vector of nine clinical-moral scores, each edge is an available clinical action with a non-negative weight, and each higher simplex is a care bundle whose cost is evaluated as a unit.
ExampleIn the volume’s intubation example the current state is a vertex with attribute vector (0.25, 0.5, 0.5, 0.2, 0.4, 0.3, 0.4, 0.6, 0.3), and intubation is an edge to the vertex (0.35, 0.5, 0.4, 0.1, 0.3, 0.2, 0.2, 0.7, 0.25). The outcomes score rises by 0.10 and the dignity score falls by 0.20.
VolumeGeometric Medicine, Volume 8 of the Geometric Series; entry id clinical-decision-complex, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, and says a clinical instrument is plausible but has not been built or gated. Its Section 18.8 says the covariance matrix has not been estimated and the clinical Bond Index has not been computed from clinical data, so every number in these entries is an illustration unless the entry says otherwise. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • It is a simplicial complex and not a smooth manifold. The volume writes clinical manifold informally and means this complex.
  • The nine dimensions are inherited from the moral manifold of Geometric Ethics, and each score lies between 0 and 1. Section 4.13 calls the nine-dimensional structure a model and an open empirical question.
  • Section 4.13 says the complex is not a bedside calculator and does not produce unique solutions, because the covariance matrix, the boundary penalties and the goal region must be estimated from data.
  • The covariance matrix has not been estimated. Section 18.8 gives the nine-dimensional claim the status theoretically grounded, empirically untested at scale.
Prior artA weighted simplicial complex. The volume gives it as the clinical instance of the moral manifold of Geometric Ethics.

Clinical edge weight concept

DefinitionThe cost of one clinical action. It is the quadratic form $\Delta a^T \Sigma^{-1} \Delta a$ in the change of the patient's nine-component attribute vector, with $\Sigma$ the 9 by 9 clinical-moral covariance matrix, plus the sum of the penalties $\beta_k$ of the clinical-moral boundaries the action crosses.
ExampleThe volume’s illustration for intubating a patient with advanced dementia has a change vector with squared Euclidean length 0.1025, an assumed covariance-weighted term of about 0.15, and a consent penalty of 10, so the weight is 0.15 + 10 = 10.15. Supportive care crosses no boundary and weighs about 0.05. Both totals are the volume’s and are marked illustrative.
VolumeGeometric Medicine, Volume 8 of the Geometric Series; entry id clinical-edge-weight, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, and says a clinical instrument is plausible but has not been built or gated. Its Section 18.8 says the covariance matrix has not been estimated and the clinical Bond Index has not been computed from clinical data, so every number in these entries is an illustration unless the entry says otherwise. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The volume calls the quadratic form the Mahalanobis distance. The formula has no square root.
  • The covariance matrix has 45 independent entries and the theorems are said to hold for any positive-definite one. None of the entries has been estimated, and Section 4.5.2 says the framework runs on the qualitative structure until it is.
  • With the identity as covariance matrix the first term reduces to the Euclidean form.
  • The two worked weights of Section 4.4.3 are marked illustrative by the volume.
Prior artnone recorded

Clinical friction concept

DefinitionThe total cost of a path on the clinical decision complex, the sum of the clinical edge weights of its steps. It splits into distance friction, the sum of the covariance-weighted terms, and boundary friction, the sum of the boundary penalties crossed.
ExampleA path of three actions with weights 0.5, 10.25 and 1.25 has friction 12. If the only boundary crossed is one with penalty 10 on the second action, boundary friction is 10 and distance friction is 2. The numbers are arithmetic from the definition.
VolumeGeometric Medicine, Volume 8 of the Geometric Series; entry id clinical-friction, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, and says a clinical instrument is plausible but has not been built or gated. Its Section 18.8 says the covariance matrix has not been estimated and the clinical Bond Index has not been computed from clinical data, so every number in these entries is an illustration unless the entry says otherwise. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Friction is a property of a path and not of a case. A clinically difficult case can have a low-friction minimum path.
  • The volume calls distance friction reducible by better treatments and boundary friction structural.
  • It inherits the unestimated covariance matrix and the uncalibrated boundary penalties of the edge weight.
Prior artnone recorded

Clinical geodesic concept

DefinitionThe minimum-cost path on the clinical decision complex from the patient's initial state to the goal region, where cost is the sum of the nine-dimensional clinical edge weights. The volume takes it as the recommended plan of care.
ExampleIn the volume’s illustration two edges leave the current state, intubation with weight 10.15 and supportive care with weight 0.05. The geodesic takes supportive care, although intubation is better on the outcomes score alone. The weights are the volume’s illustrative ones.
VolumeGeometric Medicine, Volume 8 of the Geometric Series; entry id clinical-geodesic, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, and says a clinical instrument is plausible but has not been built or gated. Its Section 18.8 says the covariance matrix has not been estimated and the clinical Bond Index has not been computed from clinical data, so every number in these entries is an illustration unless the entry says otherwise. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The goal region is the set of states at or above a minimum acceptable attribute vector, and it is set jointly by clinician and patient.
  • It may not exist. When a resource constraint removes edges, the goal region can become unreachable.
  • It depends on the covariance matrix, the boundary penalties and the goal region, and different estimates give different geodesics.
  • It is a minimum-cost path on a discrete complex and not a geodesic of a smooth metric. Section 18.8 gives the pathfinding model the status formally developed, not directly validated.
Prior artA shortest path in a weighted graph, which the volume searches with the A* algorithm of Hart, Nilsson and Raphael (1968).

Clinical heuristic admissibility result

DefinitionA clinical moral heuristic estimates the remaining cost from a state as the sum over boundaries of the penalty $\beta_k$ times the probability that the remaining path crosses boundary $k$. If each penalty is at most the true cost of crossing, the heuristic never overestimates the remaining cost, and A* search finds the clinical geodesic.
ExampleSuppose one boundary has a trained penalty of 10, a true crossing cost of 15, and a probability of 0.5 of being crossed on the remaining path. The heuristic gives 5, the true expected boundary cost is 7.5, and the heuristic is admissible. With a trained penalty of 20 it gives 10 and overestimates. The numbers are arithmetic from the definition.
VolumeGeometric Medicine, Volume 8 of the Geometric Series; entry id clinical-heuristic-admissibility, kind result.
StatusA theorem with a short proof in Section 7.1, conditional on the calibration hypothesis. Section 18.8 gives the underlying pathfinding model the status formally developed, behaviorally plausible, not directly validated. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The hypothesis is that training calibrates each penalty as a lower bound on the true cost of crossing. The volume assumes this and does not measure it.
  • The proof uses the fact that the heuristic ignores the remaining distance cost, which is non-negative.
  • When a penalty exceeds the true cost somewhere, the heuristic is inadmissible and the search may avoid the optimal path. The volume names moral injury, defensive medicine and personal trauma as mechanisms.
Prior artAdmissibility of an A* heuristic, with the optimality result of Hart, Nilsson and Raphael (1968).

Clinical-moral boundaries concept

DefinitionThresholds on the clinical decision complex where the decision regime changes discontinuously, each with a penalty added to the weight of any action that crosses it. Five are defined, namely harm, futility, consent, abandonment and sacred value. The sacred-value penalty is infinite, and the others are finite in at least some settings.
ExampleTake a harm penalty of 10 and a futility penalty of 20, both inside the volume’s typical ranges of 5 to 20 and 10 to 30. An action that crosses both adds 30 to its edge weight, and an action that crosses the sacred-value boundary has infinite weight whatever else it gains. The sum is arithmetic from the definition.
VolumeGeometric Medicine, Volume 8 of the Geometric Series; entry id clinical-moral-boundaries, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, and says a clinical instrument is plausible but has not been built or gated. Its Section 18.8 says the covariance matrix has not been estimated and the clinical Bond Index has not been computed from clinical data, so every number in these entries is an illustration unless the entry says otherwise. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The penalty ranges are given as typical calibrations in normalized units. They are not measured, and Section 4.12 says they must be calibrated for specific clinical populations.
  • The consent penalty is about infinite for a competent patient outside an emergency and drops to a finite value in an emergency or when the patient lacks capacity.
  • The harm penalty is high but finite, so a minimum-cost path may pass through harm, as in surgery.
  • Later chapters use penalties outside the five, for example a trust penalty and a justice penalty in Theorem 10.1, without adding them to this definition.

Coalition fragility index result

Definition$F(C)$ is the share of dimensions outside the coalition's agreement submanifold, multiplied by the largest ratio of within-coalition variance to squared tolerance among those outside dimensions. A coalition with $F(C)$ above 1 is called geometrically fragile.
ExampleWith six dimensions and agreement on two, the first factor is \(4/6\), about 0.67. The index reaches 1 when the worst outside dimension has variance equal to 1.5 times the squared tolerance, since \(0.67 \times 1.5 = 1\). These are the volume’s figures.
VolumeGeometric Politics, Volume 10 of the Geometric Series; entry id coalition-fragility-index, kind result.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, and says a political-argument instrument is plausible but has not been built or gated. District 7, the source of nearly every number in the volume, is a fictional district, and Chapter 18 says precise estimation of the manifold needs larger and richer datasets than currently exist. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The chapter states the theorem and gives no proof. The index and its threshold of 1 work as a definition.
  • It needs the tolerance and the within-coalition variance on each dimension, neither of which the volume measures.
  • The claim that both American party coalitions operate near the threshold is argued from the posited agreement dimension of 2.
Prior artnone recorded

codebook concept

DefinitionThe small set of allowed values a quantizer replaces each number with. Chapter 0 section 0.11. Also codeword.
ExampleA codebook of four values, 0, 1, 2, and 3, replaces 1.4 with 1 and 2.6 with 3.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id codebook, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The small set of allowed values a quantizer replaces each input with, under the nearest-codeword rule. The distortion of an input is its distance to the nearest codeword, nonnegative, zero when the input is a codeword, achieved by some codeword, and never larger for a larger codebook.
  • Two arms compared at unequal codebooks are not a flip comparison, which is the twenty-five percent codebook confound the ledger carries, and the reset content of a stored description is separate from its rate, which is row GO-7’s finding across six codebooks.

cognitive manifold concept

DefinitionThe set of cognitive states a system actually visits, hypothesized to form a smooth submanifold $M$ of the activation space whose dimension is far below the number of units. Its dimension is the number of independent ways the cognitive state can vary.
ExampleThe volume’s analogy is a body with about 244 joints at six degrees of freedom each, which has 6 times 244 = 1464 configuration dimensions, while walking varies in about two, the phase of the gait cycle and the speed.
VolumeGeometric Cognition, Volume 6 of the Geometric Series; entry id cognitive-manifold, kind concept.
StatusThe README's status block of 2026-09-13 calls the book a domain exposition at posited, graded by a claim ledger converted from the manuscript with debt ratio 1.0, so every row is retrospective and no gate has been sealed in the repository. The ledger grades the benchmark statistics exploratory because their primary run records are not in the repository, and it holds every interpretation at posited because the admission filter xbse ruled the cognitive instrument inadmissible on 2026-07-14. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • It is a hypothesis, and the volume calls it a strong claim. The ledger holds the row that cognitive states form a manifold on which distance is meaningful at posited (GC-2).
  • The formal definition adds a Riemannian metric and a smooth embedding. It requires each task trajectory in activation space to stay within a small distance of a curve on the manifold.
  • Chapter 17 leaves open whether the manifold is Riemannian or Finsler and what its dimension is for human cognition.
Prior artThe manifold hypothesis of machine learning, which the volume cites from Bengio and colleagues, Tenenbaum and colleagues, and Roweis and Saul.

cognitive signature and signature distance instrument

DefinitionThe vector of a model's normalized subtask scores, compared between models by Euclidean distance. Each subtask is rescaled so that the worst of the five models is 0 and the best is 1, with lower-is-better subtasks inverted.
ExampleSignatures (1, 0) and (0, 1) have the same mean, 0.5, and a distance of the square root of 2, about 1.41. The volume’s matrix prints 0.58 for Gemini 3 Flash and Gemini 2.5 Flash, its closest pair, and 1.03 for Claude and Gemini 2.0 Flash, its farthest.
VolumeGeometric Cognition, Volume 6 of the Geometric Series; entry id cognitive-signature, kind instrument.
StatusThe README's status block of 2026-09-13 calls the book a domain exposition at posited, graded by a claim ledger converted from the manuscript with debt ratio 1.0, so every row is retrospective and no gate has been sealed in the repository. The ledger grades the benchmark statistics exploratory because their primary run records are not in the repository, and it holds every interpretation at posited because the admission filter xbse ruled the cognitive instrument inadmissible on 2026-07-14. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The normalization uses the minimum and maximum across the five tested models, so a signature is relative to that set.
  • Euclidean distance weights all subtasks equally. The volume names weighted, cosine and rank-based distances as alternatives that change the structure of the space.
  • The ledger grades the claim of five distinct profile shapes exploratory (GC-16) and leaves the predictability of a signature from architecture open (GC-21).

coherence time concept

DefinitionThe interval over which a changing quantity stays correlated with itself. A value measured longer ago than the coherence time is a guess. Equation 0.25.
ExampleA channel whose fading repeats every 20 milliseconds has a coherence time of 20 milliseconds.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id coherence-time, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: 1 item(s), see below.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.25.

Assumptions and scope
  • Clarke’s formula gives the coherence time from the Doppler frequency alone and assumes the fading model behind it.
  • A value measured longer ago than the coherence time is a guess, and a certificate issued that long ago has decorrelated from the state it certified.
  • The proportional refresh-floor law that was fit to it was refuted and is not cited. Its sealed replacement calibrated the baseline first and found floors at a few transmission intervals.
Prior artnone recorded

Failures and corrections

  • observation-theory-campaigns/experiments/RADIO-FRESHNESS-TRACK.md:41-50 at 75e9737. The age horizon (analysis/csi/, XPROTO-CSI-SWEEP2 sealed 2026-08-27, graded PASS): at the calibrated 0.10 budget the largest compliant report period is a few TTI at 10 Hz and 1 TTI at 50 Hz and above, so there is no proportionality law to fit. The earlier CSI-refreshfloor.* claim of a floor ≈ 0.177·T_coh (R²=0.915) was an unsealed exploration measured at a relaxed 0.15 threshold against the 0.10 target, with a fresh baseline that never met the budget. It is refuted; the record is kept, not cited. Separately, the optimal linear predictor cannot beat the one-coherence-time wall (Gaussian fading → Wiener optimal), and that wall sits well outside the budget horizon. The RAN governor (analysis/ran) is the reference O-RAN rApp core: observe→measure false-clear→refresh at the floor→escalate (diversity / re-route).

cold, warm concept

DefinitionA cold measurement is taken before the cache holds anything useful, a warm one after. A cost figure without one of the two words beside it is not a cost figure. Chapter 0 section 0.13 and chapter 13.

  • A cold measurement is taken before the cache holds anything useful, a warm one after. The hit rate is zero on an empty cache, one when the cache holds the whole footprint, grows as the cache grows, and does not move when entries outside the footprint are added.

Collective aesthetic tensor concept

DefinitionA multilinear map that takes one interest covector from each reader in a population and returns a collective valence direction on the manifold. For two readers it splits into each reader's individual contribution plus an emergent component, the part of collective valence not attributable to any individual.
ExampleFor two readers and the chapter’s nine working axes the tensor has 9 times 9 times 9, which is 729 components. That is the volume’s count.
VolumeGeometric Aesthetics, Volume 13 of the Geometric Series; entry id collective-aesthetic-tensor, kind concept.
StatusPosited. No reader-level interest covectors are measured in the volume, and the Lasso axes are regression directions on aggregate ratings. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The emergent component vanishes exactly when collective valence is the sum of the individual valences.
  • Appendix F marks canon formation as geometric aggregation of individual judgments as conjectured, with no direct empirical fit (F14.1).
  • The evidence offered for a nonzero emergent component is the 71 Lasso axes. The chapter’s own caveat is that most of those axes do genre discrimination and that the point is structural, not a matter of effect size.
  • The count of 729 components assumes nine working axes per reader. Section 5.5 says the aesthetic manifold, unlike the moral one, does not start from nine known dimensions.

Collective alignment gap concept

DefinitionThe distance on the value manifold between the Nash equilibrium of several AI systems, in which each maximizes its own scalar reward, and their Bond Geodesic Equilibrium, in which each follows the value-aligned geodesic given the others. Theorem 18.1 says the gap is positive when some value dimension lies in every system's reward kernel.
ExampleIn the volume’s fictional three-system scenario the components are 0.21 on fairness and 0.13 on institutional legitimacy, and the printed total of 0.34 is their sum. After the shared value tensor the printed gap is 0.04.
VolumeGeometric AI, Volume 11 of the Geometric Series; entry id collective-alignment-gap, kind concept.
StatusA posited quantity resting on a theorem stated without proof. No value of it has been measured. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Theorem 18.1 is written as an equivalence with a non-empty intersection of the individual kernels. The paragraph after it adds that an interaction between dimensions can lie in the collective kernel even when that intersection is empty.
  • Theorem 18.1 has no proof in the chapter and is not among the theorems proved in Appendix D.
  • The proposed remedy is a shared value tensor with system-specific emphasis weights. The claim that the Nash equilibrium then converges to the Bond Geodesic Equilibrium is asserted, and Chapter 20 lists the matching containment question as open.
  • The gap values printed (0.21 on fairness, 0.13 on institutional legitimacy, and a fall from 0.34 to 0.04) belong to a fictional three-system scenario.
Prior artThe comparison point is the Nash equilibrium of game theory.

Collective geodesic concept

DefinitionFor a population, the allocation of a resource such as vaccine doses that minimizes the sum of clinical friction over all its members. It differs from the Nash equilibrium of individual geodesics, in which each member minimizes their own friction without counting effects on others.
ExampleA healthy young adult bears friction 1 from vaccination and friction 0 from refusing, and vaccination lowers the friction of contacts by 3 in total. Alone the adult refuses. Summed over the population vaccination changes total friction by 1 - 3 = -2, so the collective geodesic includes it. The numbers are arithmetic from the definition.

Corrections: none recorded.

commit hash instrument

DefinitionThe fingerprint git assigns to a snapshot of a repository and its history, which identifies the content exactly and does not by itself prove when it existed. Chronology comes from a public push, a signed tag, or an archival deposit. Chapter 0 section 0.12. Also commit.
ExampleCommit 3172e00 identifies one snapshot of the book’s repository and every file in it, and says nothing about the clock.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id commit-hash, kind instrument.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The fingerprint git assigns to a snapshot of a repository together with its history. It identifies exact content, so a changed hash proves a changed file and an equal hash is strong evidence of an unchanged one, but it does not by itself prove when that content existed, since git’s author and committer dates are supplied fields.
  • Chronology comes from a public repository receipt, a signed tag, a transparency log, or an archival deposit such as a Zenodo DOI, and a sealed prediction names one of those beside its hash.

Communication BIP (Bond Invariance Principle for communication) concept

DefinitionAn evaluation $\phi$ that claims to measure meaning must satisfy $\phi(\tau(m)) = \phi(m)$ for every act m and every transformation $\tau$ of the communication gauge group. A dependence on the signal coordinates that is not mediated by the signal-pragmatic and signal-content cross-terms is called a gauge anomaly.
ExampleTake a reference translation and a perfect paraphrase of it. They are related by an element of R, so a meaning evaluation must score them equally. The volume notes that the BLEU score of the paraphrase may be near zero, which is a gauge anomaly.
VolumeGeometric Communication, Volume 7 of the Geometric Series; entry id communication-bond-invariance-principle, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments. It says that no communication-domain instrument has been evaluated by the series' admission filter (xbse), that none currently passes its gate, and that the claims are theory at licensed strength and not validated measurement. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The chapter calls it a diagnostic criterion, not a normative aspiration. The test is to apply gauge transformations to a tool and check whether its output changes.
  • Chapter 10 reads it as the claim that translation has zero holonomy, and says the principle is an ideal and not a description, because the content manifold is not flat everywhere.
  • Features computable from the signal are invariant under a subgroup of the gauge group only. The chapter says they are not fully gauge-invariant.
Prior artnone recorded
