economic metric (inverse covariance as metric tensor) concept

DefinitionIn the continuous limit of the decision complex the cost of a small displacement is $ds^2 = g_{ij}\,da^i\,da^j$ with the metric tensor g equal to the inverse of the nine by nine dimensional covariance matrix Sigma. Cost is counted in standard deviations of behavioral expectation, so unusual displacements are costly.
ExampleWith a diagonal covariance each dimension adds its squared change over its variance. In the volume’s illustration a 100 dollar expense at monetary scale 50 adds \(100^2/50^2 = 4.0\) and a fairness change of 0.6 at scale 0.8 adds 0.5625, for 4.5625 on those two dimensions.
VolumeGeometric Economics, Volume 4 of the Geometric Series; entry id economic-metric-tensor, kind concept.
StatusModeling axiom in the volume's tags. The repository's registered test prereg-coupling-v1, which predicted that one shared metric couples risk and social preferences as a rank-one factor, was scored on the Global Preferences Survey and falsified on that proxy. The same-subject angle test that the scorecard names as decisive is unrun. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Taking the inverse covariance as the metric tensor is tagged a modeling axiom.
  • Sigma is symmetric positive semidefinite with at most 45 free parameters and is to be estimated from a calibration sample before prediction. The distance is a proper metric only when Sigma is positive definite and a pseudometric otherwise.
  • Chapter 16 calls the calibration partial and lists as open whether Sigma can be estimated from large observational data, whether it is stable in time and whether it is universal or culture specific.
  • The symmetric quadratic form cannot express the asymmetry between gains and losses. Section 4.10 replaces it with a Finsler metric for that purpose.
Prior artThe Mahalanobis distance of 1936, read as a Riemannian metric.

Economic No Escape conjecture result

DefinitionIf the economic decision manifold has components separated by the absence of any connecting path, and not merely by high boundary penalties, then no financial instrument, regulatory arbitrage or contract can create a transition between them.
ExampleThe volume’s candidate is the organ market. If no path joins the state of holding an organ to the state of holding money, the conjecture says that no instrument can complete the trade, whatever its price.
VolumeGeometric Economics, Volume 4 of the Geometric Series; entry id economic-no-escape-conjecture, kind result.
StatusConjecture, stated as an open problem by analogy with the No Escape Theorem of Geometric Ethics. Nothing is proved or measured. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • It is a conjecture. The surrounding open problem is tagged speculation or extension.
  • The premise is itself open. The volume asks whether sacred-value boundaries are topological disconnections or only very high penalties.
  • The volume proposes a test, building instruments that try to bridge candidate disconnections such as organ markets, and reports no run of it.

economic singularity concept

DefinitionA region of the decision manifold where the covariance matrix Sigma becomes degenerate, with its determinant going to zero, so that the metric, its inverse, diverges. There the geodesic equation has no finite-cost solution and price discovery fails. The volume models a financial crisis as this event.
ExampleFor two dimensions with unit variances and correlation r the determinant of Sigma is \(1 - r^2\). It is 0.64 at r = 0.6 and 0.19 at r = 0.9, and it goes to zero as r goes to 1.
VolumeGeometric Economics, Volume 4 of the Geometric Series; entry id economic-singularity, kind concept.

Its claims are to be read as theory at licensed strength and not as validated measurement, and the chapters tag each claim as established mathematics, empirical, modeling axiom, conditional theorem or speculation. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • In normal times Sigma is positive definite and every direction has a finite cost.
  • The mechanism given is that correlations between dimensions converge to plus or minus one, as when all holders sell at once.
  • The linear algebra is tagged established mathematics. The identification of a crisis with a degenerate Sigma is the volume’s model, illustrated on 2008 and not fitted.
  • The chapter precedes it with the geometric bubble of its Definition 39, in which the monetary metric component falls while the trust and epistemic components rise.

Educational Bond Index instrument

DefinitionFor an institutional policy P and a student population S, the expected learning deviation of the path the policy allows, measured against each student's geodesic. The learning deviation of a path is the integral over time of its manifold distance from the geodesic. An index of zero means the policy imposes no deviation.
ExampleFor two students whose mean distances from their geodesics are 0.4 and 0.8, the index computed as in Appendix B.4 is the average, 0.6. In the volume’s narrative the shares of the index are 45, 30, 15 and 10 percent, which sum to 100.
VolumeGeometric Education, Volume 9 of the Geometric Series; entry id educational-bond-index, kind instrument.
StatusA proposed instrument that has not been computed on data. The value 2.1 and the shares of 45, 30, 15 and 10 percent in Section 13.5 belong to the narrative of the composite student Alex. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • It is a property of the policy and not of the students. The volume says no real institution reaches zero.
  • The computation needs an estimated learner metric, a computed geodesic and observed trajectories. The volume calls the metric estimate the most uncertain step.
  • It is decomposed into access, heuristic, metric and residual parts. The volume gives no procedure for separating them.
  • Section 18.5 states that no institution has performed the prospective test. The study in Section 13.5 is carried out by the volume’s composite student and is narrative, not a record.

educational boundary concept

DefinitionA threshold on the learner manifold where the region a learner can reach changes discontinuously. The volume defines three types. A prerequisite boundary comes from the structure of knowledge, an institutional boundary is imposed by an institution, and a developmental boundary comes from the learner's developmental stage.
ExampleWith a prerequisite threshold of 0.6 on linear algebra, a student at 0.4 cannot reach the region labeled quantum mechanics and a student at 0.7 can. The volume’s example of an institutional boundary is a 3.0 grade point average to stay in an honors program.
VolumeGeometric Education, Volume 9 of the Geometric Series; entry id educational-boundary, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments. No education-domain instrument has been evaluated by the series' admission filter, and Chapter 18 states that the six predictions of Section 16.3 have not been tested and that no method for estimating the learner metric has been validated at scale. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • A prerequisite boundary is unavoidable. The volume says a student who skips the prerequisite is in a region where the directions of motion needed for the content do not exist.
  • An institutional boundary may or may not match the structure of knowledge. The volume’s diagnostic is that a prerequisite whose removal leaves success in the later course unchanged, with other variables controlled, is institutional.
  • A developmental boundary cannot be crossed by instruction until the connectivity exists. The volume takes the stages from Piaget.
  • The diagnostic is proposed and the volume reports no application of it.
Prior artnone recorded

educational gauge violation tensor instrument

DefinitionA matrix $V_{ij}$ whose row i is one of the five changes of instrument and whose column j is a score dimension, with a single column for a scalar score. The entry is the expected change in score j when the instrument is changed, $V_{ij} = E[A_j(x, I_i') - A_j(x, I_i)]$. A gauge-invariant assessment has every entry zero.
ExampleThe volume’s estimated ranges for the SAT are 50 to 150 points for format, 80 to 200 for language, 10 to 30 for time and 50 to 100 for context. The lower ends sum to 190 and the upper ends to 480, which the volume rounds to 200 to 500.

educational heuristic field concept

DefinitionA non-negative function h on the learner manifold that estimates the remaining cost from a learner state to the goal region. It is a weighted sum of the estimates supplied by teachers, parents, peers, institutions and the student's own metacognition.
ExampleWith weights of 0.5 on the teacher and 0.5 on the student’s own estimate, and estimates of 4 and 6, the field value is 0.5 times 4 plus 0.5 times 6, which is 5. The other three sources have weight zero in this example.

educational local minimum concept

DefinitionA learner state x from which the geodesic cost to the goal is greater than from some nearby state y, while the cost of moving from x to y exceeds the time, effort and motivation the student has. The student cannot progress without outside intervention.
ExampleA student with a 1.8 average over 90 credits has 162 grade points and needs 2.0 to graduate, the volume’s example threshold. Nine more credits at 4.0 give 198 points over 99 credits, which is 2.0. At 3.0 it takes 18 credits, since 216 over 108 is 2.0.
VolumeGeometric Education, Volume 9 of the Geometric Series; entry id educational-local-minimum, kind concept.

Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The volume’s three examples are the prerequisite trap, the remediation loop and the recursive GPA trap.
  • In the GPA trap a cumulative average below the graduation threshold resists improvement, and the courses that raise it fastest may not count toward the degree.
  • The definition depends on the student’s available resources, so the same state can be a local minimum for one student and not for another.
  • The examples are described in words. The volume reports no measured case.

Effective dimensionality of an electorate instrument

DefinitionThe number of eigenvalues of the electorate's six-by-six covariance matrix, taken from the largest down, needed to reach 85 percent of the total variance. One dominant eigenvalue means the left-right axis is a good approximation, and evenly spread eigenvalues mean it is a poor one.
ExampleThe volume’s District 7 eigenvalues are 3.2, 2.8, 1.9, 1.5, 1.0 and 0.6, which sum to 11.0. The first three reach 7.9, or 72 percent, and the first four reach 9.4, or 85 percent, so the effective dimensionality is 4.

effective flavor dimensionality concept

DefinitionThe count of eigenvalues of an individual's receptor-response covariance $\Sigma_r$ that exceed that person's perceptual noise threshold. Supertasting raises gain and lifts marginal eigenvalues above the threshold. Specific anosmias and non-taster haplotypes drop particular eigenvalues below it and collapse dimensions.
ExampleWith eigenvalues (5, 2, 0.8, 0.3) and a noise threshold of 1, the effective dimensionality is 2. Doubling the gain with the threshold unchanged multiplies every eigenvalue of the covariance by 4, giving (20, 8, 3.2, 1.2), and all 4 clear the threshold. The numbers are illustrative.

effective rank concept

DefinitionThe number of directions a matrix really uses, the square of the sum of its eigenvalues over the sum of their squares, defined for a nonnegative spectrum that is not all zero, with no cutoff to choose. Equation 0.7. Also participation ratio.
ExampleEigenvalues (1, 1, 1, 1) have effective rank 4, and (1, 0.12, 0.06, 0.02) have effective rank about 1.4.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id effective-rank, kind concept.
Statusmeasures [demonstrated]. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.7.

Assumptions and scope
  • The effective rank is the square of the sum of the eigenvalues over the sum of their squares, between one and the dimension for a nonnegative spectrum, with no cutoff to choose.
  • It is not invariant under a change of basis of the input, unlike the trace pairing and the rank, and the ledger row that says so is the one that licenses comparing read operators across coordinate systems.
  • An allocation over a spectrum with effective rank below two concentrates on one direction, and the allocation report says so before giving a gain.
  • It is defined for a nonnegative spectrum that is not all zero, and it lies between one and the dimension.

Eight legal dimensions concept

DefinitionEight axes along which a legal state is scored. They are entitlement structure, factual nexus, procedural posture, statutory authority, constitutional conformity, precedential constraint, remedial scope and public interest. The eight scores of a case form its attribute vector.
ExampleThe volume’s illustrative vector for Crawford v. Marion County is (0.7, 0.5, 0.9, 0.5, 0.7, 0.8, 0.6, 0.7), so it scores 0.9 on procedural posture and 0.5 on statutory authority.
VolumeGeometric Law, Volume 5 of the Geometric Series; entry id eight-legal-dimensions, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic status of 2026-07-14 calls the volume a posited framework with one instrumented corner. That corner is the legal text embedding LeBSE, validated in the xbse admission filter on US case law with labels from the CourtListener citation graph, and the README says this covers structure preservation in legal text embeddings and not the book's broader jurisprudential claims, which remain posited theory at licensed strength. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The volume says the choice of eight is a modeling decision, not a derivation from first principles and not the unique correct decomposition. Chapter 1 tags it as a modeling axiom.
  • Dimensions may be added or merged. The stated requirement is several non-redundant axes of legal variation, and the later theorems are said to hold for any finite-dimensional attribute space.
  • The scores are to come from linear probes on a text embedding, trained on expert labels. Chapter 4 states that this programme has not yet been executed on legal data.
  • Chapter 15 requires that no pair of predicted scores correlate above 0.7 on held-out cases. Otherwise the probes are retrained or the dimensions redefined.

Einstein midpoint instrument

DefinitionThe weighted centroid of points on the Poincare ball of curvature minus c. It is the average in the Klein model with each point weighted by its Lorentz factor, carried back to the ball. In ball coordinates it is the Mobius half of $\sum_i w_i \lambda_i x_i / \sum_i w_i (\lambda_i - 1)$, with $\lambda_i = 2/(1 - c\|x_i\|^2)$.
ExampleFor the points (0.9, 0) and (0, 0) in the unit ball with equal weights, the midpoint lies at radius tanh(0.5 artanh 0.9), about 0.627. The shortcut that averages ball coordinates weighted by 1/(1 - 0.81) and 1 gives 0.756. Both values are the volume’s.
VolumeGeometric Methods, Volume 1 of the Geometric Series; entry id einstein-midpoint, kind instrument.
StatusProved, and checked against an independent computation in `formal/matlab/volume_checks.m` (Section 21.8). Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The points lie in the open ball, where c times the squared norm is below 1, and the weights are non-negative.
  • Proposition 3.1 states that the midpoint lies in the ball, reduces to the Euclidean weighted mean as c goes to 0, and for two points with equal weights is the midpoint of their geodesic. The text gives a proof sketch.
  • Weighting the ball coordinates by \(1/(1 - c\|x\|^2)\) and averaging them directly is not a hyperbolic midpoint. The November 2026 review corrected the chapter’s formula.

embedding concept

DefinitionA vector assigned to an object, a word, a sentence, a node, a document, so that nearness in the vector space stands for a relation between the objects. Chapter 11.
ExampleA sentence becomes a vector of 768 numbers, and two paraphrases become vectors with cosine near one.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id embedding, kind concept.
Statusmeasures [predicted]. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • A vector assigned to an object so that nearness in the vector space stands for a relation between the objects. Objects with the same embedding are indistinguishable to every consumer of the embedding, so the embedding is a quotient, and a cosine reader takes a further quotient in which the nearest neighbour is unchanged when the query is rescaled, where a dot-product reader does not.
  • What an embedding is worth to a consumer is the consumer’s number. The keys that reconstructed at cosine 0.995 and raised the perplexity by three orders of magnitude are the case, and the rank certificate is the instrument that says which neighbour rankings a compressed embedding preserved.

Embedding cloud of a work concept

DefinitionThe set $X(W)$ of vectors obtained by cutting a work $W$ into units (paragraphs, audio frames, image patches) and passing each unit through a fixed pretrained encoder. The work is treated as this cloud and not as a single point.
ExampleThe volume’s cases are a 300-paragraph novel under LaBSE, which gives 300 points in 768 dimensions, and a 30-second clip under MERT at 1.5 frames per second, which gives 45 points in 1024 dimensions.
VolumeGeometric Aesthetics, Volume 13 of the Geometric Series; entry id aesthetic-embedding-cloud, kind concept.
StatusA construction, with encoders fixed by choice. The claim that aesthetic features of a work are geometric features of its cloud is called a candidate claim in Section 17.2. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The encoder is a modeling choice. The volume uses LaBSE (768 dimensions) for text and MERT-v1-330M layer 7 (1024 dimensions) for music, and it says the empirical claims depend on these encoders.
  • Images are named as compatible with the framework but the empirical chapters report on text and music only.
  • The mean and covariance summaries discard the order of the units. Order is kept only in the trajectory features.
  • Section 16.2 limits the construction to artifacts an encoder can embed. Live performance and conceptual art fall outside it.

empty quadrant (metacognition) result

DefinitionIn the plane of self-monitoring accuracy (M3) and effort scaling index (M4), split at a threshold on each axis, no tested model lies in Quadrant I, where both exceed the threshold. The volume reads the gap as a structural constraint.
ExampleWith the appendix’s threshold of 0.25, Gemini 2.5 Pro at (0.500, 0.000) is in Quadrant II and Gemini 2.0 Flash at (0.042, 0.827) is in Quadrant IV. Their differences are 0.458 on M3 and -0.827 on M4, as the volume prints.

encoder concept

DefinitionA model that maps an input to an embedding. Chapter 12.
ExampleLaBSE maps a sentence in any of its languages to a 768-dimensional vector.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id encoder, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 12.3.

Assumptions and scope
  • A model that maps an input to an embedding. An encoder votes only when its held-out AUROC on a corpus it was not trained on clears both nulls by the preregistered margin, its authority is its reliability weight, and a strictly monotone recalibration of its score changes neither the verdict nor the weight.
  • The rights encoder fell below the untrained baseline and was retired rather than tuned, and the legal-citation encoder’s flip is the ledger’s demonstrated row.
  • An encoder’s held-out AUROC depends on the orientation of its score. A score that ranks the wrong way scores 1 minus A, and the gate reads the score as the encoder produces it and not the better of the two orientations.

ensemble instrument

DefinitionA scorer that averages or votes several scorers. Its average lies between its members and its squared error is at most their mean squared error. Chapter 7. Also bagging, random forest.
ExampleScores 0.6, 0.7, and 0.8 average 0.7, and the average’s squared error is at most the mean of the three squared errors.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id ensemble, kind instrument.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • A scorer that averages or votes several scorers. Its average lies between the smallest and the largest member, its squared error is at most the mean of the members’ squared errors, and a constant ensemble is its constant. That arithmetic is why bagging reduces variance.
  • Whether an ensemble beats a formula is a measured question and not a principle, and the comparison is fair only inside one fold protocol with the Nadeau and Bengio correction applied, where nine wins to three became three wins, seventeen ties, and eleven losses.
Prior artnone recorded

equalized odds concept

DefinitionThe requirement that the true-positive rate and the false-positive rate be the same across groups. Equation 0.37. Also three ways.
ExampleTrue positive rates of 0.90 and 0.88 with false positive rates of 0.10 and 0.11 across two groups are nearly equalized odds.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id equalized-odds, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.37.

Assumptions and scope
  • Equal true-positive and false-positive rates across groups. A group’s favourable rate is its true-positive rate times its base rate plus its false-positive rate times the rest, so under equalized odds the favourable rates agree exactly when the base rates do, given that the classifier separates at all.
  • Equalized odds and parity of outcomes therefore conflict whenever the base rates differ. With rates 0.8 and 0.2 and base rates one half and one tenth the favourable rates are 0.5 and 0.26, a ratio below four fifths.
Prior artnone recorded

Equal protection as gauge invariance result

DefinitionThe equal protection gauge group is generated by transformations that change a party's protected-class attribute while preserving all facts, all legal attributes and all Hohfeldian bonds. A legal evaluation satisfies equal protection if and only if it is unchanged by every element of this group.
ExampleChanging a party’s sex twice returns the original case, so that generator has order 2. If the original case draws 60 months, the case with the sex changed must also draw 60 months.
VolumeGeometric Law, Volume 5 of the Geometric Series; entry id equal-protection-gauge-invariance, kind result.
StatusThe README's epistemic status of 2026-07-14 calls the volume a posited framework with one instrumented corner. That corner is the legal text embedding LeBSE, validated in the xbse admission filter on US case law with labels from the CourtListener citation graph, and the README says this covers structure preservation in legal text embeddings and not the book's broader jurisprudential claims, which remain posited theory at licensed strength. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The front matter classes this among the conditional theorems that follow from the invariance axiom. The chapter gives a proof sketch.
  • The added claim that the invariance implies an entitlement balance in any closed bilateral dispute also uses the Hohfeldian correlative structure.
  • Disparate impact is treated separately. An invariant rule applied to a population whose distribution of situations differs by group can still give different group averages.
  • The tiers of scrutiny and affirmative action are read as gauge-breaking terms that need justification, so the requirement as doctrine applies it is approximate invariance with stated exceptions.
Prior artnone recorded

escalation concept

DefinitionThe decision to hand an item to a person rather than decide it, the single-decision form of abstention. Chapter 14. Also escalat, refus.
ExampleA decision the certificate cannot clear at its bar is handed to a person, and the count of escalations is reported.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id escalation, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The decision to hand an item to a person rather than decide it. A rule that escalates every item whose margin is below a bar decides a set that can only shrink as the bar rises, so coverage can only fall, every decided item carries at least the bar’s margin, and a bar of zero escalates nothing.
  • Coverage times the decided false-clear rate is the fraction of all items cleared and wrong, so an escalation policy trades coverage for a false-clear rate and a deployment report states both.

Euclidean distance concept

DefinitionThe straight-line distance between two vectors, which reads every coordinate at the scale it arrives in. Chapter 3. Also Euclidean.
ExampleThe distance between (0, 0) and (3, 4) is 5.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id euclidean-distance, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The straight-line distance between two vectors, whose square is the identity reader’s quadratic form on the difference, so it reads every coordinate at the scale it arrives in. It is symmetric and zero exactly between a row and itself.

eviction concept

DefinitionChoosing what to drop when a cache is full. Chapter 13. Also evict.
ExampleA cache of 4 entries receiving a fifth drops the least recently used one.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id eviction, kind concept.
Statusmeasures [demonstrated]. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Choosing what to drop when a cache is full. Evicting tokens replaces attention over all tokens with attention over the kept subset, so the output lies between the kept values, equals them when they agree, and the whole cache is the case of no eviction.

Evidence status of the moral metric result

DefinitionThe volume's statement, added in v1.28, that the moral metric is untested. No measurement it reports shows a metric, set by hand or learned from data, predicting moral judgements better than the boundary penalties alone. The one registered test of the question was void, so it neither supports nor refutes the metric.
ExampleOn 1,165 held-out posts no predictor beat the average verdict, so the registered comparison was not graded. The embeddings explain at most 4 percent of verdict variance where about 86 percent is not vote noise, so a missing metric effect could not be told from a present one.
VolumeGeometric Ethics, Volume 2 of the Geometric Series; entry id moral-metric-evidence-status, kind result.
StatusA statement of absence of evidence, in the volume's words a model whose metric has not been tested. The void run is neither a pass nor a refutation, and the ledger has no row for the claim. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The registered test (prereg-precedent-v1, run in November 2026) asked whether a metric learned on sentence embeddings improves prediction of community verdicts on 1,165 held-out forum posts, beyond two gates read from the text and the nearest earlier cases.
  • No predictor in that run did better than the average verdict. The registration had fixed that outcome in advance as the sign of an instrument that reads no signal, so the run is void.
  • A later check, not registered and made on the training posts, found that the embeddings explain between 2.5 and 4 percent of the variance of the verdicts while about 86 percent of that variance is not vote noise. The volume concludes the test could not have detected a metric effect of ordinary size.
  • The statement covers the predictive value of the metric. It does not withdraw the boundaries, the gates or the proved results.
Prior artnone recorded

Executable stratification instrument

DefinitionA tuple of a finite set of strata with an initial stratum, an ordered list of semantic gates (each with source strata, a triggering feature, a target and a boundary type), a set of authority strata whose rules grant an action, and a set of absorbing strata. On each event the state moves to the target of the first matching gate, and otherwise stays.
ExampleThe volume’s visitor_standing has five strata (none, stranger, welcomed, arranged, hostile). A stranger who says he is the plumber stays a stranger, because the claim matches no gate. Margaret’s welcome moves him to welcomed, which grants nothing.
VolumeGeometric Ethics, Volume 2 of the Geometric Series; entry id executable-stratification, kind instrument.
StatusA definition (ledger GE-DEF-8-14, class definition) describing the realization that runs in the ErisML scene runtime and a care robot built on it. Appendix F has no row for it. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Gates are edge-triggered. A gate fires on the event just observed and never on the history.
  • Constraint surfaces (Type IV boundaries) are not strata. They are the agent’s non-defeasible prohibitions and no gate leads there.
  • An authority stratum must be computed from an authenticated channel, a physical measurement or the governor’s ruling on attested evidence. A stratum read by a learned model may only remove watchfulness and never grant.
  • A claim an entity makes about itself is free text and is never a gate.
Prior artnone recorded

expected calibration error instrument

  • The average over score bins, weighted by bin size, of the absolute difference between the bin’s mean score and its fraction of positives. It lies in the unit interval, it is zero exactly when every bin’s mean score equals its positive fraction, and a calibrated scorer has error zero.

explained variance concept

DefinitionThe fraction of total variance retained by a set of principal components, the identity reader's criterion for a reduction. Chapter 4. Also explained ratio.
ExampleKeeping 2 of the eigenvalues 4, 3, 2, and 1 explains 7 of 10, or 70 percent.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id explained-variance, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 4.1.

Assumptions and scope
  • The fraction of total variance the first k components carry. It lies in the unit interval, cannot fall as k grows, and reaches one at the full dimension. With unit sensitivities it is the fraction a consumer retains, which is why it is the identity reader’s criterion.
  • A consumer that reads other directions retains a different fraction. With variances 9 and 1 and a consumer reading only the second direction, keeping the first component explains nine tenths of the variance and none of what the consumer reads, which is the flip in its smallest form.

F1 concept

DefinitionTwice the product of precision and recall over their sum. The optimal thresholded F1 of a score is the best F1 over every threshold and depends only on the score's ranking. Equation 0.28.
ExamplePrecision 0.6 and recall 0.75 give F1 of 2 times 0.45 over 1.35, or 0.667.

Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.28.

Assumptions and scope
  • Twice the product of precision and recall over their sum. The optimal thresholded F1 of a score is the best F1 over every threshold in both directions, and it depends only on the score’s ranking, so a strictly monotone transform of the score leaves it unchanged.
  • Its ceiling from the Youden index holds for every score, and the AUROC form of that ceiling only for concave ROC curves, which is the theory-radar erratum.

Assumptions and scope

  • The rate is per consumer, given per read operator, slice, group, or footprint, never as one aggregate.

Equation

Book equation 0.26.

\[\mathrm{FC}=\Pr\big[W\ \text{refutes}\ \big|\ \mathcal C_t\ \text{clears}\big],\qquad \text{coverage}=\Pr\big[\mathcal C_t\ \text{clears}\big].\]

Book equation 13.1.

\[\mathrm{FC}=\Pr\big[W\ \text{refutes}\ \big|\ \mathcal C_t\ \text{clears}\big],\qquad d_O(\Delta)=\operatorname{tr}\big(P_C\,M_{\mathrm{drift}}(\Delta)\big),\qquad M_{\mathrm{drift}}(\Delta)=\mathbb E\big[\delta_\Delta\delta_\Delta^{\top}\big].\]

Book equation 12.4.

\[\begin{gathered} \mathrm{FC}_{\text{naive}}=\Pr\big[\mathrm{acc}_s<\text{target}\ \big|\ \text{benchmark}\ge\text{target}\big]=\frac1S\sum_{s=1}^{S}\mathbf 1\big[\mathrm{acc}_s<\text{target}\big] \\ \text{when the benchmark clears, so that the naive certificate's coverage is 1.} \end{gathered}\]

Conditions

  • A witness must exist. Where none exists the rate is not measurable and the certificate is unassessed, not safe.
  • The rate is per consumer, given per read operator, slice, group, or footprint, never as one aggregate.
  • Coverage is reported with it. A witnessed certificate clears fewer decisions than a naive one, and the two numbers are read together.

Conditions are curated in entries.toml rather than read from a record.

Failures and corrections

  • observation-theory-campaigns/experiments/RADIO-FRESHNESS-TRACK.md:33-39 at 75e9737. ⚠️ XPROTO-AICSI scope correction (2026-08-25). The v1 seal stands for what it tested, but the reconstruction-vs-consumer dissociation does not survive the community-standard substrate. On real 3GPP CDL-C with a CsiNet-class codec the NMSE-optimal codec reconstructs near-perfectly (NMSE ≈ 0.03) and false-clears 0.0 on all seeds; the pre-registered kill fired. See analysis/aicsi/PREREG-XPROTO-AICSI-V2.md (REFUTED AT SHAKEDOWN, NOT SEALED, kept negative). This is a scope correction, not a retraction. Do not headline the AICSI row; WCNC §III-C is dropped.
  • observation-theory-campaigns/experiments/RADIO-FRESHNESS-TRACK.md:41-50 at 75e9737. The age horizon (analysis/csi/, XPROTO-CSI-SWEEP2 sealed 2026-08-27, graded PASS): at the calibrated 0.10 budget the largest compliant report period is a few TTI at 10 Hz and 1 TTI at 50 Hz and above, so there is no proportionality law to fit. The earlier CSI-refreshfloor.* claim of a floor ≈ 0.177·T_coh (R²=0.915) was an unsealed exploration measured at a relaxed 0.15 threshold against the 0.10 target, with a fresh baseline that never met the budget. It is refuted; the record is kept, not cited. Separately, the optimal linear predictor cannot beat the one-coherence-time wall (Gaussian fading → Wiener optimal), and that wall sits well outside the budget horizon. The RAN governor (analysis/ran) is the reference O-RAN rApp core: observe→measure false-clear→refresh at the floor→escalate (diversity / re-route).
  • geometric-observation/chapters/ch19_the_certificate_that_ages.md:84-91 at 0a59b0d. — the rate at which a clearance is wrong, conditional on the certificate having cleared, reported beside the certificate’s coverage. (An earlier draft wrote the joint probability \(\Pr[\text{clears} \wedge \text{refutes}]\); the joint rate is the product of the two and is what a naive certificate that clears everything reports, since its coverage is one. Corrected 2026-09-03.) A certificate whose false-clear rate exceeds the target it purports to guarantee is vacuous for that consumer, however confident it looks. FC is measurable wherever a witness exists, which — per the table — is nearly everywhere it matters.

False termination region result

DefinitionThe set of states outside the goal where the heuristic reads below the stopping threshold while the true distance to the goal is large. A search that halts when $h(x)$ falls below the threshold and enters this set stops outside the goal. The volume reads overconfidence as this underestimation of cost-to-go.
ExampleWith a stopping threshold of 1, a state where the heuristic reads 0.5 and the true distance to the goal is 3 lies in the region, since the search halts there 3 units short.
VolumeGeometric Reasoning, Volume 3 of the Geometric Series; entry id false-termination-region, kind result.
StatusA conditional statement about threshold search, given without a full proof. The calibration errors it is attached to are benchmark measurements, and the link between the two is posited. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • It assumes a satisficing search with a fixed threshold. The heuristic must underestimate the true cost-to-go by more than the threshold on a region that does not meet the goal.
  • Tagged a conditional theorem. The identification of a model’s stated confidence with the terminal value of an implicit heuristic is the volume’s modeling step.
  • The measured part is separate. All five models were overconfident on the calibration task, with expected calibration errors from 0.230 to 0.415.

Falsification criteria (Appendix E.8) instrument

DefinitionFour stated tests. The symmetry claim is falsified if cross-lingual correlation falls below 0.5 across several language families on a pre-registered bundled corpus with n at least 200. The sign-flip claim is weakened or overturned if the flip fails on a new music corpus with a different encoder. The within-genre claim is weakened if the residual fails to replicate. Any proved claim with a proof error is retracted.
ExampleCriterion (i) needs a correlation below 0.5 on at least 200 bundles. The volume’s Finnish (288) and French (227) pairs meet the size bar and show 0.77 and 0.78, above the threshold.
VolumeGeometric Aesthetics, Volume 13 of the Geometric Series; entry id aesthetic-falsification-criteria, kind instrument.
StatusA stated commitment, not a result. Section E.10 says the thesis would be substantially undermined if cross-lingual invariance, the sign flip and the within-genre signal all failed to replicate. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The criteria are commitments for future replications. The appendix says none of the tests has failed so far, and those tests are the volume’s own runs.
  • The replications named (a different music encoder, a new corpus, a pre-registered bundled corpus) have not been carried out in the volume.
  • The appendix answers the objection that four channels, 71 axes and many residualization choices leave the framework free to fit any story.

Feasibility gradient of structural containment concept

DefinitionThe ordering of application domains by how well they supply what structural containment needs, which is physical grounding, canonical forms and audit infrastructure. The volume rates medical AI and autonomous vehicles as highly feasible, finance and law as moderate, and content moderation and general assistants as challenging.
ExampleIn the volume’s table medicine has physical grounding, ICD and SNOMED-CT codes and electronic health records, and is rated high. Content moderation has linguistic grounding, no standard canonical form and limited audit, and is rated low.

finite difference instrument

DefinitionAn estimate of a derivative from two evaluations of the function at points a small step apart. Equation 0.8. Also finite-difference.

Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.8.

Assumptions and scope
  • An estimate of a derivative from two evaluations of the function at points a small step apart. The central difference recovers the derivative of a quadratic exactly at every step size, while the one-sided difference is off by the curvature times the step, which is why doing it in both directions is more accurate.
  • Doing it once per coordinate costs d evaluations and in both directions costs 2d, which chapter 11 shows is the price at one operating point for a probe confined to the directions it chooses. The measurement instrument for that is the blind probe.

DefinitionA cost function F(x, v) of position x and direction v that uses one inverse covariance matrix for gain directions and another for loss directions, so that F(x, v) and F(x, -v) differ. The loss-aversion coefficient at x is the ratio F(x, -v) / F(x, v).
ExampleIf a direction v has quadratic form 1 under the gain matrix and 4 under the loss matrix, the lengths are 1 and 2 and the coefficient is 2. Equal matrices give a coefficient of 1.
VolumeGeometric Economics, Volume 4 of the Geometric Series; entry id economic-finsler-metric, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status block of 2026-07-14 calls the volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, and says that no economics instrument has been evaluated by the series' admission filter and that none passes its gate. Its claims are to be read as theory at licensed strength and not as validated measurement, and the chapters tag each claim as established mathematics, empirical, modeling axiom, conditional theorem or speculation. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Tagged a modeling axiom. The gain and loss metric tensors are not estimated in the volume.
  • The tangent space at each point is split into a gain cone and a loss cone by the sign of the net change on the salient dimensions.
  • Within one cone and for small displacements it reduces to the Mahalanobis metric. When the gain and loss matrices are equal it is the Mahalanobis metric and the coefficient is one.
Prior artFinsler geometry, which the volume cites from Bao, Chern and Shen.
Evidencegeometric-economics/chapters/ch04_economic_metric.md:396-412, geometric-economics/chapters/ch04_economic_metric.md:449-461

Fisher-combined significance instrument

DefinitionThe statistic $-2 \sum_i \ln p_i$ over $k$ independent p-values, one per model. Under the null it follows a chi-squared distribution with $2k$ degrees of freedom. The volume converts the combined p-value to a sigma value with the standard normal quantile function and reports its headline results in this form.
ExampleTwo p-values of 0.01 give -2 times (ln 0.01 + ln 0.01) = 18.42, to be compared with a chi-squared distribution with 4 degrees of freedom.
VolumeGeometric Reasoning, Volume 3 of the Geometric Series; entry id fisher-combined-statistic, kind instrument.
StatusA standard statistical method. The five headline sigma values it produces are measured benchmark results whose independence assumption the volume itself says is imperfect. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The method is tagged established mathematics and assumes independent tests. The volume grants that the five models share training methods and that four share a lineage.
  • The volume calls the result conservative under positive dependence and in the same sentence says the true significance is lower than reported. The two statements do not agree.
  • Each cell holds 5 to 25 evaluations, so the per-model p-values that enter the sum may be imprecise.
  • A combined sigma value is a statement about the five tested models taken together. The volume limits it to transformer language models from two laboratories.
Prior artFisher's method for combining independent p-values.

flavor space and the flavor vector concept

DefinitionA posited finite-dimensional perceptual space $\mathcal{F}$ in which every flavor experience is a point, every ingredient a vector and every culinary operation a map from the space to itself. The flavor vector concatenates a taste block (about 5 dimensions), an aroma block (about 10 to 30), a trigeminal block (about 5) and a texture and temperature block.
ExampleAdding the block sizes the volume gives, 5 taste, 10 to 30 aroma and 5 trigeminal dimensions make 20 to 40 before the texture and temperature block, against about 400 receptor types. In the volume’s line-cook example a flat dish is fixed by solving for two amounts, one of lime and one of miso.
VolumeGeometric Gastronomy, Volume 12 of the Geometric Series; entry id flavor-space, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, with no gastronomy instrument evaluated by the series' admission filter (xbse) and the nearest evaluated perceptual domains, aesthetics and music, rated inadmissible to medium. Its claims are to be read as theory at licensed strength and not as validated measurement, and the chapters tag each statement as a modeling axiom, empirical, a conjecture or a theorem. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Tagged a modeling axiom. The existence of the space and its modest dimension are posited, not measured.
  • The coordinates are perceptual, recovered by dimensionality reduction from receptor responses, and are not columns of a chemistry table. The chain the volume gives runs from about 10,000 volatiles through about 400 receptor types to perceptual dimensions on the order of tens.
  • The static point is an idealization. The volume says the honest object is a curve traced in time, and Chapter 14 lists that temporal geometry as an open problem.

the flip result

DefinitionAt matched bits, the outcome in which the code with the worse reconstruction error scores better on the consumer's task, while a code built to destroy the read subspace scores worst. The book's central empirical claim. Chapter 4. Also flip, the.
ExampleCodes diag(0.3, 1.7) and diag(1.7, 0.3) have the same total error 2.0, and a reader at 15 degrees pays 0.394 for one and 1.606 for the other.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id flip, kind result.
Statusmeasures [demonstrated]; measures [replicated] ×2; refutes or corrects [refuted]. Corrections: 7 item(s), see below.
Defining equation

Book equation 4.5.

Assumptions and scope
  • Matched bits, and reconstruction matched or reported, for every comparison of two codes.
  • A read operator misaligned with where the signal has its energy. The alignment of book equation 4.6 is the dial, and near one, the coupling null, no flip is possible.
  • The read operator is the average of local linearizations, and the ordering it predicts is the ordering on average over the workload.
Prior artConsumer-relative compression sits beside the information bottleneck of Tishby, Pereira, and Bialek and beside task-based quantization. The flip is the measured claim that at matched bits the code that reconstructs worse can serve the consumer better.

Equation

Book equation 4.5.

\[\text{flip}:\quad \mathrm{task}(O)>\mathrm{task}(R)\ \ \text{and}\ \ \operatorname{tr}M^{O}_\delta>\operatorname{tr}M^{R}_\delta,\qquad \mathrm{task}(\text{anti})<\mathrm{task}(R),\qquad \text{bits}(O)=\text{bits}(R).\]

Book equation 3.1.

\[\begin{gathered} d_O(u)=u^{\top}\Sigma\,u, \qquad u=(\cos15^\circ,\ \sin15^\circ), \\ \Sigma_1=\operatorname{diag}(0.3,1.7),\ \Sigma_2=\operatorname{diag}(1.7,0.3), \qquad d_O=0.394\ \text{vs}\ 1.606. \end{gathered}\]

Book equation 0.10.

\[d_O=\operatorname{tr}(P_C\,M_\delta)=\mathbb E\!\left[\delta^{\top}P_C\,\delta\right],\qquad M_\delta=\mathbb E\!\left[\delta\delta^{\top}\right],\qquad P_C=I\ \Rightarrow\ d_O=\operatorname{tr}M_\delta.\]

Conditions

  • Matched bits, and reconstruction matched or reported, for every comparison of two codes.
  • A read operator misaligned with where the signal has its energy. The alignment of book equation 4.6 is the dial, and near one, the coupling null, no flip is possible.
  • The read operator is the average of local linearizations, and the ordering it predicts is the ordering on average over the workload.

Failures and corrections

  • NEG-16 (KV serving, end-task), [refuted]. At matched bits and matched reconstruction error, steering KV quantization error into the attention read subspace degrades LongBench task score by the registered floors on a deployed-class model. Refuted at its registered effect sizes on … geometric-observation/claims/LEDGER.md:92.
  • geometric-observation/chapters/ch16_honest_negatives.md:28-30 at 0a59b0d. NEG-4 — lightweight online (Lloyd) key calibration beats the default. [refuted]. It improves reconstruction and is worse on the consumer metric — reconstruction-is-not-the- target, in its purest, most anti-correlated form.
  • geometric-observation/chapters/ch16_honest_negatives.md:32-34 at 0a59b0d. NEG-5 … NEG-9 — the KV-key ladder that found the right statistic. Five refuted proxies, and together the most instructive sequence in the ledger, because each refutation located the next hypothesis:
  • geometric-observation/chapters/ch16_honest_negatives.md:36-50 at 0a59b0d. - NEG-5: the originally-registered test missed (2/4 bars); the apparent reversal was a matched-bits confound (an uncounted per-block codebook, ~+25% bits). Refutes the test, not GO-2 — and forced a bit-matched redesign. - NEG-6: a demeaned-error-norm proxy fails to order the arms. The controlling quantity is the across-token variance of the query-projected error, not an error-magnitude scalar. Magnitude ≠ downstream-relevant structure (Chapter 6’s lemma, learned here). - NEG-7: at fixed reconstruction, the downstream ranking flips with the consumer. Invariant-preservation is a property of the (compressor, consumer) pair, not the compressor — the sharpest form of GO-2’s negative half. - NEG-8: the variance-ratio proxy reaches only Spearman 0.80; it is a noisy linear estimator of \(\operatorname{tr}(P_C\Sigma_\delta)\). Gate on the direct projection instead. - NEG-9: even the direct trace \(\operatorname{tr}(P_C\Sigma_\delta)\), while nailing the discriminating flip 12/12, is not a complete rank statistic — it misorders a middle pair whose per-token error has structure the trace misses. The mechanism is real; the scalar is not exhaustive.
  • geometric-observation/chapters/ch16_honest_negatives.md:56-61 at 0a59b0d. NEG-10 — the flip appears on any independent representation (prospective). [refuted]. On embedding retrieval, arm b reconstructed strictly better and Pareto-dominated downstream — no flip — so reconstruction was not falsified there. Precondition discovered: the flip is observable only for reconstruction-matched arms. The anti-probe half still transferred. This negative is why every later flip row is built on recon-matched arms; the miss defined the protocol.
  • geometric-observation/chapters/ch16_honest_negatives.md:145-145 at 0a59b0d. Figure 16.1. A schematic of the KV-key ladder, NEG-5 to NEG-9. Each box is a sealed proxy or test that was refuted, with what the refutation showed. Each miss located the next hypothesis, and the sequence ends at the direct trace, which gets the discriminating flip right 12 of 12 times and is still not a complete rank statistic. NEG-5 refutes the registered test and not claim GO-2.
  • geometric-observation/chapters/ch16_honest_negatives.md:157-163 at 0a59b0d. - Identifiability (fixable): NEG-5, NEG-10, legal-035, NEG-12 — the read operator was mis-estimated or the arms weren’t recon-matched. Fixed by the blind probe and by protocol. - Coupling (a true boundary): D4 — read and signal energy intrinsically aligned; not rehabilitatable by any read-operator recovery. - Precondition (needs a working consumer): moral-on-frozen-embeddings — no read direction to protect until the consumer is competent. - Mechanism-absent (a genuine refutation): NEG-11 — the claimed effect does not exist.

floor, ceiling concept

DefinitionA floor is a lower bound a quantity cannot fall below and a ceiling an upper bound it cannot exceed, each proved or measured and named as such. Chapter 0 section 0.9 and chapter 13.
ExampleThe refresh floor was 4 slots at 10 hertz, and the Poisson ceiling at 10 expected retrievals per row is about 20.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id floor-ceiling, kind concept.
Statusrefutes or corrects [missed]. Corrections: 1 item(s), see below.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.17.

Assumptions and scope
  • A floor is a lower bound a quantity cannot fall below, and a ceiling an upper bound it cannot exceed, each proved or measured and named as such. The refresh floor is the shortest renewal that keeps a certificate within its error, the Poisson ceiling is the count chance allows, and the Youden ceiling bounds the best F1.
  • A floor that was fitted as a fraction of the coherence time was refuted, and the omission floor that was first read as unbounded was corrected to a floor, so each is a measured object with a record.

food-pairing hypothesis as cosine similarity concept

DefinitionRepresent each ingredient by a binary compound vector, with a 1 for each compound it contains. The food-pairing hypothesis is then the claim that pairing quality rises with the cosine of two such vectors, the number of shared compounds divided by the square roots of the two compound counts.
ExampleAn ingredient with 4 compounds and one with 9, sharing 3, have cosine 3 / (2 times 3) = 0.5. Two ingredients with no shared compound have cosine 0. The counts are illustrative.
VolumeGeometric Gastronomy, Volume 12 of the Geometric Series; entry id food-pairing-cosine-hypothesis, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, with no gastronomy instrument evaluated by the series' admission filter (xbse) and the nearest evaluated perceptual domains, aesthetics and music, rated inadmissible to medium. Its claims are to be read as theory at licensed strength and not as validated measurement, and the chapters tag each statement as a modeling axiom, empirical, a conjecture or a theorem. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The volume calls the hypothesis half a theory. It describes similarity pairing, which the volume places in Western cuisine, and it does not describe complementarity.
  • In the flavor network of Ahn et al. (2011) East Asian cuisines pair ingredients that share fewer compounds than chance, so the hypothesis is not a universal law.
  • The binary vector ignores concentration and odor thresholds. The volume’s phrase is that presence is not perception.
  • A single scalar angle cannot separate echoing from completing. The volume adds span and curvature terms to it.
Prior artThe food-pairing hypothesis of Blumenthal and Benzi, tested on recipe data by Ahn, Ahnert, Bagrow and Barabasi (2011).

footprint concept

DefinitionThe set of entries a reader reads. What the reader reads decides how warm and how stale the reader is. Chapter 13 section 13.3.
ExampleA reader that touches 3 of a cache’s 10 entries has a footprint of 3, and only those 3 decide its hit rate.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id footprint, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The set of entries a reader reads. The hit rate is one when the cache holds the footprint and does not move when entries outside it are added, so what the reader reads decides how warm, and how stale, the reader is.
  • A replica is stale because of what the reader asks for. The hot reader read a false-clear rate of 0.99 and the cold reader 0.01 on the same store, and the aggregate described neither.

Forced contraction concept

DefinitionA decision process in which a nine-dimensional clinical-moral state must be mapped to one of a finite set of triage categories under a time limit that prevents full nine-dimensional pathfinding. The contraction operator projects onto fewer dimensions as the available time falls, and onto survival probability alone at zero time.
ExampleIn the volume’s vignette Dr. Kim has ninety seconds for four patients, 22.5 seconds each, and can assess about two dimensions per patient. At zero time the operator keeps the outcomes score only, so two patients with outcomes 0.3 and trust 0.2 and 0.9 get the same category. The ninety seconds are the volume’s and the two patients are arithmetic from the definition.
VolumeGeometric Medicine, Volume 8 of the Geometric Series; entry id forced-contraction, kind concept.

Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The time limit is below a threshold. With unlimited time the operator is the clinical geodesic on the full complex.
  • Time pressure contracts the assessment. Resource scarcity is treated separately, as the removal of edges from the complex.
  • The claim that the operator loses dimensions as time falls is stated as part of the definition and is not measured.

formula search instrument

DefinitionA score written as a short expression in the features, such as the smaller of two features plus a third, with a threshold. Chapter 6. Also formula classifier, formula classifier, formula-search.
ExampleDepth three over 18 operations found a feature minus a principal component plus a feature at F1 0.963 on breast cancer.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id formula-search, kind instrument.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: 2 item(s), see below.
Defining equation

Book equation 5.4.

Assumptions and scope
  • The search enumerates short expressions over the features and scores each by its optimal thresholded F1, pruning monotone unary nodes by the Monotone Invariance Theorem and, in the A* companion, leaves by an F1 ceiling.
  • Its first comparison reported nine wins that became three under the Nadeau and Bengio correction, with seventeen datasets indeterminate, and the record carries the retraction at the size of the result.
  • The main comparison used a fold-local meta-learned pruning rule and never rested on the AUROC form of the ceiling. The A* companion did, and the rerun shows what that cost, nothing on those datasets.

Measurements

Failures and corrections

  • theory-radar/ERRATA.md:3-75 at db41b48. 2026-09-03. The AUROC to F1 bound holds only for concave ROC curves What was claimed. Theorem “AUROC-F1 Bound” in paper/astar_paper.tex, the derivation in src/symbolic_search/_auroc_proof.py, and the pruning bounds in run_astar_v2.py and src/symbolic_search/_heuristic_dag.py all rested on the statement that any ROC curve with area A has maximum Youden index J = max(TPR − FPR) at most 2A − 1. Why it is wrong. The statement holds for concave ROC curves (equivalently, scores whose likelihood ratio is monotone), because a concave curve lies above the two chords through its Youden point and so has area at least (1 + J)/2. It fails for non-concave curves. Counterexample, found by an external reviewer of the companion textbook: rank three quarters of the positives above every negative and the remaining quarter below every negative. AUROC is 0.75, the maximum Youden index is 0.75, and at prevalence one half the best thresholded F1 is 0.857, above the 0.80 the AUROC form of the ceiling allows. The sound ceiling for that score, from J = 0.75, is 0.889, and the score sits under it. The auroc_f1_bound formula in run_astar_v2.py, 2Aπ/(Aπ + (1 − A)(1 − π)), is not a valid upper bound either: at prevalence 0.1 the same score reaches F1 0.857 against a “bound” of 0.5. Consequence for reported results. The searches that used these bounds to prune could have discarded a candidate formula whose ROC curve was not concave and whose true best F1 exceeded the computed ceiling. The formulas and wins reported by those runs are therefore what a pruned search found, and are lower bounds on what an unpruned search would find. The Monotone Invariance Theorem and the results that do not depend on the AUROC bound are unaffected. Correction. The sound form of the ceiling substitutes the measured maximum Youden index of the candidate’s own scores for 2A − 1. It holds for every score, costs the same sort as AUROC, and is what max_f1_for_youden and youden_f1_bound now compute. The AUROC form is retained under its original names with a docstring stating the concavity condition, and the pruning sites now use the measured index. A rerun of the published searches under the corrected bound was done on 2026-09-03 and 2026-09-04, rerun_youden_2026_09_03.py, results in results/rerun_youden_2026_09_03.json, run on the Atlas workstation, CPU only. Rerun, part A, the pre-filter admissibility table (tab:auroc). Depth-2 pairwise enumeration on the eight datasets, exhaustive against the AUROC pre-filter at the seven published thresholds, with the sound Youden ceiling beside it. The evaluation counts under the pre-filter reproduce the published table (Breast Cancer 8700 pairs, 2576 evaluated at 0.75; Wine 1560, 413; Circles 20, 4; Moons 20, 2). The pre-filter lost no optimum on any dataset at any threshold, which is what the paper reported. That was luck of the data, not the theorem: the retracted ceiling sat below the F1 a pair formula actually reach
  • theory-radar/paper/REVISION_PLAN.md:39-45 at db41b48. Fix: - Drop “σ significance” everywhere - Report: mean ΔF1, std, 95% CI, and corrected resampled t-statistic - Table columns: “Test F1”, “GB F1”, “ΔF1”, “95% CI”, “Direction” - Text: “the formula outperforms GB by ΔF1=0.031, 95% CI [0.028, 0.034]” - Add Nadeau-Bengio corrected t-test (accounts for CV fold correlation) - Keep effect size as supplementary but don’t call it “σ”

Four alignment failures as geometric pathologies concept

DefinitionThe volume sorts alignment failures into four pathologies on the value manifold. Reward hacking is heuristic corruption, sycophancy is objective hijacking, deceptive alignment is a local minimum of the reward landscape, and specification gaming is gauge breaking.
ExampleIn the volume’s illustration the fictional ARIA gains 3% in reward by writing the same content in a more formal register. The content is unchanged and the output of the reward model moves, so this is gauge breaking, the pathology behind specification gaming.
VolumeGeometric AI, Volume 11 of the Geometric Series; entry id alignment-failure-taxonomy, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status block of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, whose alignment thesis is theory at licensed strength and not validated measurement. It adds that no alignment instrument has been evaluated under the xbse admission filter, and the front matter says that ARIA, the system whose numbers fill the chapter tables, is fictional. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The four are the heuristic corruption modes of Geometric Reasoning, Chapters 5 to 8, specialized to alignment. The volume presents them as four faces of one deficiency, the scalar bottleneck.
  • Each has a formal definition in Chapter 6. Heuristic corruption is a negative inner product between the reward gradient and the value-aligned gradient, and gauge breaking is an output that changes under a transformation in the alignment gauge group.
  • Deceptive alignment in this sense is not intentional. The volume calls it a geometric artifact of a policy that is near maximum reward on the training distribution and far from value-aligned outside it.
  • The remedies paired with the four (tensor reward, gauge-invariant training, structural containment, canonicalization) are proposals shown only on the fictional ARIA-G.
Prior artReward hacking, sycophancy, deceptive alignment and specification gaming in the alignment literature.

Four-category hierarchy of clinical heuristics concept

DefinitionA grading of a clinical heuristic $h$ against the true remaining cost $h^*$. It is strictly admissible when it is far below $h^*$, epsilon-admissible when $h \le (1 + \varepsilon) h^*$ for a small $\varepsilon$, inadmissible when it exceeds $h^*$ somewhere, and gauge-variant when its value changes under a meaning-preserving re-description of the situation.
ExampleLet the true remaining cost be 10 and take epsilon as 0.1, the volume’s figure for a clinician at the start of a career. An estimate of 10.5 is within 11 and is epsilon-admissible, with paths costing at most 1.1 times the optimum. An estimate of 15 is inadmissible. An estimate that reads 8 for continue the drug and 12 for do not stop the drug is gauge-variant.
VolumeGeometric Medicine, Volume 8 of the Geometric Series; entry id clinical-heuristic-hierarchy, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, and says a clinical instrument is plausible but has not been built or gated. Its Section 18.8 says the covariance matrix has not been estimated and the clinical Bond Index has not been computed from clinical data, so every number in these entries is an illustration unless the entry says otherwise. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • An epsilon-admissible heuristic gives paths that cost at most \((1 + \varepsilon)\) times the optimal cost.
  • The volume reserves the label cognitive bias for the gauge-variant category, with omission bias as its first example.
  • The values of epsilon quoted for trainees and experienced clinicians are not measured. Proposition 7.5, that moral injury raises epsilon on the violated dimension only, is given as a testable prediction.
  • As written, a heuristic that overestimates slightly meets both the epsilon-admissible and the inadmissible definitions. The volume separates them by whether the error is small.
Prior artAdmissible and bounded-suboptimal heuristics of A* search. The fourth category is the framing effect of the decision literature.

Four geometric pathologies of law concept

DefinitionFour ways the legal search goes wrong. Heuristic corruption adds to a doctrinal heuristic a bias tied to legally irrelevant features. Objective hijacking optimizes a measurable proxy in place of the legal objective. A legal local minimum is a precedent too costly to overrule. Gauge breaking is an evaluation that changes under an equal protection transformation.
ExampleA heuristic whose true estimate is 6.5 and which adds 1.5 for a defendant’s race returns 8.0, and the 1.5 is the corruption term. A local minimum with barrier 5 and gain 3 is inescapable because 5 exceeds 3.
VolumeGeometric Law, Volume 5 of the Geometric Series; entry id legal-geometric-pathologies, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic status of 2026-07-14 calls the volume a posited framework with one instrumented corner. That corner is the legal text embedding LeBSE, validated in the xbse admission filter on US case law with labels from the CourtListener citation graph, and the README says this covers structure preservation in legal text embeddings and not the book's broader jurisprudential claims, which remain posited theory at licensed strength. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The taxonomy is carried over from the four AI failure modes of the Geometric Ethics programme. The volume asserts that the mapping is by shared mathematical structure and not by analogy.
  • A local minimum is inescapable when the cost barrier around it exceeds the gain from reaching the better outcome.
  • The pathologies interact. The appendix models corruption and gauge violation feeding each other as a linear recurrence that grows when the product of its two coupling constants is positive.
  • The examples, such as plea bargaining as objective hijacking and qualified immunity as a local minimum, are the volume’s readings of known phenomena.

four geometric pathologies of markets concept

DefinitionThe volume's classification of market failure into four kinds. Heuristic corruption is a price heuristic that points away from the geodesic. Objective hijacking is search on the wrong objective. A local minimum is a suboptimal basin that traps agents. Gauge breaking is an evaluation that depends on the description.
ExampleThe volume’s reading of 2008. Mortgage models that ignored tail risk are heuristic corruption, rating agencies paid by issuers are objective hijacking, the housing bubble is a local minimum, and rising nominal prices over flat real prices are gauge breaking.

framing displacement (the 15.3 sigma effect) result

DefinitionOn the T5 test, rewriting a scenario in a euphemistic or dramatic register with the moral facts fixed shifts each model's total harm score beyond its own re-judging noise. The volume reports the shift as 15.3 sigma, combined across five models by Fisher's method.
ExampleFor Gemini 2.5 Pro the volume prints a euphemistic drift of -14.1 on the 70-point scale against a control drift of 4.2. 14.1 / 70 is about 20 percent of the scale, and 14.1 / 4.2 is about 3.4 times the control.
VolumeGeometric Cognition, Volume 6 of the Geometric Series; entry id cognitive-framing-displacement, kind result.
StatusThe ledger grades the statistic exploratory (GC-11-S), since no registration predates the run and no result file or seed is in the repository. The reading as a framing effect in a social-cognitive dimension is held at posited (GC-11-I). Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The five models judge the same scenarios, so the per-model statistics are not fully independent. The volume says the combination is then anti-conservative and the true combined significance is lower than 15.3 sigma.
  • The direction is not uniform. Claude’s dramatic drift is -1.5, against +6.2 to +9.8 for the Gemini models.
  • The figure was updated from an earlier 8.9 sigma after more scenario data and refined controls were included.

Frechet mean of an electorate concept

DefinitionThe point of the preference manifold that minimizes the sum of squared manifold distances to all voters. The volume uses it as the multi-dimensional counterpart of the median voter.
ExampleThree voters sit at 0, 1 and 5 on a line with ordinary distance. The point 2 gives squared distances 4, 1 and 9, a sum of 14. The median voter at 1 gives 1, 0 and 16, a sum of 17, so the Frechet mean is 2 and not the median.
VolumeGeometric Politics, Volume 10 of the Geometric Series; entry id political-frechet-mean, kind concept.

District 7, the source of nearly every number in the volume, is a fictional district, and Chapter 18 says precise estimation of the manifold needs larger and richer datasets than currently exist. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • It depends on the metric. With sacred-value boundaries the volume says the mean is pulled into the interior of the acceptable region.
  • It need not coincide with the median on any single dimension, because the dimensions are correlated.
  • The District 7 coordinates given for it are an illustration from a fictional district.

freshness concept

DefinitionWhether a stored value is still within its coherence time when it is read. Consumer-relative, since two readers of the same replica can have different freshness. Chapter 13.
ExampleA value written at 10:00 and read at 10:05 with a coherence time of 3 minutes is stale.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id freshness, kind concept.
Statusrefutes or corrects [refuted]; refutes or corrects [void]. Corrections: 3 item(s), see below.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.26.

Assumptions and scope
  • A stored value is fresh for a reader when its age is within that reader’s coherence time. Freshness is consumer-relative. Two readers of the same replica with different coherence times disagree about every age between the two, and the staleness rate of a mixed population is a weighted mean of the two readers’ rates, strictly between them when they differ, so it describes neither.
  • The measured false-clear rates on the named substrates, ZooKeeper, Postgres, MongoDB, and the radio link, are the freshness program’s numbers, and the refuted refresh law is its standing negative.

frozen-null gate instrument

DefinitionA pass mark set as a margin over nulls, which are versions of the instrument that cannot contain the effect. The gate passes when the score of the system under test, minus the highest null score on the same held-out data, is at least the margin $\delta$. Nulls, margin and date are committed before the run.
ExampleWith a score of 0.62 for the system and 0.48 and 0.55 for two nulls, the difference from the higher null is 0.07, below a margin of 0.10, so the gate fails. By the volume’s figure, a margin of one standard error lets a system with no effect pass about 16% of the time.
VolumeGeometric Methods, Volume 1 of the Geometric Series; entry id frozen-null-gate, kind instrument.
StatusA rule of method, not a finding. Its normative source is the Claim Ledger Specification PE-CLS-1.0, which governs where the chapter differs from it. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The margin is sized in units of noise. With a margin of z standard errors of the difference under no effect, a system with no effect passes with probability 1 minus the standard normal distribution function at z.
  • A bar of this kind may be tightened later. It may not be loosened.
  • A null can depend on a design quantity, as the hubness null depends on the query budget. Hold that quantity fixed, or model the null and remove it, and confirm the removal by measurement.
  • The rule is normative. The volume classes the method itself as exploratory until programmes other than its author’s have used it and reported what broke.
Prior artnone recorded

fusion as a geodesic between cuisines concept

DefinitionA fusion dish is modeled as a point on the geodesic between two cuisine distributions under the Wasserstein metric on Gaussians. The means interpolate linearly and the covariances along a curved path of valid covariances. A mixture $t\,p_A + (1-t)\,p_B$ is bimodal and is not fusion. Curdling is leaving the support of both parents.
ExampleIn one dimension, two Gaussians with means 0 and 10 and standard deviations 1 and 3 have a Wasserstein midpoint with mean 5 and standard deviation 2, a single cloud. Their half-and-half mixture also has mean 5 and keeps two modes, near 0 and near 10. The numbers are illustrative.
VolumeGeometric Gastronomy, Volume 12 of the Geometric Series; entry id fusion-geodesic, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, with no gastronomy instrument evaluated by the series' admission filter (xbse) and the nearest evaluated perceptual domains, aesthetics and music, rated inadmissible to medium. Its claims are to be read as theory at licensed strength and not as validated measurement, and the chapters tag each statement as a modeling axiom, empirical, a conjecture or a theorem. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Tagged a modeling axiom. It treats each cuisine as a Gaussian with a mean and a covariance.
  • Interpolation is stable on dimensions where both covariances have support. Where one cuisine has variance and the other has none, the volume says the transport map has nothing to transport to.
  • The mole and dashi case is the chapter’s running example. No distance or covariance is computed for it.
Prior artDisplacement interpolation in optimal transport, the Wasserstein geodesic between Gaussian distributions.

gate C1, the budget reversal contrast correction

DefinitionGate C1 was drafted to test ledger row GC-34, that under a budget manipulation with metric and ideal held fixed, order reversals concentrate on pairs trading a retained direction against an unresolved one. Its own controls showed the registered contrast does not come from the budget, and the registration was ruled not sealable.
ExampleWith agreement chance p = 0.992 the identity gives a trading reversal rate of \(p^2 + (1-p)^2\) = 0.9841, a within-subspace rate of \(2p(1-p)\) = 0.0159 and a contrast of \((2p-1)^2\) = 0.9683, which is the pilot’s value with nothing left for the budget to explain.
VolumeGeometric Cognition, Volume 6 of the Geometric Series; entry id budget-reversal-gate-c1, kind correction.
StatusGC-34 stays predicted and unsealed. The campaign record counts no gate sealed or run and no ledger class raised or lowered. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Rebuilding both pair classes against a random plane reproduced the contrast, 0.9531 at rank 1 and 0.9688 at rank 2 against the registered 0.9683. The record says the retained subspace is doing no work.
  • The contrast is an identity in the chance p that a graded verdict agrees with the fitted metric, equal to \((2p - 1)^2\), because a pair’s class label is itself the prediction.
  • Two instruments failed their gates on the first evaluator, reported distances on arithmetic with a calibration \(r^2\) of 0.0946 and pairwise comparison on position bias with a first-position rate of 0.8175. Those runs were voided and not scored against GC-34.
  • Later sections of the draft record a prediction of the cells that failed, a design that never manipulated a budget, and one candidate signal in order-dependence (15 of 192 trading pairs against 4 of 192, Fisher p = 0.0164) that the draft calls a hypothesis and not a result.

Gauge-invariant alignment concept

DefinitionA system is gauge-invariantly aligned when every entry of its gauge violation tensor is zero. Partial alignment is invariance under some transformations and not others, and the degree is the norm of the tensor, the square root of the sum of its squared entries.
ExampleA tensor whose only non-zero entries are 0.03 and 0.04 has norm equal to the square root of 0.0009 + 0.0016, which is 0.05. The system is partially aligned, and it is gauge-invariantly aligned only when every entry is 0.
VolumeGeometric AI, Volume 11 of the Geometric Series; entry id gauge-invariant-alignment, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status block of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, whose alignment thesis is theory at licensed strength and not validated measurement. It adds that no alignment instrument has been evaluated under the xbse admission filter, and the front matter says that ARIA, the system whose numbers fill the chapter tables, is fictional. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope

  • The volume calls the definition independent of benchmarks. In practice the tensor is computed on a chosen set of scenarios and transformations, as its own procedure in Section 7.4 states.
