Gauge transformation of a problem description concept

DefinitionA map $\tau$ on problem descriptions that changes the surface presentation and keeps the task-relevant content. With $\pi$ the projection from descriptions to content, $\tau$ is a gauge transformation exactly when $\pi(\tau(x)) = \pi(x)$ for every description $x$. Such maps form a group under composition.
ExampleSwapping the genders of the actors in a scenario changes the description and not who did what to whom, so it is a gauge transformation, while changing what was done is not.
VolumeGeometric Reasoning, Volume 3 of the Geometric Series; entry id reasoning-gauge-transformation, kind concept.
StatusPosited framework. The README's epistemic-status block of 2026-07-14 calls the volume speculative theory awaiting instruments, to be read as theory at licensed strength and not as validated measurement. Its chapters tag each claim as established mathematics, empirical, modeling axiom, conditional theorem or speculation, and the empirical tags rest on one benchmark of five language models. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • It presupposes a content projection, a decision about which features of a description are task-relevant. The volume does not construct this projection for its benchmark and relies on rewrites judged to preserve content.
  • The group claim needs every transformation to have a content-preserving inverse, which the definition asserts.
  • The standard applied to gauge transformations is invariance, an identical output, and not robustness, a nearby one.
Prior artGauge transformations of physics, used by analogy. The same structure is a group action whose orbits are the classes of equivalent descriptions.

gauge-variant pedagogical heuristic concept

DefinitionA teacher's estimate of a student's distance to the goal that depends on features of the student that are not coordinates on the learner manifold, such as race, gender, accent, first language or family background. Two students at the same learner state then receive different estimates.
ExampleTwo students are at the same learner state, at true distance 5 from the goal. A teacher who estimates 4 for one and 7 for the other because of their accents has a gauge-variant heuristic, since the state is the same and the estimates differ by 3.
VolumeGeometric Education, Volume 9 of the Geometric Series; entry id gauge-variant-pedagogical-heuristic, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments. No education-domain instrument has been evaluated by the series' admission filter, and Chapter 18 states that the six predictions of Section 16.3 have not been tested and that no method for estimating the learner metric has been validated at scale. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • It need not be conscious bias. The volume says it can arise when a teacher applies a correct statistical observation about a group to a new student without checking that student’s state.
  • The volume states that the damage is directional, underestimating students from disadvantaged backgrounds and overestimating students from advantaged ones. This is asserted and not measured in the volume.
  • It is the fourth of the four heuristic failure modes of Section 6.5, which the volume takes from Geometric Reasoning.

Gauge violation tensor instrument

DefinitionA matrix whose entry for transformation $i$ and outcome $j$ is the mean over cases of the absolute change in outcome $j$ when protected characteristic $i$ is swapped, divided by the original outcome. Rows are characteristics such as race or gender, columns are outcomes such as sentence length or bail, and the mean of all entries is the Legal Bond Index.
ExampleIn the volume’s hypothetical district the race row is 0.187, 0.213, 0.038, 0.082 and 0.104, which sums to 0.624. The five row sums 0.624, 0.479, 0.637, 0.156 and 0.444 add to 2.340, where the chapter prints 2.520, and 2.340 / 25 is about 0.094.
VolumeGeometric Law, Volume 5 of the Geometric Series; entry id gauge-violation-tensor, kind instrument.
StatusThe README's epistemic status of 2026-07-14 calls the volume a posited framework with one instrumented corner. That corner is the legal text embedding LeBSE, validated in the xbse admission filter on US case law with labels from the CourtListener citation graph, and the README says this covers structure preservation in legal text embeddings and not the book's broader jurisprudential claims, which remain posited theory at licensed strength. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • A swap cannot be applied to a real defendant. The volume estimates entries from matched pairs of cases alike in drug type, quantity, criminal history, role, district and year.
  • The appendix floors the denominator at a small positive constant to avoid division by zero.
  • The intersectional term is the violation under two simultaneous swaps minus the two separate violations. A positive value is superadditive and a negative value subadditive.
  • The tensor printed in the volume is for a hypothetical district. No tensor computed from real sentencing data is reported.
Prior artnone recorded

Genre confound correction (books) correction

DefinitionThe books discovery result, R = 0.241 between cloud geometry and Goodreads rating on 4,998 books, was mostly genre. After residualizing rating against Library of Congress top-level genre the result is R = 0.093 (R squared 0.009, 6.5 sigma), and the volume reports that figure as the result.
ExampleR squared falls from 0.241 squared, about 0.058, to 0.093 squared, about 0.009. The share removed is 1 minus 0.009 divided by 0.058, about 0.85, the volume’s 85 percent.
VolumeGeometric Aesthetics, Volume 13 of the Geometric Series; entry id aesthetic-genre-confound-correction, kind correction.
StatusVerified empirically in Appendix F (F17.1 to F17.5), with the nulls listed as nulls. The README calls the structural-channels finding the volume's one validated result and says it was pre-registered. The book chapters do not describe the registration. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • 85 percent of the discovery R squared was genre confound. The volume’s summary is that geometry carries additional signal beyond genre, not that geometry predicts rating.
  • Within Fiction (n = 2,250) the signal reproduces at R = 0.131 (6.2 sigma). Within Non-fiction and History/Biography the result is null.
  • The corpus is English-language Project Gutenberg books paired with average Goodreads rating, with author-disjoint 5-fold cross-validation and LaBSE embeddings.
  • Section 17.8 says the effect is too small to predict the reception of an individual work and that no causal claim is made.

Geodesic deviation of a reasoning trajectory concept

DefinitionThe cost of a reasoning trajectory minus the cost of the geodesic that joins the same endpoints. The optimal trajectory is the path from the problem state to the goal region that minimizes the cost functional. The deviation is never negative and is zero only for a geodesic.
ExampleIn the volume’s illustrative triage example the geodesic costs about 2.1 nats and the corrupted trajectory about 4.6 nats, so the deviation is 4.6 - 2.1 = 2.5 nats.
VolumeGeometric Reasoning, Volume 3 of the Geometric Series; entry id reasoning-geodesic-deviation, kind concept.
StatusPosited framework. The README's epistemic-status block of 2026-07-14 calls the volume speculative theory awaiting instruments, to be read as theory at licensed strength and not as validated measurement. Its chapters tag each claim as established mathematics, empirical, modeling axiom, conditional theorem or speculation, and the empirical tags rest on one benchmark of five language models. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Tagged a modeling axiom. It needs a cost metric on the reasoning manifold, which the volume posits and does not measure.
  • It measures the efficiency of the path and not whether the answer is right. A lucky shortcut can be accurate and still have a large deviation.
  • The volume computes it only in illustrations. Its one empirical pointer is framework-switching efficiency, which it calls a proxy.
Prior artPath length excess over the shortest path. It is not the geodesic deviation equation of differential geometry, which describes how nearby geodesics separate.

\[R(i,j)=\sum_{k\ge2}\frac1{\lambda_k}\left(\frac{u_k(i)}{\sqrt{d_i}}-\frac{u_k(j)}{\sqrt{d_j}}\right)^{2}\ \longrightarrow\ \frac1{d_i}+\frac1{d_j}\quad(n\to\infty,\ \dim\ge3).\]

Book equation 3.3.

\[X_i=r_i\,\theta_i,\qquad r_i\ \to\ \frac1{\sqrt{d_i}},\qquad \theta_i=\frac{X_i}{\|X_i\|}\in S^{m-1}.\]

Conditions

  • The length of the shortest path along edges between two nodes. It is zero from a node to itself, symmetric, one between adjacent nodes, and on a connected graph obeys the triangle inequality.
  • The geodesic-rank reader reads only the ordering of these distances, so a strictly increasing transform of them leaves its nearest neighbour unchanged. That the angle of the spectral embedding carries the ordering and the radius carries degree is the measured claim of chapter 3, with the refuted commute-filter row beside it.

geodesic divergence of the assessment-optimal path result

DefinitionThe path that maximizes a scalar assessment G at each step differs from the learner geodesic to the goal. The divergence, the integral over the path parameter of the manifold distance between the two paths, is strictly positive whenever G is not proportional to the distance-to-goal function.
ExampleIn the volume’s illustration Ethan ends at (0.90, 0.55, 0.40, 0.50, 0.40, 0.30) with a 3.7 average and Alex at (0.70, 0.90, 0.80, 0.75, 0.85, 0.70) with 3.2. The coordinate sums are 3.05 and 4.70, so the higher score goes with the lower sum, as Corollary 5.3.2 says.
VolumeGeometric Education, Volume 9 of the Geometric Series; entry id assessment-geodesic-divergence, kind result.
StatusStated as a theorem. The text says the proof uses the calculus of variations and gives the argument in prose, with no displayed derivation. No trajectory data support it. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The two paths coincide only when the gradient of G is parallel to the gradient of the distance to the goal, that is when the assessment weights match the true educational costs up to a scalar multiple.
  • The theorem also states that the divergence grows without bound as the dimension increases. The text supports this with the remark that a scalar captures at most one direction in d.
  • Corollary 5.3.2 concludes that a student who maximizes G ends with a higher score and a lower sum across all dimensions than a student on the geodesic.
  • The four-year trajectories of Alex and Ethan that illustrate it are posited, with composite students.
Prior artnone recorded

geometric decision cost concept

DefinitionThe cost of an alternative in a decision task is the Mahalanobis distance between the encoding of the alternative and the encoding of the task's reference point under the inverse covariance. It is the pullback distance of the observer whose consumer is the scenario encoding, whose output metric is the inverse covariance, and whose inactive dimensions are directions in the kernel of that metric. The read operator of the program, written for a displacement from a reference point instead of for a code's error. Also decision cost.
ExampleIn the ultimatum encoding an offer of 48 percent has social, identity, and epistemic displacements 0.373, 0.278, and 0.003 from the reference, so its cost is the square root of 0.373 squared over 78.26 plus 0.278 squared over 32.28 plus 0.003 squared over 0.01262, about 0.071, and no offer on the integer grid costs less.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id geometric-decision-cost, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: 1 item(s), see below.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • For a discrete menu no Jacobian is needed and the cost is the exact pullback of the quadratic form through the encoding. On a continuous scenario manifold the local metric is the encoding’s Jacobian transposed, times the inverse covariance, times the Jacobian, which is the read operator of read-operator with the inverse covariance as output metric, geometric-observation/paper/observer-representation.tex:303-330.
  • The consumer is the hand-coded encoding of each task as a reference point and a menu of alternatives in nine dimensions, erisml-lib/docs/papers/foundations/submission/ieee-tcss/final_manuscript.tex:339-376, and the three active dimensions are a sparsity pattern of the metric chosen by a search, not a demonstrated budget of the reader.
  • The three active variances are 78.26, 32.28, and 0.01262 on social impact, virtue and identity, and epistemic status. They were fitted on nine game targets by a search over every active set of size at most five, with a 20-point log grid from 0.01 to 100 for one and two dimensions and 5,000 seeded log-uniform draws on the same range for three or more, eris-econ/src/eris_econ/structural_fuzz.py:94-186. Candidate active sets were then ranked on all sixteen targets, eris-econ/src/eris_econ/structural_fuzz.py:693-740, so no lottery target is out of sample and the lottery matches are parameter reuse within a jointly selected architecture.
  • The reference implementation, eris-econ 0.1.0, reproduces every reported prediction, 16 of 16 targets within tolerance at an unweighted mean absolute error of 2.70 percentage points and 3.95 on the six Ruggeri lottery items, eris-econ/src/eris_econ/targets.py:338-461 and erisml-lib/docs/papers/foundations/submission/ieee-tcss/final_manuscript.tex:692-722. The calibration objective is a weighted mean absolute error, with weights 1 on the ultimatum mean, the dictator mean, and the responder threshold and 0.5 on the other game targets.
  • Game predictions are cost minima on an integer percentage grid and involve no temperature. Lottery predictions are a binary logit whose temperature is the larger of 0.5 and 0.24 times the cost gap to the power 2.13, eris-econ/src/eris_econ/targets.py:40-42. That rule is not monotone above a cost gap of 1.41, four of the six lottery targets lie above it with gaps 3.48, 2.21, 2.24, and 2.21, and the ordering of the Allais problem against the strong-certainty problem is carried by the temperature and not by the geometry, since the encoding gives the Allais problem the larger gap while the data give it the higher risky-choice rate and no constant temperature reproduces both, erisml-lib/docs/papers/foundations/submission/ieee-tcss/final_manuscript.tex:234-266. The two temperature constants were set from those two targets.
  • An inactive dimension is a direction in the kernel of the output metric. With the monetary dimension inactive, multiplying every stake by a constant leaves every prediction unchanged, and conversely a model whose predictions are unchanged for two distinct multipliers has no monetary weight, geometric-observation/paper/observer-representation.tex:333-345. The reference implementation also normalizes the monetary coordinate to the stake, so the encoding is stake-blind for every metric and a rejection of invariance refutes encoding and metric together.
  • On the high-stakes ultimatum data of Andersen, Ertac, Gneezy, Hoffman, and List, collected in eight villages of Meghalaya in northeast India with 458 responders and stakes from 20 to 20,000 rupees against an average yearly income of about 17,000, three pre-specified tests reject invariance, Kruskal-Wallis H 60.7 at p 4.17e-13, chi-squared 16.18 at p 0.0010, and a likelihood-ratio test of a logit with a log-stake term at p 8.77e-5 with AIC falling from 584.9 to 571.5, erisml-lib/docs/papers/foundations/submission/ieee-tcss/final_manuscript.tex:1005-1019. The calibrated model predicts invariance and that prediction fails. The result motivates and does not test a monetary coordinate in absolute or income units with finite sensitivity, and no stake at which invariance fails is located, erisml-lib/docs/papers/foundations/submission/ieee-tcss/final_manuscript.tex:1031-1043.
  • The fitted model is not a strong-utility model, because the Allais problem has both a larger cost gap and a higher risky-choice rate than the strong-certainty problem. On binary menus it predicts nothing outside the random-utility class. The non-reducibility theorem of the observer-representation draft concerns the budgeted observer whose read subspace is selected from the menu, and not this model.
  • The cumulative-prospect-theory baseline passes all six lottery problems at a mean absolute error of 5.7 percentage points with its canonical parameters, erisml-lib/docs/papers/foundations/submission/ieee-tcss/final_manuscript.tex:1194-1221, and the baseline used does not specify strategic behavior. The two models differ in flexibility and fitting protocol, so the difference in error is not a ranking of the theories.
Prior artMahalanobis, 1936, for the distance. Luce, 1959, for the logit choice rule the lottery predictions use. Kahneman and Tversky, 1979, for the six lottery problems, and Fehr and Schmidt, 1999, for the inequality-aversion baseline. The specialization is Corollary 2 of the observer-representation draft, which identifies this cost with the pullback of Theorem 1(b) and identifies nothing about the map from cost gaps to lottery frequencies beyond the rule as written.

Geometric Evaluation Theory concept

DefinitionAn evaluator-relative theory of preference, value, and choice. An evaluation object is a six-tuple of states with a belief, actions, an evaluator mapping actions and states into a consequence space, a metric of evaluation with an ideal point, a resolution budget, and an admissible set. The distinctions the evaluator can make are derived from the object, and preference and choice are derived from the distinctions. The world supplies the states, the actions, and the map; the evaluator owns the metric, the ideal, the budget, and the admissible set. Written GET, always spelled out, and distinct from Geometric Decision Theory. Also evaluation object.
ExampleTwo actions with consequences (1, 0) and (0.9, 2), an ideal at the origin, and an evaluator that resolves only the first coordinate rank the second action first at distance 0.9 against 1, while resolving both coordinates ranks it last at distance 2.19, so one evaluator with one metric and one ideal reverses its preference when its budget changes.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id geometric-evaluation-theory, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The evaluation object is E = (X, A, C, G, B, K), geometric-evaluation-theory/paper/geometric-evaluation-theory.tex:108-130. The world supplies (X, A, C) and the evaluator supplies (G, B, K), geometric-evaluation-theory/paper/geometric-evaluation-theory.tex:131-140. Without that split every weak order on a finite set is trivially an evaluation object, so the split is where the theory’s content lives.
  • Unbudgeted distinctions are an equivalence relation whose local tangents are the kernel of the evaluator’s Jacobian. A rank budget coarsens it into a coarser equivalence. A length budget gives a tolerance, reflexive and symmetric, that is transitive only when no three distances form a chain of steps within the budget whose ends lie outside it, geometric-evaluation-theory/paper/geometric-evaluation-theory.tex:174-208.
  • Preference is derived, not assumed. At zero threshold it is a weak order represented by minus the distance to the ideal. At a positive threshold it is a Luce semiorder whose threshold is the budget itself, so intransitive indifference is the signature of finite resolution and its size is a property of the evaluation object, geometric-evaluation-theory/paper/geometric-evaluation-theory.tex:209-241. Choice on a finite admissible menu is nonempty, and satisficing is the length budget with the aspiration as ideal, geometric-evaluation-theory/paper/geometric-evaluation-theory.tex:242-268.
  • For a fixed world, a preference is representable exactly when a semidefinite feasibility problem has a solution. Every representable preference obeys the hull law, that no action is strictly worse than every action whose consequences surround it, which holds for every convex metric of evaluation. Affinely independent consequences represent every order on at most m+1 actions, and consequences on a line represent exactly the single-peaked orders, geometric-evaluation-theory/paper/geometric-evaluation-theory.tex:269-291. The hull law is machine checked as hull_law in geometric-evaluation-theory/lean/GET/HullLaw.lean:1-43 against Mathlib, with the semidefinite characterization and the line case not checked. A closed-form combinatorial characterization is open.
  • Uniqueness. From the order on an open connected set of consequences, the metric is identified up to a positive scale and the ideal up to the metric’s null directions, geometric-evaluation-theory/paper/geometric-evaluation-theory.tex:292-336. This is what the learned-geometry protocol can recover from choices and no more.
  • Special cases with their conditions, geometric-evaluation-theory/paper/geometric-evaluation-theory.tex:337-374. Expected utility, mean-variance evaluation, additive multi-attribute value and the ideal-point models, the geometric decision cost of the TCSS paper, satisficing, the Dawid-Lauritzen decision geometry, and Nash equilibrium through the behavioral game. Loss aversion and lexicographic priority as a metric are not in the theory as written.
  • Four theorems a scalar utility on the action set does not provide. A change of rank budget reverses preference between two fixed actions with the evaluator unchanged, geometric-evaluation-theory/paper/geometric-evaluation-theory.tex:375-396. Two evaluators share a standard of correctness exactly when their induced distances are ordinally equivalent, and agreement on every pair of one menu does not transfer to another, geometric-evaluation-theory/paper/geometric-evaluation-theory.tex:397-419. A representation shared by several evaluators at rank k is optimal for all of them exactly when their geometries share a top-k eigenspace, and otherwise the least weighted regret is attained by the top-k eigenspace of the weighted sum and is strictly positive, geometric-evaluation-theory/paper/geometric-evaluation-theory.tex:420-447. Admissibility that depends on the menu produces choice violating the weak axiom of revealed preference, so an obligation of that kind is not a preference at any strength, geometric-evaluation-theory/paper/geometric-evaluation-theory.tex:448-481.
  • Five predictions are stated in a form a measurement can fail. The threshold tracks the budget, rank changes reverse preference, shared representations pay the regret bound, the hull law holds in a population with a known consequence map, and menu-dependent obligations produce the weak-axiom pattern, geometric-evaluation-theory/paper/geometric-evaluation-theory.tex:482-502. The campaign that grades them is geometric-evaluation-theory/CAMPAIGN.md:1-40, gates G0 to G8. Done at commit 91095c9: G0, the frozen foundations; G1, the Lean core; G2, the hull law, which passed; G3, the threshold tracks the budget on a language-model scorer, which passed; G4 with its follow-up G4b, the shared-code regret, both indeterminate, together establishing what the prediction can and cannot test; and G5, identification from choices in its synthetic stage, which passed in all twelve cells on a fresh seed, recovering the metric and the ideal at 64 points above the dimension and recovering nothing at or below the design bound, off a subspace battery’s span, or in a singular metric’s kernel, geometric-evaluation-theory/CAMPAIGN.md:108-125 at b54d55f.
  • The hull law has been measured once, under a registration sealed before any rating was read, on the 1972 American National Election Study, where respondents placed Nixon, McGovern, Wallace, and the two parties on seven-point issue scales and rated them on feeling thermometers, geometric-evaluation-theory/CAMPAIGN.md:42-53 at dc14015. On the registered pair of scales, liberal-conservative and guaranteed jobs, 489 respondents had a menu in which the law could bind, 246 of them, 50.3 percent, violated it at least once, against 66.4 percent with a standard deviation of 1.6 when each respondent’s ratings are shuffled among that respondent’s own objects, and no shuffle in 200 reached the observed rate, geometric-evaluation-theory/experiments/G2/results.json:1-87. Five other pairs of the four scales gave the same ordering, observed rates of 54 to 63 percent against shuffled rates of 67 to 74 percent, the two tax-rate pairs at margins of 0.108 and 0.109 against the sealed bar of 0.10. The verdict is a pass by the sealed bars, and the number that matters more than the verdict is that half of the testable respondents violate the law at least once, so on this world the hull law holds as a population tendency, 10 to 16 points below the geometric base rate of violation, and fails as the deterministic statement of the representation theorem for about half the respondents. Placements are integers on seven-point scales, ratings are integers on a thermometer capped at 97, ties are counted as not strictly better, and no error model was registered, so no part of the half is attributed to rounding.
  • The shared-representation regret prediction was measured once, under a registration sealed after one recorded revision and before any loss under any code was read, on Llama-3.2-3B, with the three query heads of each grouped-query group as the evaluators of one key cache and shared codes of rank 2, 4 and 8 in 128 dimensions, geometric-evaluation-theory/CAMPAIGN.md:73-81 at 8eda439. The verdict by the sealed rule is indeterminate at every rank, geometric-evaluation-theory/experiments/G4/grade.json:1-239: at those ranks the measured attention loss is 20 to 330 times the second-order prediction, median 75, with a mean KL divergence of about 4 nats per query, so the regret formula and the deficiency bound were not tested. The registration’s second-order bar was also defective as written, comparing the probe’s one-key prediction to an all-keys measurement, and that is recorded as a registration defect. The ordering claim, measured on the actual losses, held in 32 of 32 non-vacuous cell-ranks: the leading eigenspace of the summed read operators beat all 32 random codes and the key-covariance code for the group’s total loss. The own-code claim failed: a head’s own leading eigenspace was the best code for that head in 1, 3 and 6 of 16 cells at ranks 2, 4 and 8, and the compromise was often better for a head than the head’s own code. Outside the quadratic regime the theorem orders the shared codes and does not identify the private optimum. The probe that preceded the run, at the drafted ladder 8 to 64, had found the operators of effective rank 2.6 to 8.3 and the three heads largely coincident, geometric-evaluation-theory/CAMPAIGN.md:71-71 at 8eda439.
  • A second sealed run, G4b, measured the object the formula predicts: one key at each probed operating point perturbed by a small isotropic error in the discarded subspace, with an antithetic pair and common random numbers, on the same operators, geometric-evaluation-theory/CAMPAIGN.md:89-98 at 8eda439. The second-order regime is reached, the ratio of measured to predicted loss is flat in the perturbation size up to a tenth of a whitened unit and its median over cells is 1.02 to 1.05, so the recovered operators predict the loss without bias; but 64 draws per cell leave each cell’s ratio offset by a factor with standard deviation 0.16 to 0.24, the registered per-triple bar of 80 percent within 25 percent is missed at 64 to 70 percent, and the sealed verdict is indeterminate, geometric-evaluation-theory/experiments/G4b/grade.json:1-814. An exploratory seed check with fresh draws re-centered the five most extreme cells on one, so the offsets are draw noise. The registration’s Monte Carlo error estimate and its diagnosis rule were both wrong and are recorded as registration errors. What the two gates establish together: inside the quadratic regime the regret formula, the bound and the compromise’s optimality follow from the recovered operators by the theorem, so the prediction’s only empirical content there is whether the loss is quadratic with the recovered operator, which holds at the median; outside it, the ordering claim survives and the own-code claim does not.
  • The threshold prediction was measured once, under a registration sealed before any pair of the run seed was scored, on a language model, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, used as a scorer that reports how far a value is from a target, with the induced order comparing reported distances and equal reports counted as indifference, geometric-evaluation-theory/CAMPAIGN.md:56-64 at 91095c9. Three budgets were set independently, the decimals at which values are rendered, the number of tokens the report may use, and the weight precision. On fresh pairs the threshold, the gap at which 90 percent of pairs are ordered correctly, was 0.869, 0.0868, 0.00856 and 0.00087 at 0 to 3 decimals against rendering steps of 1, 0.1, 0.01 and 0.001, and 0.872, 0.872, 0.0873, 0.00877 and 0.00087 at 2 to 6 report tokens against the resolutions 1, 1, 0.1, 0.01 and 0.001 those tokens afford, every graded threshold at 0.87 to 0.88 of its step, which is where the 90 percent level of a rounding scorer falls, geometric-evaluation-theory/experiments/G3/grade.json:1-120. Pairs separated by 20 were ordered alike in every cell at accuracy at least 0.985. Reducing the weights to 8 or 4 bits left every threshold where bfloat16 put it, so on this evaluator the two output budgets are the resolution budget of the semiorder and the weight precision at 8 or 4 bits is not one. Sealed verdict PASS on all four bars at the registered tolerance 1.5. Two instruments tried before the scorer are kept in the record, a pairwise chooser that was vacuous with options on both sides of the target and had a floor of 7.5 from position bias with options on one side. Not established: anything about a human evaluator, which is gate G7, or a weight ladder coarse enough to move the threshold.
  • The three branches under the theory are descriptive choice, normative judgment, and multi-agent interaction, each with what is measured and what is posited stated, geometric-evaluation-theory/paper/geometric-evaluation-theory.tex:503-526. The correspondence of the ethics stack’s deontic gate to the admissible set and of the invariance principle to factoring through the quotient is posited.
Prior artThe ideal-point models of Coombs and of spatial voting theory (weighted distance from an ideal) are its unbudgeted single-evaluator case. Luce's semiorders supply the form of finite-resolution preference, with the threshold here fixed by the budget. Rational inattention and limited attention are the nearest theories with a budget, and theirs acts on information about states while this one acts on the resolution of consequences. Dawid and Lauritzen's decision geometry is the identity-evaluator, unbudgeted case. Sen's menu-dependence argument supplies the admissibility theorem. Observation Theory supplies the pullback, the regret, and the budget cliff, and an evaluator is an observer whose output is scored from an ideal point.

Conditions

  • The evaluation object is E = (X, A, C, G, B, K), geometric-evaluation-theory/paper/geometric-evaluation-theory.tex:108-130. The world supplies (X, A, C) and the evaluator supplies (G, B, K), geometric-evaluation-theory/paper/geometric-evaluation-theory.tex:131-140. Without that split every weak order on a finite set is trivially an evaluation object, so the split is where the theory’s content lives.
  • Unbudgeted distinctions are an equivalence relation whose local tangents are the kernel of the evaluator’s Jacobian. A rank budget coarsens it into a coarser equivalence. A length budget gives a tolerance, reflexive and symmetric, that is transitive only when no three distances form a chain of steps within the budget whose ends lie outside it, geometric-evaluation-theory/paper/geometric-evaluation-theory.tex:174-208.
  • Preference is derived, not assumed. At zero threshold it is a weak order represented by minus the distance to the ideal. At a positive threshold it is a Luce semiorder whose threshold is the budget itself, so intransitive indifference is the signature of finite resolution and its size is a property of the evaluation object, geometric-evaluation-theory/paper/geometric-evaluation-theory.tex:209-241. Choice on a finite admissible menu is nonempty, and satisficing is the length budget with the aspiration as ideal, geometric-evaluation-theory/paper/geometric-evaluation-theory.tex:242-268.
  • For a fixed world, a preference is representable exactly when a semidefinite feasibility problem has a solution. Every representable preference obeys the hull law, that no action is strictly worse than every action whose consequences surround it, which holds for every convex metric of evaluation. Affinely independent consequences represent every order on at most m+1 actions, and consequences on a line represent exactly the single-peaked orders, geometric-evaluation-theory/paper/geometric-evaluation-theory.tex:269-291. The hull law is machine checked as hull_law in geometric-evaluation-theory/lean/GET/HullLaw.lean:1-43 against Mathlib, with the semidefinite characterization and the line case not checked. A closed-form combinatorial characterization is open.
  • Uniqueness. From the order on an open connected set of consequences, the metric is identified up to a positive scale and the ideal up to the metric’s null directions, geometric-evaluation-theory/paper/geometric-evaluation-theory.tex:292-336. This is what the learned-geometry protocol can recover from choices and no more.
  • Special cases with their conditions, geometric-evaluation-theory/paper/geometric-evaluation-theory.tex:337-374. Expected utility, mean-variance evaluation, additive multi-attribute value and the ideal-point models, the geometric decision cost of the TCSS paper, satisficing, the Dawid-Lauritzen decision geometry, and Nash equilibrium through the behavioral game. Loss aversion and lexicographic priority as a metric are not in the theory as written.
  • Four theorems a scalar utility on the action set does not provide. A change of rank budget reverses preference between two fixed actions with the evaluator unchanged, geometric-evaluation-theory/paper/geometric-evaluation-theory.tex:375-396. Two evaluators share a standard of correctness exactly when their induced distances are ordinally equivalent, and agreement on every pair of one menu does not transfer to another, geometric-evaluation-theory/paper/geometric-evaluation-theory.tex:397-419. A representation shared by several evaluators at rank k is optimal for all of them exactly when their geometries share a top-k eigenspace, and otherwise the least weighted regret is attained by the top-k eigenspace of the weighted sum and is strictly positive, geometric-evaluation-theory/paper/geometric-evaluation-theory.tex:420-447. Admissibility that depends on the menu produces choice violating the weak axiom of revealed preference, so an obligation of that kind is not a preference at any strength, geometric-evaluation-theory/paper/geometric-evaluation-theory.tex:448-481.
  • Five predictions are stated in a form a measurement can fail. The threshold tracks the budget, rank changes reverse preference, shared representations pay the regret bound, the hull law holds in a population with a known consequence map, and menu-dependent obligations produce the weak-axiom pattern, geometric-evaluation-theory/paper/geometric-evaluation-theory.tex:482-502. The campaign that grades them is geometric-evaluation-theory/CAMPAIGN.md:1-40, gates G0 to G8. Done at commit 91095c9: G0, the frozen foundations; G1, the Lean core; G2, the hull law, which passed; G3, the threshold tracks the budget on a language-model scorer, which passed; G4 with its follow-up G4b, the shared-code regret, both indeterminate, together establishing what the prediction can and cannot test; and G5, identification from choices in its synthetic stage, which passed in all twelve cells on a fresh seed, recovering the metric and the ideal at 64 points above the dimension and recovering nothing at or below the design bound, off a subspace battery’s span, or in a singular metric’s kernel, geometric-evaluation-theory/CAMPAIGN.md:108-125 at b54d55f.

Invariance envelope

Proved invariant.

  • GET:change-of-basis, invertible change of basis of the consequence space, z’ = A z, with the metric transported as G’ = A^-T G A^-1. Claim: The evaluative distance (y - t)^T G (y - t) is unchanged. geometric-evaluation-theory/paper/geometric-evaluation-theory.tex:108-130.

Survived.

  • GET:battery-below-design-bound, restriction of the battery of consequences to fewer than m + 1 points, or to a proper affine subspace, in the identification gate. Claim: The metric’s action off the affine span of the battery and the ideal’s component in the metric’s kernel are not revealed by choices, while the in-span part and the range component are. geometric-evaluation-theory/CAMPAIGN.md:108-125.
  • GET:output-resolution-coarsening, coarsening of the resolution at which a computational evaluator receives and reports consequences: values rendered at fewer decimals, or the report limited to fewer generated tokens. Claim: The indifference threshold of the induced semiorder equals the resolution budget within a registered factor 1.5 wherever the budget exceeds the evaluator’s floor, is monotone along each ladder, and the ordering of pairs separated by more than twice the largest threshold is unchanged. geometric-evaluation-theory/CAMPAIGN.md:56-64. Witness: on fresh pairs every graded threshold sits at 0.87 to 0.88 of its step (rendering 0.869, 0.0868, 0.00856, 0.00087 against 1, 0.1, 0.01, 0.001; report 0.872, 0.872, 0.0873, 0.00877, 0.00087 at 2 to 6 tokens against 1, 1, 0.1, 0.01, 0.001), the constant a rounding scorer imposes; accuracy at the one well-separated gap, 20, at least 0.985 in every cell. Absorbed by: .
  • GET:weight-precision-reduction, reduction of the evaluator’s own weight precision at fixed rendering and report length, bfloat16 to 8-bit to 4-bit NF4. Claim: The threshold is non-decreasing as weight bits are removed, within the factor 1.5, and well-separated pairs stay ordered. geometric-evaluation-theory/CAMPAIGN.md:56-64. Witness: held as an equality: 8-bit and 4-bit weights left every threshold where bfloat16 put it (4-bit at 3 decimals 0.00093 against 0.00087, accuracy at gap 20 0.985 against 1.00), so on this scorer and task weight precision at 8 or 4 bits is not a resolution budget; a ladder coarse enough to move the threshold was not registered. Absorbed by: .
  • OD:budget, change of the observation budget B at fixed consumer and output metric. Claim: A single-direction probe along coordinate e_i at size rho is reported identifiable at budget B exactly when P_ii > B^2 / rho^2, and a ladder of sizes brackets P_ii between B^2 / r_hi^2 and B^2 / r_lo^2 (article Theorem 2(b), Corollary 3). experiments/DISCOVERY-TRACK.md, D1 record; experiments/OD/D1/grade.json axis. Witness: exact in every evaluator of all fifteen World A cells (three worlds, five budgets, 20 evaluators each) on the run seed, as in every pilot. Absorbed by: .
  • OD:observer-family, change of observer within a declared family: read operators of declared spectrum, coordinate subsets, coarsenings, and learned consumers’ recovered read operators. Claim: In a positive definite world the analytic centre returns the pencil’s end P* = s* P + (1 - s) c I, s = c / (c - lambda_min), so the estimate is nearer P* than P (article Corollary 4). experiments/OD/D1/grade.json, B4; experiments/OD/D1/pencil_probe.json. Witness: nearer P* in 20 of 20 evaluators at B = 1 and at B = 1.5 on the run seed (Frobenius 0.223 against P, 0.181 against P*; 0.117 against 0.102), 20 of 20 in the third pilot, 6 of 6 cells in the pre-seal probe; in the kernel worlds the pencil’s end is P itself and the two errors coincide. Absorbed by: .
  • OD:observer-family, change of observer within a declared family: read operators of declared spectrum, coordinate subsets, coarsenings, and learned consumers’ recovered read operators. Claim: Second version, the rehabilitation of D1: mixed probes at one radius, where the sphere crosses the ellipsoid substantially, recover the read operator up to the pencil s P + (1 - s)(B^2 / rho^2) I, below-threshold eigenvalues included, with Frobenius, above-threshold and below-threshold medians at most REC = 0.39 of chance at 960 queries, REC fixed before the pilot as 1.5 times the pilot’s largest graded ratio. experiments/DISCOVERY-TRACK.md, D1v2 record; experiments/OD/D1v2/grade.json. geometric feature vector (156 dimensions) instrument

DefinitionFor one audio signal, the concatenation of 136 SPD features (the upper triangle of the matrix logarithm of the 16 by 16 frequency-band covariance), 4 spectral-trajectory features (path length, geodesic distance, deviation, step count) and 16 TDA features (8 persistence summary statistics each for $H_0$ and $H_1$).
ExampleA symmetric 16 by 16 matrix has 16 times 17 over 2 = 136 independent entries. Adding 4 trajectory features and 2 times 8 = 16 persistence features gives 156, as the volume prints.
VolumeGeometric Communication, Volume 7 of the Geometric Series; entry id acoustic-geometric-feature-vector, kind instrument.
StatusA definition of a feature pipeline. The complementarity claim made for it (Proposition 4.3) is stated without printed numbers. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The covariance is computed from 16 bands of a mel spectrogram with a regularization of 0.0001 times the identity. The TDA features come from a time-delay embedding of the waveform with delay 10 and dimension 3.
  • The chapter calls the parameter values design choices that can be adjusted for other domains.
  • Proposition 4.3 claims that the combined vector classifies better than any one part on the BirdCLEF 206-species data. Neither Chapter 4 nor Chapter 8 prints the accuracies.
  • In Chapter 8 the vector feeds a LightGBM model that carries 0.30 of the ensemble weight beside two convolutional networks.
Prior artnone recorded

Geometric justification of a public health mandate concept

DefinitionA mandate is geometrically justified when three conditions hold together. The collective geodesic differs from the Nash equilibrium of individual choices, the restriction of autonomy crosses no sacred-value boundary, and the collective benefit on outcomes and social impact exceeds the individual cost on autonomy under the community's covariance matrix.
ExampleIf the covariance-weighted collective benefit is 4 and the autonomy cost is 1, the ratio is 4 and the third condition holds. If the same mandate crosses a sacred-value boundary it fails the second condition and is not justified at any ratio. geometric loss-aversion coefficient result

DefinitionThe ratio of the edge weight of a loss to the edge weight of an equal gain, $\lambda = w_- / w_+$. A gain is taken to move the state on $d_1$ alone while a loss also moves it on rights, fairness, social and identity dimensions, so the ratio exceeds one and grows with the number and intensity of dimensions activated.
ExampleThe volume’s Remark 35. A loss that activates four further dimensions at half a standard deviation each gives \(1 + 4 \times 0.25 = 2.0\), against 1.0 for a loss that moves \(d_1\) alone.
VolumeGeometric Economics, Volume 4 of the Geometric Series; entry id geometric-loss-aversion-coefficient, kind result.
StatusA derivation from posited activations, tagged in parts as conditional theorem and as empirical prediction. The chapter cites the eris-econ validation for a range of 1.0 to 3.53, and the README of 2026-07-14 says no economics instrument has passed the series' admission filter. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The theorem is given with an argument that posits which dimensions a loss activates. The activations are not measured.
  • Section 4.2 takes the ratio of edge weights, which are squared distances. Section 4.10 and the technical appendix take the ratio of Finsler lengths, which is the square root of that ratio.
  • The volume states its falsifiers. A coefficient that is constant across conditions, or one that varies but not monotonically with the count of activated dimensions, would show the derivation wrong.
  • The chapter says the value 2.25 should be derivable from a fitted Sigma and calls that fitting an empirical programme.

Geometric RLHF instrument

DefinitionA training protocol in which raters score responses on individual value dimensions, the value metric is fitted to those scores by inverse optimization under the constraint that it be symmetric positive-definite, and the policy is trained to minimize geodesic deviation from the value-aligned trajectory.
ExampleWith d = 9 the metric has 9 times 8 over 2, which is 36, off-diagonal components. Rating k = 3 dimensions per interaction gives 3 pairs each time, so 12 interactions give only 36 observed pairs and the volume’s condition asks for far more than that.
VolumeGeometric AI, Volume 11 of the Geometric Series; entry id geometric-rlhf, kind instrument.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status block of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, whose alignment thesis is theory at licensed strength and not validated measurement. It adds that no alignment instrument has been evaluated under the xbse admission filter, and the front matter says that ARIA, the system whose numbers fill the chapter tables, is fictional. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Rating all nine dimensions on every interaction is called impractical. The volume asks about 2 or 3 dimensions per interaction and says the metric is estimable when the observed pairwise relationships far exceed the \(d(d-1)/2\) metric components.
  • In practice the geodesic objective is replaced by a weighted multi-objective optimization with a KL penalty toward a reference policy.
  • The stated costs (2.4 times the rater effort, about 1.5 times the training compute) and the reported gains come from the fictional ARIA-G run of 10,000 interactions with 15 raters. Chapter 20 calls the chapter a proof of concept and leaves the precision of the estimated metric open.
Prior artAn extension of reinforcement learning from human feedback to per-dimension ratings and multi-objective optimization.

geometric taxonomy of cognitive pathology concept

DefinitionThe volume's classification of four conditions by the geometric object that is defective. geometric types of culinary transformation concept

DefinitionEach cooking process is a map $\Phi_\theta$ on flavor space set by process variables such as temperature, time, water activity and pH. The volume sorts the maps into five types. Maillard browning expands dimension, caramelization follows a one-dimensional curve, protein denaturation collapses dimensions, fermentation is a slow flow, and smoking, curing and aging are approximately translations.
ExampleIn the volume’s translation model, smoked salmon is the salmon vector plus a smoke vector. With salmon at (5, 1, 0) and smoke at (0, 0, 2) the result is (5, 1, 2), so the base survives and one new component is added. The numbers are illustrative.

Its claims are to be read as theory at licensed strength and not as validated measurement, and the chapters tag each statement as a modeling axiom, empirical, a conjecture or a theorem. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Tagged a modeling axiom. The types are a classification, and no map is fitted.
  • The Maillard map is close to the identity until the surface dries and passes about 140 degrees Celsius, where it switches on sharply.
  • Caramelization cannot be reversed, since its progress coordinate is monotone in accumulated heat.
  • The volume qualifies two types. Denaturation also frees substrate for other maps and can open texture dimensions, and the translations carry second-order couplings through water activity and pH.

Gerrymandering index instrument

DefinitionFor a districting of $n$ voters, $GI$ is the average manifold distance from each voter to the Frechet mean of that voter's district. The Gerrymandering Surgery Theorem calls a map a gerrymander when its index exceeds the expected index of random compact, contiguous, population-equal maps.
ExampleFour voters sit at 0, 1, 10 and 11 on a line. Districts {0, 1} and {10, 11} have means 0.5 and 10.5, and every voter is 0.5 from the mean, so the index is 0.5. Districts {0, 10} and {1, 11} have means 5 and 6, every voter is 5 away, and the index is 5.
VolumeGeometric Politics, Volume 10 of the Geometric Series; entry id gerrymandering-index, kind instrument.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, and says a political-argument instrument is plausible but has not been built or gated. District 7, the source of nearly every number in the volume, is a fictional district, and Chapter 18 says precise estimation of the manifold needs larger and richer datasets than currently exist. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • It needs each voter’s six-dimensional position and an ensemble of random valid maps. Appendix C uses 10,000 maps and treats a rank above the 95th percentile as evidence of manifold gerrymandering.
  • Theorem 5 is stated as a criterion and the chapter gives no proof of it.
  • A dimension-specific index can be high while the overall index is ordinary. The Map C example of an algorithmic map shows this on the trust and identity dimensions.
  • The index values for the three District 7 maps are illustrative.
Prior artIt sits beside the efficiency gap, which the volume treats as a one-dimensional test, and the ensemble method of computational redistricting.

Governance margin concept

DefinitionThe smallest geodesic distance, over the whole of a reasoning trajectory, from the trajectory to the safety boundary that separates permitted from forbidden states. It is positive when the trajectory stays inside the permitted region, zero when it touches the boundary, and negative when it enters the forbidden region.
ExampleIn the volume’s illustration a margin of 3.0 standardized units against a displacement of 4.2 means the trajectory crosses the safety boundary, by 1.2 if the displacement points straight at it.
VolumeGeometric Reasoning, Volume 3 of the Geometric Series; entry id governance-margin, kind concept.
StatusPosited framework. The README's epistemic-status block of 2026-07-14 calls the volume speculative theory awaiting instruments, to be read as theory at licensed strength and not as validated measurement. Its chapters tag each claim as established mathematics, empirical, modeling axiom, conditional theorem or speculation, and the empirical tags rest on one benchmark of five language models. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Tagged a modeling axiom. It assumes a safety boundary that is a codimension-1 submanifold of the reasoning manifold and a metric to measure distance to it.
  • It is a property of the whole path and not of the output alone. The volume calls this path governance.
  • Under a bounded perturbation of the heuristic the margin is said to shrink at most linearly, by a Lipschitz constant times the perturbation size times the trajectory duration. Governance robustness is the largest perturbation that leaves the margin positive.
  • No margin is measured. The numbers in the volume’s triage example are illustrative.

GPA Irrecoverability Theorem result

DefinitionOn a connected learner manifold of dimension at least 2, a continuous surjective scalar assessment G is not injective, so distinct learner states share one score. No function then maps the score back to the state. For k scalar assessments with k below the dimension d, the joint assessment is still not injective.
ExampleWith the volume’s weights (0.60, 0.25, 0.05, 0.05, 0.03, 0.02), the states (0.5, 0.4, 0, 0, 0, 0) and (0.4, 0.64, 0, 0, 0, 0) both score 0.40, since 0.30 + 0.10 and 0.24 + 0.16 are equal. For six dimensions the level set of any score has dimension 5.
VolumeGeometric Education, Volume 9 of the Geometric Series; entry id gpa-irrecoverability-theorem, kind result.
StatusTheorems 5.1 and 5.2 are proved in the text and are elementary. The volume calls the result the education-specific instance of the Scalar Irrecoverability Theorem of Geometric Reasoning. Its application to real grades rests on the posited six-dimensional manifold. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The only restriction on G is continuity. The printed proof takes a regular value of G and applies the preimage theorem, so the level set has dimension d minus 1.
  • It is a statement about the map and holds for the six learner dimensions only if they are independent dimensions of a real space of learner states, which the volume posits.
  • The estimate that one grade value is compatible with 100 to 1000 qualitatively distinct profiles is called a rough estimate. No computation is printed.
  • Scores that all project mainly onto domain knowledge are correlated, so a battery of them spans fewer independent dimensions than it has scores.
Prior artnone recorded

gradient reversal layer instrument

DefinitionA layer between an encoder and a domain head that passes its input unchanged on the forward pass and multiplies the gradient by minus lambda on the backward pass. The domain head learns to predict the nuisance variable while the encoder is trained to make that prediction harder.
ExampleWith lambda 0.5, a domain-loss gradient of (2, -1) arriving at the layer reaches the encoder as (-1, 0.5), and the forward output equals the input.
VolumeGeometric Methods, Volume 1 of the Geometric Series; entry id gradient-reversal-layer, kind instrument.
StatusThe README's status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume the series' metrology discipline, a method that is normative and not a finding. Its Section 21.8 (November 2026) classes each result as proved, posited, or measured on a recorded run, and the tables of Chapters 1, 8, 9, 11 and 12 are posited illustrations. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • A domain head at chance means the representation defeats that discriminator. It does not mean the representation holds no information about the nuisance.
  • The method fails when the nuisance and task subspaces coincide, when the domain head is too weak to detect the nuisance, or when the minimax training does not converge.
  • Invariance is measured by a probe fitted after training on held-out data and by accuracy on a test set where the shortcut is broken. In the recorded run of Section 14.9 the probe recovered the nuisance 99.9% of the time under full reversal.
Prior artThe domain-adversarial neural network of Ganin et al. (2016).
Evidencegeometric-methods/chapters/chapter-14-gradient-reversal.md:75-80, geometric-methods/chapters/chapter-14-gradient-reversal.md:97-103

gradient reversal shortcut experiment result

DefinitionOn synthetic spectrograms in which the recording condition predicts the coda type 90% of the time, full gradient reversal lowered the domain head's training accuracy from 95.9% to 37.7%. A probe fitted afterwards still recovered the condition 99.9% of the time, and accuracy on the shifted test stayed at chance.
ExampleP3 required the probe’s accuracy to fall by at least 15 points under full reversal. It was 99.9% without reversal and 99.9% with it, a fall of 0.0, so P3 failed. The numbers are from the volume’s recorded run.
VolumeGeometric Methods, Volume 1 of the Geometric Series; entry id reversal-shortcut-experiment, kind result.
StatusThree predictions registered in the script before it ran, graded on one recorded run of 16 November 2026. One of the three failed. Priority is shown by file hash, not by version-control ancestry (Section 21.8). Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Three predictions with thresholds were written into the script before it ran. P1 and P2 held and P3 failed.
  • Every setting was at chance on the shifted test, 16.7% to 17.6%, so no model learned the true signal. The experiment cannot say whether reversal helps a model that is able to learn it.
  • The data are synthetic, each setting was run with three seeds, and the setting lambda 0.5 was run without a prediction.
  • The section replaces an earlier version that used random data with random labels, a test that could not fail.
Prior artThe finding of Elazar and Goldberg (2018) that an adversary at chance is compatible with a representation from which a fresh classifier recovers the attribute.

grading moral injury concept

DefinitionThe injury a teacher incurs when a mandated assessment G requires a grade the teacher judges to be a lossy projection of the true learner state x. Its increment is $\|x - \psi(G(x))\|$, the distance from x to the state an observer would infer from the grade alone, and the career total is the sum over assessment events and students.
ExampleIf the teacher sees a state (0.3, 0.9) on two dimensions and the grade alone suggests (0.6, 0.6), the increment is the square root of 0.09 + 0.09, about 0.42. Ten assessment events with 30 students at 0.42 each total about 127.
VolumeGeometric Education, Volume 9 of the Geometric Series; entry id grading-moral-injury, kind concept.
StatusPosited, by analogy with the moral injury of Geometric Medicine. Theorem 8.1 is an accounting identity for a quantity that has not been measured. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The reconstruction \(\psi\) is called the best reconstruction and is not specified, so the increment has no computed value in the volume.
  • Theorem 8.1 is the sum of the increments. The volume draws from it that injury is greatest for teachers who grade often, teach diverse students and perceive the full learner state accurately.
  • The volume separates it from burnout, which it ties to workload. Prediction 16.3.6 proposes a survey test of that dissociation, and Chapter 18 says the predictions have not been tested.
  • The reading of the rise in average grades from 2.52 in 1950 to 3.15 in 2020 as moral numbing is the volume’s interpretation, not a tested claim.
Prior artnone recorded

Gram and Schmidt concept

DefinitionThe procedure that turns independent vectors into an orthonormal basis for their span, dividing the first by its length and subtracting from each next vector its projections onto the basis made so far. Primer L section L.5. Also Gram-Schmidt.
ExampleFrom (3, 4) and (1, 0), the first basis vector is (0.6, 0.8), then (1, 0) - 0.6 (0.6, 0.8) = (0.64, -0.48), so the second is (0.8, -0.6).

graph concept

DefinitionA set of nodes and a set of edges joining pairs of them. A neighbourhood graph joins each row of a dataset to its nearest rows. Chapter 0 section 0.10.
ExampleFour nodes joined in a square have four edges, and every node has degree 2.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id graph, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.19.

Assumptions and scope
  • A set of nodes and a set of edges joining pairs of them. A neighbourhood graph joins each row to its k nearest rows, so every node has exactly k out-neighbours. The mutual form keeps an edge only when each node is among the other’s neighbours, is symmetric, is a subgraph of the directed form, and gives no node more than k mutual neighbours.
  • The Laplacian of the graph carries the dimension in its eigenvalue count and the geodesic ranking in its low eigenvectors’ angles, which is what chapters 3 and 9 read.

harness concept

DefinitionThe code that evaluates a model. It is itself a consumer with a read subspace, and chapter 8 shows how it reads the test fold when allowed to.
ExampleTen folds, five seeds, and 100 samples per fold is a budget of 5000 reads of the data.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id harness, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: 1 item(s), see below.
Defining equation

Book equation 8.1.

Assumptions and scope
  • The harness is the code that evaluates a model, and it is a consumer with its own read subspace, its output metric, and a budget of folds, samples, and seeds. What it reads decides what the reported score measures.
  • A harness that is allowed to see the test fold, through feature selection before the split, through repeated selection on one split, or through a metric that discriminates nothing, reports a score of itself.
  • Repeated cross-validation folds are not independent, so the variance of a fold mean is understated unless corrected, and the program’s own retracted comparison is the case.

hash instrument

DefinitionA short fixed-length fingerprint of a file, computed so that any change to the file changes the fingerprint. Chapter 0 section 0.12.
ExampleChanging one byte of a file changes its SHA-256 digest, and two files with different digests are different files.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id hash, kind instrument.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • A short fixed-length fingerprint of a file, computed so that any change to the file changes the fingerprint. A changed hash proves a changed file, an unchanged file has an unchanged hash, and a digest with fewer values than there are files sends two distinct files to the same digest, so an equal hash is evidence and not proof.
  • The seal ledger records the hash beside the commit, and the recognizer’s templates and the probe’s records carry theirs, so that a reader with the repository can check what was fixed before the measurement.
  • A hash proves content and not time. When a file existed in the hashed state is established by a public push, a signed tag, a transparency log, or an archival deposit.
Prior artnone recorded

head concept

DefinitionOne attention operation. A model has many, each with its own queries, keys, and values. Chapter 0 section 0.11.
ExampleOne head reads a query against 512 keys and returns one weighted mix of the values.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id head, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.23.

Assumptions and scope
  • One attention operation, with its own queries, keys, and values. A head’s output lies between the smallest and largest value, it reads the keys only through their scores against its query, and a key change the query does not read leaves its output unchanged however large the change.
  • Each head has its own read subspace, a few query-weighted directions of each key, so a compression that serves one head can fail another, and the serving-stack measurement of chapter 13 is per head.

hedonic manifold concept

DefinitionA hedonic function $H$ assigns each flavor point a scalar pleasantness. The hedonic manifold is its high-value region, the set where $H$ exceeds a threshold $\theta$, or its ridge, where $H$ is locally maximal across the transverse directions. Pairing is the choice of two flavors whose sum lands on it.
ExampleOn one axis with \(H(f) = -(f - 3)^2\) and a threshold of -1, the high-value region is the interval from 2 to 4 and the ridge is the point 3. Pleasantness falls on both sides of the optimum, the inverted-U the volume describes. The function is illustrative.
VolumeGeometric Gastronomy, Volume 12 of the Geometric Series; entry id hedonic-manifold, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, with no gastronomy instrument evaluated by the series' admission filter (xbse) and the nearest evaluated perceptual domains, aesthetics and music, rated inadmissible to medium. Its claims are to be read as theory at licensed strength and not as validated measurement, and the chapters tag each statement as a modeling axiom, empirical, a conjecture or a theorem. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Tagged a modeling axiom. The field is indexed by person and culture, with an evolved component common to the species and a learned component that deforms it.
  • The volume describes the manifold as bounded, curved and thin, from inverted-U responses whose optima interact. The split into a rigid low-dimensional biological layer and a plastic cultural layer is tagged a conjecture, and the volume says the decisive cross-cultural factor analysis has not been run.
  • The five principal components proposed in Section 5.5 (intensity, balance, complexity, contrast, familiarity) are tagged a conjecture.
  • Chapter 14 treats the field as deforming with satiety and over a lifetime. Both are listed as open problems.
Prior artnone recorded

Hellinger saturation in music correction

DefinitionIn the music corpus the Hellinger feature saturated to about 1.0, because a Gaussian was being fitted to about 45 audio tokens per clip in a 128-dimensional PCA subspace. The volume recomputed the divergences in a 32-dimensional subspace and used the Bhattacharyya divergence directly as a check.
ExampleWith about 45 tokens per clip the sample covariance has rank at most 44, which is less than the 128 dimensions of the first fit and more than the 32 dimensions of the refit.
VolumeGeometric Aesthetics, Volume 13 of the Geometric Series; entry id aesthetic-hellinger-saturation, kind correction.
StatusA reported measurement failure and its repair. Section 17.7 lists the raw Hellinger feature in music among the features that were discarded. Corrections: none recorded.

  • The cause is few samples in many dimensions. It applies to 30-second clips and not to the books corpus.

Hessian concept

DefinitionThe matrix of second derivatives of a score, whose off-diagonal entries are the interactions. Naive Bayes has a diagonal one. Chapter 6. Also cross-partial.
ExampleFor the score 3x1 + 2x2 + x1 x2 the Hessian has 1 off the diagonal; for naive Bayes it has 0.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id hessian, kind concept.
Statusmeasures [predicted]. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The matrix of second derivatives of a score, whose off-diagonal entries are the interactions. The second difference recovers a quadratic’s curvature exactly, and a score that is additive across features, naive Bayes, has a diagonal Hessian because one feature’s contribution is the same whatever the others are.
  • The read operator is not the Hessian. Two features’ sensitivities can rise and fall together across rows even when neither changes the other’s effect, so a diagonal Hessian does not give a diagonal read operator.

heuristic field concept

DefinitionA smooth real-valued function $h$ on the cognitive manifold that assigns each state an estimate of the cost of reaching the goal state, approximating the geodesic distance to it. System 1 processing follows its negative gradient.
ExampleOn a line with the goal at 0 and \(h(x) = |x|\), the state 3 has estimated cost 3 and the negative gradient points toward 0. If \(h\) also had a dip at 5, a gradient-following search started at 6 would stop at 5 and never reach the goal.
VolumeGeometric Cognition, Volume 6 of the Geometric Series; entry id cognitive-heuristic-field, kind concept.
StatusThe README's status block of 2026-09-13 calls the book a domain exposition at posited, graded by a claim ledger converted from the manuscript with debt ratio 1.0, so every row is retrospective and no gate has been sealed in the repository. The ledger grades the benchmark statistics exploratory because their primary run records are not in the repository, and it holds every interpretation at posited because the admission filter xbse ruled the cognitive instrument inadmissible on 2026-07-14. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The field is an estimate and can be wrong. A local minimum of \(h\) far from the true goal traps gradient-following search, which the volume calls premature convergence.
  • The volume reads framing, anchoring and sycophancy as corruption of the field. Those readings are interpretations on benchmark axes, and the ledger holds each interpretation at posited.
  • Chapter 17 lists measuring the field from neural activations as an open question.
Prior artThe heuristic function of A* search, which the volume's notation table gives as $f(x) = g(x) + h(x)$.

Heuristic field concept

DefinitionA smooth function $h$ from the reasoning manifold to the non-negative reals that estimates the cost of reaching the goal region from each state. It is zero on the goal region and positive elsewhere, and its negative gradient is the direction the search follows.
ExampleOn the half line of states x at or above 0 with the goal at 0 and unit cost per unit distance, the field h(x) = x gives h(3) = 3, and its negative gradient points toward 0.
VolumeGeometric Reasoning, Volume 3 of the Geometric Series; entry id heuristic-field, kind concept.

Its chapters tag each claim as established mathematics, empirical, modeling axiom, conditional theorem or speculation, and the empirical tags rest on one benchmark of five language models. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Tagged a modeling axiom. That a reasoning system’s guidance is one scalar field on a manifold is a structural choice of the volume.
  • Smoothness is assumed so that the gradient exists. The integral curves of the negative gradient approximate geodesics only when the heuristic equals the true cost-to-go.
  • For language models the field is implicit. Chapter 15 lists measuring it from activations as an open question.

Heuristic Truncation Theorem (moral heuristics as admissible heuristics) result

DefinitionA moral heuristic that charges, at each state, the sum over boundaries of the penalty times the probability that the action crosses the boundary is admissible when each penalty is a lower bound on the true cost of crossing. A* search with it then finds the optimal path on the decision complex.
ExampleOne boundary with penalty 5, true crossing cost 8 and crossing probability 0.5 gives a heuristic value of 2.5. The same sum with the true cost is 4, so the heuristic does not overestimate.
VolumeGeometric Economics, Volume 4 of the Geometric Series; entry id economic-heuristic-truncation-theorem, kind result.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status block of 2026-07-14 calls the volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, and says that no economics instrument has been evaluated by the series' admission filter and that none passes its gate. Its claims are to be read as theory at licensed strength and not as validated measurement, and the chapters tag each claim as established mathematics, empirical, modeling axiom, conditional theorem or speculation. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The decision is modelled as A* search with cost f = g + h, where g is the accumulated edge weight and h the heuristic estimate of the remaining cost. The identification of g with deliberate and h with intuitive judgment is the volume’s modelling.
  • The premise is that each penalty does not exceed the true cost of crossing. A heuristic that overestimates moral cost is inadmissible, and the volume calls that case genuine bias.
  • Theorem 10 makes admissibility relative to the space. An infinite penalty can be admissible on the full complex and inadmissible on the monetary projection.
  • Definition 11 and Theorem 12 relax the claim to a heuristic within a factor one plus epsilon of the true cost, with path cost at most that factor times the optimum.
Prior artThe admissibility theorem for A* search of Hart, Nilsson and Raphael, and the bounded suboptimality of weighted A*.

hierarchical clustering instrument

DefinitionA clustering that merges the closest pair of clusters at each step, under a linkage that reads the nearest pair, the farthest, or the average, so that merge heights never decrease. Chapter 9. Also linkage, dendrogram.
ExamplePoints at 0, 1, 5, and 6 merge 0 with 1 and 5 with 6 at height 1, then the two pairs at height 4 under single linkage.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id hierarchical-clustering, kind instrument.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 9.1.

Assumptions and scope
  • A clustering that merges the closest pair of clusters at each step under a linkage that reads the nearest pair, the farthest pair, or the average. When the merged pair was the closest at some height, no updated distance falls below it, so the merge heights never decrease, single linkage is never above complete, and average linkage lies between them.
  • The dendrogram inherits the distance’s quotient at every level, so the tree is a certificate about the chosen quotient and not about the data.
Prior artnone recorded

Hohfeldian D4 group result

DefinitionThe four first-order Hohfeldian positions, right, duty, liberty and no-right, are permuted by a correlative rotation $r$ of order 4 and an opposite swap $s$ of order 2 that satisfy $srs = r^{-1}$. These generate the dihedral group of order 8, which acts faithfully on the four positions.
ExampleApply s, then r, then s to right. Right goes to no-right, no-right goes to right, and right goes to no-right. The reverse rotation also sends right to no-right, so the two agree on this position, as the volume checks.
VolumeGeometric Law, Volume 5 of the Geometric Series; entry id hohfeldian-d4-group, kind result.
StatusA theorem the volume proves by direct verification of the three defining relations. The group theory is standard, and the legal reading of it belongs to the posited framework. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Geometric Ethics, the founding volume, withdrew the dihedral group for the Hohfeldian positions in its version 1.25 and uses the Klein four-group. This volume’s text predates that change and has not been revised.
  • The rotation \(r\) sends right to duty, duty to liberty, liberty to no-right and no-right to right. The swap \(s\) exchanges right with no-right and duty with liberty.
  • The result covers the first square only. The second square of power, liability, immunity and disability carries its own copy, and the two are joined in the octad gauge group.
  • Reading each of the eight elements as a re-description that leaves the underlying legal bond unchanged is the volume’s interpretation. That evaluation must be invariant under them is a separate axiom.
Prior artHohfeld's jural correlatives and opposites, and the dihedral group of symmetries of a square.

Hohfeldian Klein four-group (V4) result

DefinitionThe four Hohfeldian positions Obligation, Claim, Liberty and No-claim carry two operations, the correlative s (O with C, L with N) and the jural flip n (O with L, C with N). They are commuting involutions and generate the Klein four-group $V_4 = \{e, n, s, sn\}$, which acts regularly on the four positions.
ExampleWith the volume’s two-bit code O = 00, L = 10, C = 01, N = 11, n = 10 and s = 01, operations act by XOR. From O, s then n gives 00, 01, 11, which is N. From O, n then s gives 00, 10, 11, which is N again, so the order does not matter.
VolumeGeometric Ethics, Volume 2 of the Geometric Series; entry id hohfeldian-klein-four-group, kind result.
StatusTagged Proved in the text and Proved (Lean) in Appendix F, machine-checked in Lean 4 with Mathlib. Ledger rows GE-PROP-8-3-V4 and GE-THM-12-2-V4 have class proved. The full gauge group V4 times U(1)_H is Posit 12.3, a modeling choice (GE-POSIT-12-3, exploratory). Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The theorem is about the permutation group of four labels under the two stated operations. That moral positions are these four, with these two operations, is a modeling choice (Axioms A1 and A2).
  • No operation in the group cycles the four positions. The quarter-turn O to C to N to L to O lies outside it, and the earlier dihedral claim is withdrawn.
  • The group is abelian, so the result of a sequence of operations depends only on how many times s and n occur modulo 2. Order effects in judgment cannot come from this group.
  • The measured correlative rates are below 100 percent (O with C at 87 percent, L with N at 82 percent in the volume’s corpus). The group is the structure, not a description of how people always reason.
Prior artHohfeld's jural relations (correlatives and opposites), with the Klein four-group of elementary group theory.

Hohfeldian octad gauge group result

DefinitionThe symmetry group of the full Hohfeldian octad is the semi-direct product of two copies of the dihedral group of order 8. One copy acts on the first-order positions and the other on the second-order positions, and a homomorphism $\varphi$ lets second-order operations twist first-order ones. The volume works with 64 elements.
ExampleEach copy of the dihedral group has 8 elements, so the pairs number 8 x 8 = 64. With a trivial coupling the product of (g1, g2) and (h1, h2) is (g1 h1, g2 h2).
VolumeGeometric Law, Volume 5 of the Geometric Series; entry id hohfeldian-octad-gauge-group, kind result.
StatusThe README's epistemic status of 2026-07-14 calls the volume a posited framework with one instrumented corner. That corner is the legal text embedding LeBSE, validated in the xbse admission filter on US case law with labels from the CourtListener citation graph, and the README says this covers structure preservation in legal text embeddings and not the book's broader jurisprudential claims, which remain posited theory at licensed strength. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The volume gives a proof sketch. The appendix specifies the coupling homomorphism on one generator of the second copy.
  • When the coupling is trivial the group is the direct product, which the volume identifies as the Geometric Ethics result and calls adequate for ethics and inadequate for law.
  • The chapter body says the order is at most 64 and depends on the coupling. The appendix states order 64.
  • That the legal evaluation must be unchanged by all 64 elements is the Judicial Bond Invariance Principle, which is an axiom.
