hub concept

DefinitionA row retrieved as a nearest neighbour far more often than chance allows. The book shows hubness is almost entirely a property of the queries and the reader, not of the corpus. Chapters 3 and 10. Also hubness.
ExampleOne row appeared in 287 of the queries’ neighbour lists, far above what chance allows.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id hub, kind concept.
Statusrefutes or corrects [refuted]. Corrections: 1 item(s), see below.
Defining equation

Book equation 10.3.

Assumptions and scope
  • A row retrieved as a nearest neighbour far more often than chance allows, a count above the Poisson ceiling. Since the counts sum to the slots handed out, the number of rows with count above a ceiling is at most the slots over the ceiling plus one, so hubs are few by arithmetic, and a higher ceiling names fewer of them.
  • Whether a row is a hub depends on the queries and the retrieval rule alone, which is the sense in which hubness is a query property, and the program’s first hub counts fell by a factor of several when query coupling was removed.

hubness result

DefinitionThe excess of a few rows in the nearest-neighbour lists of many queries over what the Poisson ceiling allows, measured by the busiest count and the Robin Hood index, a property of the queries. Chapter 3 section 3.5 and chapter 10.
ExampleThe busiest row’s count fell from 287 to 213 and the skew from 3.970 to 3.177 when the query coupling was removed.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id hubness, kind result.
Statusmeasures [demonstrated]; refutes or corrects [refuted] ×2. Corrections: 2 item(s), see below.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.17.

Assumptions and scope
  • A hub is a row retrieved as a nearest neighbour far more often than the Poisson null allows, and the ceiling of that null is derived from the query count, the neighbourhood size, and the corpus size.
  • Hubness is measured against a query workload and belongs to it. The two corpus-side mechanisms that were registered to explain it were refuted under seal.
  • Anti-hubs come in kinds, and one kind is manufactured by the query budget through the pigeonhole floor, so a count of never-retrieved rows changes with the number of slots per row.

\[N_k(x\mid Q)=\big|\{q\in Q:\ x\in\operatorname{top}_k(q)\}\big|,\qquad \text{anti-hub}:\ N_k(x)=0.\]

Conditions

  • A hub is a row retrieved as a nearest neighbour far more often than the Poisson null allows, and the ceiling of that null is derived from the query count, the neighbourhood size, and the corpus size.
  • Hubness is measured against a query workload and belongs to it. The two corpus-side mechanisms that were registered to explain it were refuted under seal.
  • Anti-hubs come in kinds, and one kind is manufactured by the query budget through the pigeonhole floor, so a count of never-retrieved rows changes with the number of slots per row.

Witness: in all 26 worlds, Gaussian, uniform, heavy-tailed, mixture, Wikipedia and SIFT, at N from 2000 to 16000: overlap 0.19 to 0.45 across orientations against 0.03 to 0.29 across spectra.   • OD:observer-family, change of observer within a declared family: read operators of declared spectrum, coordinate subsets, coarsenings, and learned consumers’ recovered read operators. Witness: 44 of 44 worlds for both: overlap gap at least 0.08; rank ratios 0.09 to 0.69, the largest on the sphere and the balls. Absorbed by: .
  • OD:world-transfer, transfer of a law frozen on synthetic worlds to embedding corpora, ANN corpora, and dynamical state spaces without retuning. Claim: Across three registrations with one declared feature family and one search, the law discovered depends on the discovery set alone: Gaussian clouds give a concentration law, seven full-dimensional families give a shape-blind spectral law, manifold worlds give an intrinsic-dimension law that fits real embeddings. experiments/OD/D2/law.json, experiments/OD/D2v2/law.json, experiments/OD/D2v3/law.json.   • OD:observer-family, change of observer within a declared family: read operators of declared spectrum, coordinate subsets, coarsenings, and learned consumers’ recovered read operators. Claim: The cross-observer hubness matrix has effective rank at most 0.48 of its column-shuffled null. experiments/OD/D2/grade.json X1. Boundary: ratios 0.10 to 0.30 in 23 of 26 worlds; 0.44 and 0.59 for the 64- and 128-dimensional uniform balls and 0.42 for the Wikipedia scale cell, the least concentrated clouds. Revision: not registered, and what a successor changes is the bar rather than the claim: the 0.48 limit was declared from Gaussian pilots and all three exceedances are the least concentrated clouds, so a successor sets the limit from a pilot that includes balls and a sphere, or declares it per family. The low-rank claim itself is not at issue, the latent structure being present in all 26 worlds.
  • OD:budget, change of the observation budget B at fixed consumer and output metric. Claim: Coarsening the observer’s resolution changes hub polarity monotonically in the resolution, and a resolution of a tenth of the nearest-neighbour distance changes little (exploratory, reported). experiments/OD/D2/grade.json B1. Boundary: monotone in all four sweeps; at a tenth of the neighbour distance 12 percent of Gaussian points and 6 percent of Wikipedia points change polarity under the isotropic observer, at a quarter 24 and 79 percent, against 4 to 7 percent under the anisotropic observer. Witness: the finite budget is a first-order effect on real embeddings under an isotropic reader; not graded, as declared. Absorbed by: declaration. Revision: not registered, and nothing here was refuted: the clause that a tenth of the neighbour distance changes little carried no bar, the test having been declared exploratory and reported ungraded, so there is no commitment to revise. A successor would register a threshold on the fraction of points changing polarity, and this sweep says that threshold has to be declared per reader, the isotropic reader moving 12 percent of Gaussian points where the anisotropic moves 4 to 7.

Revision: the standing law of the track is the D2v7 law with this scope; its second boundary, in N for the Laplace family, is on record and not declared; a registration that declared it would need a term in N, a change of family, and is not registered.

Failed, with witness.

  • OD:world-transfer, transfer of a law frozen on synthetic worlds to embedding corpora, ANN corpora, and dynamical state spaces without retuning. Claim: The hubness law frozen on Gaussian clouds, skew = -0.026 + 0.421 / cv_d + 0.817 sqrt(d_eff) / k, predicts hubness on distributions it was not discovered on, on real embeddings and at larger N, within declared multiples of its pilot error. experiments/DISCOVERY-TRACK.md, D2 record; experiments/OD/D2/grade.json. Witness: fresh seeds of the discovery family replicate (0.93 against 1.19) but uniform balls (error up to 4.5, the law over-predicting by up to 2.8), Student t (under-predicting by up to 2.4) and Wikipedia embeddings (5.3, measured skewness at most 1.1 at effective dimension 156 where the law says 10) fail; the nominal-dimension competitor is worse pooled (14.8 against 2.9) and better on the unseen synthetic group alone (1.74 against 2.45). Absorbed by: representation. Revision: not proposed here: a successor would need a shape variable that separates tails and roundness from the spectrum and a discovery set of more than one family.
  • OD:world-transfer, transfer of a law frozen on synthetic worlds to embedding corpora, ANN corpora, and dynamical state spaces without retuning. Claim: With heavy-tailed clouds placed in the discovery set at the transfer dimensions (Student t with 3 and 5 degrees at d = 256, Laplace at d = 192 and 256) bracketing the unseen worlds, the frozen law predicts hubness on the bracketed heavy tails, on D2v5’s other unseen families, on fresh real slices and at larger N, and beats the nominal formula and the frozen D2 to D2v5 laws. experiments/DISCOVERY-TRACK.md, D2v6 record; experiments/OD/D2v6/grade.json. Boundary: every bracketed heavy-tailed unseen world inside the limit and below every competitor (t with 4 degrees at d = 256 1.64, Laplace at d = 224 1.18, t with 6 degrees at d = 192 1.04, t with 2.5 degrees at d = 128 0.74, log-normal at d = 192 0.68); real slices 0.21 to 0.63; the d = 512 clouds lost relative to D2v5 (cube 4.65 outside the per-world limit of 2.91, Gaussian 2.64 inside it, against D2v5’s 1.09 and 2.54); t with 4 degrees at d = 128 and N = 12000 at 3.31; pooled over the transfer groups the frozen D2v5 law at 1.45 beats the law’s 1.51, the fail clause. Witness: coverage moves the family’s error between the heavy tails at d = 256 and the light-tailed clouds at d = 512 and does not remove it; the pilot recorded before the run that the family, not the set, is the limit, and the run confirmed it; the largest errors of every law of the track sit where the hubness skewness exceeds 12. Absorbed by: declaration. Revision: not another discovery set: a D2v7 changes the target (Poisson hub excess or tail share instead of skewness) or the functional shape, and is a new family and a new registration.
  • OD:world-transfer, transfer of a law frozen on synthetic worlds to embedding corpora, ANN corpora, and dynamical state spaces without retuning. Claim: With full-dimensional clouds at d = 384 and 512 in the discovery set under the log hub-excess target, the frozen law log(excess) = -0.950 - 0.010 / hill_rk + 0.219 log(d_eff) + 0.366 sqrt(id_twonn) predicts hubness on the bracketed clouds, on a cube one step beyond, on the heavy tails, on fresh real slices and at larger N, and beats the nominal law, the chance level and the frozen D2v7 law. experiments/DISCOVERY-TRACK.md, D2v8 record; experiments/OD/D2v8/grade.json. Boundary: the clouds beyond d = 256 all inside the limit and better than D2v7 (cube at d = 448 0.53, Gaussian at d = 512 0.50, cube at d = 640 0.65 against 0.73); real slices 0.14 to 0.24, the best of the track; heavy tails inside the limit but worse than D2v7 on every world (t with 4 degrees at d = 256 0.25 against 0.14); Laplace at N = 12000 at 0.96 outside 0.73; the unseen ball at d = 384 at 1.44, outside and worse than chance; pooled over the transfer groups the frozen D2v7 law at 0.44 beats the law’s 0.47, the fail clause. Witness: coverage of the clouds beyond d = 256 moves the excess family’s error onto the heavy tails and the ball, the sign D2v6 found for the skewness family at about a third of the size; the first law to take a neighbour-distance tail variable misreads the lightest-tailed family, the uniform ball, where the reciprocal Hill term is largest; the D2v7 law, frozen without the clouds, stands as the track’s law. Absorbed by: declaration. Revision: not registered: a change of shape, a term carrying the dimension and the neighbour-distance tail together rather than either alone, is the one repair of D2v6’s list not yet tried; D2v7’s law is the standing law until a registration beats it on the transfer groups.

hyperbolic attention bias instrument

DefinitionA term $B_{geo}(i, j) = -\alpha \, d_{\mathbb{B}}(e_i, e_j)$ added to a transformer's attention logits beside the position bias. Here $e_i$ and $e_j$ are Poincare ball embeddings of the tokens at positions i and j, $d_{\mathbb{B}}$ is the Poincare distance, and $\alpha$ is a learnable scalar. Tokens with nearby embeddings attend to each other more.
ExampleAt the initial scale of 0.1, token pairs at hyperbolic distances 2 and 5 receive biases of -0.2 and -0.5, so the nearer pair gets more attention. The module adds 384 times 32 plus 1 = 12,289 parameters, as the volume prints.
VolumeGeometric Communication, Volume 7 of the Geometric Series; entry id hyperbolic-attention-bias, kind instrument.
StatusA construction with an ablation that the volume reports only as relative trends. The volume's claim is a measurable improvement concentrated on rare and polysemous signs, with no score stated. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • In the cuneiform model the embeddings are learnable, 32-dimensional, one for each of ByT5’s 384 byte tokens, with curvature fixed at 1.0 and the scale initialised to 0.1. The bias enters the first four encoder layers.
  • The bias is monotonically decreasing in hyperbolic distance when the scale is positive (Proposition 5.5).
  • The ablation is reported as qualitative trends. A footnote of Chapter 9 says final numbers are not reported because they depend on seed, hardware and session, and the validation split has about 156 examples.
  • Chapter 9 lists what was not measured. Supplementary data and augmentation are confounded, the number of biased layers and the curvature were not varied, and the bias acts on bytes and not on signs.
Prior artnone recorded

identity reader concept

DefinitionThe consumer whose read operator is the identity, for which read distortion is mean squared error. Every consumer-blind metric assumes it. Chapter 0 section 0.5. Also identity quotient.
ExampleThe identity reader charges 0.3 + 1.7 = 2.0 for either of the two codes and cannot tell them apart.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id identity-reader, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.10.

Assumptions and scope
  • Read distortion equals the trace of the error’s second moment for every admissible error exactly when the read operator is the identity. A particular error can make the two agree by accident.
  • Explained variance and the rule of picking rank at 95 percent are the identity reader’s criteria, and the book records them as the benchmark’s rules rather than its own.

importance instrument

DefinitionA per-feature score of how much a classifier reads it. For a tree it counts splits, which is the right sensitivity for a reader that is flat within leaves. Permutation importance and partial dependence answer related questions. Chapter 7 and chapter 14. Also permutation importance, partial dependence.
ExampleA tree that splits on x1 twice and on x3 once and never on x2 gives importances 2, 0, and 1.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id importance, kind instrument.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • A per-feature score of how much a classifier reads it. For a gradient reader the averaged squared sensitivity is the read operator’s diagonal, and for a tree, whose finite difference is zero at every row that does not straddle a split, counting splits is the right sensitivity.
  • Permutation importance averages the consumer over rows that may never occur together, and partial dependence reads it at inputs it was never trained on, so the three answer different questions and the report names which.

imputation instrument

DefinitionWriting a value into a missing cell that the consumer will read. Mean imputation leaves the column mean unchanged and shrinks its variance. Chapter 2. Also imput.
ExampleFilling three missing cells of a column with mean 5 leaves the mean at 5 and shrinks the variance.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id imputation, kind instrument.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 2.1.

Assumptions and scope
  • Writing a value into a missing cell that the consumer will read. Mean imputation leaves the column mean unchanged, the filled cells add nothing to the sum of squared deviations, and the variance shrinks because the same sum of squares is spread over more rows.
  • An imputation is a claim about the mechanism that produced the gap, and it is fit inside the fold and stated in the preregistration, because an imputation fit on all rows leaks the test fold into the training fold.

independence concept

DefinitionTwo events are independent when knowing one changes nothing about the other, so that the probability of both is the product. Independent variables have variances that add, and tests on overlapping data are not independent. Primer S, equation S.2.
ExampleThe first die showing three and the sum being seven have joint probability 1/36, the product of 1/6 and 1/6, so they are independent.

individual variation as a rotation of the receptor basis concept

DefinitionHeritable receptor variation is modeled as a near-identity linear transformation $R$ of the reference affinity matrix, so an individual's basis is $A' = RA$ and their receptor vector is $\mathbf{r}' = R\mathbf{r}$. For a single-receptor polymorphism the action is approximately a rotation in the plane of the affected axis and its perceptual neighbors.
ExampleLet \(R\) multiply the bitter coordinate by 2 and leave the rest fixed. A dish at bitter 1 in the reference frame reads as 2 for that eater, so a target of 1 needs a reference-frame design at 0.5, the pre-image under the inverse. The factor 2 is illustrative.
VolumeGeometric Gastronomy, Volume 12 of the Geometric Series; entry id receptor-basis-rotation, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, with no gastronomy instrument evaluated by the series' admission filter (xbse) and the nearest evaluated perceptual domains, aesthetics and music, rated inadmissible to medium. Its claims are to be read as theory at licensed strength and not as validated measurement, and the chapters tag each statement as a modeling axiom, empirical, a conjecture or a theorem. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Tagged a modeling axiom. The rotation is an approximation for single-receptor polymorphisms such as TAS2R38 and OR6A2, where \(R\) rescales or reorients one coordinate and leaves the others fixed.
  • Variation in receptor density and gain is a second form that changes resolution and not orientation. The volume treats it separately as effective flavor dimensionality.
  • Personalized design in Section 13.5 replaces the target by its pre-image \(R^{-1}\mathbf{f}^\star\). The volume conjectures that the binding constraint is measuring \(R\) for one eater with enough fidelity, not the optimization.
Prior artnone recorded

inequality tensor concept

DefinitionFor a population of N agents, the entrywise variance across agents of the metric tensor each agent experiences. Its entry for dimensions i and j is the mean over agents of the squared deviation of that agent's $g_{ij}$ from the population average.
ExampleIn the volume’s illustration a 100 dollar expense costs 4.0 at monetary scale 50 and 0.0004 at scale 5,000, a ratio of 10,000. For two agents whose \(g_{11}\) are 1 and 3 the average is 2 and the monetary entry of the tensor is 1.
VolumeGeometric Economics, Volume 4 of the Geometric Series; entry id inequality-tensor, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status block of 2026-07-14 calls the volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, and says that no economics instrument has been evaluated by the series' admission filter and that none passes its gate. Its claims are to be read as theory at licensed strength and not as validated measurement, and the chapters tag each claim as established mathematics, empirical, modeling axiom, conditional theorem or speculation. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • It presumes that each agent has its own metric. Proposition 40 gives the monetary part, where an agent with monetary scale sigma pays D squared over sigma squared for a displacement of D dollars.
  • Proposition 42 states that the Gini coefficient is proportional to the square root of the monetary entry and discards the rest. The chapter states this without derivation.
  • The agents’ metrics are not measured in the volume. The chapter’s ratio of scalar to full-manifold inequality, a factor of two to three, is called a prediction and comes from an illustrative example.

ingredient embedding as a lossy projection correction

DefinitionAn ingredient embedding assigns each food one fixed vector. The volume models it as a lossy projection $\Pi$ that quotients out concentration, matrix context and time. Two foods with the same embedding can taste different, and no operation on the projected vector recovers what was discarded.
ExampleDescribe a food by a pair (direction, dose) and let the embedding keep the direction only. A blue cheese at dose 1 and the same cheese at dose 10 map to the same vector, so no function of the embedding tells them apart. This is the volume’s case of the two blue cheeses, with illustrative doses.
VolumeGeometric Gastronomy, Volume 12 of the Geometric Series; entry id embedding-lossy-projection, kind correction.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, with no gastronomy instrument evaluated by the series' admission filter (xbse) and the nearest evaluated perceptual domains, aesthetics and music, rated inadmissible to medium. Its claims are to be read as theory at licensed strength and not as validated measurement, and the chapters tag each statement as a modeling axiom, empirical, a conjecture or a theorem. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Tagged a modeling axiom. It applies to compound vectors and to recipe-trained embeddings such as word2vec on ingredient lists.
  • The volume says an embedding answers which directions, which neighbors and which feasible partners. It does not answer how much, in what form, in what order or against what background.
  • The irrecoverability is cited from the scalar irrecoverability result of Volume 4 and is not proved in this volume.
  • The statements that 10 to 15 principal components recover most of the variance, and that a 12-dimensional prefix predicts pairing nearly as well as the full vector, are tagged empirical or stated in passing and printed without data.

inherited heuristic and the empty-heuristic problem concept

DefinitionThe inherited heuristic $h_P$ is the part of the educational heuristic field supplied by parents or family who have already been through the educational system. For a first-generation student it is about zero, and the volume calls navigation without it the empty-heuristic problem.
ExampleWith the parents’ estimate at zero and all other sources absent, the field is zero everywhere and A* expands states in order of cost from the start alone. The volume’s stated indicator is 1.5 to 2 extra semesters to a degree for first-generation students, given without a source.

Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The claim is that the field is deficient and not the student, who may sit at the same learner state as a continuing-generation peer.

  • Chapter 7 identifies the hidden curriculum with this field.

Internal coherence (pair_sim_mean) instrument

DefinitionThe mean cosine similarity over all pairs of embeddings in a work's cloud. High values mean the work keeps returning to a narrow region of content space, and low values mean it ranges widely.
ExampleA work with three units whose pairwise cosine similarities are 0.9, 0.5 and 0.4 has pair_sim_mean equal to 1.8 divided by 3, which is 0.6.
VolumeGeometric Aesthetics, Volume 13 of the Geometric Series; entry id aesthetic-internal-coherence, kind instrument.
StatusA measured instrument on two corpora. The sign of its association with reception reversed between books and music. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The statistic carries no built-in sign. Whether coherence goes with higher or lower reception is left to measurement.
  • In books it correlates with Goodreads rating at \(\rho = +0.126\) (8.4 sigma). In music it correlates with log listens at \(\rho = -0.076\).
  • Its value transfers across translations of the same book at a mean Spearman correlation of 0.712.
  • Values are relative to the encoder. Section 17.8 says other encoders would give different values and, in principle, different signs.

intrinsic dimension concept

DefinitionThe number of directions a dataset varies along locally, whatever the number of its coordinates and whatever the number of its covariance directions. Chapter 0 section 0.10. Also Weyl.
ExampleA circle drawn in three coordinates has intrinsic dimension 1; the recognizer read 1.81, 2.80, and 1.74 on its three templates.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id intrinsic-dimension, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.31.

Assumptions and scope
  • The number of directions a dataset varies along locally, whatever its number of coordinates. Read from the slope of the Laplacian eigenvalue count on log axes by Weyl’s law, it is an asymptotic estimate that depends on the graph’s construction and the range of eigenvalues fitted. It is not the number of covariance directions, since a circle has intrinsic dimension one and two covariance directions.
  • The recognizer reads dimension before shape, and the battery’s dimensions of 1.81, 2.80, and 1.74 were read against sealed bars on templates built for the purpose.

inverse flavor problem instrument

DefinitionGiven a target flavor $\mathbf{f}^\star$, a palette matrix $B$ and a positive-definite metric matrix $M$, choose nonnegative doses $\mathbf{x}$ to minimize $(B\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{f}^\star)^\top M (B\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{f}^\star)$ under a cost ceiling and admissibility constraints. It is a convex quadratic program. Zero distance is reachable exactly when the target lies in the admissible hull of the palette.
ExampleWith palette vectors (1, 0) and (0, 1), the identity as metric and no other constraint, the target (2, 3) is reached exactly by doses (2, 3). The target (2, -1) is outside the hull, the best doses are (2, 0), and the residual distance is 1. The numbers are illustrative.
VolumeGeometric Gastronomy, Volume 12 of the Geometric Series; entry id inverse-flavor-problem, kind instrument.
StatusA theorem in the volume's tagging, with a one-sentence proof and no machine-checked proof. The metric matrix and palette vectors it needs are posited, and the volume conjectures that measuring the metric for a given eater is the binding constraint. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The program is a modeling axiom and the reachability statement is tagged a theorem. It is stated for the linear-mixing regime with a positive-definite metric and a convex admissible set, and the volume’s proof is one sentence from strict convexity.
  • Convexity fails where mixing is nonlinear, in synergy and antagonism and in threshold and saturation effects at high dose. There the program is a local model, refined by panel-tested iterations.
  • When the target lies outside the reachable polytope, the residual distance is what the volume calls the artificiality gap, and the active constraints say which limit blocks a closer match.
  • Masking, mimicry, cost-limited formulation and personalization are presented as the same program under different targets, palettes, constraints and metrics.
Prior artNonnegative least squares and convex quadratic programming.

inverted file instrument

DefinitionAn index that partitions vectors into cells by k-means and answers a query by searching only the cells nearest to it. The number of cells searched is the probe count. Chapter 11. Also probe count, probes.
ExampleA million vectors in 1024 cells, probing 8 cells, scores about 8000 candidates per query.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id inverted-file, kind instrument.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • An index that partitions vectors into cells by k-means and searches only the cells nearest the query. Probing more cells never loses a candidate, a neighbour is found exactly when its cell is probed, the scanned fraction is the probed cells’ size over the corpus, and with equal cells it is the probe count over the cell count.
  • The recall at one probe against eight in the chapter’s table is a measurement, and the vacuity threshold of the certificate predicts where single-stage retrieval dies, which is the ledger’s demonstrated row.

Irrecoverability of the binary verdict and the scalar sentence result

DefinitionA binary verdict maps the eight-dimensional legal space to one bit, and a sentence maps it to one number. Neither map is injective, so neither preserves the distances between cases, and nothing computed from the verdict or sentence alone recovers the dimensions that produced it.
ExampleTwo cases with first scores 0.9 and 0.6 that both receive the verdict 1 cannot be told apart from the verdict, although they differ by 0.3 on that dimension.
VolumeGeometric Law, Volume 5 of the Geometric Series; entry id binary-verdict-irrecoverability, kind result.

That corner is the legal text embedding LeBSE, validated in the xbse admission filter on US case law with labels from the CourtListener citation graph, and the README says this covers structure preservation in legal text embeddings and not the book's broader jurisprudential claims, which remain posited theory at licensed strength. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Tagged in the volume as a conditional theorem, with a proof sketch. It is the legal restatement of the Scalar Irrecoverability Theorem of Geometric Reasoning.
  • It presupposes that a case is described by eight dimensions, which the volume tags as a modeling axiom.
  • It says that information is lost, not that verdicts are wrong. The volume says the framework audits verdicts and does not determine them.

isotropic concept

DefinitionOf a covariance, having the same variance in every direction. Chapter 0. Also anisotropic.
ExampleCovariance diag(1, 1) is isotropic, and a reader at any angle sees variance 1.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id isotropic, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • An isotropic covariance has the same variance in every direction, so every unit reader reads it the same and no flip is possible. An anisotropic one has different variances in different directions, and two unit readers can read it differently.
  • The flip needs anisotropy. Two codes with the variances exchanged are read the same by every reader exactly when the two variances agree, which is the boundary the coupling null names from the other side.

  • A set of items that appear together in a transaction. Its support lies in the unit interval, the empty itemset has support one, a superset has support at most that of a subset, and the support of a union is at most the smaller of the two supports.
  • A closed itemset has no strict superset with the same support and a maximal frequent itemset has no frequent strict superset, and every maximal frequent itemset is closed, since a superset with the same support would be frequent too.

Jaccard concept

DefinitionThe size of the intersection of two sets over the size of their union, between zero and one, zero exactly when the sets are disjoint, which discards joint absence. Chapter 0 section 0.6 and chapter 3.
ExampleSets {a, b, c} and {b, c, d} share 2 of 4 elements, a Jaccard coefficient of 0.5.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id jaccard, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The size of the intersection of two sets over the size of their union, between zero and one, one for a nonempty set against itself, symmetric, and zero exactly when the sets are disjoint. A subset’s coefficient is its share of the larger set.
  • It reads nothing outside the union, so its distance lives on the quotient that discards joint absence, which is the right quotient for a consumer that reads presence and the wrong one for a consumer that reads counts.

Jacobian concept

DefinitionThe matrix of partial derivatives of a vector-valued consumer, whose transpose times itself averages to the read operator. A discrete stage has none. Chapter 0 section 0.5 and chapter 12. Also not differentiable.
ExampleA consumer mapping (x1, x2) to (x1 + x2, x1 − x2) has Jacobian with rows (1, 1) and (1, −1).
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id jacobian, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 2.1.

Assumptions and scope
  • The matrix of partial derivatives of a vector-valued consumer, whose transpose times itself averages to the read operator. Along a chain of stages the rank of the composed operator is at most the rank of either stage, and a stage that identifies two inputs identifies them for every stage after it.
  • Chunking and indexing have no Jacobian, since a document goes to a set of pieces and a query to a candidate list, and what survives without a derivative is the statement about distinctions.

Judicial Bond Invariance Principle (JBIP) concept

DefinitionIf a transformation of a dispute's description preserves the Hohfeldian bond structure, meaning the configuration of rights, duties, liberties, no-rights, powers, immunities, liabilities and disabilities among the parties, then the legal evaluation must be unchanged.
ExampleIn the volume’s example a landlord refuses a tenant for race in one case and for religion in another. Both cases have the same right, duty, breach, power and liability, so the evaluation must be the same.
VolumeGeometric Law, Volume 5 of the Geometric Series; entry id judicial-bond-invariance-principle, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic status of 2026-07-14 calls the volume a posited framework with one instrumented corner. That corner is the legal text embedding LeBSE, validated in the xbse admission filter on US case law with labels from the CourtListener citation graph, and the README says this covers structure preservation in legal text embeddings and not the book's broader jurisprudential claims, which remain posited theory at licensed strength. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Stated as an axiom. It is the Bond Invariance Principle of Geometric Ethics specialized to law.
  • The volume calls it stronger than the Legal Invariance Principle because it fixes what counts as legally relevant. Two cases with isomorphic bond structures must receive the same evaluation.
  • The volume identifies the bond-preserving transformations with the 64-element Hohfeldian gauge group of Chapter 5.
  • The volume notes that existing doctrine applies different levels of scrutiny to race and to sex, and says the axiom suggests this asymmetry is problematic.

Judicial complex concept

DefinitionThe judicial complex $\mathcal{K}$ is a directed weighted simplicial complex. Each decided case is a vertex carrying a vector of eight legal dimension scores, a court level and a date. A directed edge with an asymmetric non-negative weight runs from a cited case to the citing case, and a set of mutually citing cases that establish a doctrine is a higher simplex.
ExampleIn the volume’s illustrative mini-complex, five voter ID cases are the vertices and six citations are the directed edges, one of which runs from Crawford (Supreme Court, 2008) to Judge Rivera’s district case of 2026.
VolumeGeometric Law, Volume 5 of the Geometric Series; entry id judicial-complex, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic status of 2026-07-14 calls the volume a posited framework with one instrumented corner. That corner is the legal text embedding LeBSE, validated in the xbse admission filter on US case law with labels from the CourtListener citation graph, and the README says this covers structure preservation in legal text embeddings and not the book's broader jurisprudential claims, which remain posited theory at licensed strength. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The front matter classes the structural choices of the model as modeling axioms, and Chapter 16 calls the complex a model of legal reasoning and not a replica.
  • Citation edges respect time, so the citation subgraph is acyclic. Binding authority runs from a higher court to a lower one, and the reverse direction has high or infinite cost.
  • The continuum limit to a Riemannian manifold is used as a theoretical tool. The discrete complex is primary and every computation on it is finite.
  • Chapter 4 states that scoring a case corpus and calibrating the weights has not yet been executed on legal data. The five-case complex in Chapter 3 is an illustration.
Prior artCitation networks of case law and the simplicial complexes of algebraic topology.

Kendall correlation concept

DefinitionThe fraction of item pairs two rankings order the same way, minus the fraction they order differently. Equation 0.15. Also Kendall, rank correlation, rank agreement.
ExampleRankings (1, 2, 3) and (1, 3, 2) agree on two pairs and disagree on one, Kendall tau one third.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id kendall-correlation, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.15.

Assumptions and scope
  • The fraction of item pairs two rankings order the same way minus the fraction they order differently. It lies between minus one and one, it is one when no pair disagrees, and since it depends only on the orderings a strictly increasing transform of either score leaves it unchanged.
  • It is the rank-agreement statistic the rank certificate bounds from below, and a floor on it is a floor on the consumer’s rankings, not on any distance.

kernel concept

DefinitionThe directions a matrix sends to zero. The kernel of the read operator is the nuisance. Chapter 0 section 0.5.

Defining equation

Book equation 0.9.

Assumptions and scope
  • The directions a matrix sends to zero. The kernel of the read operator is the nuisance, the directions the consumer never reads, and a direction is in it exactly when every row’s sensitivity is orthogonal to it. The kernel’s dimension is the dimension less the rank.

KL divergence concept

DefinitionA measure of how far one probability distribution is from another, zero when they are identical. Equation 0.24. Also Kullback, perplexity.
ExampleA fair coin coded as if heads had probability 0.9 costs about 0.74 bits of divergence per toss.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id kl-divergence, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.24.

Assumptions and scope
  • The expected log ratio of two distributions’ masses under the first. It is nonnegative by Gibbs’ inequality, zero when the distributions agree, and not symmetric, so the direction of the comparison is part of the claim.
  • The book’s use is through perplexity. A reconstruction at cosine 0.995 raised the perplexity by three orders of magnitude, which is the case that reconstruction error is not the consumer’s error.

k-means instrument

DefinitionA clustering that minimizes the sum of squared errors to the cluster centres. The mean minimizes each cluster's error and assigning each row to its nearest centre never raises the total, so it is the identity reader's clustering. Chapter 9.
ExamplePoints 1, 2, and 6 with two centres settle at 1.5 and 6, with sum of squared errors 0.5.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id k-means, kind instrument.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 9.1.

Assumptions and scope
  • A clustering that minimizes the sum of squared errors to the cluster centres. The error about any centre is the error about the mean plus the row count times the squared distance between the two, so the mean minimizes each cluster’s error, and assigning each row to its nearest centre never raises the total.
  • It is the identity reader’s clustering. It weighs every direction equally, and a direction with large variance and no group structure pulls its centres exactly as variance-based reduction pulls its components.

The error about any centre is the error about the mean plus the row count times the squared distance between the two, so the mean minimizes each cluster’s error, and assigning each row to its nearest centre never raises the total.

knowledge transfer as parallel transport, and transfer holonomy concept

DefinitionA piece of understanding is a tangent vector k at a point in one domain chart of the learner manifold. Transfer is parallel transport of k along a path into a second chart, giving k'. The holonomy H, equal to k' minus k, measures the distortion. Transfer succeeds when the norm of H is small.
ExampleWith a maximum curvature of 2 and a path that encloses an area of 0.3, the bound of Theorem 11.1 gives a holonomy norm of at most 0.6. On a flat region the curvature is 0 and the holonomy is 0.
VolumeGeometric Education, Volume 9 of the Geometric Series; entry id knowledge-transfer-holonomy, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments. No education-domain instrument has been evaluated by the series' admission filter, and Chapter 18 states that the six predictions of Section 16.3 have not been tested and that no method for estimating the learner metric has been validated at scale. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Theorem 11.1 states that the holonomy is zero where the manifold is flat between the domains, is at most the maximum curvature times the area enclosed by the path, and depends on the path taken.
  • The theorem is stated without proof, with a reference to the Ambrose-Singer theorem. It writes the holonomy as an integral of the connection form around a closed curve, while the path of the definition runs from one domain to another.
  • Near transfer is read as low curvature between similar domains and far transfer as high curvature. A route through an intermediate domain may have lower total holonomy than the direct route.
  • No curvature between domains has been measured. Prediction 16.3.3, on interdisciplinary courses and transfer scores, has not been tested.
Prior artNear, far and negative transfer in educational research, and holonomy of parallel transport in differential geometry.
Evidencegeometric-education/manuscript/part_iii/ch11_transfer_learning.md:20-24, geometric-education/manuscript/part_iii/ch11_transfer_learning.md:56-66

KV cache concept

DefinitionThe stored keys and values of earlier tokens, kept so they need not be recomputed. Compressing it is where several of the book's examples go wrong. Chapters 0 and 11. Also KV serving, key quantizer.
ExampleServing 14000 tokens with 32 heads keeps 14000 keys and values per head for the next token to read.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id kv-cache, kind concept.
Statusmeasures [demonstrated]. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.23.

Assumptions and scope
  • The stored keys and values of every earlier token for every layer, so its size is the product of layers, tokens, two, the head width, and the bits per number. Compressing it changes the keys the heads read.
  • A compression that preserves every query-key score preserves every head output, and one that preserves the keys’ cosine need not, since two keys of the same direction and different lengths have cosine one and different scores. That is the attention-key finding in one sentence.

lag concept

DefinitionHow far a replica trails the primary. The same lag gives two readers two staleness rates. Chapter 0 section 0.13 and chapter 13.
ExampleA replica 50 writes behind the primary is fresh for a reader that touches none of those 50 rows and stale for one that does.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id lag, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • How far a replica trails the primary, in writes or in time. A read of the replica is stale for a consumer whose footprint the lag has touched and fresh for one it has not, so the same lag gives two readers two staleness rates, and a mixed workload’s rate lies between them.
  • Postgres read 0.50 to 0.06, MongoDB 0.47 to 0.03, and production Postgres 0.47 to 0.02 across readers on the same lag, with disjoint seeds.

Landauer's principle result

DefinitionErasing one bit costs at least Boltzmann's constant times the absolute temperature times the natural log of two. Equation 0.27. Also Landauer, reset.
ExampleErasing one bit at 300 kelvin costs at least 2.87 times 10 to the minus 21 joules.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id landauers-principle, kind result.
Statusmeasures [replicated] ×3. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.27.

Assumptions and scope
  • Erasing one bit costs at least Boltzmann’s constant times the absolute temperature times the natural logarithm of two, 2.87 times ten to the minus twenty-one joules at 300 kelvin. The reset bound of chapter 13 charges that price per bit of the record’s conditional entropy given what the consumer keeps.
  • Conditioning cannot raise entropy, so the consumer-relative bound is never above the consumer-free one, and a record that keeps nothing about the erased part costs nothing to reset. The entropies themselves are the ledger’s measurements, two source families and six codebooks.

language chart and translation map concept

DefinitionA language L is a coordinate chart on the content manifold, a domain $U_L$ of expressible meanings with a map $\varphi_L$ to the language's expressions. The translation map from $L_1$ to $L_2$ is the transition function $\varphi_{L_2} \circ \varphi_{L_1}^{-1}$, defined on the overlap of the two domains.
ExampleIn the volume’s example the English word silver, the Akkadian word kaspum and the Sumerian logogram KU.BABBAR label one point of the content manifold. The translation map sends the Akkadian label to the English one through that point.
VolumeGeometric Communication, Volume 7 of the Geometric Series; entry id language-chart, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments. It says that no communication-domain instrument has been evaluated by the series' admission filter (xbse), that none currently passes its gate, and that the claims are theory at licensed strength and not validated measurement. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The chart is partial. The domain need not cover the whole content manifold, and different languages have different domains.
  • A meaning outside the overlap is untranslatable in this formulation. A meaning charted at lower resolution in the target language translates with a loss of precision.
  • The chapter calls the transition map incomplete because it is pointwise. It adds parallel transport along a path, on the assumption that the content manifold is curved.
Prior artnone recorded

language model concept

DefinitionA model that reads a sequence of tokens and outputs a probability for the next one, scored by perplexity. Chapter 0 section 0.11.
ExampleA model with perplexity 12 on a text is as uncertain, per token, as a fair choice among 12 tokens.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id language-model, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.22.

Assumptions and scope
  • A model that reads a sequence of tokens and outputs a probability for the next one. Its perplexity is two to the power of the average bits per token, at least one and equal to the vocabulary size for a uniform guess, and its attention weights are a softmax, positive and summing to one.
  • A seven-billion-parameter model served passage retrieval over contexts of fourteen thousand tokens across three registered attempts, and a key quantizer with reconstruction cosine 0.995 broke it to a perplexity near ten thousand.

Laplacian concept

DefinitionA matrix built from a graph's edges whose eigenvectors, from the smallest eigenvalue up, are the smoothest functions on the graph. The unnormalized form is zero on the constant vector, and the normalized form of equation 0.19 is zero on the square root of the degree. Equation 0.19. Also eigenvector.
ExampleA path of three nodes has unnormalized Laplacian with rows (1, −1, 0), (−1, 2, −1), and (0, −1, 1), which is zero on (1, 1, 1).
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id laplacian, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.19.

Assumptions and scope
  • The unnormalized Laplacian, the degree matrix less the adjacency, has quadratic form the sum over edges of the squared difference, so it is positive semidefinite, zero on the constant vector, and positive across any edge. The normalized form of equation 0.19 has the same ordering of eigenvalues, but its zero-eigenvalue vector is the square root of the degree times the constant vector, not the constant vector.
  • The Lean file checks the unnormalized form. The embedding of equation 0.20 divides each eigenvector entry by the square root of the degree, which is the scaling that carries the normalized eigenvectors back to the unnormalized ones.
Prior artnone recorded

Book equation 0.20.

\[\Psi_i=\left(\frac{u_k(i)}{\sqrt{\lambda_k\,d_i}}\right)_{k\ge2},\qquad \|\Psi_i-\Psi_j\|^{2}=R(i,j)=\frac{C(i,j)}{\operatorname{vol}(G)}.\]

Conditions

  • The unnormalized Laplacian, the degree matrix less the adjacency, has quadratic form the sum over edges of the squared difference, so it is positive semidefinite, zero on the constant vector, and positive across any edge. The normalized form of equation 0.19 has the same ordering of eigenvalues, but its zero-eigenvalue vector is the square root of the degree times the constant vector, not the constant vector.
  • The Lean file checks the unnormalized form. The embedding of equation 0.20 divides each eigenvector entry by the square root of the degree, which is the scaling that carries the normalized eigenvectors back to the unnormalized ones.

Lasso-on-spectrum channel instrument

DefinitionCompute the per-component variances of a work's cloud in a fixed 128-component PCA basis learned from a reference corpus, then fit an L1-regularized linear model from those variances to the reception target. The nonzero coefficients name the PCA directions that align with reception.
ExampleIn the books experiment 71 of the 128 PCA coordinates get nonzero weight, so the L1 penalty set the other 57 coefficients to zero.
VolumeGeometric Aesthetics, Volume 13 of the Geometric Series; entry id lasso-on-spectrum-channel, kind instrument.
StatusA measured instrument. The interpretation of the selected axes is post-hoc inspection, and their reading as discovered canonical directions in Chapter 14 is posited. Corrections: none recorded.

latent semantic analysis instrument

DefinitionThe truncated singular value decomposition of the term-document matrix, ordinarily uncentred, which coincides with principal components on documents only after centring. Chapter 12. Also latent semantic.
ExampleA term-document matrix of 20000 terms by 5000 documents reduced to 100 singular components gives each document 100 coordinates.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id latent-semantic-analysis, kind instrument.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The truncated singular value decomposition of the term-document matrix, ordinarily uncentred, with the top components kept. It coincides with principal components on documents only after the matrix is centred, or under an explicitly uncentred convention, and the fraction of squared singular values kept grows with the components kept and reaches one at full rank.
  • It is the identity reader on term-document variance, and the components it keeps are the directions of largest variance whether or not the consumer reads them. The non-oracle test fit a frozen embedding of 100 components on the training split only and recovered the reader blind.

leakage concept

DefinitionAny information in the training data that could only be known after the decision, or any identifier that lets the model recognize a row it will be tested on. Chapter 8.
ExampleAn imputation fit on all 1000 rows before the split has read the 100 test rows.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id leakage, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 8.1.

Assumptions and scope
  • Leakage is any information in the training data that could only be known after the decision, or any identifier that lets the model recognize a row it will be tested on. It is a property of the harness’s read subspace, not of the model.
  • Selecting features on the whole data and then cross-validating leaks the test fold into the selection, and the reported error can fall from the true rate to a fraction of it, as the ESL example shows.
  • Coupling between the queries and the corpus of a retrieval benchmark is leakage of the same kind, and the program’s hubness numbers moved by a factor of several when the coupling was removed.

learner geodesic concept

DefinitionThe path from a student's current state to the goal region that minimizes total learning cost, the integral of $\sqrt{g_{ij} \dot{\gamma}^i \dot{\gamma}^j}$ along the path. The goal region is the set of states at or above a minimum acceptable attribute vector.
ExampleSuppose two routes reach the goal region. One has segments of cost 2 and 3 and the other has segments of cost 1.5 and 4.5. The totals are 5 and 6, so of the two the first is the geodesic even though its first segment costs more.
VolumeGeometric Education, Volume 9 of the Geometric Series; entry id learner-geodesic, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments. No education-domain instrument has been evaluated by the series' admission filter, and Chapter 18 states that the six predictions of Section 16.3 have not been tested and that no method for estimating the learner metric has been validated at scale. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The geodesic is in general not a straight line, and it differs between students because the cost of a transition depends on the student’s position.
  • The goal is a region and not a point. The university, the employer and the student may each define a different one.
  • The manifold changes as the student traverses it, so the optimal path at one time may not be optimal later.
  • It is a posited object. Computing it needs the learner metric, which the volume has not estimated from data.
Prior artnone recorded

learner manifold concept

DefinitionThe six-dimensional Riemannian manifold of learner states. A state is a point $(d_1, \ldots, d_6)$ whose coordinates are domain knowledge, procedural skill, metacognitive awareness, motivation and engagement, transfer ability, and creativity, each scored from 0 to 1. Learning is a path on it.
ExampleThe volume’s illustrative state for Alex at college entry is (0.45, 0.85, 0.70, 0.80, 0.75, 0.65). The first coordinate, domain knowledge, is the lowest and the second, procedural skill, is the highest, and all six lie between 0 and 1.
VolumeGeometric Education, Volume 9 of the Geometric Series; entry id learner-manifold, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments. No education-domain instrument has been evaluated by the series' admission filter, and Chapter 18 states that the six predictions of Section 16.3 have not been tested and that no method for estimating the learner metric has been validated at scale. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The description is exact where learning is continuous and smooth. Where learning has discontinuities such as sudden insight, the volume calls it an approximation.
  • Whether six is the right number of dimensions is, in the volume’s words, an open empirical question. Proposition 4.1 is checked against six scenarios the volume itself lists.
  • Domain knowledge is treated as one aggregate of many subject-specific dimensions, and the volume notes that this aggregation is itself a contraction.
  • The manifold grows as the student learns, so a path is planned on a space that will have changed by the time the student reaches each waypoint.
Prior artnone recorded

learner metric concept

DefinitionA symmetric positive-definite tensor field $g_{ij}(x)$ on the learner manifold. The squared length of a small step is $ds^2 = \sum_{i,j} g_{ij}(x) dx^i dx^j$, read as the educational effort of that transition. In practice the volume takes it as the inverse of the 6 by 6 learner covariance matrix, which gives a Mahalanobis distance.
ExampleA symmetric 6 by 6 covariance matrix has 6 diagonal and 15 off-diagonal entries, 21 in all, as the volume counts. With the identity as covariance, two states that differ by 0.3 on one dimension and 0.4 on another are at distance 0.5.
VolumeGeometric Education, Volume 9 of the Geometric Series; entry id learner-metric, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments. No education-domain instrument has been evaluated by the series' admission filter, and Chapter 18 states that the six predictions of Section 16.3 have not been tested and that no method for estimating the learner metric has been validated at scale. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The metric depends on position. The same increment of knowledge costs less for a student with strong knowledge and metacognition than for a student weak in both, and the volume calls this dependence curvature.
  • Chapter 10 adds that the metric also differs between two students at the same position. A uniform metric is an approximation the volume accepts only for a homogeneous population, content on one dimension, and a short course.
  • No covariance matrix is printed. The volume describes three cross terms in words and says the matrix is to be estimated from data.
  • Section 10.4 states that no current adaptive learning system estimates the 6 by 6 metric or computes a geodesic from it.
Prior artThe Mahalanobis distance, with the inverse covariance matrix as a constant metric.

Legal Bond Index (LBI) instrument

DefinitionThe mean, over test cases and bond-preserving transformations, of the size of the change in the legal outcome under the transformation divided by the size of the original outcome. A value of 0 is perfect invariance, and the index can be split by transformation type, such as race or sex.
ExampleSentences of 100, 50 and 80 months that become 110, 50 and 72 under a transformation change by 0.10, 0 and 0.10 of the original, so the normalized index is 0.20 / 3, about 0.067.
VolumeGeometric Law, Volume 5 of the Geometric Series; entry id legal-bond-index, kind instrument.
StatusThe README's epistemic status of 2026-07-14 calls the volume a posited framework with one instrumented corner. That corner is the legal text embedding LeBSE, validated in the xbse admission filter on US case law with labels from the CourtListener citation graph, and the README says this covers structure preservation in legal text embeddings and not the book's broader jurisprudential claims, which remain posited theory at licensed strength. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • It needs a transformed version of each test case. The volume says submitting transformed cases to a real court is impractical, and that for AI legal systems the index is directly computable.
  • The 0.155 baseline is the Bond Index of Geometric Ethics, from 20,030 normative evaluations. The volume says it is not a standard for legal systems and that the legal baseline remains to be measured.
  • The volume says Sentencing Commission data suggests a racial index of about 0.19 for federal sentencing and does not give the computation. The per-judge and per-district figures in its running example illustrate the method.
  • The definition varies across chapters. Chapters 5 and 8 state it unnormalized with a range of 0 to 1, the Chapter 8 appendix divides by the original outcome, and Chapter 15 uses Mahalanobis distances between system outputs with a suggested threshold of 0.05.
Prior artnone recorded

Legal embedding and dimension probes instrument

DefinitionA function from legal documents to vectors of fixed dimension such that documents on the same legal issue have high cosine similarity and a change of wording or style moves the vector by less than a tolerance. Eight linear probes then read the eight legal dimension scores from the vector.
ExampleWith a tolerance of 0.05, an opinion and its plain-language restatement that embed 0.02 apart pass the style condition, and a pair 0.2 apart fails it. A probe whose linear score is 0 outputs 0.5, which the volume flags as uncertain.
VolumeGeometric Law, Volume 5 of the Geometric Series; entry id legal-embedding, kind instrument.
StatusThis is the one corner the README of 2026-07-14 reports as instrumented. It says the legal text embedding LeBSE is validated in the xbse admission filter on US case law, with labels from the CourtListener citation graph, and that this covers structure preservation in legal text embeddings and not the book's broader jurisprudential claims. The chapters do not mention LeBSE or report that test. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The embedding is frozen at a fixed version and the probes are logistic regressions, so the same text always gives the same scores.
  • Chapter 3 names the multilingual encoder LaBSE with 768 dimensions. Chapter 15 describes a legal-domain transformer for JurisGraph, the system of its running example.
  • The probe accuracies the volume quotes, F1 from 0.74 to 0.91, are for the nine moral-dimension probes of the parent framework. For the legal probes it calls for about 200 expert-scored validation cases and at least 500 labeled cases per dimension.
  • The front matter classes AI implementation as speculation or extension, and Chapter 4 states that the scoring and calibration programme has not yet been executed on legal data.

Legal friction concept

DefinitionThe legal friction of a path of cases is the sum of its edge weights plus, for each evidentiary requirement $j$, a weight $\omega_j$ times the shortfall of the path's evidence below that requirement's threshold. A strong argument is a low-friction path, and the burden of proof is the least friction from the starting case to the goal region.
ExampleA path of two edges with weights 2 and 3, plus one evidentiary requirement of weight 4 whose evidence falls 0.25 short of its threshold, has friction 2 + 3 + 4 x 0.25 = 6.
VolumeGeometric Law, Volume 5 of the Geometric Series; entry id legal-friction, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic status of 2026-07-14 calls the volume a posited framework with one instrumented corner. That corner is the legal text embedding LeBSE, validated in the xbse admission filter on US case law with labels from the CourtListener citation graph, and the README says this covers structure preservation in legal text embeddings and not the book's broader jurisprudential claims, which remain posited theory at licensed strength. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The path must follow directed edges of the judicial complex. An edge of infinite weight makes the argument impossible.
  • Standards of proof are stated as thresholds on this quantity. Preponderance asks the plaintiff’s best path to be shorter than the defendant’s, clear and convincing asks it to be shorter by a factor below 1, and beyond reasonable doubt asks it to be below a small bound.
  • The chapter’s body formula lists boundary penalties as a separate term, while its appendix folds them into the edge weights. The appendix form is the one given here.
  • The friction values in the volume’s worked examples are illustrative units. No friction computed from real cases is reported.

Legal Invariance Principle (LIP) concept

DefinitionA legal judgment procedure is well-posed if and only if its output is unchanged by every legally irrelevant transformation of the case. The listed transformations are renaming the parties, changing their race, gender, religion or national origin, rephrasing arguments without changing their logical content, reordering the presentation, and translating between languages.
ExampleRenaming Smith v. Jones as Doe v. Roe, with everything else unchanged, must leave the judgment unchanged.
VolumeGeometric Law, Volume 5 of the Geometric Series; entry id legal-invariance-principle, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic status of 2026-07-14 calls the volume a posited framework with one instrumented corner. That corner is the legal text embedding LeBSE, validated in the xbse admission filter on US case law with labels from the CourtListener citation graph, and the README says this covers structure preservation in legal text embeddings and not the book's broader jurisprudential claims, which remain posited theory at licensed strength. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Stated as an axiom. The volume presents it as a formalization of equal protection, due process and the rule that like cases be decided alike, and not as a reform proposal.
  • It requires identical treatment only when all legally relevant features are identical. A prior felony conviction is a relevant feature, so a longer sentence for it is no violation.
  • The principle does not itself say which features are irrelevant. Chapter 15 calls that choice a normative commitment, and the Judicial Bond Invariance Principle is the volume’s answer.

Legal Mahalanobis distance concept

DefinitionThe distance between two cases is the square root of $\Delta v^T \Sigma^{-1} \Delta v$, where $\Delta v$ is the difference of their eight-dimensional attribute vectors and $\Sigma$ is the covariance matrix of the eight dimensions over the case corpus.
ExampleIn the volume’s illustration every variance is 0.04, so a difference of 0.3 on one dimension contributes 0.09 / 0.04 = 2.25. Its eight contributions sum to 5.3125, and the square root gives a distance of about 2.30.
VolumeGeometric Law, Volume 5 of the Geometric Series; entry id legal-mahalanobis-distance, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic status of 2026-07-14 calls the volume a posited framework with one instrumented corner. That corner is the legal text embedding LeBSE, validated in the xbse admission filter on US case law with labels from the CourtListener citation graph, and the README says this covers structure preservation in legal text embeddings and not the book's broader jurisprudential claims, which remain posited theory at licensed strength. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The covariance matrix must be positive definite. When it is diagonal the distance reduces to a Euclidean distance with each dimension weighted by the inverse of its variance.
  • The front matter classes the Mahalanobis metric as a modeling axiom. The volume says the metric is calibrated from data and can be miscalibrated, for example by a biased corpus.
  • Chapter 4 states that the calibration programme has not yet been executed on legal data. Chapter 16 lists metric calibration as its first open problem and says no calibration protocol, sensitivity bound or uncertainty procedure exists yet.
  • The predicted off-diagonal entries, such as a positive covariance of statutory authority with remedial scope, are stated as falsifiable predictions. The volume reports no test of them.

Legal phase transition (overruling as graph surgery) concept

DefinitionOverruling a precedent is a discrete graph surgery. The old precedent's weight deformation is removed from every nearby edge and the new precedent's is added, which changes shortest paths discontinuously. Its cost is the sum, over the cases that relied on the old precedent, of each case's weight times the size of its weight change.
ExampleTwo relying cases with weights 3 and 1 whose edge weights change by 0.5 and 2 give an overruling cost of 3 x 0.5 + 1 x 2 = 3.5.
VolumeGeometric Law, Volume 5 of the Geometric Series; entry id legal-phase-transition, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic status of 2026-07-14 calls the volume a posited framework with one instrumented corner. That corner is the legal text embedding LeBSE, validated in the xbse admission filter on US case law with labels from the CourtListener citation graph, and the README says this covers structure preservation in legal text embeddings and not the book's broader jurisprudential claims, which remain posited theory at licensed strength. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The volume’s criterion is that a precedent is overruled when the holonomy around its doctrinal loop exceeds a tolerance and the benefit exceeds the reliance cost. Neither threshold is given a value.
  • A first-order transition flips a holding. A second-order transition changes a rule continuously with a jump in its rate of change, and the volume’s example is the erosion of Bivens.
  • The volume offers the model as an explanation of why overruling is rare and comes in clusters. It reports no test of the criterion.
Prior artnone recorded

Legal Wilson loop instrument

DefinitionThe ordered product of the Hohfeldian gauge transformations along the edges of a closed path of cases. If the product is the identity the cycle is consistent. Any other group element means the chain of precedents returns to its starting point with the rights and duties relabeled.
ExampleIn the volume’s running example the four edges carry rs, e, e and s. The product is rs times s, and since s times s is the identity the loop equals r, which is not the identity, so the cycle is inconsistent.
VolumeGeometric Law, Volume 5 of the Geometric Series; entry id legal-wilson-loop, kind instrument.
StatusThe README's epistemic status of 2026-07-14 calls the volume a posited framework with one instrumented corner. That corner is the legal text embedding LeBSE, validated in the xbse admission filter on US case law with labels from the CourtListener citation graph, and the README says this covers structure preservation in legal text embeddings and not the book's broader jurisprudential claims, which remain posited theory at licensed strength. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Each edge needs a group element saying how the citing case relabels the positions of the cited case. In the volume’s examples these are assigned by reading the cases.
  • Relabeling at the vertices changes the product by conjugation. Only its conjugacy class, and so whether it is trivial, is gauge-invariant.
  • The proposition that a body of case law is consistent if and only if all loops are trivial is stated without proof.
  • Chapter 3 states that the time-ordered citation graph is acyclic. The running example closes its loop with a return step from the last case to the first that is not a citation.
Prior artWilson loops and holonomy in gauge theory.

Liability-damages conservation result

DefinitionIn a closed bilateral dispute under a fixed legal framework, the net liabilities of the two parties sum to zero. Every right that adjudication assigns to one party is a correlative duty of the other, and every dollar of damages awarded to one is a dollar of liability on the other.
ExampleIf the court awards A 100 dollars against B, the net liability of B is +100 and that of A is -100, and the sum is 0.
VolumeGeometric Law, Volume 5 of the Geometric Series; entry id liability-damages-conservation, kind result.
StatusThe front matter classes conservation among its conditional theorems, results that follow from the model's axioms. No measurement of it is reported. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Closed means two fixed parties and a fixed legal framework. The volume names three operations that break the law, which are legislation, constitutional amendment and third-party intervention.
  • Punitive damages are handled by extending the system to include the state as a third party, after which the three net liabilities sum to zero.
  • The proof rests on Hohfeld’s correlative pairs and on the premise that adjudication assigns positions already existing in the framework and creates none.
  • Chapter 1 says the conservation laws are conditional on assumptions that may not hold in all legal contexts.
Prior artnone recorded

lift concept

DefinitionConfidence divided by the consequent's support, so that lift one is the independence baseline. It fails at low support. Chapter 5.
ExampleConfidence 0.8 for bread implies butter against a butter base rate of 0.4 is lift 2.

Defining equation

Book equation 5.2.

Assumptions and scope
  • Confidence over the consequent’s support, the joint support over the product of the two supports. It is one under independence, symmetric in the two itemsets, and bounded by the reciprocal of the consequent’s support.
  • It fails at low support. One transaction in N containing both items, and neither elsewhere, gives lift N, which is why the rules with the highest lift are the ones chapter 8’s multiple-comparison rule applies to.

linear classifier instrument

DefinitionA classifier that scores by a weighted sum, logistic regression or a linear support vector machine. Its read subspace is the one direction of its weight vector. Chapter 6. Also weighted sum, support vector.

Defining equation

Book equation 6.1.

Assumptions and scope
  • A classifier that scores by a weighted sum, logistic regression or a linear support vector machine. Its decision boundary is the hyperplane where the weighted sum is zero, its read subspace is the one direction of its weight vector, and its read operator is the outer product of that vector with itself, scaled by the score’s slope.
  • Its nuisance is everything orthogonal to the weight vector, and a planted linear consumer is the case a probe is tested against before it is trusted on a real model.

log-diagonal Cholesky parameterization instrument

DefinitionWrite a symmetric positive definite matrix as L times its transpose, with L lower triangular, and store the diagonal of L as logarithms. The n(n+1)/2 stored numbers are unconstrained, and any real values give a symmetric positive definite matrix.
ExampleFor a 2 by 2 matrix, log-diagonal entries of 0 and 0 with an off-diagonal entry of 1 give L with rows (1, 0) and (1, 1), and the product has rows (1, 1) and (1, 2), with determinant 1. A 9 by 9 matrix needs 36 + 9 = 45 numbers.
VolumeGeometric Methods, Volume 1 of the Geometric Series; entry id log-cholesky-parameterization, kind instrument.
StatusThe surjection is Theorem C.5 of Appendix C with its Corollary C.5.1, proved in writing. No machine-checked proof. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The map from the parameters to the positive definite matrices is smooth, onto, and has a smooth inverse, the Cholesky decomposition followed by the logarithm of the diagonal.
  • Setting every parameter to zero gives the identity matrix, the volume’s starting point for optimization.
  • When the training signal is too limited to fit a full matrix, Section 15.8 restricts the factor to its n diagonal numbers, which gives a diagonal matrix.
Prior artThe Cholesky factorization with a log-transformed diagonal.
Evidencegeometric-methods/chapters/chapter-15-cholesky-parameterization.md:66-75, geometric-methods/chapters/chapter-15-cholesky-parameterization.md:97-106

log-Euclidean distance concept

DefinitionThe distance between two symmetric positive definite matrices is the Frobenius norm of the difference of their matrix logarithms, $d_{LE}(S_1, S_2) = \|\log S_1 - \log S_2\|_F$. The logarithm is taken on the eigenvalues.
ExampleThe logarithm of the identity is the zero matrix and the logarithm of diag(e, e) is diag(1, 1), so their distance is the square root of 2, about 1.414.
VolumeGeometric Methods, Volume 1 of the Geometric Series; entry id log-euclidean-distance, kind concept.
StatusA definition. Its metric property is stated with a proof sketch as Proposition 4.1 and proved in writing as Theorem C.4 of Appendix C, with no machine-checked proof. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Both matrices are symmetric positive definite, so every eigenvalue is strictly positive and its logarithm exists. The printed code clamps eigenvalues at 1e-10.
  • It is a proper metric, because the logarithm maps the positive definite matrices one to one onto the symmetric matrices, where the Frobenius norm is a metric.
  • The Frechet mean under this distance has a closed form, the exponential of the weighted average of the logarithms. Under the affine-invariant metric the mean needs an iterative algorithm.
  • The contribution the volume claims for this layer in the bioacoustics case study is posited. The comparison of Section 20.9.4 has not been run.
Prior artThe log-Euclidean metric of Arsigny et al. (2006).
Evidencegeometric-methods/chapters/chapter-04-spd-manifolds.md:45-55

logistic regression instrument

DefinitionA linear classifier whose score is the sigmoid of a weighted sum, strictly between zero and one, above one half exactly on one side of the hyperplane. Chapter 6. Also logistic, linear classifier, sigmoid.
ExampleA weighted sum of 0 gives score 0.5, of 2 gives 0.881, and of −2 gives 0.119.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id logistic-regression, kind instrument.
Statusmeasures [predicted]. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 6.1.

Assumptions and scope
  • A linear classifier whose score is the sigmoid of a weighted sum. The sigmoid lies strictly between zero and one, is one half at zero, is symmetric about one half, and is strictly increasing, so the decision at threshold one half is the sign of the weighted sum and the decision boundary is the hyperplane.
  • Its score moves only along its weight vector, so its read subspace is one direction and its nuisance is everything orthogonal, and its read operator is the outer product of the weight vector with itself scaled by how steep the sigmoid is at each row.
