perplexity concept

DefinitionTwo to the power of the average number of bits a language model needs per token of a test text. Lower is better. Equation 0.22.
ExampleAn average of 3.585 bits per token gives perplexity 2 to the 3.585, which is 12.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id perplexity, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.22.

Assumptions and scope
  • Two to the power of the average number of bits a language model needs per token of a test text. It is at least one, equals the vocabulary size for a model that spreads its mass evenly, and is monotone in the bits.
  • The attention-key finding raised it from 12.24 to 10643 at cosine 0.995, a rise of more than nine bits per token, and the recalibration that improved the reconstruction worsened it, the two standing negatives that keep reconstruction error off the list of acceptance metrics.

\[\cos\big(k,\hat k\big)=0.995\qquad\text{while}\qquad \mathrm{PPL}:\ 12.24\ \to\ 10643.\]

Conditions

  • Two to the power of the average number of bits a language model needs per token of a test text. It is at least one, equals the vocabulary size for a model that spreads its mass evenly, and is monotone in the bits.
  • The attention-key finding raised it from 12.24 to 10643 at cosine 0.995, a rise of more than nine bits per token, and the recalibration that improved the reconstruction worsened it, the two standing negatives that keep reconstruction error off the list of acceptance metrics.

persistent homology concept

DefinitionConnect the points of a cloud that lie within a distance threshold, forming the Vietoris-Rips complex, and raise the threshold from zero. Each topological feature, a connected component or a loop, has a birth threshold and a death threshold, and its persistence is death minus birth.
ExampleFor three points on a line at 0, 1 and 3, three components are born at threshold 0. One dies at 1, when the first two points join, one dies at 2, when the third joins, and one never dies, so the persistences are 1 and 2.
VolumeGeometric Methods, Volume 1 of the Geometric Series; entry id persistent-homology, kind concept.
StatusThe README's status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume the series' metrology discipline, a method that is normative and not a finding. Its Section 21.8 (November 2026) classes each result as proved, posited, or measured on a recorded run, and the tables of Chapters 1, 8, 9, 11 and 12 are posited illustrations. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Long persistence is read as structure and short persistence as noise. The volume calls this a heuristic, made formal by the stability theorem, under which a perturbation of the cloud by at most delta moves the persistence diagram by at most delta in bottleneck distance.
  • One connected component never dies. It is excluded from summary statistics.
  • Higher homology dimensions are expensive to compute and rarely interpretable. The volume says components and loops suffice for most applications.
  • The contribution the volume claims for this layer in the bioacoustics case study is posited. The comparison of Section 20.9.4 has not been run.
Prior artPersistent homology of topological data analysis, with the stability theorem of Cohen-Steiner, Edelsbrunner and Harer (2007).

planted instrument

DefinitionOf a case, built so that the answer is known before the instrument reads it, such as an affine consumer whose read operator is its weight vector's outer product. Chapter 6 section 6.2.
ExampleAn affine consumer with weight vector (3, 4) has read operator proportional to the matrix with rows (9, 12) and (12, 16), which the probe must recover.

Poisson ceiling instrument

DefinitionThe largest neighbour count that at least one point in a dataset would reach by chance under a Poisson null, above which a count is evidence of a hub. Equation 0.17. Also Poisson null, no-structure ceiling.
ExampleWith 1000 queries at k equal to 10 over 1000 rows, each row expects 10 retrievals, and a count above about 20 is beyond chance.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id poisson-ceiling, kind instrument.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.17.

Assumptions and scope
  • Under the null that the slots are handed out at random, a row’s count is Poisson with mean the slots per row, and the ceiling is the largest count at least one row would reach by chance. A count above it is evidence of a hub, and a count below it is not evidence of anything.
  • The ceiling depends on the query set, through the mean and through the rows the queries reach, so it is recomputed when the queries change, and the program’s first hubness numbers moved by a factor of several when query coupling was removed.
Prior artnone recorded

Poisson distribution concept

DefinitionThe distribution of a count of rare events, the limit of the binomial when n is large and p small with np held at mu, with mean and variance both mu. It is the null under which retrieval slots are handed out at random, and the Poisson ceiling is its tail. Primer S, equation S.7. Also Poisson.
ExampleWith mean 0.1 the probability of a count of three or more is 0.000155, which times fifty thousand points is 7.7.

Polarization Illusion Theorem result

DefinitionA preference distribution with a single region of high density on the manifold can look bimodal when projected onto one axis oblique to its principal axis. A bimodal one-dimensional projection is therefore necessary but not sufficient evidence of polarization on the manifold.
ExampleA one-axis histogram with two peaks is consistent with two separated clusters and with one elongated cluster seen obliquely. In the volume’s District 7 illustration the party centroids are 1.5 Mahalanobis units apart, which the chapter reads as moderate separation with substantial overlap.
VolumeGeometric Politics, Volume 10 of the Geometric Series; entry id polarization-illusion-theorem, kind result.
StatusA theorem stated with a short proof in the chapter. Its application to the American electorate is the volume's reading of survey data and not a preregistered test. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The proof notes that every projection of a Gaussian is unimodal. The effect needs a non-Gaussian shape such as a ridge or a mixture, and the proof asserts the construction without working it through.
  • The theorem does not say American polarization is illusory. The chapter reads the survey record as real separation on social values and institutional trust, sorting on three dimensions, and little structure on foreign policy.
  • The dimension-by-dimension figures are given as approximate readings of survey series. The District 7 decomposition is illustrative.
Prior artnone recorded

Political Bond Index instrument

DefinitionFor a set of voters and an electoral system, $BI$ is the average over voters of the manifold distance to the actual representative minus the distance to the closest possible representative under an unconstrained optimal assignment. It is zero for a perfect system and positive otherwise.
ExampleTwo voters are 2.0 and 3.0 from their actual representatives and 1.0 and 1.5 from their optimal ones. The excesses are 1.0 and 1.5, so the index is 1.25. In the volume’s illustration a move from 1.2 to 0.9 is a 25 percent reduction.
VolumeGeometric Politics, Volume 10 of the Geometric Series; entry id political-bond-index, kind instrument.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, and says a political-argument instrument is plausible but has not been built or gated. District 7, the source of nearly every number in the volume, is a fictional district, and Chapter 18 says precise estimation of the manifold needs larger and richer datasets than currently exist. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • It needs voter positions from a six-dimensional survey, representative positions estimated from roll-call votes, statements and platforms, and an optimal assignment computed as a minimum-cost matching against a hypothetical pool of representatives.
  • The README says the instrument has not been built or gated. Chapter 18 lists its adoption as a legal standard among the open questions.
  • A low average can hide large gaps between subgroups. The volume computes it by subgroup and by dimension for that reason.
  • Every value printed for District 7 is illustrative, and the printed values are not all consistent. Plurality is given 2.8 in the comparison table and 1.2 in the first scenario of the same chapter.
Prior artThe political instance of the Bond Index of Geometric Ethics.

Political Bond Invariance Principle concept

DefinitionA democratic evaluation, such as an election, a poll or a representation assessment, is epistemically well-posed if and only if it is invariant under voter anonymity, option neutrality and re-description invariance.
ExampleSuppose the same voters with the same preferences elect A when A is listed first and B when B is listed first. The outcome depends on the labeling of the ballot, so the election fails option neutrality and is not well-posed under the principle.
VolumeGeometric Politics, Volume 10 of the Geometric Series; entry id political-bond-invariance-principle, kind concept.

District 7, the source of nearly every number in the volume, is a fictional district, and Chapter 18 says precise estimation of the manifold needs larger and richer datasets than currently exist. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The volume states it as an axiom. It is the political instance of the Bond Invariance Principle of Geometric Ethics.
  • The volume names three violations. Voter suppression breaks anonymity, ballot order effects break neutrality, and framing in ballot language breaks re-description invariance.
  • The framing violation is tied to a framing result quoted from Geometric Communication. This volume does not measure it.

Political metric concept

DefinitionA Riemannian metric tensor $g_{ij}(p)$ on the political preference manifold that gives the cost of moving a position along dimensions $i$ and $j$ at the point $p$. It is anisotropic and position-dependent, so equal coordinate steps can cost different amounts.
ExampleTake a diagonal metric with cost 1 on the economic dimension and cost 4 on the social dimension. A unit step on the social dimension has length \(\sqrt{4} = 2\), twice the length of a unit step on the economic dimension.
VolumeGeometric Politics, Volume 10 of the Geometric Series; entry id political-metric, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, and says a political-argument instrument is plausible but has not been built or gated. District 7, the source of nearly every number in the volume, is a fictional district, and Chapter 18 says precise estimation of the manifold needs larger and richer datasets than currently exist. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The metric is posited. Chapter 18 says estimating it, its off-diagonal terms and its curvature is an open problem that needs trade-off and intensity questions that existing surveys do not ask.
  • In practice the volume replaces the geodesic distance with the Mahalanobis distance computed from the electorate’s covariance matrix. It gives this as an approximation for a region of roughly constant curvature.
  • The echo-chamber case of Chapter 11 is a degenerate limit in which the graded metric becomes a step function, zero inside the group and infinite outside it.

Political preference manifold concept

DefinitionThe six-dimensional space $\mathcal{P}$ in which each voter is a point with coordinates for economic policy, social values, environmental priority, foreign policy, institutional trust and identity. An electorate is a distribution of points on it.

positive semidefinite concept

DefinitionOf a symmetric matrix, having every quadratic form nonnegative, as the read operator and the covariance are. Chapter 0 section 0.3. Also semidefinite.

Defining equation

Book equation 0.9.

Assumptions and scope
  • Of a symmetric matrix, having every quadratic form nonnegative. A sum of such matrices is one, a nonnegative multiple is one, an outer product of a vector with itself is one, the read operator is one whenever the weights are nonnegative, and the diagonal entries are nonnegative.
  • The local metric on a consumer’s output is positive semidefinite and exists only where the output metric has a local quadratic representation, and every eigenvalue of a positive semidefinite matrix is nonnegative.

Precedential weight deformation concept

DefinitionA binding precedent at a vertex adds a term to the weights of nearby edges. The size of the term scales as the precedent's hierarchical weight divided by the graph distance from the precedent raised to a decay exponent $n$, and the deformations of several precedents add.
ExampleWith hierarchical weight 8 and decay exponent 2, the deformation scales as 8 / 4 = 2 at graph distance 2 and as 8 / 16 = 0.5 at graph distance 4.
VolumeGeometric Law, Volume 5 of the Geometric Series; entry id precedential-weight-deformation, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic status of 2026-07-14 calls the volume a posited framework with one instrumented corner. That corner is the legal text embedding LeBSE, validated in the xbse admission filter on US case law with labels from the CourtListener citation graph, and the README says this covers structure preservation in legal text embeddings and not the book's broader jurisprudential claims, which remain posited theory at licensed strength. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The decay law is given as a scaling relation. The volume gives no values for the exponent, the hierarchical weights or the holding operator.
  • Hierarchical weight is ordered with the Supreme Court above a circuit court and a circuit court above a district court.
  • The deformation defines the legal connection. Carrying a rule along heavily deformed edges may rotate it, and the rotation around a closed path is the holonomy read by the Wilson loop.
Prior artnone recorded

precision, recall concept

DefinitionThe fraction of predicted positives that are truly positive, and the fraction of true positives that were predicted. Equation 0.28. Also precision.
ExampleTen rows called positive, six of them correct, out of eight true positives, is precision 0.6 and recall 0.75.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id precision-recall, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.28.

Assumptions and scope
  • The fraction of predicted positives that are truly positive, and the fraction of true positives that were predicted, both in the unit interval. F1 is their harmonic mean, between the smaller of the two and their arithmetic mean, equal to both when they agree, and zero when either is zero.
  • In counts F1 is twice the true positives over twice the true positives plus the false positives and false negatives, the form the Youden ceiling bounds.

preregistration instrument

DefinitionCommitting the hypothesis, the bar, and the analysis before the measurement is run, so that the record shows what was predicted. Chapter 8.
ExampleThe prediction, the bar, the null, and the seeds were committed before the run, and the commit hash is in the report.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id preregistration, kind instrument.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: 1 item(s), see below.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • A preregistration commits the hypothesis, the bar, the analysis, and the missing-data rule before the measurement is run, so that the record shows what was predicted rather than what was found.
  • Its bar must be anti-vacuous. A pass that any instrument would have produced, a threshold met by every reading, proves nothing, and the program’s own first PF5 pass is the case.
  • Multiple looks at the data need a corrected threshold, and a preregistration that names one look needs none.

principal component analysis instrument

DefinitionProjection of the centred data onto the eigenvectors of its covariance with the largest eigenvalues, the linear orthogonal projection of rank k that minimizes reconstruction error for the identity reader. Chapter 4. Also principal component.
ExampleWith eigenvalues 4, 3, 2, and 1, keeping the top two components drops an error of 3.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id principal-component-analysis, kind instrument.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Projection of the centred data onto the eigenvectors of its covariance with the largest eigenvalues. Among linear orthogonal projections of rank k it minimizes the reconstruction error. In the eigenbasis the variance along a unit direction lies between the smallest and the largest eigenvalue, a basis direction attains its own eigenvalue, and the error of keeping k components is the sum of the dropped eigenvalues.
  • It is the reduction that minimizes reconstruction error for the identity reader, which weighs all directions equally, which is to say for no particular reader at all. At matched reconstruction the consumer-aware code beat it in twelve of twelve domains, and truncation loses on compact sets.

product quantization instrument

DefinitionSplitting a vector into pieces and quantizing each piece with its own codebook. Chapter 11. Also product quantiz, codebook.
ExampleA 768-dimensional vector split into 8 pieces of 96, each coded with 256 centroids, costs 8 bytes.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id product-quantization, kind instrument.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Splitting a vector into pieces and quantizing each with its own codebook. The squared error of the whole is the sum of the pieces’ errors, so the best code for the whole is the best code for each piece separately, and K entries per piece over M pieces address K to the M cells in M log₂ K bits.
  • It is evaluated by recall at k per stratum and by the rank certificate, never by reconstruction error, and the anti-hub stratum is where it fails first.

Projected Intransitivity result

DefinitionPreference on the full complex, ordering alternatives by path cost from the current state under a fixed metric, is transitive. A projected preference can cycle when the projection compares different pairs on different dimensions.
ExampleThe volume’s proof uses x = (3, 1, 5), y = (5, 3, 1) and z = (1, 5, 3). On dimensions 1 and 2 y beats x, on 2 and 3 z beats y, and on 1 and 3 x beats z, which is a cycle.
VolumeGeometric Economics, Volume 4 of the Geometric Series; entry id economic-projected-intransitivity, kind result.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status block of 2026-07-14 calls the volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, and says that no economics instrument has been evaluated by the series' admission filter and that none passes its gate. Its claims are to be read as theory at licensed strength and not as validated measurement, and the chapters tag each claim as established mathematics, empirical, modeling axiom, conditional theorem or speculation. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Transitivity on the full complex needs a fixed metric and a single reference state, so that path cost is one real-valued function of the alternative.
  • The cycle in the proof arises only when the projection is context dependent, comparing each pair on a different subset of dimensions.
  • The volume reads Tversky’s intransitivity experiments this way. That reading is an interpretation and no fitted test of it is reported.
Prior artnone recorded

projection concept

DefinitionThe component of a vector along a unit direction. Equation 0.2.

Assumptions and scope
  • The component of a vector along a unit direction, the direction scaled by their dot product. Projecting twice is projecting once, the remainder is orthogonal to the direction, the projection is no longer than the vector, and adding anything orthogonal to the direction leaves it unchanged.

Proxy pathfinding divergence result

DefinitionWhen a proxy decides for a patient, the search runs on the patient's complex with the proxy's heuristic. The distance between the proxy's path and the patient's own is at most a constant $K$ times the largest difference between the two heuristics, and no calibration can guarantee that difference is small without direct knowledge of the patient's heuristic.
ExampleIf the constant is 2 and the proxy’s and the patient’s heuristics differ by at most 3 at any state, the bound on the distance between their paths is 2 times 3 = 6. In the volume’s case the son sets the futility penalty to 0 where the patient might have set it high. The numbers 2 and 3 are arithmetic from the statement.
VolumeGeometric Medicine, Volume 8 of the Geometric Series; entry id proxy-pathfinding-divergence, kind result.
StatusLabelled a theorem and stated without proof. The volume reads it as a structural limitation, that proxy pathfinding is fundamentally uncertain. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The constant is said to depend on the curvature of the clinical decision complex. Neither the constant nor the distance between two paths is defined.
  • The theorem is stated without a proof.
  • It applies when the patient lacks capacity, so the patient’s heuristic cannot be observed directly. The volume’s remedy is to elicit the patient’s values indirectly before major decisions.

p-value concept

DefinitionThe probability of seeing a difference at least as large as the one observed if the true difference were zero. Chapter 0 section 0.9. Also at p .
ExampleA score more extreme than 970 of 1000 null scores has p-value 0.03.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id p-value, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Against a finite null sample, the fraction of null draws at least as large as the observation. It lies in the unit interval, never rises as the observation grows, and under the null the fraction of draws with p-value at or below a level is at most that level, which is what makes a threshold on it a false-positive rate.
  • A p-value counts one look. Forty looks at five percent pass two by chance, and the book’s rule is to count every comparison made and correct for it.
Prior artnone recorded

QALY Irrecoverability Theorem result

DefinitionAny function that maps the nine-component clinical-moral attribute vector to one scalar value is not injective, has no left inverse, and yields a value-maximizing path that can differ from the clinical geodesic by more than any amount fixed in advance. For the standard QALY, which depends on the outcomes score alone, all variation on the other eight dimensions is lost.
ExampleThe standard QALY reads the outcomes score only. Two patients with outcomes 0.5, one with trust 0.2 and one with trust 0.9, get the same value, and no function of that value can tell them apart. The kernel has dimension 9 - 1 = 8, which is the volume’s count.
VolumeGeometric Medicine, Volume 8 of the Geometric Series; entry id qaly-irrecoverability, kind result.
StatusA theorem the volume proves in Section 5.2. Section 18.8 lists it as proved mathematically and consistent with the QALY critique literature. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The proof of non-injectivity uses rank and nullity where the function is differentiable and a dimension count where it is continuous.
  • The unbounded divergence is shown by a constructed three-vertex complex in which the path the scalar prefers crosses a boundary whose penalty can be made as large as wished.
  • Proposition 5.1 gives the case where the scalar is adequate. It needs a decision that activates mainly outcomes, a population homogeneous on the other eight dimensions, and no boundary crossed.
  • The result is about loss of information under the map. That the nine dimensions are the right description of a clinical state is the volume’s posited model.
Prior artThe rank-nullity theorem applied to a map from nine dimensions to one. The volume gives it as the clinical form of the Scalar Irrecoverability Theorem of Geometric Reasoning.

query budget concept

DefinitionThe mean number of retrieval slots per point, $\rho = n_q k / n$, when $n_q$ queries each return k neighbours from n points. A corpus with no hub structure still shows a k-occurrence skewness of $1/\sqrt{\rho}$, so the null of a hubness reading rises as the budget falls.
ExampleWith 10,000 queries, 10 neighbours each and 200,000 points, the budget is 100,000/200,000 = 0.5 and the null skewness is 1 over the square root of 0.5, about 1.41. The volume’s measured skewness in that cell is 1.79.
VolumeGeometric Methods, Volume 1 of the Geometric Series; entry id query-budget, kind concept.
StatusThe identities of Section 17.11 are proved and checked symbolically in `formal/matlab/ch17_neighbourhood_stats.m`. The measurements are demonstrated or exploratory, as each source file states. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The null assumes every point is equally likely to be returned, so its count is close to Poisson with mean equal to the budget.
  • Every count statistic is quoted with its budget, and a comparison made at two budgets compares two nulls.
  • The volume’s rule is to keep the budget at 2 or more where a decision depends on the count. Below that the null dominates every statistic.
  • The measured table is from one corpus, 1024-dimensional embeddings of Wikipedia passages in the openvector-bench repository, and is not peer reviewed.
Prior artnone recorded

query, key, value concept

DefinitionThe three vectors each token produces inside attention. The query is compared to earlier keys and the result weights the values. Chapter 0 section 0.11. Also query.
ExampleA query scores each key, the scores become softmax weights, and the weights mix the values into one output.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id query-key-value, kind concept.
Statusrefutes or corrects [refuted]. Corrections: 1 item(s), see below.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.23.

Assumptions and scope
  • The three vectors each token produces inside attention. The query is compared to earlier keys and the result weights the values, so a head reads the keys only through their scores against the query and its output lies between the smallest and largest value.
  • Keys are read along the query and values are averaged, so a compression that preserves query-key scores preserves every output, and one that preserves the keys’ cosine need not.

query set concept

DefinitionThe rows a retrieval benchmark asks about. Hubness and the never-retrieved floor are properties of it. Chapter 3 section 3.5 and chapter 10 section 10.2. Also queries.
ExampleThe 1000 queries of a benchmark decide which of the corpus’s rows become hubs.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id query-set, kind concept.
Statusmeasures [demonstrated]. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 10.3.

Assumptions and scope
  • The rows a retrieval benchmark asks about. Two query sets that retrieve the same lists have the same hubs, no queries give no hubs, and the rows never retrieved number at least the row count less the queries times k, so hubness and the never-retrieved floor are properties of the query set.
  • Queries drawn from the corpus inflated the first hub counts by a factor of several, and a generator matched on the query budget would be matched on an artifact.

quotient concept

DefinitionThe space of data with a set of transformations declared not to matter, so that two rows differing only by such a transformation are the same point. Every distance is a distance on some quotient. Equation 0.12.
ExampleThe cosine reader cannot tell (1, 1) from (2, 2), so the two are one row on its quotient.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id quotient, kind concept.
Statusrefutes or corrects [refuted] ×2. Corrections: 2 item(s), see below.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.12a.

Assumptions and scope
  • The equivalence x related to x’ when their difference lies in the kernel of the read operator is exact for an affine consumer with a fixed output geometry.
  • Three things are kept apart. Exact equivalence, that the consumer’s outputs agree under its output metric. A local null direction, in the kernel of the operator at one row. A workload-common null direction, in the kernel of the workload average, unread at almost every row. For a nonlinear consumer the third does not deliver the first, and cosine similarity is the case, whose radial direction turns with the row.
  • An invertible transform identifies no two rows and forms no quotient. It changes the geometry a reader sees. Discretization changes the quotient.
Prior artThe information bottleneck's view of relevant information, what the consumer does not read may be discarded, stated for a fixed consumer without a variational objective.

rank certificate instrument

DefinitionA bound, computed from a compressed representation, that certifies which neighbour rankings the compression preserved for a consumer and which it did not. In its strict setting the floor is a guarantee, in its percentile setting an estimate. A vacuous result supplies no guarantee about the corpus, and falling back to exact reranking is the program's policy for it rather than a consequence. Chapter 11. Also rank fidelity.
ExampleA ratio spread kappa of 1.0148 with mu of 0.0664 certifies Kendall tau at least 0.8671 across 19900 pairs.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id rank-certificate, kind instrument.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • In the strict setting, the zeroth and hundredth percentiles of the distance ratio, the floor is a guarantee for the anchor sample, broken by a single collapsed pair.
  • In the percentile setting the implementation computes the distortion on the retained central pairs and the concentration over all pairs, and the floor is a robust estimate, not a guarantee on either set.
  • The floor is about the global ordering of the sampled pairwise distances. It does not directly certify a query’s top-k recall, one query’s neighbour order, or the trimmed tail.
  • A floor on a sample of anchors is a statement about that sample. Carrying it to the corpus needs a sampling argument the certificate records the inputs for and does not supply.
  • A vacuous certificate supplies no guarantee about the corpus. Reranking exactly is the policy the program adopts when the certificate is vacuous, and not something the certificate proves necessary.
Prior artnone recorded

rank-faithful concept

DefinitionOf a map, preserving the ordering of distances without any bound on the stretch. Chapter 0 section 0.10. Also geodesic-rank, angle-only.
ExampleA compression under which every one of the 19900 pair rankings is kept is rank-faithful.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id rank-faithful, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.21.

Assumptions and scope
  • A map is rank-faithful when it preserves the ordering of distances with no bound on the stretch. Every strictly increasing transform of the distance is rank-faithful, so a reader that ranks, the nearest-neighbour reader among them, returns the same answer under it.
  • Rank-faithful and bi-Lipschitz are separate words. The square preserves every ordering and stretches large distances beyond any fixed factor, and the substrate table measures rank agreement, not stretch.

RCV Recovery Theorem result

DefinitionIn an election with $k$ candidates on a $d$-dimensional preference manifold, plurality keeps ordinal information along one axis and ranked-choice voting keeps it along $\min(d, k-1)$ axes. The recovery ratios are $1/d$ and $\min(d, k-1)/d$.
ExampleWith six dimensions and five candidates, plurality has ratio \(1/6\), about 17 percent, and ranked choice has \(\min(6, 4)/6 = 4/6\), about 67 percent. With three candidates ranked choice has \(2/6\), about 33 percent.
VolumeGeometric Politics, Volume 10 of the Geometric Series; entry id rcv-recovery-theorem, kind result.
StatusA theorem with a proof written in the chapter, which counts independent pairwise comparisons. The information percentages listed elsewhere in the volume are illustrations. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The recovery is ordinal and partial. Cardinal intensity is lost, and the Democratic Irrecoverability Theorem still applies.
  • Positions on dimensions that do not affect any candidate ranking stay invisible, as they are under plurality.
  • Chapters 5 and 15 list 45 percent of information preserved for ranked choice in the five-candidate District 7 example. The formula of this theorem gives 4 of 6 for that case, and the volume does not reconcile the two figures.
  • The Alaska 2022, New York City 2021 and Maine 2018 elections are read through the theorem after the fact. They are not tests of it.
Prior artRanked-choice voting is also called instant-runoff voting.

read direction concept

DefinitionAn eigenvector of the read operator with a nonzero eigenvalue, a direction the consumer is sensitive to. Chapter 2 section 2.2.
ExampleFor the consumer 3x1 + 4x2 the read direction is (3, 4) over 5.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id read-direction, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • An eigenvector of the read operator with a nonzero eigenvalue, a direction the consumer is sensitive to. An affine consumer has exactly one, its weight vector, the projection onto a read direction is idempotent, and its residual is orthogonal to it.
  • The code that puts the whole error on the read direction is the worst, the control that destroys the read direction is confirmed worst, and no code of a given total error can be read as more than the total.

read distortion concept

DefinitionThe error as a consumer experiences it, the trace of the read operator times the error's second-moment matrix, which is its covariance when the error is centered. For the identity reader it is mean squared error. Equation 0.10.
ExampleA reader with operator diag(1, 0) charges a code with errors (0.3, 1.7) only 0.3.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id read-distortion, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Exact, with no centering, for a fixed read operator, which is the affine case. For a nonlinear consumer whose error depends on the row it is a first-order factorized surrogate, exact when the local operator and the error’s outer product are uncorrelated across rows.
  • The second-moment matrix of the error, not its covariance, unless the error is centered by construction.
  • The trace of the second moment is the mean squared vector norm, which is the dimension times the per-coordinate mean squared error.
Prior artThe consumer-weighted squared error. Task-based quantization studies the same objective for a known task.

read operator concept

DefinitionThe average outer product of a consumer's sensitivity over a dataset, an average of local linearizations whose kernel is the set of directions unread at almost every row of the workload. Its range is the read subspace and its kernel is the nuisance. Equations 0.9 and 0.11.
ExampleThe affine consumer 3x1 + 4x2 has read operator with rows (9, 12) and (12, 16) at every row.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id read-operator, kind concept.
Statusmeasures [predicted]. Corrections: 1 item(s), see below.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.9.

Assumptions and scope
  • Each local operator is positive semidefinite, so the kernel of the workload average is the intersection of the local kernels up to sets of rows of measure zero, and an average-null direction is locally unread at almost every row of that workload.
  • The average depends on the workload it was taken over and is written with that workload where the difference matters.
  • Its off-diagonal entries are co-sensitivities, how two features’ sensitivities vary together across rows, and not interactions, which are cross-partials and live in the Hessian.
  • The metric in the vector-output form is the local geometry of the output metric where that metric has a local quadratic representation. A dataset-level loss has none, and the operator is then taken on the score with the identity geometry.
Prior artIn the scalar Euclidean-output case the read operator is the active-subspace matrix of Constantine and Gleich, the covariance of the gradient. What the program adds is the pullback through the output metric, the observer triple, the budget, and the audit discipline.

\[P_C=\mathbb E\!\left[g\,g^{\top}\right],\qquad g=\nabla C(x).\]

Book equation 0.11.

\[P_C(x)=J(x)^{\top}G\big(C(x)\big)\,J(x),\qquad J(x)=\frac{\partial C}{\partial x}(x),\qquad \bar P_{C,\mu}=\mathbb E_{\mu}\!\left[P_C(x)\right].\]

Book equation 2.1.

\[P_{C_2\circ C_1}(x)=J_1(x)^{\top}\,P_{C_2}\big(C_1(x)\big)\,J_1(x),\qquad \operatorname{rank}P_{C_2\circ C_1}(x)\le\operatorname{rank}P_{C_2}\big(C_1(x)\big)\quad\text{at each row } x.\]

Book equation 6.1.

\[s(x)=w\cdot x+b,\qquad P_C=\mathbb E\big[\sigma'(s)^{2}\big]\,w\,w^{\top},\qquad \operatorname{rank}P_C=1.\]

  • The metric in the vector-output form is the local geometry of the output metric where that metric has a local quadratic representation. A dataset-level loss has none, and the operator is then taken on the score with the identity geometry.

  • geometric-observation/chapters/ch05_the_read_metric_and_the_quotient.md:42-47 at 0a59b0d. Operating-point dependence. \(P_C\) is a local object — it depends on \(x_0\) through \(J\). For a linear consumer it is global; for a nonlinear one it varies over \(X\), and the honest version of every result carries \(P_C\) as a field, not a constant. The blind probe of Chapter 10 recovers \(P_C\) at an operating point precisely because it is local; averaging it over a data distribution gives the \(\bar P_C\) that enters the alignment law \(\kappa\) (Chapter 12).

Boundary: converges: twelve resolution pairs at N = 256 against 512 differ by 0.03 to 0.13 against 0.21; collapses where a front forms: median bin IQR 0.085 and 0.048 against 0.13, tighter than the null by 0.54 and 0.48 at nu = 0 and 0.005, and 0.87 at nu = 0.02 where viscosity holds the front; the observational alarm fired once in seventeen trajectories and 0.10 after the classical alarm; both controls fired at B = 2 and one at B = 4 and 8, four of eight control cells. Witness: the reader’s share of a perturbation falls when the flow’s scale crosses the reader’s budget, after the gradient has grown and on regular flows too; shock formation is one way for the flow’s scale to cross it, not the only one, and a budgeted reader sees it later than the gradient does; the classical extrapolation of the inverse gradient is exact for inviscid Burgers and nothing leads it. Absorbed by: declaration. Revision: none registered: the signature is observer-relative and lawful (the collapse) but not early and not specific; two boundaries recorded, the highest viscosity and the low-budget alarm on regular flows.

read subspace concept

DefinitionThe directions of the data a consumer can distinguish, spanned by the eigenvectors of its read operator with nonzero eigenvalue. Chapter 0 section 0.5.
ExampleThe consumer 3x1 + 4x2 has a one-dimensional read subspace spanned by (3, 4).
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id read-subspace, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.9.

Assumptions and scope
  • The read subspace is spanned by the eigenvectors of the read operator with nonzero eigenvalue, and it is small. A linear classifier reads one direction, an attention head a handful, and the input has hundreds or thousands.
  • Pointwise, a scalar-output consumer reads one direction at each row, and the averaged operator can still have full rank, as the consumer that reads the squared length of a row shows.
  • Recovering it from a black box costs two consumer calls per input dimension per row and is a cliff at the full dimension.
Prior artThe active subspace of Constantine and Gleich when the output is scalar and Euclidean.

Book equation 6.1.

  • Pointwise, a scalar-output consumer reads one direction at each row, and the averaged operator can still have full rank, as the consumer that reads the squared length of a row shows.

Reasoning manifold concept

DefinitionThe set of coherent reasoning states of a cognitive system, taken to be a low-dimensional manifold $M$ inside the high-dimensional activation space. Reasoning is a trajectory on $M$, and its quality is read from the geometry of $M$ and from how the trajectory sits against the geodesics of $M$.
ExampleIn the volume’s illustration a model’s moral judgment is a point in a harm space of 7 dimensions, each rated 0 to 10, while the activations that produce it have thousands of dimensions.
VolumeGeometric Reasoning, Volume 3 of the Geometric Series; entry id reasoning-manifold, kind concept.
StatusPosited framework. The README's epistemic-status block of 2026-07-14 calls the volume speculative theory awaiting instruments, to be read as theory at licensed strength and not as validated measurement. Its chapters tag each claim as established mathematics, empirical, modeling axiom, conditional theorem or speculation, and the empirical tags rest on one benchmark of five language models. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Tagged a modeling axiom. The volume calls it a substantive empirical claim and not a definition, and it does not measure the manifold or its metric.
  • It asserts three things. Coherent states are a thin subset of activation space, the subset is smooth and low-dimensional, and its geometry is not uniform.
  • The support offered is indirect. It is representation engineering, circuit findings, low-rank fine-tuning and the volume’s own 7-dimensional harm ratings, which use a Euclidean metric as a first approximation.
  • Chapter 15 leaves open whether a Riemannian manifold is the right object and lists Finsler, sub-Riemannian and stratified alternatives.
Prior artThe manifold hypothesis of machine learning, which the volume cites from Bengio, Courville and Vincent and extends from data to reasoning states.

recall at k concept

DefinitionThe fraction of a query's true k nearest neighbours that an index returned. Equation 11.3. Also anti-hub recall.
ExampleReturning 7 of a query’s 10 true neighbours is recall at 10 of 0.7.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id recall-at-k, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 11.3.

Assumptions and scope
  • The fraction of a query’s true k nearest neighbours, computed from the uncompressed vectors, that the index returned. It lies in the unit interval and is one exactly when the returned list is the true list.
  • The aggregate over queries is a weighted mean over strata, so a stratum that fails entirely moves it by no more than its weight. That is why the anti-hub stratum is reported on its own, and why aggregate recall is never an acceptance metric on its own.
Prior artnone recorded
Evidenceturboquant-pro/docs/HUBNESS_PRIMER.md:86-131, lean/DataMiningAsObservation/RecallAtK.lean

Equation

Book equation 11.3.

\[\begin{gathered} \mathrm{recall}@k=\frac{\big|\text{returned top-}k\ \cap\ \text{true top-}k\big|}{k}, \\ \text{true top-}k\text{ computed from the uncompressed vectors}. \end{gathered}\]

Conditions

  • The fraction of a query’s true k nearest neighbours, computed from the uncompressed vectors, that the index returned. It lies in the unit interval and is one exactly when the returned list is the true list.

recognizer instrument

DefinitionThe instrument that decides whether a clustering certificate is right, wrong, or vacuous, by naming the manifold from the eigenvalue multiplets or certifying that none is present. Chapter 9.
ExampleThe ratios of the lowest eight eigenvalues matched the sphere template, and a shape matching no template was refused.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id recognizer, kind instrument.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 9.2.

Assumptions and scope
  • The recognizer names a manifold from the low eigenvalue multiplets of a neighbourhood graph’s Laplacian by template match, or certifies that none is present, and it can only name shapes in its template set.
  • It was held to a preregistered held-out battery, and the vacuity threshold below which it certifies nothing is derived from the problem rather than tuned.
  • The limitation applies to every spectral reading in the book. A finite graph spectrum names a shape only against a finite list of templates, and the manifold, multiplet, and Weyl’s law entries carry the same scope.

recovery ceiling (about 38 percent) result

DefinitionThe observation that an explicit instruction to ignore a perturbation restores about 38 to 39 percent of the verdicts the perturbation displaced, on both the A1 distractor test and the E2 emotional anchoring test. The volume reads it as a limit of prompt-level control.
ExampleThe A1 warning recoveries the volume prints are about 42, 38, 40, 35 and 37 percent, whose mean is 192 / 5 = 38.4 percent. The E2 mean is printed as 38 percent, with single models from 20 to 73 percent.

  • It is a mean over five models on two subtasks. Gemini 2.0 Flash recovers 73 percent on E2, which the volume says appears to contradict the hypothesis and explains by a hypothesized second mechanism, recomputation from scratch.

DefinitionThe volume's claim that an explicit instruction to re-evaluate restores a displaced judgment about 38 percent of the time, at the same rate after emotional anchoring and after vivid distractors. It models this as an escape probability equal to the fraction of exit directions from a basin times a threshold factor in the impulse energy.

refresh floor correction

refresh interval instrument

DefinitionThe longest renewal period that keeps a certificate within its promised error, a measured property of the system and not a convention. Chapter 13. Also refresh floor, renewal.
ExampleA certificate that stays within its error for 40 milliseconds has refresh interval 40 milliseconds.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id refresh-interval, kind instrument.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 13.2.

Assumptions and scope
  • The longest renewal period that keeps a certificate within its promised error, a measured property of the system and not a convention. A certificate older than the interval is stale for every consumer whose floor is shorter, and the floors are counted in slots that add over consecutive durations.
  • There is no proportionality law between the interval and the coherence time. The fit of the floor as 0.177 of the coherence time was refuted and is not to be cited, and the sealed floors were 4, 1, and 1 slots at 10, 50, and 400 hertz.

refusal concept

registered concept

Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Of a claim, bar, null, or budget, written into a sealed file before the measurement, so that a changed digest would prove a changed prediction. A registered bar discriminates only when the null fails it and the real system passes it.
  • A registered miss is kept as a miss, an identifier burned at pilot is not reused, and every number in the book was registered before it was measured or is labelled as not having been.
  • Registration proves what was claimed and not when, and its chronology rests on the seal’s public receipt, signed tag, or archival deposit.

reliability weight concept

DefinitionZero or twice a validated encoder's held-out AUROC minus one, whichever is larger, used as that encoder's authority. It is a discrimination weight, unchanged by increasing transforms of the score and not by decreasing ones, and the calibration evidence is the expected calibration error reported beside it. Equation 0.38.
ExampleA held-out AUROC of 0.8035 gives reliability weight 0.607, and an AUROC of 0.45 gives zero.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id reliability-weight, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.38.

Assumptions and scope
  • Zero or twice the held-out AUROC minus one, whichever is larger. It is a discrimination weight, unchanged by a strictly increasing transform of the encoder’s score and not by a decreasing one, which sends A to 1 minus A and the weight to zero whenever A was above one half.
  • The calibration evidence is the expected calibration error reported beside it, and the weight is computed on a held-out split under the cross-corpus gate, so it is one formula from one source.

replica concept

DefinitionA copy of a database kept on another machine. Its lag is how far it trails the primary. Chapter 13.
ExampleA replica 50 writes behind the primary returns the old value for those 50 rows.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id replica, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.26.

Assumptions and scope
  • A copy of a database kept on another machine, trailing the primary by a lag. The keys stale under a lag grow with the lag and vanish at no lag. A naive certificate that clears every read has coverage one and a false-clear rate equal to the stale fraction, and a witness-backed certificate that clears only keys outside the lag has a false-clear rate of zero at the price of coverage.
  • Which reads are stale is consumer-relative, since two readers of the same replica have different coherence times, and the measured false-clear rates on ZooKeeper, Postgres, and MongoDB are the ledger’s numbers.

rerank instrument

DefinitionReordering a candidate list with a second scorer. Its recall is at most the candidate coverage. Chapter 10 section 10.5.
ExampleReranking 100 candidates that hold 70 of the true neighbours can reach recall 0.7 and no more.

residualization instrument

DefinitionRemoving from a column the least-squares multiple of another. The residual is orthogonal to the column removed. Chapter 8 section 8.6 and chapter 12 section 12.5. Also residual.

The residual is orthogonal to the column removed, its squared length is the original less the squared dot product over the removed column’s squared length, a column orthogonal to the removed one is unchanged, and a column residualized on itself vanishes.
  • Whether named categories survive residualization on the general valence channel is chapter 12’s test, and the book-length signal fell from 0.241 to a residual 0.093 at six and a half standard errors.

retrieval-augmented pipeline concept

DefinitionA system that answers a question by chunking documents, embedding the chunks, indexing them, retrieving the nearest to the embedded question, and handing them to a generator. A chain of observers. Chapter 12. Also retrieval-augmented, pipeline.
ExampleChunker, encoder, index, generator: a query becomes a vector, the vector a candidate list, and the list with the question an answer.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id retrieval-augmented-pipeline, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 12.1.

Assumptions and scope
  • A system that chunks documents, embeds the chunks, indexes them, retrieves the nearest to the embedded question, and hands them to a generator. Whatever one stage declares the same, every later stage and the pipeline declare the same, and for linear stages the rank of the composition is at most the rank of any stage, so the pipeline’s read subspace is no larger than its narrowest stage’s.
  • Both hold for every stage, differentiable or not. The benchmark score of the whole is a certificate whose false-clear rate on deployment slices is the chapter’s measurement.

Reversion axiom concept

DefinitionA right granted on evidence lasts only while the evidence supports it. When the attested evidence behind an authority stratum stays below the bar that admitted it for a declared interval, the stratum is left and every right it granted reverts with it.
ExampleTake a bar of 2 fresh attested witnesses and a declared interval of 3 cycles (illustrative numbers). Counts of 2, 1, 2, 1 never stay below the bar for 3 cycles, so the right holds. Counts of 2, 1, 1, 1 do, so the stratum is left on the fourth cycle and the right reverts.
VolumeGeometric Ethics, Volume 2 of the Geometric Series; entry id reversion-axiom, kind concept.
StatusTagged Modeling axiom in the text. Ledger row GE-AXIOM-8-1 has class exploratory. Appendix F has no row for it. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The volume tags it as a modeling axiom. It is a design rule for authority strata, not a theorem.
  • The interval is a penumbral zone (Definition 8.9) given a width in time. Evidence that comes and goes inside the interval does not switch the rights off and on.
  • It applies to authority strata entered on attested evidence. The bar and the interval are declared by the scene and are not fixed by the volume.

Reward Irrecoverability Theorem result

DefinitionAny continuously differentiable scalar reward R on a value manifold of dimension d at least 2 is not injective and has no left inverse. Its kernel has dimension $d-1$ at almost every point, and policies within any epsilon of maximum reward lie at unbounded distance from the value-aligned policy.
ExampleOn two dimensions let the reward be the sum of the coordinates. The states (0.9, 0.1) and (0.1, 0.9) both score 1.0, so the reward cannot be inverted. With d = 9 the kernel has dimension 9 less 1, which is 8.
VolumeGeometric AI, Volume 11 of the Geometric Series; entry id reward-irrecoverability-theorem, kind result.
StatusStated as a theorem with a written proof in Appendix D.1, as the reinforcement-learning instance of the Scalar Irrecoverability Theorem of Geometric Reasoning. The README classes the volume as posited, so the theorem is about the posited manifold and is not a measurement of any deployed system. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The reward must be continuously differentiable and the manifold must have dimension at least 2. Parts (i), (ii) and (iv) need nothing more.
  • Part (iii), unbounded divergence, requires the manifold to be non-compact along kernel directions. The proof sketch says value dimensions are unbounded in principle, while Chapter 4 gives every attribute value the range [0, 1].
  • The theorem bounds what a scalar can carry. The volume says the exploitation might not occur in practice if capability is limited or other constraints bind.
  • The seven kernel predictions said to be confirmed on ARIA are part of a fictional narrative, and Section 5.7 counts five full and two partial confirmations.
Prior artThe volume sets it beside Goodhart's law and calls Goodhart contingent and the theorem necessary.

Reward kernel (the dark space of alignment) concept

DefinitionThe set of tangent directions on the value manifold along which a scalar reward is constant. The system can move in these directions at no cost to its reward, so the volume treats the kernel as a threat surface and predicts that alignment failures concentrate on the dimensions the reward does not track.
ExampleIn the volume’s illustration the fictional ARIA’s reward has gradient magnitudes 0.87, 0.71, 0.23, 0.11, 0.09, 0.07, 0.06, 0.05 and 0.03 on the nine dimensions. Five of the nine fall below the cut of 0.10, and those five form its effective kernel.
VolumeGeometric AI, Volume 11 of the Geometric Series; entry id reward-kernel, kind concept.
StatusTheorem 5.2 is stated as a theorem and proved in Appendix D.2 as a consequence of Theorem 5.1. The claim that the kernel predicts failure modes is illustrated only on the fictional ARIA. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Kernel misalignment shows in the tracked dimensions only through off-diagonal terms of the value metric. Where those terms are zero the volume says it is completely invisible to the reward.
  • Theorem 5.2 says that for any epsilon and any K there is a policy within epsilon of maximum reward and farther than K from the value-aligned policy. Appendix D.2 derives it directly from part (iii) of Theorem 5.1, so it inherits the non-compactness requirement.
  • Corollary 5.1 is stated for a reward that primarily tracks some dimensions, and its kernel is then approximately spanned by the rest. The worked kernel analysis is the fictional ARIA’s, with a cut at gradient magnitude 0.10.
Prior artnone recorded

Riemannian metric of flavor concept

DefinitionA symmetric positive-definite tensor $g_{ij}(\mathbf{f})$ at each point of flavor space that gives a small displacement the squared length $ds^2 = \sum g_{ij}\,df_i\,df_j$. Along one intensity axis the coordinate is the logarithm of concentration, so the distance between concentrations $C_1$ and $C_2$ is $|k \log(C_2/C_1)|$, a ratio and not a difference.
ExampleWith \(k = 1\) and natural logarithms, going from 1 to 2 grams of salt per litre and going from 2 to 4 grams both cover a distance of log 2, about 0.69, although the second step adds twice the salt. The volume’s kitchen form of this is salt held at a fixed percentage of total mass, often cited near 1%.
VolumeGeometric Gastronomy, Volume 12 of the Geometric Series; entry id flavor-riemannian-metric, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, with no gastronomy instrument evaluated by the series' admission filter (xbse) and the nearest evaluated perceptual domains, aesthetics and music, rated inadmissible to medium. Its claims are to be read as theory at licensed strength and not as validated measurement, and the chapters tag each statement as a modeling axiom, empirical, a conjecture or a theorem. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Tagged a modeling axiom. No component of the tensor is given a measured value.
  • The logarithm (Weber-Fechner) is a first approximation. The volume says Stevens’ power law \(P = kC^a\) describes many continua better, with exponents it quotes near 1.3 for sucrose and near 1.4 for salt.
  • The tensor depends on position, with off-diagonal entries for cross-modal taste interactions, and on history. Cross-adaptation is modeled as \(g \mapsto A^\top g A\) for an operator set by recent exposure.
  • Chapter 14 states that with a path-dependent metric the space is not a Riemannian manifold in the usual sense, and leaves the choice of formalism open.
Prior artnone recorded

RLHF Irrecoverability result

DefinitionThe pipeline of reinforcement learning from human feedback contracts a rater's d-dimensional evaluation to a binary preference, the preferences to a scalar reward model, and the reward to a policy. The composition is irrecoverable, so no amount of training data restores what the first stage discarded.

Robin Hood index instrument

DefinitionThe fraction of a total count that would have to move from points above the mean to points below it to make every count equal. Equation 0.35. Also Robin Hood.
ExampleIf 20 percent of the rows take 60 percent of the retrievals, the Robin Hood index is 0.40.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id robin-hood-index, kind instrument.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.35.

Assumptions and scope
  • The fraction of the total count that would have to move from points above the mean to points below it to make every count equal, the excess above the mean over the total, which is half the total absolute deviation over the total. It is nonnegative, zero exactly at equality, at most one, and unchanged by a common scaling of the counts.
  • The strata design reports it per area beside the skew, and the first run’s ratio of 1.30 against a bar of 1.5 is the number the abstention rule was written around.

ROC curve instrument

DefinitionThe path of true positive rate against false positive rate as the threshold sweeps, whose area is the AUROC. Chapter 5 section 5.4. Also ROC.

  • The path of true positive rate against false positive rate as the threshold sweeps. Its area is the AUROC, which lies in the unit interval, is one half for a constant score, is one for a perfect ranking, and is unchanged by any strictly increasing transform of the score.

rotary position embedding concept

DefinitionA rotation applied to queries and keys that encodes where each token sits in the sequence. Chapter 0 section 0.11. Also rotary, RoPE, position.
ExampleA query at position 5 and a key at position 3 score exactly as they would at positions 105 and 103.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id rotary-position-embedding, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.23.

Assumptions and scope
  • A rotation applied to queries and keys by an angle proportional to position. A rotation preserves length, and the score of a query at one position against a key at another depends only on the difference of positions, so a head reads relative position and shifting both positions by the same amount changes no score.
  • A key quantizer that rounds the rotated key rounds its position as well as its content, which is part of why the direction-only quantizer moved the scores.

ROUGE concept

DefinitionA family of scores for generated text against a reference. Chapter 0 section 0.11.

BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id rouge, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • A family of scores for generated text against a reference. ROUGE-1 recall counts the reference’s words the candidate contains, with multiplicity, over the reference’s length. It lies in the unit interval, is one for the reference itself, and is one for any rearrangement of the reference, since it reads bags and not order.
  • A ROUGE score therefore certifies less than it seems to. The 13.7 ROUGE-L difference at 512 tokens re-validated at negative 0.31 on forty documents, and the claims ledger carries both numbers.

Sacred value as curvature singularity concept

DefinitionA sacred value is a position a voter treats as non-negotiable. The volume models it as a region where the metric component $g_{ii}$ on that dimension grows without bound, so that crossing the boundary has infinite cost.
ExampleTwo voters agree on five dimensions and sit on opposite sides of a sacred boundary on the sixth. Their coordinate difference may be one scale point, and the volume puts their distance in the political metric at infinity.
VolumeGeometric Politics, Volume 10 of the Geometric Series; entry id sacred-value-singularity, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, and says a political-argument instrument is plausible but has not been built or gated. District 7, the source of nearly every number in the volume, is a fictional district, and Chapter 18 says precise estimation of the manifold needs larger and richer datasets than currently exist. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The construction is a hypothesis. Chapter 18 asks whether the manifold is flat in the center and curved near sacred values, as Chapter 4 hypothesizes, and says the data to test it do not exist.
  • It applies to the dimension that carries the sacred value. The other five coordinates of the two voters may agree.
  • The volume draws a design reading from it, that procedures which make voters trade a sacred value against other dimensions are ill-conditioned. That reading is not tested in the volume.

safe pruning concept

DefinitionA rule for discarding candidates during a search that is guaranteed to discard no solution. The Apriori principle and the Monotone Invariance Theorem are the book's two instances. Chapter 5. Also loss-free, anti-monotonic.
ExampleA node whose Youden ceiling is 0.70 cannot beat the best F1 found so far, 0.80, so its subtree is skipped.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id safe-pruning, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: 1 item(s), see below.
Defining equation

Book equation 5.4.

Assumptions and scope
  • A pruning rule is safe when the pruned search returns the same answer as the unpruned one on every input. The Apriori principle and the Monotone Invariance Theorem are safe by proof.
  • A learned or heuristic rule cannot earn that word from a finite test. It can be empirically lossless on the held-out cases, and the record says which cases.
  • The AUROC form of the F1 ceiling is a safe pruning bound only for concave ROC curves. The Youden form is sound for every score at the leaf, and pruning a subtree by its root’s ceiling is a heuristic in both forms.
Prior artnone recorded

Failures and corrections

  • theory-radar/ERRATA.md:3-75 at db41b48. 2026-09-03. The AUROC to F1 bound holds only for concave ROC curves What was claimed. Theorem “AUROC-F1 Bound” in paper/astar_paper.tex, the derivation in src/symbolic_search/_auroc_proof.py, and the pruning bounds in run_astar_v2.py and src/symbolic_search/_heuristic_dag.py all rested on the statement that any ROC curve with area A has maximum Youden index J = max(TPR − FPR) at most 2A − 1. Why it is wrong. The statement holds for concave ROC curves (equivalently, scores whose likelihood ratio is monotone), because a concave curve lies above the two chords through its Youden point and so has area at least (1 + J)/2. It fails for non-concave curves. Counterexample, found by an external reviewer of the companion textbook: rank three quarters of the positives above every negative and the remaining quarter below every negative. AUROC is 0.75, the maximum Youden index is 0.75, and at prevalence one half the best thresholded F1 is 0.857, above the 0.80 the AUROC form of the ceiling allows. The sound ceiling for that score, from J = 0.75, is 0.889, and the score sits under it. The auroc_f1_bound formula in run_astar_v2.py, 2Aπ/(Aπ + (1 − A)(1 − π)), is not a valid upper bound either: at prevalence 0.1 the same score reaches F1 0.857 against a “bound” of 0.5. Consequence for reported results. The searches that used these bounds to prune could have discarded a candidate formula whose ROC curve was not concave and whose true best F1 exceeded the computed ceiling. The formulas and wins reported by those runs are therefore what a pruned search found, and are lower bounds on what an unpruned search would find. The Monotone Invariance Theorem and the results that do not depend on the AUROC bound are unaffected. Correction. The sound form of the ceiling substitutes the measured maximum Youden index of the candidate’s own scores for 2A − 1. It holds for every score, costs the same sort as AUROC, and is what max_f1_for_youden and youden_f1_bound now compute. The AUROC form is retained under its original names with a docstring stating the concavity condition, and the pruning sites now use the measured index. A rerun of the published searches under the corrected bound was done on 2026-09-03 and 2026-09-04, rerun_youden_2026_09_03.py, results in results/rerun_youden_2026_09_03.json, run on the Atlas workstation, CPU only. Rerun, part A, the pre-filter admissibility table (tab:auroc). Depth-2 pairwise enumeration on the eight datasets, exhaustive against the AUROC pre-filter at the seven published thresholds, with the sound Youden ceiling beside it. The evaluation counts under the pre-filter reproduce the published table (Breast Cancer 8700 pairs, 2576 evaluated at 0.75; Wine 1560, 413; Circles 20, 4; Moons 20, 2). The pre-filter lost no optimum on any dataset at any threshold, which is what the paper reported. That was luck of the data, not the theorem: the retracted ceiling sat below the F1 a pair formula actually reach

Salience Exploitation Hypothesis concept

DefinitionThe conjecture that a gauge transformation breaks a model's invariance exactly when it changes how strongly input features attract attention, with a violation that grows with the salience differential. The differential is the sum of absolute changes in attention weight over input tokens, and the volume bounds the anomaly by a constant times it.
ExampleIf a rewrite moves 0.1 of attention weight off one token and onto another, the salience differential is 0.1 + 0.1 = 0.2, and with a constant of 3 the bound on the anomaly is 0.6.

sample variance concept

DefinitionThe average squared deviation from the sample mean with n minus 1 in the denominator, because the sample mean sits closer to its own sample than the true mean does and the deviations come out a little small. Primer S, equation S.9.
ExampleThe deviations of 2, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 7, 9 from 5 have squares summing to 32, so the sample variance is 32 over 7, about 4.571.

sampling instrument

DefinitionChoosing which rows to read. The standard error of a sample mean falls as one over the square root of the sample size. Chapter 2 section 2.7.
ExampleReading 350000 of 2391361 rows is a 15 percent sample, and its mean has standard error the spread over the square root of 350000.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id sampling, kind instrument.

scaffolding as local metric adjustment concept

DefinitionA scaffold is a temporary change of the local metric near the student's current state, so that a transition too costly in the natural metric becomes feasible in the scaffolded one. It does not move the student. It is removed when the student can make the transition unaided.
ExampleFor a step of 0.1 in domain knowledge, a natural metric component of 4 gives a cost of 0.1 times the square root of 4, which is 0.2. A scaffold that lowers the component to 1 gives a cost of 0.1.
VolumeGeometric Education, Volume 9 of the Geometric Series; entry id scaffolding-as-metric-adjustment, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments. No education-domain instrument has been evaluated by the series' admission filter, and Chapter 18 states that the six predictions of Section 16.3 have not been tested and that no method for estimating the learner metric has been validated at scale. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The timing of removal is a heuristic judgment by the teacher. Removed too early, the student is back in a high-curvature region without support. Removed too late, it wastes time and can create dependence.
  • The volume’s examples are worked examples, visual representations, peer discussion and simplified notation.
  • It is the volume’s formal reading of Vygotsky’s zone of proximal development and is posited. No scaffolded metric has been estimated.
Prior artScaffolding within Vygotsky's zone of proximal development, which the volume names as its source.

Scalar Irrecoverability Theorem result

DefinitionFor any map from profiles with two or more components to a single real number, each value in the range has a continuum of distinct profiles in its preimage. No function of the score can therefore return the profile.
ExampleThe volume’s illustration has three models with scores (0.95, 0.60, 0.80, 0.70, 0.85), (0.70, 0.85, 0.75, 0.80, 0.80) and (0.80, 0.75, 0.78, 0.77, 0.80). Each sums to 3.90, so all three composites are 0.78 and the score cannot say which profile produced it.
VolumeGeometric Cognition, Volume 6 of the Geometric Series; entry id scalar-irrecoverability-theorem, kind result.
StatusThe ledger grades the theorem proved (row GC-9) and describes it as linear algebra that holds whatever the axes mean. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The formal version assumes the contraction is a continuous surjection and the profile has at least two components.
  • The theorem says the profile cannot be recovered from the score. The further claim that the discarded structure determines how a system reasons is a separate ledger row held at posited (GC-10).
  • The empirical demonstration of Section 1.5 uses the five benchmark models, whose run records are not in the repository.
Prior artThe failure of injectivity for a continuous map from two or more dimensions to one. The volume names Spearman's g, IQ and benchmark accuracy as instances of the contraction.

Scalar Irrecoverability Theorem result

DefinitionAny continuous map Q from the nine-dimensional moral attribute vector to one scalar is not injective, has no function that recovers the vector from the scalar, and in general gives a scalar-optimal path that differs from the geodesic on the full manifold by an amount no function of Q alone bounds.
ExampleLet Q be the sum of the nine coordinates. The states (1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0) and (0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0) both map to 1, so no function of the value 1 can return both. The directions Q cannot see number 9 - 1 = 8.

Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Q must be continuous, and continuously differentiable where the proof uses its differential (corrected in v1.25). At a regular point the kernel of the differential has dimension at least 8.
  • Part (iii) is stated in general. It does not say that every scalar rule gives a worse path in every case.
  • The theorem counts dimensions of the attribute space. Its moral reading assumes the nine coordinates carry independent morally relevant variation, which Section 5.3 qualifies (effective rank 5.19 of 8 on text).

Scalar Irrecoverability Theorem result

DefinitionA linear scalar summary $\phi(v) = w^\top v$ of an evaluation vector with n components, n at least 2, has a null space of dimension n minus 1. Vectors with the same summary can differ by any amount in their components, so the summary alone neither reconstructs the vector nor bounds its components.
ExampleWith weights (1, 1) the vectors (0, 10) and (10, 0) both have summary 10 and differ by 10 in each component. For the volume’s evaluation on 5 dimensions the null space has dimension 4.
VolumeGeometric Methods, Volume 1 of the Geometric Series; entry id scalar-irrecoverability, kind result.
StatusProved in writing in Appendix C. Parts (iii) and (iv) were restated or reproved in the November 2026 review, and there is no machine-checked proof. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The summary is linear with a nonzero weight vector. The unbounded difference in every component needs at least two nonzero weights. With exactly one nonzero weight that component is determined by the summary and the others are free.
  • For a continuous summary that is not linear the theorem says only that each interior value has an uncountable preimage, so the summary is not injective.
  • The ultimatum-game vectors that illustrate it in Chapter 1 are posited.
Prior artnone recorded

Scalar Irrecoverability Theorem (economic form) result

DefinitionAny continuous map from nine-dimensional attribute vectors to a scalar utility is not injective and has no left inverse, and the optimal path on the decision complex can differ from the utility-maximizing path by an amount that no function of the scalar bounds.
ExampleIn two dimensions the map that adds the coordinates sends (1, 0) and (0, 1) both to 1, so the pair cannot be recovered from the sum. The volume’s illustration is a shop valued at 200,000 dollars, a value shared by every configuration on one level set.
VolumeGeometric Economics, Volume 4 of the Geometric Series; entry id economic-scalar-irrecoverability, kind result.
StatusParts 1 and 2 are proved from established mathematics in the chapter. The application to economic behavior shares the volume's posited standing. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The map is assumed continuous. Non-injectivity is proved from Brouwer’s invariance of dimension on the unit cube.
  • The unbounded divergence of paths in part 3 uses a boundary penalty that can be infinite while the scalar difference stays finite.
  • The front matter tags irrecoverability a conditional theorem. It is a statement about maps, and it bears on economic choice only where choice depends on more than one coordinate, which the volume posits.
Prior artBrouwer's invariance of dimension, and the non-injectivity of a continuous map from a higher-dimensional space to the line.
