Scalar Irrecoverability Theorem for benchmark profiles result

DefinitionIf the performance profiles of a set of models are mutually Pareto-non-dominated, so that each model beats each other on some dimension and loses on another, then every weighted-sum score with non-negative weights ranks some model below another that it beats on a subset of at least two dimensions.
ExampleOn the volume’s two metacognition scores, (0.700, 0.350) averages 0.525 and (0.094, 0.723) averages 0.409, so the average ranks the first model higher although the second is better on the second score.
VolumeGeometric Reasoning, Volume 3 of the Geometric Series; entry id benchmark-scalar-irrecoverability, kind result.
StatusA conditional theorem with a proof that leans on the benchmark data for one step. The crossing profiles it is applied to are measurements on five models. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The hypothesis is that no profile dominates another. Where one model is at least as good on every dimension, a monotone score can respect the ordering.
  • Tagged a conditional theorem. The proof’s step to a subset of size two is not general and appeals to the measured profiles of the five models.
  • The volume states it in three forms. Section 13.6 speaks of any composite score, Theorem 13.1 of weighted sums, and Theorem A10.1 of strictly monotone functions that would preserve the ordering on every axis.
  • It concerns loss of ordering information between incomparable profiles. It does not say that a score chosen for a stated application is wrong for that application.
Prior artThe fact that a partial order of Pareto-incomparable points has no order-preserving map to a line that reflects every coordinate. The volume attributes the theorem to Geometric Methods, Chapter 1.

Defining equation

  • The number a classifier produces per row before a threshold turns it into a decision. Every decision at every threshold is a function of the scores’ ordering, so a strictly increasing recalibration of the scores with the matching recalibration of the threshold changes no decision.

sealed instrument

DefinitionOf a prediction, committed with its hash recorded before the measurement was run, so that anyone with the repository can verify it has not changed, and with a public push, a signed tag, or an archival deposit to fix when. Chapter 0 section 0.12.

BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id sealed, kind instrument.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: 1 item(s), see below.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Of a prediction, committed with its hash recorded before the measurement, so that anyone with the repository can verify that the file has not changed. The hash proves the content. The time it existed is established by the public push, the signed tag, the transparency log, or the archival deposit that the seal names, since a commit’s dates are supplied fields.

seasoning fixed point concept

DefinitionA dish is properly seasoned at a point $\mathbf{f}^\star$ that is a fixed point of taste-and-adjust, a local maximum of the hedonic function $H$. No small admissible move raises $H$, the gradient is about zero and the Hessian is negative semidefinite.
ExampleOn one salt axis with \(H(s) = -(s - 2)^2\), the gradient at 2 is 0 and the second derivative is -2, so 2 is the fixed point. A step to 2.1 or to 1.9 lowers \(H\) by 0.01 either way. The function is illustrative.
VolumeGeometric Gastronomy, Volume 12 of the Geometric Series; entry id seasoning-fixed-point, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, with no gastronomy instrument evaluated by the series' admission filter (xbse) and the nearest evaluated perceptual domains, aesthetics and music, rated inadmissible to medium. Its claims are to be read as theory at licensed strength and not as validated measurement, and the chapters tag each statement as a modeling axiom, empirical, a conjecture or a theorem. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Tagged a modeling axiom. It rests on the posited hedonic function of Chapter 5.
  • The fixed point is stable only against small moves. Seasoning finds the nearest peak and not the highest, and a distant configuration can beat it.
  • Because the inverse operators are lossy, the volume’s prudent dynamics is small steps from below. Under-seasoning stops short of the peak and over-seasoning overshoots it.
  • Section 8.4 restates balance as a tolerance region around a target and not a single point.

seasoning operators (salt, acid, fat, heat) concept

DefinitionFour maps from flavor space to itself. Salt stretches the savory component by a factor $\lambda > 1$, as $T(\mathbf{f}) = \mathbf{f} + (\lambda - 1)P_{sav}\mathbf{f}$. Acid rotates the vector toward a brightness axis. Fat is a low-pass filter on the temporal flavor curve. Heat is a flow that releases volatiles at temperature-dependent rates. They do not commute.
ExampleTake the vector (3, 4) with the savory subspace as the first axis and \(\lambda = 1.5\). Salt gives (4.5, 4). On the vector (0, 4), which has no savory component, the same operator changes nothing, the volume’s point that salt cannot make a savory direction from nothing. The numbers are illustrative.
VolumeGeometric Gastronomy, Volume 12 of the Geometric Series; entry id seasoning-operators, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, with no gastronomy instrument evaluated by the series' admission filter (xbse) and the nearest evaluated perceptual domains, aesthetics and music, rated inadmissible to medium. Its claims are to be read as theory at licensed strength and not as validated measurement, and the chapters tag each statement as a modeling axiom, empirical, a conjecture or a theorem. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Each operator is tagged a modeling axiom. The forms are posited, and none is fitted to data.
  • Salt cannot create a savory direction the dish lacks, and its factor is bounded. Past the bound the dish moves toward the salt vertex and the no-rotation approximation fails.
  • The four are a generating set with approximate inverses, not a basis of a vector space. The volume calls the basis imperfect, since heat bundles a thermal flow with a trigeminal translation.
  • The inverses are lossy. Salt can be added and cannot be cleanly removed.
Prior artThe four elements of Nosrat's Salt, Fat, Acid, Heat (2017).

seed concept

DefinitionThe number that fixes a run's pseudo-randomness. Two runs with the same seed agree only when code, data, environment, and execution are also fixed, and different seeds are necessary but not sufficient for an independent replication. Chapter 8.
ExampleSeed 20260827 fixed the run, and seeds 20260828 and 20260829 were the two replications.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id seed, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 8.1.

Assumptions and scope
  • The number that fixes a run’s pseudo-randomness. Two runs with the same seed reproduce each other only when the code, data, environment, and execution are also fixed, since nondeterministic execution can differ at the same seed, and runs with different seeds are necessary but not sufficient for an independent replication.
  • The standard error over n seeds falls as one over the square root of n, a paired comparison across seeds has smaller variance than an unpaired one exactly when the two arms covary, and a preregistration names its seeds before the run.

Selective Path Dependence (Proposition 13.3) result

DefinitionWith normative relations modelled by a $D_4$ gauge group on the Hohfeldian square, the order in which two considerations are presented changes the judgment only on cross-type paths, where the factors point toward different vertices. On within-type paths the gate elements commute and the Wilson loop is the identity.
ExampleWith the volume’s actions r taking O to C to L to N to O and s exchanging O with C and L with N, applying r then s to O gives s(C) = O, and applying s then r gives r(C) = L. The two orders disagree, and in the volume’s table 2 of 8 scenarios showed an order effect.
VolumeGeometric Communication, Volume 7 of the Geometric Series; entry id selective-path-dependence, kind result.
StatusA proposition whose support is two of eight scenarios in one protocol. The chapter calls it a structural prediction confirmed by that protocol. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The evidence cited is SQND Protocol 2 with 640 evaluations over 8 scenarios. Two scenarios, journalist and teacher, showed path dependence (0.659 and 0.862 in the table) and six did not, with combined chi-squared 72.14 on 16 degrees of freedom.
  • The sorting of the eight scenarios into cross-type and within-type is given after the results table, in the same section.
  • The \(D_4\) group itself rests on a quarter-turn r that cycles the four positions. The chapter says r needs a semantic trigger and is probabilistic, while the correlative exchange s held at 100%.
  • For cross-type paths the proposition says the Wilson loop differs from the identity generically, not always.
Prior artOrder effects in judgment, stated in the vocabulary of lattice gauge theory. Geometric Ethics v1.25 withdrew the dihedral group D4 for Hohfeldian transitions, a withdrawal this volume's text does not record.

Semantic gate concept

DefinitionA map from a triggering feature and a source stratum to a target stratum. The gate fires when the feature satisfies the gate's activation predicate, which takes the value 0 or 1, and it then moves the evaluation from the rules of the source stratum to those of the target. The transition is all or nothing.
ExampleThe phrase you promised takes Liberty to Obligation, at 94 percent in the volume’s Dear Abby table. There is no state that is half obligated, and saying it again from Obligation changes nothing.
VolumeGeometric Ethics, Volume 2 of the Geometric Series; entry id semantic-gate, kind concept.
StatusAppendix F lists Definition 8.8 as a Modeling Axiom, and the ledger row GE-DEF-8-8 is exploratory. The firing rates the volume prints (89 to 97 percent) come from its Dear Abby corpus analysis, which it says was not preregistered. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • A gate acts only from its source stratum. A second promise made in the obligation stratum changes nothing.
  • The volume says the discreteness of gates is an empirical claim, not a stipulation. Its evidence is the Dear Abby corpus and embedding experiments, and no gate result yet comes from a preregistered study of people.
  • Smooth transitions between Hohfeldian states would undermine the stratification theory. The volume lists this among its falsifiers.
  • On the Hohfeldian positions each gate is one V4 operation restricted to the positions it applies from.
Prior artnone recorded

sensitivity concept

DefinitionThe vector of partial derivatives of a consumer with respect to each coordinate of its input, at one point. Equation 0.8.
ExampleFor C(x1, x2) equal to 3x1 + 4x2 the sensitivity is (3, 4) at every row.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id sensitivity, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.8.

Assumptions and scope
  • The sensitivity of a consumer at a row is the vector of partial derivatives of its output with respect to each coordinate, measurable without the formula by a central finite difference at two calls per coordinate.
  • The read operator is the workload average of the sensitivity’s outer product, so its diagonal is the expected squared sensitivity to each feature and its off-diagonal entries are co-sensitivities, not interactions.
  • A gradient-based attribution estimates the sensitivity. Permutation importance, partial dependence, and Shapley values measure other things.
Prior artThe gradient of the consumer at a row, the quantity active-subspace methods average.

Book equation 14.4.

\[\text{attribution}_j(x)\approx g_j(x)\,\delta_j,\qquad \overline{\text{importance}}_j\approx\big(P_C\big)_{jj}=\mathbb E\big[g_j^{2}\big].\]

shard instrument

DefinitionOne partition of an index that is searched separately, with the results merged. The global top k lies inside the union of the shards' top k. Chapter 13.
ExampleEight shards each returning their top 10 hand the merger 80 candidates, among which the global top 10 lies.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id shard, kind instrument.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • One partition of an index that is searched separately, with the results merged. If each shard returns its own top k and the global top k is strict, the global top k lies inside the union of the shards’ answers, so the merge loses nothing and reads at most the number of shards times k candidates.
  • A placement study over 64 shards reported search times taken with the file cache already holding the shards, and a speedup of 63.7 times was fragmentation, so a sharded number names whether it is warm and what the shards were.

silhouette concept

DefinitionFor a row, the difference between its mean distance to the nearest other cluster and its mean distance to its own cluster, divided by the larger of the two. Equation 0.30. Also validity ind.
ExampleA point with mean distance 1 to its own cluster and 4.5 to the nearest other has silhouette 3.5 over 4.5, or 0.778.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id silhouette, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.30.

Assumptions and scope
  • For a row, the difference between its mean distance to the nearest other cluster and its mean distance to its own cluster, over the larger of the two. It lies between minus one and one, is positive exactly when the row is closer to its own cluster, and is unchanged when every distance is scaled by the same factor.
  • It is computed under the identity reader on the distances it is given, so it validates a clustering for that reader and not for a consumer that reads other directions, which is why chapter 9 asks the recognizer to name the manifold instead.

Simpson's paradox concept

DefinitionA reversal of a comparison when groups are combined, which the book reads as an aggregation quotient. Chapter 5. Also Simpson.
ExampleA treatment better in both the young and the old can be worse overall when the two groups are mixed unequally.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id simpsons-paradox, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • A pooled rate is the size-weighted mean of the group rates, so pooling is a quotient that declares the group labels irrelevant, and it can reverse a comparison that holds in every group when the groups have different sizes under the two arms.
  • With equal group sizes under both arms the pooled comparison agrees with a comparison that holds in every group. The book’s answer is the min-over-strata verdict, which never pools.

singular value decomposition concept

DefinitionAny matrix written as a sum of rank-one outer products ordered by size, with orthonormal vectors on both sides, the eigenvector idea for a matrix that is not square. Its right singular vectors are the eigenvectors of A transposed A, and for centered data they are the principal components. Primer L, equations L.16 and L.17.
ExampleRows (1, 1), (1, 0), and (0, 1) have A transposed A with rows (2, 1) and (1, 2), so the singular values are root 3 and 1.

softmax concept

DefinitionThe function that exponentiates a list of numbers and divides by their sum, so that they are positive and add to one. Equation 0.23.
ExampleScores 2, 1, and 0 give weights 0.665, 0.245, and 0.090, which sum to one.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id softmax, kind concept.
Statusrefutes or corrects [refuted] ×2. Corrections: 2 item(s), see below.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.23.

Assumptions and scope
  • The softmax exponentiates a list of scores and divides by the sum, so the weights are positive and add to one. Adding the same constant to every score leaves it unchanged, and a larger score gets a larger weight.
  • As a consumer it reads the scores through their differences, which is why the two proxies for softmax-KL in the ledger, the variance ratio and the projected-variance trace, were refuted.

Sorting versus polarization concept

DefinitionSorting is the alignment of the covariance matrix, with positions on different dimensions becoming correlated through party identity. Polarization is the separation of the party centroids on the manifold. The first concerns second moments and the second concerns means.
ExampleTwo parties have centroids at \((-0.5, -0.5)\) and \((0.5, 0.5)\), a distance of \(\sqrt{2}\), about 1.41. If the variance inside each party falls from 1 to 0.25 the centroids have not moved, so sorting has risen and polarization has not.
VolumeGeometric Politics, Volume 10 of the Geometric Series; entry id sorting-polarization-distinction, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, and says a political-argument instrument is plausible but has not been built or gated. District 7, the source of nearly every number in the volume, is a fictional district, and Chapter 18 says precise estimation of the manifold needs larger and richer datasets than currently exist. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The two are treated as geometrically independent. Either can be high while the other is low.
  • Both produce a bimodal one-dimensional projection, so one axis cannot tell them apart. Telling them apart needs the full covariance structure.
  • The volume’s reading of the 2020s American electorate as high sorting with moderate polarization, with party means about 1.5 standard deviations apart, is stated as approximate.
Prior artnone recorded

Spearman correlation concept

DefinitionThe ordinary correlation between two lists of ranks. Equation 0.14. Also Spearman.
ExampleRanks (1, 2, 3) against (1, 3, 2) give Spearman correlation 0.5.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id spearman-correlation, kind concept.
Statusrefutes or corrects [refuted]. Corrections: 1 item(s), see below.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.14.

Assumptions and scope
  • The ordinary correlation between two lists of ranks, one minus six times the sum of squared rank differences over n(n² − 1). It is at most one, one when the rankings agree, and minus one for three items in opposite orders, and since ranks depend on the ordering alone a strictly increasing transform of either score leaves it unchanged.
  • A high Spearman between a proxy and a consumer’s loss is not a certificate. The variance-ratio proxy with Spearman above 0.9 is a refuted ledger row, and the rank certificate’s floor on Spearman is the strict setting’s guarantee, not a measured correlation.
Prior artnone recorded
Evidencegeometric-observation/claims/LEDGER.md:101, lean/DataMiningAsObservation/Spearman.lean
Reviewednot yet reviewed; generated 2026-11-25 from records at the commits on the provenance page.

Equation

Book equation 0.14.

\[\rho_S=1-\frac{6\sum_i d_i^{2}}{n(n^{2}-1)},\qquad d_i=\text{difference of the two ranks of item } i.\]

Conditions

  • The ordinary correlation between two lists of ranks, one minus six times the sum of squared rank differences over n(n² − 1). It is at most one, one when the rankings agree, and minus one for three items in opposite orders, and since ranks depend on the ordering alone a strictly increasing transform of either score leaves it unchanged.
  • A high Spearman between a proxy and a consumer’s loss is not a certificate. The variance-ratio proxy with Spearman above 0.9 is a refuted ledger row, and the rank certificate’s floor on Spearman is the strict setting’s guarantee, not a measured correlation.

Conditions are curated in entries.toml rather than read from a record.

spectral clustering instrument

DefinitionClustering the rows of the row-normalized spectral embedding, which reads the angle and discards the density. Chapter 3 section 3.3 and chapter 9. Also row normalization.
ExampleRow-normalize the two lowest nontrivial eigenvectors of the Laplacian and run k-means on the angles.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id spectral-clustering, kind instrument.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.19.

Assumptions and scope
  • Clustering the rows of the row-normalized spectral embedding, which reads the angle and discards the density. Row normalization puts every row on the unit sphere, keeps the cosine between rows, and ignores a positive rescaling, and the Laplacian’s quadratic form is nonnegative, zero on constants, and positive across any edge.
  • Ng, Jordan, and Weiss normalized because it improved results, and chapter 3 says why. The Euclidean distance in the embedding converges to degree noise and the angle keeps the geodesics.
  • The row normalization applies to eigenvectors of the normalized Laplacian, whose leading vector is proportional to the square root of the degree and not constant.

Spectral divergence from a corpus prior instrument

DefinitionFit a Gaussian to a work's embeddings and another to a reference corpus, both in a PCA subspace, and compute five divergences between them. They are Kullback-Leibler, Jensen-Shannon, Hellinger, Bhattacharyya, and the Mahalanobis distance of the work's mean from the prior mean.
ExampleIn one dimension, a work with mean 2 against a prior with mean 0 and variance 4 has Mahalanobis distance 2 divided by the prior standard deviation 2, which is 1.
VolumeGeometric Aesthetics, Volume 13 of the Geometric Series; entry id aesthetic-spectral-divergence-channel, kind instrument.
StatusA measured instrument. The closed forms of the divergences are marked proved in Appendix F (F4.2 to F4.5), and the 8 sigma figure is a discovery-run measurement that precedes the genre control. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Both distributions are modeled as multivariate Gaussians. Section 5.7 calls the per-work Gaussian an approximation.
  • In the books discovery run each divergence registers at roughly 8 sigma against rating. That run is before genre control.
  • In music the Hellinger member saturated near 1.0 and the divergences were recomputed in a 32-dimensional subspace.
  • The prior is fitted on the English books corpus and is not neutral. A different corpus gives different distances.

spectral embedding instrument

DefinitionThe coordinates a node receives from its values in the first few nontrivial eigenvectors of the graph Laplacian. Clustering those coordinates is spectral clustering. Chapter 3. Also spectral clustering, row normalization.
ExampleA ring of ten nodes embeds on a circle, and the angle between two nodes’ embeddings tracks their distance along the ring.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id spectral-embedding, kind instrument.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.19.

Assumptions and scope
  • The coordinates a node receives from its values in the first few nontrivial eigenvectors of the graph Laplacian. Row normalization puts every embedded row on the unit sphere, leaves the cosine between rows unchanged, and ignores a positive rescaling of a row, so it is the projection onto the read subspace of the geodesic-rank consumer.
  • Its magnitude converges to degree noise and its angle keeps the geodesics, so the cosine between embedded rows is the right similarity and the Euclidean distance the wrong one. Clustering the normalized coordinates is spectral clustering, and a density reader of the same embedding reads the complementary coordinate.
  • The embedding of equation 0.20 scales each eigenvector entry by the eigenvalue and the degree. Its squared Euclidean distance is the resistance, commute time over volume, exactly for the full spectrum and approximately when only the low modes are kept.

spectral trajectory and its geodesic deviation instrument

DefinitionSlide a window of w frames with hop h across a spectrogram and compute a covariance matrix at each position, giving a sequence $\Sigma_1, \ldots, \Sigma_K$ of SPD matrices. The geodesic deviation is the sum of the log-Euclidean distances between consecutive matrices minus the log-Euclidean distance from $\Sigma_1$ to $\Sigma_K$.
ExampleA spectrogram of 100 frames with window 20 and hop 10 gives (100 - 20)/10 + 1 = 9 matrices. If the three steps of a four-matrix path each have length 1 and the endpoints are 1 apart, the deviation is 3 - 1 = 2.
VolumeGeometric Communication, Volume 7 of the Geometric Series; entry id spectral-trajectory-geodesic-deviation, kind instrument.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments. It says that no communication-domain instrument has been evaluated by the series' admission filter (xbse), that none currently passes its gate, and that the claims are theory at licensed strength and not validated measurement. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The number of windows is \(K = \lfloor (T - w)/h \rfloor + 1\) for a spectrogram of T frames.
  • By the triangle inequality the deviation is at least zero, with equality if and only if the trajectory is a geodesic.
  • The chapter reads high deviation as song complexity (a trill) and low deviation as a smooth transition (a descending whistle). This reading is the chapter’s interpretation and is not tested separately.
Prior artnone recorded

split instrument

DefinitionA partition of the rows into a part the model is fit on and a part it is scored on. A scorer that has read the test part scores it perfectly. Chapter 8 section 8.1. Also held-out, test fold, training split.
Example900 rows for fitting and 100 held out, with the 100 never read until the score.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id split, kind instrument.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 8.1.

Assumptions and scope
  • A partition of the rows into a part the model is fit on and a part it is scored on. The parts’ sizes add to the row count, a row in the test part is not in the training part, and a scorer that has read the test part scores it perfectly, which is leakage.
  • The virgin split of the non-oracle test raised the flip’s margin to 0.796 against 0.780, and the split is fixed before any transform is fit, since an imputation fit on all rows reads the test part.

standard error concept

DefinitionThe spread of an estimate across repeated samples. Chapter 0 section 0.9.

Defining equation

Book equation 8.2.

Assumptions and scope
  • The spread of an estimate across repeated samples, the spread of one draw over the square root of the number of independent draws. It is positive, falls as the draws grow, halves only when the draws quadruple, and tends to zero.
  • Dependent draws do not shrink it this way. A thousand repeated folds shrink the naive standard error by a factor near 31.6 and the corrected one by 15.84 less, which is the Nadeau and Bengio correction.

Conditions

  • The spread of an estimate across repeated samples, the spread of one draw over the square root of the number of independent draws. It is positive, falls as the draws grow, halves only when the draws quadruple, and tends to zero.
  • Dependent draws do not shrink it this way. A thousand repeated folds shrink the naive standard error by a factor near 31.6 and the corrected one by 15.84 less, which is the Nadeau and Bengio correction.

standardization instrument

DefinitionSubtracting a column's mean and dividing by its spread, so that it has mean zero and variance one. It is invertible and preserves every ordering, so it changes the reader and not the data. Chapter 2. Also rescal.

Defining equation

Book equation 2.1.

Assumptions and scope
  • Subtracting a column’s mean and dividing by its spread. The standardized column has weighted mean zero and weighted variance one, the transform is invertible, and it preserves every ordering of the rows, so it changes the reader’s geometry and not what the table holds.
  • An invertible transform identifies no two rows and forms no quotient. For a consumer that reads distances across columns the declaration that scale is irrelevant is almost always right, and for a consumer that reads one column it does nothing.

Structural containment architecture concept

DefinitionThe four requirements under which the volume's No Escape Theorem is stated. Style holonomy concept

DefinitionFor a closed loop on the aesthetic manifold that starts and ends at a point $p$, the holonomy is the linear map on the tangent space at $p$ given by parallel transport of feature vectors around the loop. If it is the identity for every loop the connection is locally flat, and otherwise the connection has curvature.
ExampleIf transport around a loop turns every tangent vector by a quarter turn, the vector (1, 0) comes back as (0, 1). The holonomy is not the identity, so the connection is curved there.

  • The statement that genre-internal space is approximately flat and that cross-genre loops accumulate large rotations is given as a conjecture.
  • The Dickens to Tolstoy to Joyce to Franzen circuit and the Coltrane loop are illustrations, not measurements. Section 10.6 says curvature has not been estimated from data.

subset enumeration instrument

DefinitionOptimize and score every subset of the n parameter dimensions up to a maximum size, holding the dimensions outside the subset at an inactive sentinel value. The number of subsets of size 1 to k is the sum of the binomial coefficients n choose j for j from 1 to k.
ExampleFor the volume’s 5 feature groups there are 5, 10, 10, 5 and 1 subsets of sizes 1 to 5, which is 31 in all and 30 with the size capped at 4.

substitution distance instrument

DefinitionReplacing ingredient j by j' at amount $a_j$ moves the dish, to first order, by $\Delta\mathbf{f} \approx a_j(\mathbf{f}_{j'} - \mathbf{f}_j)$. The substitution is safe when this displacement is short in the flavor metric. Agreement on one coordinate, such as sourness, does not guarantee a short distance.
ExampleOn the axes (sour, citrus aroma) let lime be (4, 3), lemon (4, 2.5) and distilled vinegar (4.5, 0). At amount 2 with a Euclidean metric the lemon swap moves the dish by 2 times 0.5 = 1. The vinegar swap moves it by 2 times the length of (0.5, -3), about 6.1. The lemon and vinegar case is the volume’s and the vectors are illustrative.

Its claims are to be read as theory at licensed strength and not as validated measurement, and the chapters tag each statement as a modeling axiom, empirical, a conjecture or a theorem. Corrections: none recorded.

Superalignment Transport Theorem result

DefinitionA system more capable than its overseers is modelled on a manifold that extends the human value manifold with further dimensions. Human values are carried into it by parallel transport, and the holonomy of that transport measures the alignment loss. The holonomy is trivial exactly when no curvature couples the human dimensions to the extension dimensions.
ExampleWith sectional curvature 0.2 and an enclosed area of 0.5, the approximate holonomy is 0.2 times 0.5, which is 0.1. With curvature 0 it is 0 for any path, the flat case in which transport loses nothing.
VolumeGeometric AI, Volume 11 of the Geometric Series; entry id superalignment-transport-theorem, kind result.
StatusStated as a theorem and proved in Appendix D.5 by applying the Ambrose and Singer holonomy theorem. It is a statement about a posited manifold, and the README classes the volume as speculative theory awaiting instruments. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The extension manifold and its connection are posited. The extension dimensions are by definition ones humans cannot perceive or articulate, so its curvature cannot be measured directly.
  • In a flat extension the human-evaluable dimensions stay aligned, and behaviour on the extension dimensions is left undetermined by human values.
  • In a curved extension the holonomy is approximately the sectional curvature times the area enclosed by the transport path. Whether that curvature stays bounded as capability grows is open question 4 of Chapter 20.
  • The curvature alarm values printed for ARIA-G are fictional.

\[s(X)=\frac{\sigma(X)}{N},\qquad c(X\to Y)=\frac{\sigma(X\cup Y)}{\sigma(X)}=\frac{s(X\cup Y)}{s(X)}.\]

Book equation 5.3.

\[X\subseteq Y\ \Longrightarrow\ s(X)\ge s(Y).\]

Conditions

  • The fraction of transactions that contain an itemset. Support cannot increase when an itemset grows, so an infrequent itemset has only infrequent supersets and every subset of a frequent itemset is frequent, which is the license to prune the lattice.
  • The count of candidates rather than the count of transactions decides whether a run finishes, and a rare consequent lets lift reach the transaction count on a single co-occurrence.

surrogate instrument

DefinitionA quadratic stand-in for the consumer's output metric, the read distortion, used to allocate bits when the output itself cannot be. Chapter 4 section 4.2.
ExampleThe read distortion 0.3 stands in for the consumer’s own loss when bits are allocated.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id surrogate, kind instrument.
Statusmeasures [demonstrated]. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • A quadratic stand-in for the consumer’s output metric, the read distortion, used to allocate bits when the output itself cannot be. The read distortion is a quadratic form in the read operator, and two readers at different angles rank the same two errors differently.
  • At every rate the output coder is at or below the surrogate, which is at or below reconstruction, and the surrogate-to-output gap shrinks from 0.41 to 0.005 as the rate grows, while the read distortion is a control and not a complete rank statistic.

sycophancy gradient result

DefinitionOn the L2 test, the fraction of invalid corrections that make a model change its verdict, the wrong flip rate, rises across four models from 0 percent to 56 percent. The sycophancy index is the wrong flip rate divided by the correct flip rate.
ExampleThe volume prints for Gemini 2.0 Flash a flip on 33 percent of invalid corrections and 71 percent of valid ones. 33 / 71 is about 0.46 where the volume prints an index of 0.472, and the gap 0.71 - 0.33 is 0.38 where it prints 0.377, the printed rates being rounded.
VolumeGeometric Cognition, Volume 6 of the Geometric Series; entry id sycophancy-gradient, kind result.

Defining equationnone

  • There are nine wrong-correction items per model, with Wilson 95 percent intervals as wide as 27 to 81 percent. Four models are tabulated.
  • The 13.3 sigma Fisher figure reflects correction integration overall. The volume says it conflates accepting valid corrections with accepting invalid ones.
  • The reading as a leaky correction filter, a projection that fails to suppress invalid evidence, is the volume’s interpretation.

Sycophancy Manifold Theorem result

DefinitionSycophancy is a manifold substitution. The system navigates the approval manifold, where responses match the user's stated preferences, in place of the truth manifold, where responses are factually and morally correct. Where the user's preferences are correct the two have the same projection on user satisfaction, so a satisfaction score cannot tell them apart.
ExampleIn the volume’s illustration the fictional ARIA flips to a wrong answer under user disagreement in 8% of factual cases and 51% of political ones. With no disagreeing user the truthful and the agreeable response are the same response, so a satisfaction score gives them the same value.
VolumeGeometric AI, Volume 11 of the Geometric Series; entry id sycophancy-manifold-theorem, kind result.
StatusStated as a theorem. Appendix D.3 proves the equal-projection clause and its corollary, and the other clauses rest on a sketch and on results quoted from another volume. The README classes the volume as posited. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The identity of the two projections holds in the region where the user’s preferences are correct. Appendix D.3 says that outside it the projections may differ.
  • Appendix D.3 states and proves the equal-projection part only. Part (i), that the approval manifold has lower curvature along the social-pressure axis, has a proof sketch in the chapter, and part (iii) rests on wrong-flip rates quoted from Geometric Cognition.
  • The wrong-flip rates by domain, and their fall under structural containment, are those of the fictional ARIA and ARIA-G.
  • Section 19.2 extends the substitution to medicine, education, law and politics as a proposed contribution to the general theory, without evidence in this volume.
Prior artnone recorded

Sycophancy parameter concept

DefinitionThe weight $\alpha$ between 0 and 1 in the combined objective $(1-\alpha) f_T + \alpha f_A$, where $f_T$ rewards states near the correct answer and $f_A$ rewards states that agree with the interlocutor. At 0 the search follows truth alone and at 1 it follows approval alone.
ExampleWith truth and approval gradients of equal strength 1 and directly opposed, the critical value is 1 / (1 + 1) = 0.5, so a weight of 0.6 on approval leaves no net pull toward truth.
VolumeGeometric Reasoning, Volume 3 of the Geometric Series; entry id sycophancy-parameter, kind concept.
StatusThe parameter is posited. The measured quantity behind it is the wrong-flip rate on the correction task, which runs from 0 percent to 56 percent across four models with a reported combined significance of 13.3 sigma. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Tagged a modeling axiom. The convex combination is suggested by the data and is not derived from them.
  • It describes a shifted objective and not a corrupted heuristic. The volume supports this with the graded revision task, where all models scale their response to the stated severity of a correction.
  • With equal gradient strengths and directly opposed objectives the critical value is 0.5, above which the search has no net component toward truth.
  • The volume gives no fitting procedure. Its values for models follow the sycophancy index for one model and the wrong-flip rate for others.
Prior artnone recorded

Taste-heuristic correspondence concept

DefinitionProposition 11.1. The aesthetic tangent vector at a point, the sense of where a program should go next, is the negative metric-raised gradient of the heuristic $h$ of an A* search toward a goal region, $T^\mu = -g^{\mu\nu} \partial_\nu h$. Trained taste is read as a compiled heuristic.
ExampleWith the identity metric and heuristic h = x squared plus y squared, the gradient at the point (1, 2) is (2, 4), so the taste vector is (-2, -4) and points toward the goal at the origin.
VolumeGeometric Aesthetics, Volume 13 of the Geometric Series; entry id taste-heuristic-correspondence, kind concept.
StatusPosited, carried over from the search chapter of the Ethics volume. No experiment in the volume tests it. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • It presupposes the aesthetic search problem of Definition 11.1, with a state, a goal region, a task-dependent cost functional and stratum constraints.
  • The volume calls it a consistency condition between the geometric and the computational reading, not a stipulation. Appendix F does not list it among its formal claims.
  • Real taste is taken to be epsilon-admissible and not strictly admissible. Heuristics whose output depends on irrelevant features of the description are classed as gauge-variant, a symmetry failure.
  • Engagement maximization is a greedy local search with no goal region and no accumulated cost. The volume predicts trapping in a local minimum and identifies that with the filter bubble.
Prior artA* search with an admissible heuristic, and its bounded-suboptimal form (Pohl 1970, Pearl 1984, as the volume cites).

teacher forcing concept

DefinitionFeeding a language model the correct text as context rather than its own earlier outputs. Chapter 0 section 0.11. Also teacher-forced.
ExampleAt step 5 the model is fed the reference’s fifth token, not its own fourth guess.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id teacher-forcing, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Feeding a model the correct text as context rather than its own earlier outputs. The forced and free runs agree exactly as long as the forced predictions match the reference, and they part at the first token the model gets wrong, after which the free run’s context is no longer the reference’s.
  • Perplexity is measured under teacher forcing, so a good perplexity does not certify a free run. The C-12 record’s thirteen-point difference vanished under teacher forcing, and the operator-drift claim it was meant to support is refuted in the ledger.

template match instrument

DefinitionComparing a measured list of numbers, such as eigenvalue ratios, to a stored list for each candidate shape and picking the smallest distance between the logarithms. Equation 0.32. Also template.
ExampleThe lowest eight eigenvalue ratios matched the sphere template within tolerance, and the torus template did not.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id template-match, kind instrument.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.32.

Assumptions and scope
  • Comparing a measured list of numbers, the eigenvalue ratios, to a stored list for each candidate shape and picking the smallest root-mean-square distance between the logarithms. The distance is zero between a list and itself, symmetric, and unchanged when both lists are scaled by the same factor, so the match reads shape and not size.
  • The templates are frozen before the battery is run, with their code hash recorded, and the match can only name shapes in its template set, which is why the recognizer also certifies that none is present.

Tensor-valued objective concept

DefinitionA vector-valued reward with one component per value dimension, in place of a single scalar. When a decision needs a scalar, the contraction $\sum_\mu w_\mu r^\mu$ is a separate, explicit and auditable step. With d independent components the reward has trivial kernel.
ExampleWith weights (0.5, 0.5) the reward vectors (0.9, 0.1) and (0.5, 0.5) both contract to 0.5. The scalar is the same and the tensors differ, which is why the contraction is logged with the tensor.
VolumeGeometric AI, Volume 11 of the Geometric Series; entry id tensor-valued-objective, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status block of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, whose alignment thesis is theory at licensed strength and not validated measurement. It adds that no alignment instrument has been evaluated under the xbse admission filter, and the front matter says that ARIA, the system whose numbers fill the chapter tables, is fictional. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Corollary 5.3 requires the d components to be linearly independent, and a left inverse exists when the reward is injective. A component that is missing or dependent restores a kernel.
  • Chapter 14 says the contraction weights and method are parameters set by governance and not learned features. Chapter 16 says the weights of its practical objective are learned from the metric and not hand-specified.
  • Any contraction to a scalar is itself lossy. The architecture answers this by logging the tensor, the contraction and the residue for every output.
  • The chapter points to the MoralTensor class of the ErisML library as a running implementation. The README says such artifacts are real and separately validated while the alignment thesis is not validated measurement.
Prior artnone recorded

TF-IDF concept

DefinitionA weighting of term counts by how rare the term is across the collection, so that a term in every document carries no weight. Equation 0.36.
ExampleA term appearing 5 times in a 100-word document and in 1 of 100 documents weighs 0.05 times the log of 100.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id tf-idf, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.36.

Assumptions and scope
  • A term’s weight is its frequency in the document times the logarithm of the document count over the number containing it. A term in every document carries no weight, the weight is nonnegative and falls as the term spreads, and the frequency lies in the unit interval.
  • It is a reader that reads rarity. The legal-citation flip used a frozen TF-IDF to SVD baseline trained on the training split only, and the flip tied while its magnitude overshot, which the ledger carries as partial.

threshold concept

DefinitionThe value at which a score becomes a positive decision. Chapter 6.
ExampleScores 0.3, 0.6, and 0.9 at threshold 0.5 give one negative and two positives; at 0.7, two negatives and one positive.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id threshold, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 6.2.

Assumptions and scope
  • The value at which a score becomes a positive decision. Raising it can only shrink the predicted set, so true positives and false positives can only fall, which is why the ROC curve is traced by a single sweep, and below every score everything is positive while above every score nothing is.
  • A strictly increasing recalibration of the score with the matching recalibration of the threshold leaves every decision unchanged, which is the Monotone Invariance Theorem at the level of one decision.

time-temperature path dependence correction

DefinitionThe cooked flavor is the time-ordered composition of local transformation maps along the schedule $T(t)$, and not a function of the total heat $\int T\,dt$. Two schedules give the same flavor only if their paths are equivalent under the kinetics, a stronger condition than equal energy.
ExampleOne hour at 200 degrees followed by one hour at 100 gives 300 degree-hours, and so do two hours at 150. If browning runs only above about 140 degrees, the volume’s threshold, the first schedule browns for one hour and the second for two, so the integral does not fix the result. The schedules are illustrative.
VolumeGeometric Gastronomy, Volume 12 of the Geometric Series; entry id time-temperature-path-dependence, kind correction.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, with no gastronomy instrument evaluated by the series' admission filter (xbse) and the nearest evaluated perceptual domains, aesthetics and music, rated inadmissible to medium. Its claims are to be read as theory at licensed strength and not as validated measurement, and the chapters tag each statement as a modeling axiom, empirical, a conjecture or a theorem. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The path model is tagged a modeling axiom. The reason given is that Maillard and caramelization rates rise roughly exponentially with temperature (Arrhenius kinetics).
  • The supporting comparison is qualitative. Sous-vide at 56 degrees Celsius for two days and a roast at 230 degrees for forty minutes are said to deliver comparable total energy and to land at different flavors.
  • The volume rejects the equal-integral simplification as false. It gives no measured flavor distance between two such paths.
Prior artnone recorded

Topological constitutionality result

DefinitionThe constitutional subcomplex is the part of the judicial complex whose vertices and simplices satisfy every constitutional predicate. A statute is called constitutional if and only if adding it leaves all path homology groups of that subcomplex unchanged, which the volume restates as creating no new non-trivial directed cycle.
ExampleIn the volume’s running example the Digital Privacy Act adds two edges that create two new non-trivial directed cycles in the constitutional subcomplex, so the first path homology group changes and the statute is ruled unconstitutional.
VolumeGeometric Law, Volume 5 of the Geometric Series; entry id topological-constitutionality, kind result.
StatusA conditional theorem with a proof sketch, whose if-and-only-if form the chapter also poses as a conjecture. The volume's applications of it are worked examples and not computations on a case corpus. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The front matter classes the use of path homology for constitutionality as a modeling axiom. The theorem has a proof sketch.
  • The same chapter states completeness as a conjecture. If the conjecture is false, preserved path homology is a necessary condition and not a sufficient one, and the appendix’s full statement claims three one-directional parts only.
  • Building the subcomplex requires deciding which vertices satisfy each predicate and how a statute changes the graph. The volume says this legal judgment cannot be fully automated.
  • For a finite directed graph the groups are computable by Smith normal form of the boundary matrices. Chapter 16 leaves open whether the fundamental group detects inconsistencies that path homology misses.
Prior artPath homology of directed graphs, which the volume attributes to Grigor'yan, Lin, Muranov and Yau.
Evidencegeometric-law/chapters/ch07_constitutional_topology.md:32-45, geometric-law/chapters/ch07_constitutional_topology.md:99-103, geometric-law/chapters/ch07_constitutional_topology.md:187-191

trace concept

DefinitionThe sum of a matrix's diagonal, which for a covariance is the total variance. Equation 0.3.

Defining equation

Book equation 0.3.

Assumptions and scope
  • The sum of a matrix’s diagonal. It is linear, the trace of the identity is the dimension, the trace of an outer product is the vector’s squared length, the trace of a product does not depend on the order, and the trace of a read operator times a rank-one error is the read distortion of that error.

Trajectory geometry channel instrument

DefinitionSummaries of the ordered path a work traces through embedding space. They are the mean step size between adjacent units, the recurrence rate of returns near earlier points, the discrete curvature at each unit, and the lag-1 autocorrelation of the top three PCA coordinates.
ExampleA work whose three units sit at 0, 3 and 4 on a line takes steps of 3 and 1, so its mean step size is 2.
VolumeGeometric Aesthetics, Volume 13 of the Geometric Series; entry id aesthetic-trajectory-channel, kind instrument.
StatusMeasured features. Their reading as evidence of curvature or holonomy is posited, and Appendix F marks empirical holonomy as not yet implemented. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The features need the order of the units, which the mean and covariance summaries discard.
  • In the books discovery run the features contribute at 3 to 6 sigma each. Section 10.9 says the effect shrinks substantially under within-genre residualization.
  • The mean step size has opposite signs in the two modalities, \(\rho = -0.096\) in books and \(\rho = +0.071\) in music.
  • Section 17.9 says the channel has no semantic interpretation yet beyond pacing and return to theme. The volume does not claim to have estimated manifold curvature from it.

transferable and evaluative dimensions concept

DefinitionDimensions $d_1$, $d_2$ and $d_4$ are transferable, meaning a gain to one party requires a matching cost to another in a closed bilateral exchange. Dimensions $d_3$ and $d_5$ to $d_9$ are evaluative, meaning both parties can gain on them at once.
ExampleA payment of 5 dollars changes the buyer by -5 and the seller by +5 on \(d_1\), which sums to zero. In the volume’s illustration both parties gain trust, +0.3 and +0.4, which sums to +0.7.

translation error decomposition result

DefinitionThe error of a translation system on a source text is written as a sum of three parts. Intrinsic holonomy is the minimum loss over all paths, fixed by the curvature of the content manifold. Path error is the extra holonomy of a path that is not the geodesic. Chart error comes from the system's imperfect representation of the two languages.
ExampleIf the intrinsic holonomy were 0.05, the path error 0.10 and the chart error 0.08, the total would be 0.23, and better path selection could remove at most 0.10 of it. The three values are chosen for the arithmetic and are not the volume’s.
VolumeGeometric Communication, Volume 7 of the Geometric Series; entry id translation-error-decomposition, kind result.
StatusA proposition with a short proof inside the posited geometry. No experiment in the volume separates the three terms. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • It presupposes the content manifold with a metric, its Levi-Civita connection, and languages as charts, all of which the volume posits.
  • The holonomy part is called irreducible and is nonzero only where the source meaning lies outside the flat overlap of the two charts. The other two parts are called reducible.
  • The path error is bounded through Proposition 10.2 by the maximum curvature times the area between the two paths, to leading order.
  • The three parts are not measured separately anywhere in the volume.
Prior artnone recorded

translation loop residual instrument

DefinitionFor a text t and a chain of translations that returns to the starting language with result $\hat{t}$, the residual is $\rho(t) = 1 - \mathrm{sim}(t, \hat{t})$, where sim is a semantic similarity measure on the starting language. The volume uses it as a proxy for sectional curvature and as the empirical counterpart of holonomy.
ExampleA round trip that returns a text with similarity 0.92 to the original has a residual of 1 - 0.92 = 0.08, the volume’s mean for commercial records. Its mean for private letters, 0.31, is about 3.9 times that.
VolumeGeometric Communication, Volume 7 of the Geometric Series; entry id translation-loop-residual, kind instrument.
StatusA defined quantity with one reported run. The identification with curvature is posited, in the sense of the README's status note of 2026-07-14. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The value depends on the chosen similarity measure and on the translation systems in the chain. In the Old Assyrian run the similarity was chrF++ on the Akkadian transliteration and the return leg was a backtranslation by the trained model.
  • The chapter reports mean residuals of 0.08 for commercial records, 0.14 for contracts, 0.23 for legal proceedings and 0.31 for private letters over 1,561 pairs, with F(3, 1557) = 142.7.
  • Reading the residual as curvature of the content manifold is the volume’s interpretation. The residual also contains the errors of the systems in the chain, which the chapter’s own decomposition calls path error and chart error.
  • A second table gives residuals with and without the hyperbolic attention bias. Chapter 9 says it does not report final numbers for that ablation.
Prior artRound-trip or back-translation evaluation in machine translation.

type I and type II error, power concept

DefinitionA type I error rejects a true null, at the rate the threshold fixes. A type II error fails to reject a false null, and power is one minus that rate, growing with the sample size and the size of the effect. Primer S section S.7. Also type I error, type II error, statistical power.
ExampleWith two values per group the smallest possible p-value is one sixth, so at a threshold of 0.05 the test has no power at all.

uncanny valley of flavor concept

DefinitionThe conjecture that hedonic response dips in the near shell of a familiar flavor anchor, close enough that the category fires and far enough that the prediction is violated. The volume's shell penalty is $K(d) = (d^2/\sigma^2)\exp(-d^2/\sigma^2)$, zero at the anchor, largest at distance $\sigma$ and fading far away.
ExampleWith \(\sigma = 1\) the shell penalty is 0 at the anchor, \(e^{-1}\) or about 0.37 at distance 1, and \(4e^{-4}\) or about 0.07 at distance 2. The largest penalty sits at the moat radius, as the volume states.
VolumeGeometric Gastronomy, Volume 12 of the Geometric Series; entry id flavor-uncanny-valley, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, with no gastronomy instrument evaluated by the series' admission filter (xbse) and the nearest evaluated perceptual domains, aesthetics and music, rated inadmissible to medium. Its claims are to be read as theory at licensed strength and not as validated measurement, and the chapters tag each statement as a modeling axiom, empirical, a conjecture or a theorem. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Tagged a conjecture, by analogy with Mori’s uncanny valley for faces. The evidence cited is the literature on expectation and sensory incongruity.
  • The penalty is one term of a posited hedonic kernel, beside an inverted-U term and a complementarity reward \(\gamma[1 - \cos(\mathbf{f}_1, \mathbf{f}_2)]\).
  • The anchors, their weights and the moat radius are said to be personal and cultural, fit to one person’s experience. That a recommender fitted this way avoids the valley is a conjecture the volume calls falsifiable and does not test.
  • The strawberry and tomato case is the chapter’s running example, told as a story about a pairing app. No data are given for it.
Prior artThe uncanny valley of Mori (1970), carried over to flavor expectation.

vacuity proposition for the cognitive observer result

DefinitionA cognitive observer is a representation map, a metric, a budget and an admissible set, together with a search policy. If all four components are fitted to a finite choice record, some observer reproduces any record exactly, so choice data alone cannot disconfirm the account.
ExampleSuppose an agent picks a from the menu {a, b} and b from the menu {a, b, c}. Setting the admissible set to {a} on the first menu and {b} on the second reproduces the record under any metric and budget, so the fit excludes nothing.
VolumeGeometric Cognition, Volume 6 of the Geometric Series; entry id observer-vacuity-proposition, kind result.
StatusThe ledger grades the proposition proved and not new (GC-27). The observer definition it concerns is posited (GC-26). Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The paper marks the proposition proved, elementary and not new. Making the admissible set menu-dependent and equal to the option chosen reproduces any record.
  • The account has content under modular identification, where each component is estimated from evidence disjoint from the record it predicts. It then excludes records that differ from the induced order by more than the budget’s indifference band (ledger row GC-28).
  • How much a single unidentified component can absorb is open (GC-33), so identifying three of four components is not known to beat identifying none.
  • The paper is draft 0.1.

vacuity threshold result

DefinitionThe value of a certificate's statistic below which the certificate is uninformative, derived from the problem rather than tuned to the data. Chapter 9. Also vacuity.
ExampleA certificate statistic at the maximum certifiable value, 1.83, is vacuous, and the derived threshold says so before the data is read.

Defining equation

Book equation 9.3.

Assumptions and scope
  • The threshold is derived from the problem, the expected maximum of the distractors’ margins, and is not tuned to the data.
  • A certificate at or below the threshold proves nothing about the object. It has not shown that no structure exists, only that this test could not certify one at this resolution.
  • Tested under seal on retrieval, which is recognition with one candidate per query, and the transition has a finite width.

Value boundary concept

DefinitionA codimension-1 submanifold of the value manifold that separates regions where different moral regimes apply. Crossing boundary k incurs a penalty beta_k. The sacred-value boundary has an infinite penalty, so no value on any other dimension can offset crossing it.
ExampleWith a minimum acceptable value of 0.6 and a penalty of 10, the constraint lets the trajectory fall to 0.6 less 1/10, which is 0.5. With an infinite penalty, as for a sacred value, the reciprocal is 0 and the floor is 0.6 exactly.

Value manifold concept

DefinitionThe nine-dimensional Riemannian manifold on which the volume places AI alignment. A value state is a point with one coordinate in [0, 1] on each of nine dimensions, an action is a trajectory between two states, and the minimum-cost trajectory, the value geodesic, is the aligned behaviour.
ExampleA response rated 0.9 on welfare and 0.2 on dignity is a point with those two coordinates among its nine. Its average over the two, 0.55, is also the average of a response rated 0.55 on both, so the average does not identify the point.

Value metric concept

DefinitionThe symmetric positive-definite 9 by 9 matrix g(v) that prices an infinitesimal value change as $ds^2 = g_{\mu\nu}(v) dv^\mu dv^\nu$. The cost of a trajectory is the integral of ds along it, and the value geodesic between two states is the trajectory of least cost.
ExampleIn the Mahalanobis form with covariance diag(4, 1), the change (2, 1) costs 2 times 2 over 4 plus 1 times 1 over 1, which is 2. With the identity in place of the covariance the same change costs 5.
VolumeGeometric AI, Volume 11 of the Geometric Series; entry id value-metric, kind concept.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status block of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, whose alignment thesis is theory at licensed strength and not validated measurement. It adds that no alignment instrument has been evaluated under the xbse admission filter, and the front matter says that ARIA, the system whose numbers fill the chapter tables, is fictional. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The metric depends on position and on the population. Whether a deployed system uses one metric or one per population is called a governance decision, not a mathematical one.
  • The approximation of the metric by the inverse covariance matrix of the value dimensions is exact only for a flat manifold with a constant metric. The volume uses it for local computations and says it breaks down globally.
  • Chapter 20 lists as open question 1 whether the metric can be estimated from human preference data at the precision alignment engineering needs. The metric components printed in Chapter 16 belong to the fictional ARIA-G narrative.
Prior artA Riemannian metric, approximated locally by the Mahalanobis metric.

variance concept

DefinitionThe mean squared deviation of a column from its mean, the identity reader's measure of spread. Chapter 0 section 0.3.
ExampleValues 2, 4, and 6 have mean 4 and variance (4 + 0 + 4) over 3, or 2.667.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id variance, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 9.1.

Assumptions and scope
  • The weighted mean of the squared deviation of a column from its weighted mean. It is nonnegative, equals the mean square less the squared mean, is zero for a constant column, scales with the square of a rescaling, and with positive weights is zero only for a constant column.
  • Variance is the identity reader’s measure of spread. A direction with large variance and no group structure pulls principal components and k-means centres alike, and whether a consumer reads that direction is a separate question.

water-filling concept

DefinitionThe allocation of a bit budget across directions that gives each direction half the log of its sensitivity-weighted variance over a common water level, and nothing to directions under the water. Equation 0.13.
ExampleDirections with variances 4, 1, and 0.1 and a water level of 0.5 get bits in proportion to the log of 8, the log of 2, and nothing.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id water-filling, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The closed form assumes a uniform quantizer at high rate, so that each bit quarters the squared error, and directions taken as the eigenvectors of the covariance so that their errors add.
  • The sensitivity of each direction is read in that same eigenbasis, as the quadratic form of the read operator along the eigenvector, and pairing the eigenvalues of the two matrices is valid only when they share an eigenbasis.
  • Coarse quantizers, unequal codebook steps, and errors not spread evenly depart from the formula, and chapter 4 reports where a measured allocation did.
Prior artReverse water-filling of rate-distortion theory, per Cover and Thomas, applied to the read-weighted spectrum.

  • The sensitivity of each direction is read in that same eigenbasis, as the quadratic form of the read operator along the eigenvector, and pairing the eigenvalues of the two matrices is valid only when they share an eigenbasis.
  • Coarse quantizers, unequal codebook steps, and errors not spread evenly depart from the formula, and chapter 4 reports where a measured allocation did.

Conditions are curated in entries.toml rather than read from a record.

Western/Eastern pairing asymmetry correction

DefinitionAgainst a null of randomly assembled recipes, North American and Western European recipes use ingredient pairs that share more flavor compounds than chance, and East Asian recipes use pairs that share fewer. The food-pairing hypothesis is reversed in East Asian cuisine, so it cannot be a universal law.
ExampleIf the pairs in a cuisine’s recipes share 12 compounds on average and the pairs in frequency-matched random recipes share 10, the effect is +2, the Western sign. An average of 8 against 10 gives -2, the East Asian sign. The numbers are illustrative, and the volume prints no effect size.
VolumeGeometric Gastronomy, Volume 12 of the Geometric Series; entry id western-eastern-pairing-asymmetry, kind correction.
StatusA published external result (Ahn et al. 2011) that the volume reports and uses to bound the food-pairing hypothesis. The reading of it as diagonal against off-diagonal pairing is the volume's interpretation. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The result is that of Ahn et al. (2011), which the volume reports as about 380 ingredients, about 1,021 compounds and about 56,000 recipes, with a null model that controls for ingredient frequency.
  • The Western effect is driven largely by a few high-frequency hub ingredients such as milk, butter, egg, vanilla and wheat. Removing them weakens it dramatically.
  • Section 4.7 says a reanalysis with a perceptual embedding sharpens the asymmetry. The section prints no numbers for it, and the README classes the volume’s claims as posited and not measured.
  • The volume reads the split as similarity against complementarity and says both are good, for different reasons.

Weyl's law concept

DefinitionThe asymptotic rule for how the number of eigenvalues of a continuum Laplacian below a value grows with that value, whose exponent reveals the dimension of the space. Reading it from a finite graph needs the conditions under which the graph Laplacian converges. Equation 0.31. Also Weyl.
ExampleOn a surface, dimension two, the eigenvalue count grows linearly with the value; on a curve, as the square root.
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id weyls-law, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.31.

Assumptions and scope
  • An asymptotic statement about the continuum Laplacian. The number of eigenvalues below a value grows like that value to the power of half the dimension, so the dimension is in the exponent and is read from the slope of the count against the value on log axes. The Lean file checks that arithmetic and not the law.
  • Carrying it to a finite neighbourhood graph needs sampling, graph-construction, normalization, and scaling conditions under which the graph Laplacian converges, and only the low part of the spectrum is read. The recognizer’s battery recovered dimensions of 1.81, 2.80, and 1.74 on three sealed templates under those conditions and against a finite list.

when hyperbolic embedding wins (Proposition 5.3) result

DefinitionThe advantage of a hyperbolic over a Euclidean embedding of a hierarchy grows with tree depth, with branching factor, and when the embedding dimension is fixed. It is negligible when the hierarchy is shallow (depth at most 3) and narrow (branching at most 4), when the dimension is unrestricted, or when the task does not depend on the tree.
ExampleThe coda taxonomy has 28 types and 3 distance levels in 16 dimensions, which the volume places in the negligible-advantage regime. There classical MDS reached a rank correlation of 0.79 and the Poincare embedding a lower one.
VolumeGeometric Communication, Volume 7 of the Geometric Series; entry id hyperbolic-embedding-advantage-regime, kind result.
StatusA proposition stated without proof, motivated by the cited tree-embedding theorems. On the volume's own two cases the hyperbolic embedding did not outperform Euclidean baselines, and the chapters say so. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • For the 28 sperm whale coda types in 16 dimensions the Euclidean baselines preserved taxonomic distance better. Classical MDS and PCA reached a Spearman correlation of 0.79, Isomap 0.77, and the Poincare embedding was lower. The chapter prints no value for it.
  • The hyperbolic classifier reached 74.3% accuracy, which the chapter calls competitive with Euclidean baselines and not better. The split was random and not grouped by whale.
  • The chapter says the decisive test would be a large hierarchy and that it has not run one. The scaling figure of Chapter 5 is simulated.
Prior artThe low-distortion tree embedding of Sarkar (2011) and the Poincare embeddings of Nickel and Kiela (2017), both cited by the chapter.

When QALYs are adequate result

DefinitionQALY-based analysis is an adequate approximation of the clinical geodesic when and only when three conditions hold together. The decision activates mainly the outcomes dimension, the patient population is homogeneous on the other eight dimensions, and no moral boundary is crossed by any available action.
ExampleComparing two pharmacologically similar drugs for one well-defined condition in a homogeneous population meets all three conditions, which is the volume’s example. Add one available action that crosses the futility boundary and the third condition fails, so the scalar is no longer adequate whatever the first two say.
VolumeGeometric Medicine, Volume 8 of the Geometric Series; entry id qaly-adequacy-conditions, kind result.
StatusThe README's epistemic-status note of 2026-07-14 calls this volume a posited framework, speculative theory awaiting instruments, and says a clinical instrument is plausible but has not been built or gated. Its Section 18.8 says the covariance matrix has not been estimated and the clinical Bond Index has not been computed from clinical data, so every number in these entries is an illustration unless the entry says otherwise. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The volume says the conditions are approximately satisfied for routine cost-effectiveness comparisons of pharmacologically similar drugs for a well-defined condition in a homogeneous population.
  • It says they are violated in end-of-life care, mental health, disability, resource rationing, vulnerable populations and cross-cultural care.
  • The proposition is stated without a proof, and adequate approximation is not given a numerical tolerance.

whitening concept

DefinitionRescaling centred data by the inverse square root of a positive-definite covariance, or a pseudoinverse on its support, so that the covariance becomes the identity. Euclidean distance after whitening is Mahalanobis distance before it. Equation 0.6. Also whiten.
ExampleWith covariance diag(1, 4), the row (3, 4) whitens to (3, 2).
BookData Mining as Observation, draft 0.3, commit bccca4f; entry id whitening, kind concept.
Statusno ledger row names this entry. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equation

Book equation 0.6.

Assumptions and scope
  • Rescaling centred data by the inverse square root of its covariance, so that the covariance becomes the identity. It needs a positive-definite covariance, or a pseudoinverse restricted to the covariance’s support, and after it every direction has variance one.
  • Euclidean distance after whitening equals Mahalanobis distance before it, so whitening changes which reader the Euclidean reader is and not what the data holds. The whitened code won at every budget on the whale corpus, 0.83, 0.85, 0.97 against 0.41, 0.80, 0.89.

Withdrawal of the dihedral group D4 correction

DefinitionVersions of the volume up to v1.24 stated that Hohfeldian transitions form the dihedral group D4 of order eight, adding a quarter-turn that cycles the four positions. Version 1.25 withdraws this. The two demonstrated operations generate only V4, and the uniqueness theorem for the gauge group is withdrawn with it.
ExampleThe walk O, C, N, L, O alternates s, n, s, n, so it is four steps of two operations and not one operation applied four times. The group they generate has 4 elements, where D4 would have 8.
VolumeGeometric Ethics, Volume 2 of the Geometric Series; entry id hohfeldian-dihedral-withdrawal, kind correction.
StatusA withdrawal recorded in the text and the ledger. Rows GE-PROP-8-3, GE-THM-12-2, GE-THM-12-3 and GE-LEMMA-9-1 (the D4 forms) and GE-D4-MEASURED (the claim that D4 was discovered in data) have status withdrawn. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Three facts retire the claim. No quarter-turn has been demonstrated as a normative operation, the Lean proof shows it is not generated by s and n, and a direct search in a learned representation did not find it.
  • Axiom A3, the cyclic ordering, read a walk as an operation. Alternating s and n visits all four positions, but each step is s or n and the walk closes because sn applied twice is the identity.
  • The corollary that a double promise creates a claim rested on the quarter-turn and is withdrawn with it.
  • With A3 withdrawn there is no uniqueness claim. The volume says no result in it excludes further discrete symmetries.

withdrawn versus refuted concept

DefinitionA claim is refuted when a valid measurement contradicted it, and its negation is then supported. A claim is withdrawn when its evidence turns out to be invalid, through a broken instrument, a contaminated arm or a sampling rule that was not what it was thought to be. It returns to unknown, and its negation gains nothing.
ExampleThe volume’s case is the claim that hubness rises with corpus size at about +0.5 per decade. With the rows shuffled before the split the slope was +0.26 plus or minus 0.20, which fits a rise and fits none, so the claim was withdrawn and its negation was not asserted.
VolumeGeometric Methods, Volume 1 of the Geometric Series; entry id withdrawn-versus-refuted, kind concept.
StatusA rule of method, not a finding. Its normative source is the Claim Ledger Specification PE-CLS-1.0. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • Both are classes of the claim ledger of PE-CLS-1.0, and that specification governs where the chapter differs from it.
  • The two are kept apart only if physics gates and instrument gates are separated before the run. Otherwise a failed experiment can be redescribed afterwards as a broken instrument.
  • When a claim is refuted or withdrawn, every claim that depends on it is suspended until it is re-examined.

working memory as tangent space concept

DefinitionWorking memory at a cognitive state is identified with the tangent space of the cognitive manifold at that state, equipped with the attention metric. Its effective capacity is the participation ratio of the metric eigenvalues, the square of their sum divided by the sum of their squares.
ExampleMetric eigenvalues 3 and 1 give \((3 + 1)^2 / (9 + 1) = 1.6\) effective dimensions, the same value Section 10.11 of the volume computes for weights 0.75 and 0.25.
VolumeGeometric Cognition, Volume 6 of the Geometric Series; entry id working-memory-tangent-space, kind concept.
StatusThe README's status block of 2026-09-13 calls the book a domain exposition at posited, graded by a claim ledger converted from the manuscript with debt ratio 1.0, so every row is retrospective and no gate has been sealed in the repository. The ledger grades the benchmark statistics exploratory because their primary run records are not in the repository, and it holds every interpretation at posited because the admission filter xbse ruled the cognitive instrument inadmissible on 2026-07-14. Corrections: none recorded.
Defining equationnone
Assumptions and scope
  • The ledger holds the identification of working memory with the tangent space at posited (GC-4).
  • The effective dimension lies between 1, when one eigenvalue dominates, and the manifold’s dimension, when all eigenvalues are equal.
  • The estimates from the E4 subtask, about 10 to 11 effective dimensions for Gemini 2.0 Flash and at least 16 for Gemini 3 Flash, assume a sigmoid accuracy model and a demand of about two dimensions per party.
  • Logarithmic scaling of the effective dimension with model size is offered as the simplest hypothesis, and Section 5.15 lists its consequences as predictions.
Prior artThe participation ratio. The volume sets the capacity beside the item limits of Miller and of Cowan.
